cards.s_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: *And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;* (Matthew 1:3). *And in those days Judah went to the house of Shem and took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.* (Jasher 45:23). Matthew puts Thamar in the line of the Messiah (Christ), and Jasher tells where Yahudah (Judah) found her: in the house of Shem, the daughter of Elam the son of Shem. She is not a Canaanite brought in from outside; she is a daughter of Shem's own house, inside the kept line from Noah, and her sons Phares and Zara are of that seed on both sides. The women named in Matthew 1 are there to show the seed of promise being guarded, not strangers being added to it, and Jasher 45 is the witness that settles where Tamar came from.
cards.s_text: And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;
cards.t_text: And in those days Judah went to the house of Shem and took Tamar the daughter of Elam, the son of Shem, for a wife for his first born Er.

cards.note: *And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.* (Jasher 45:32) The Jasher narrative of the conception of Peretz and Zerah — the twins through whom the Davidic kingship-line walks. Tamar's case preserved the line; Jasher walks the preservation in extra detail.
cards.s_text: And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;
cards.t_text: And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.

cards.note: *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jubilees 46:1). *When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:* (Matthew 2:14). Jubilees opens its account of Egypt with a people at rest there. After Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied, became a great nation, and loved one another all the days of Joseph; Egypt was a shelter before it was a prison. Matthew's Joseph takes the child down the same road by night, and Egypt shelters him too, until Herod is dead. The child walks the path his people walked, a sojourn in Egypt and a calling out of it, so that what happened to the nation happens again in the one who came for the nation.
cards.s_text: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: *And he commanded the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* The Yoseph who went down to Egypt willed his bones be carried out; the Yahusha (Jesus) who went down to Egypt would come up by his own resurrection. The patriarchal-Yoseph's bones-out-of-Egypt is the prototype the Messianic-Yashar'el fulfills in flesh.
cards.s_text: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16). *And the woman conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Miriam, because in those days the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Israel.* (Jasher 67:3). Jasher tells the Egyptian slaughter in fuller detail than Exodus 1 gives it, and it counts from inside one family: Miriam is named for the bitterness of the days she was born into, and in the next verse Aaron is born as Pharaoh begins to spill the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel). Herod at Bethlehem is the same hand in a later century, a king killing the infants of a town to reach one child. The kingdom of man always moves to kill the promised seed at its birth. It failed with Moses and it failed with Yahusha (Jesus).
cards.s_text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
cards.t_text: And the woman conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Miriam, because in those days the Egyptians had embittered the lives of the children of Israel.

cards.note: *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* (Matthew 2:16). *And she conceived again and bare a son and she called his name Aaron, for in the days of her conception, Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Israel.* (Jasher 67:4). Jasher gives the decree a date: it began in the days Aaron was conceived, and the boy's own name carries it. Matthew gives Herod's decree a date too, from two years old and under, reckoned from the time the wise men told him. Pharaoh spilled the blood of the male children of Yashar'el (Israel) to keep a deliverer from rising; Herod slew the children of Bethlehem to keep the King from rising. Same fear, same answer, and in both cases the king's sword missed the one child it was sharpened for.
cards.s_text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.
cards.t_text: And she conceived again and bare a son and she called his name Aaron, for in the days of her conception, Pharaoh began to spill the blood of the male children of Israel.

cards.note: *And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be thou there until I bring thee word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.* (Matthew 2:13). *There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi, whose name was Amram, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.* (Jasher 67:1). Jasher 67 opens where the story of the deliverer begins, with his father, a man of the seed of Levi living in Egypt in the years when Pharaoh would begin to spill the blood of the male children. Matthew 2 opens the story of the greater deliverer the same way, with a father warned by the angel of Yahuah (the Lord) to carry the child into Egypt because a king is seeking to destroy him. Moses was hidden in Egypt from Pharaoh; Yahusha (Jesus) was hidden in Egypt from Herod. The kingdom of man always moves to kill the promised seed at its birth, and there is always a household ready to hide the child.
cards.s_text: And when they were departed, behold, the angel of Yahuah (Lord) appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and be you there until I bring you word: for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.
cards.t_text: There was a man in the land of Egypt of the seed of Levi, whose name was Amram, the son of Kehath, the son of Levi, the son of Israel.

cards.note: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* 1 Enoch 90:6 names the late-age awakening of the lambs — the white-sheep born to the white-sheep who open their eyes and see. The fishers-of-men commission at Matt 4:19 enters the same awakening-architecture: the gathering of the scattered-and-now-awakening sheep, the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) opening their eyes when the Shepherd's voice reaches them.
cards.s_text: And he says unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
cards.t_text: But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.

cards.note: *But by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful, and have made your children to be of a good hope that you give repentance for sins.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:19). *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). Solomon says the Father's dealings with Yashar'el's (Israel's) enemies were themselves the lesson: by such works he taught his people that the just man should be merciful, and gave his children good hope that he gives repentance for sins. The King teaches the same lesson from the same source. Love your enemies, bless those who curse you, pray for those who persecute you, and the reason follows in the next verse: so that you may be children of your Father, who does exactly that. The mercy the children show is learned from watching the Father show it.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
cards.t_text: But by such works have you taught your people that the just man should be merciful, and have made your children to be of a good hope that you give repentance for sins.

cards.note: *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* (Ecclesiasticus 28:2). *And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.* (Matthew 6:12). Sirach says forgive your neighbour the hurt he did you, and then your own sins will be forgiven when you pray. That is the petition Yahusha (Jesus) taught his disciples to pray, forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors, and the condition is the same in both. Pardon received and pardon extended are named in one breath, in the same act of prayer. The disciples' prayer was not a new idea in Yashar'el (Israel); the wise had been teaching sons to pray this way for generations.
cards.s_text: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
cards.t_text: Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.

cards.note: *He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?* (Ecclesiasticus 28:4). *But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.* (Matthew 6:15). Sirach presses the question down to the heart: a man shows no mercy to another man, one made like himself, and then asks forgiveness for his own sins? Yahusha (Jesus) answers it in the Sermon: if you forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive yours. The brother who is like you is the test. The heart that withholds mercy from him has no standing to ask it from the Father, and the wise in Yashar'el (Israel) had been saying so long before the disciples' prayer was taught.
cards.s_text: But if you forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
cards.t_text: He sheweth no mercy to a man, which is like himself: and does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?

cards.note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?* (Matthew 7:16). Sirach says the fruit tells you whether the tree was dressed, and a man's speech tells you what is in his heart. Yahusha (Jesus) gives the same test for recognizing false prophets: you will know them by their fruits, because thorns do not yield grapes. The test was not new when he gave it; the wise in Yashar'el (Israel) had been teaching it for generations. What the gospel does is hand it to every disciple as the way to know a teacher, so that no one has to be fooled by the costume if he will look at the fruit.
cards.s_text: You shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles?
cards.t_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and given back their inheritance as from the beginning, twelve tribes and not two. Yahusha (Jesus) says many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom. The many from east and west are the children of those three fathers coming home from where they were scattered, which is exactly what Sirach asked for. They are not a new people put in the seat of Yashar'el (Israel); they are the tribes of Jacob taking their own seats at their fathers' table.
cards.s_text: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11). Sirach prays for mercy on the people called by the name of Yahuah (God), on Yashar'el (Israel) whom he named his firstborn. Yahusha (Jesus) says many will come from east and west and sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom. The firstborn is one people, named from the beginning, and the many from east and west are that firstborn's scattered children coming to their fathers' table. The mercy Sirach asks for the firstborn is the seat Yahusha (Jesus) says they will take.
cards.s_text: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn.

cards.note: *For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.* (2 Esdras 12:34). *And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, Thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* (Matthew 9:27). The anointed does two things in Ezra's vision: he reproves the eagle, and he delivers the rest of the people with mercy, those pressed upon the borders, and makes them joyful until the day of judgment. The blind men ask the Son of David for exactly that, mercy. The remnant pressed at the borders are the scattered of Yashar'el (Israel), and the first work of the Messiah (Christ) toward them is mercy, as it was for the two who cried out. He saw the multitudes as sheep having no shepherd and was moved for them (Matthew 9:36).
cards.s_text: And when Yahusha (Jesus) departed thence, two blind men followed him, crying, and saying, You Son of David, have mercy on us.
cards.t_text: For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Ezra is told plainly who the peaceable multitude of his vision is: the ten tribes Shalmaneser carried out of their own land and over the waters, who never came back. Those are the people the King means when he sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). A sheep is lost when it has wandered where the shepherd cannot see it, and the northern house had been lost in another land for seven centuries by the time Yahusha (Jesus) spoke these words. The mission of the twelve was aimed at the same body Ezra was shown.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt, That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.* (2 Esdras 13:41–42). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). The tribes did not simply vanish into the heathen. Ezra is told they took counsel to leave the multitude and go further out, into a country where no one lived, so that they could keep the statutes they had never kept in their own land. The carrying away became, for a remnant of them, a going out to keep Torah. Centuries later the King sends the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the same body, in the lands it went out to. The commandments they carried into the far country are what the sheep are being called back to, and Yahusha (Jesus) sends his messengers after them rather than waiting for them to find the way home alone.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,

cards.note: *The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.* (2 Esdras 13:47). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). The Most High stayed the river once so the tribes could cross out, and Ezra is promised he will stay it again so they can cross back, in the latter time. That return is the end of the story the vision tells. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they will not finish going over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) before the Son of Adam comes; the work he sends them on is not completed in their lifetime but runs until his coming. Set together, the two say the same thing: the going after the lost sheep and the gathering of the ten tribes are one work, begun with the sending and finished when the Highest opens the way home and the King returns.
cards.s_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee you into another: for verily I say unto you, You shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.
cards.t_text: The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6). Tobit lays out the whole order in one breath: Yahuah (God) scourges his people for their iniquities, has mercy again, and gathers them out of all the nations he scattered them into. The scourge was the scattering. The mercy is the gathering. When Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve, he points them at the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), the very people Tobit said would be gathered, and the sending is that mercy beginning to move. The gathering Tobit prayed for as a thing still to come is the mission the King commissions.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them. There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Elohim (God), and he is Yahuah (God) our Father for ever.* (Tobit 13:3–4). *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). Tobit sings this from the land of the captivity, and the instruction is not to hide among the Gentiles but to confess Yahuah (God) in front of them, to declare his greatness in the very places he scattered his children into. Yahusha (Jesus) is sending the twelve to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) in this same chapter, and he gives them the same charge with a promise attached: confess me before men, and I will confess you before my Father. The scattered confess him where they were scattered, and the King names them before the Father. The confession Tobit called for and the confession Yahusha (Jesus) rewards are one confession, made by the same scattered people in the same territories.
cards.s_text: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
cards.t_text: Confess him before the Gentiles, you children of Yashar'el (Israel): for he has scattered us among them.

cards.note: *And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.* (Tobit 14:5). *But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23). Tobit, dying, tells his son there will be two returns, not one. First a return to the land and a temple not like the first, which is the house Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah raised after Babylon, a return of Yahudah (Judah) only. Then, after the time of that age is fulfilled, a return from all places of the captivity, Jerusalem built gloriously and the house of Yahuah (God) built in it for ever, as the prophets spoke. That second return has not happened. Between the two stands the work Yahusha (Jesus) sends the twelve into, and he tells them it will not be finished before the Son of Adam comes. The mission to the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) runs through this age toward the return Tobit saw at the end of it.
cards.s_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee you into another: for verily I say unto you, You shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.
cards.t_text: And that again Yahuah (God) will have mercy on them, and bring them again into the land, where they shall build a temple, but not like to the first, until the time of that age be fulfilled; and afterward they shall return from all places of their captivity, and build up Jerusalem gloriously, and the house of Yahuah (God) shall be built in it for ever with a glorious building, as the prophets have spoken thereof.

cards.note: *For he had heard in Phoenicia that certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), about the time of the Assyrian captivity, had escaped by sea to "the isles afar off," as spoken by the prophet, and called by the Romans, Britain.* Sonnini Acts 29:2 names Paul's motivation for the Spain-and-Britain journey: the scattered children of Yashar'el (Israel) had fled by sea at the time of the Assyrian captivity to the isles afar off (the prophetic-language of Isaiah 49:1, Jeremiah 31:10). Matt 10:6's lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) names the same body Sonnini Acts 29 has Paul going FAR HENCE to gather — the apostolic-mission carrying the Matt 10 commission to the actual territories of the Assyrian-dispersion remnant. The wisdom-stream of the restored *Acts of Paul* extension confirms the gathering-of-the-scattered-seed thesis the Matthew commission inaugurates.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: For he had heard in Phoenicia that certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), about the time of the Assyrian captivity, had escaped by sea to "the isles afar off," as spoken by the prophet, and called by the Romans, Britain.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached far hence to the Gentiles, and to the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel).* Sonnini Acts 29:3 is the direct verbal-anchor for Matt 10:6's mission-scope in the apostolic-extension territory: the same *lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel)* phrase the King uses at Matt 10:6 (and at Matt 15:24) is the very phrase the restored Sonnini chapter names as Yahuah (the LORD)'s commissioning of Paul's far-hence mission. The Matt 10:5-6 commission scope and the Sonnini Acts 29:3 commission scope are identical — one to the disciples in the immediate region of Galilee, the other to Paul in the far-hence territories of the dispersion-isles. Both are the same gathering of the same scattered seed.
cards.s_text: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (Lord) commanded the gospel to be preached far hence to the Gentiles, and to the lost sheep of the House of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And it came to pass that certain of the Druids came unto Paul privately, and showed by their rites and ceremonies they were descended from the Yahudim (Jews) which escaped from bondage in the land of Egypt, and the apostle believed these things, and he gave them the kiss of peace.* Sonnini Acts 29:13 names the apostolic-recognition of the scattered-seed lineage in the British territories — the Druids whose rites and ceremonies disclosed Yashar'el-itish (Israel-itish) descent received the kiss of peace from Paul. The Matt 10:23 standing-mission-across-centuries reaches the territories the wisdom-stream had named as the dispersion-destinations; the gathering finds the scattered where they have been driven. Paul's reception of the Druid-disclosure is the apostolic-mission walking the Matt 10 architecture in the far-hence territories the King had named at Matt 10:23 as still-to-be-traversed.
cards.s_text: But when they persecute you in this city, flee you into another: for verily I say unto you, You shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that certain of the Druids came unto Paul privately, and showed by their rites and ceremonies they were descended from the Yahudim (Jews) which escaped from bondage in the land of Egypt, and the apostle believed these things, and he gave them the kiss of peace.

cards.note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). When Yahusha (Jesus) says John is the Elias who was to come, he is pointing at a job description everyone in the crowd knew. Sirach had written it out: Elijah is ordained to reprove, to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob. All of Jacob, all twelve tribes, the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) and the house of Yahudah (Judah) together. John began that work at the Jordan; the full restoring of the tribes waits on the great and dreadful day Malachi set it beside (Malachi 4:5). *If ye will receive it* is the hard part, because receiving it means receiving that the gathering of a scattered people is what Elijah comes to do.
cards.s_text: And if you will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
cards.t_text: Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.

cards.note: *Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.* (1 Maccabees 2:58). *And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.* (Matthew 11:14). Mattathias remembers Elijah (Elias) for one thing: he was zealous and fervent for the law, and he was taken up into heaven. That is how the faithful in Yashar'el (Israel) remembered him, as the man who stood for the commandments of Yahuah (God) against a kingdom that had traded them for Baal. When Yahusha (Jesus) says of John, this is Elijah (Elias) which was for to come, the likeness is that same zeal: John in the wilderness calling the leadership a generation of vipers, John in prison for telling Herod his marriage was unlawful. Elijah's zeal for the law is what Malachi promised would come before the great day, and it came first in John.
cards.s_text: And if you will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
cards.t_text: Elias for being zealous and fervent for the law was taken up into heaven.

cards.note: *He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.* (Baruch 3:36). *The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.* (Matthew 11:19). Baruch says the whole way of knowledge was found out by Elohim (God) and then given, not to the world at large but to Jacob his servant and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved. Wisdom has a people she was given to. Yahusha (Jesus), reproached for eating with publicans and sinners, says wisdom is justified of her children: the ones who recognize her are her own. The children of wisdom in Matthew 11 are the covenant seed Baruch names, the people the knowledge was given to, and when the one who gave it stood among them in flesh they knew his voice even when the leaders did not. Her children are the proof she was given to Jacob.
cards.s_text: The Son of Adam came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
cards.t_text: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.

cards.note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:4). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach is describing a face that stays turned toward the one in need, and Matthew 12:20 describes the Messiah's: a bruised reed he will not break, smoking flax he will not quench. The supplication of the afflicted is the bruised reed, and the poor man at the door is the smoking flax, easy to snap and easy to snuff. What Sirach asked of every son of Yashar'el (Israel), Yahusha (Jesus) did. A religious system that turns its face from the afflicted has abandoned the counsel and parted ways with the Messiah in the same motion.
cards.s_text: A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.
cards.t_text: Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.

cards.note: *And there will be great wrath from Yahuah (God) against the children of Yashar’el (Israel), because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the nations, so that they may be removed and rooted out of the land. And there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them so that there should be forgiveness and pardon for all the sin of this eternal error.* (Jubilees 15:34). *Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.* (Matthew 12:31). Jubilees says a thing most readers do not expect from the book of the covenant: there is a sin for which there will no more be pardon. It is not a slip or a weakness. It is the children of Yashar'el (Israel) knowing the ordinance, forsaking the covenant on purpose, and treating the sign in their own flesh the way the nations do. Yahusha (Jesus) draws the same line in Matthew: every manner of sin and blasphemy can be forgiven, but the one who has watched the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) at work and called it something else has stepped past the place where forgiveness reaches. Both texts describe the same posture, a deliberate turning aside from what one has plainly seen, and both say the same thing about where it ends.
cards.s_text: Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) shall not be forgiven unto men.
cards.t_text: And there will be great wrath from Yahuah (God) against the children of Yashar’el (Israel), because they have forsaken His covenant and turned aside from His word, and provoked and blasphemed, inasmuch as they do not observe the ordinance of this law; for they have treated their members like the nations, so that they may be removed and rooted out of the land. And there will no more be pardon or forgiveness to them so that there should be forgiveness and pardon for all the sin of this eternal error.

cards.note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.* (Matthew 14:19). Bread from heaven, prepared without their labour, was how the Father fed his own people in the wilderness. On the grass in a desert place Yahusha (Jesus) looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and the loaves go out through the disciples' hands to a multitude that brought nothing but its hunger. The same hand that sent the manna is feeding Yashar'el (Israel) again, and John's account of this same meal ends with him saying who the bread is: *I am the bread of life* (John 6:35).
cards.s_text: And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.
cards.t_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.

cards.note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.* (Matthew 14:20). Wisdom says come and fill yourselves with my fruits, and in the desert place Yahusha (Jesus) did exactly that: the multitude came to him, they ate, and they were filled. He is the Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus 24 feeding her children with her own hand, and the invitation of Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, is the same mouth speaking. Twelve baskets were left over, one for every tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), and the leftover says the feeding was never meant for that hillside alone. The scattered children of Wisdom will be gathered and fed the same way.
cards.s_text: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.
cards.t_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.

cards.note: *Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us:* (Ecclesiasticus 36:1). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Sirach opens his great prayer with a cry for mercy to the Elohim (God) of all, and the prayer goes on to ask that all the tribes of Jacob be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says he was not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). The one being asked for mercy in Sirach's prayer is the one who answered it in person, sent to the very scattered house the prayer was about. Behold us, Sirach prays; the Shepherd came looking for the sheep.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Have mercy upon us, O Yahuah (God) of all, and behold us:

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Sirach prays for the gathering of all the tribes of Jacob, back into the inheritance as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel). The prayer and the mission have the same object: not Yahudah (Judah) alone, who had a temple and a land, but the whole house that had been scattered and lost among the nations. The prophets promised it, Sirach prayed it, and the King came for it.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.* (2 Esdras 13:40). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). When the woman of Canaan pressed him, Yahusha (Jesus) named the scope of his sending: the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) — and she, who heard the Shepherd and would not be turned away, was one of them. Ezra had already been shown who that house is, the ten tribes Shalmaneser led away captive over the waters into another land, who never returned. The lost sheep were not a figure of speech; they were a people with a date, a captor, and a direction of travel, the same carrying away the book of Kings records (2 Kings 17:6). The King was sent to them, and the prophets who promised their gathering (Jeremiah 31; Ezekiel 37) were speaking of the same people.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.

cards.note: *But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.* (2 Esdras 13:48). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). The vision does not forget the ones who never left. After the ten tribes come home, Ezra is told that those left behind of his people are the ones found within the borders of the land, the remnant of Yahudah (Judah) that stayed. When Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), his sending reaches both of these: the multitudes of Galilee and Yahudah (Judah) he walked among inside the borders, and the scattered house beyond the waters his apostles would be sent after. The house of Yashar'el (Israel) is both of them, the ones who stayed and the ones who were carried, and the King's mission is to the whole house.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.

cards.note: *And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.* (Tobit 13:5). *But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 15:24). Tobit names who gets gathered and from where: the people Yahuah (God) scourged and scattered, brought back out of all the nations. Ezekiel had said the same, *I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side* (Ezekiel 37:21). When Yahusha (Jesus) says he is not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), he is stating the scope of that gathering, not narrowing his mercy. He said it to the woman of Canaan, and she was not turned away; the sheep hear the Shepherd's voice wherever the scattering has carried them, and the hearing shows who they are. The mission to the lost sheep is the mercy Tobit said would follow the scourge.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he has scattered us.

cards.note: *For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people.* (Jubilees 15:30). *And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.* (Matthew 15:22). Not every child of Abraham is the chosen seed. Jubilees says it flat: Ishmael, his sons, his brothers, Esau, Yahuah (God) did not bring them near, though they were Abraham's children; He chose Yashar'el (Israel) to be His people. The woman crying *Son of David* on the coast of Tyre and Sidon is not standing outside that choice. Yahusha (Jesus) says *I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 15:24) and then heals her daughter, which means she is one of those lost sheep. Canaan was the ground of her exile, the merchant coast where the divorced northern house was swallowed up among the Gentiles (Hosea 8:8), not a verdict on her blood. She knew the Shepherd's voice and called him by David's name because she was a sheep before she ever heard him. The line Jubilees draws is kept; what the story shows is that the chosen seed had been scattered to places their brothers would never have looked.
cards.s_text: And, behold, a woman of Canaan came out of the same coasts, and cried unto him, saying, Have mercy on me, O Lord, you Son of David; my daughter is grievously vexed with a devil.
cards.t_text: For Ishmael and his sons and his brothers and Esau, Yahuah (God) did not cause to approach Him, and he chose them not because they are the children of Abraham, because He knew them, but He chose Yashar’el (Israel) to be His people.

cards.note: *And He sanctified it, and gathered it from amongst all the children of men ; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.* (Jubilees 15:31). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Jubilees explains the difference between the children and the dogs. Many nations and many peoples are all His, but over them He set spirits in authority, and those spirits lead them astray; Yashar'el (Israel) He sanctified and gathered out from among all the children of men to rule Himself. Moses sang the same thing: *when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel). For the LORD’S portion is his people* (Deuteronomy 32:8–9). The woman on the coast of Canaan lives among the people under those spirits, and her daughter is vexed with a devil, but when she calls him *Son of David* and keeps asking, she shows she is not one of theirs. Yahusha (Jesus) says the bread is the children's, and then gives it to her, because she is a child of the household the Father rules directly, a lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered into the territory of the spirits (Matthew 15:24, 28).
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.
cards.t_text: And He sanctified it, and gathered it from amongst all the children of men ; for there are many nations and many peoples, and all are His, and over all has He placed spirits in authority to lead them astray from Him.

cards.note: *But over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will preserve them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of all His powers in order that He may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be His and He may be theirs from henceforth for ever.* (Jubilees 15:32). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Over Yashar'el (Israel) no angel and no spirit: He alone is their ruler, and He keeps them Himself and requires them at the hand of every power. That is why Yahusha (Jesus) says he was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 15:24). The Shepherd who said through Ezekiel *I, even I, will both search my sheep, and seek them out* (Ezekiel 34:11) had come to do it in person. The woman on the coast of Canaan is of that flock, a daughter of the divorced northern house living in the land of her scattering, and the Shepherd who was sent only to the lost sheep found one of them there. He says the bread is for the children, she answers as a child who knows whose table it is, and he gives it to her (Matthew 15:28). The line is kept; she was on the inside of it all along, and the hearing revealed it.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.
cards.t_text: But over Yashar’el (Israel) He did not appoint any angel or spirit, for He alone is their ruler, and He will preserve them and require them at the hand of His angels and His spirits, and at the hand of all His powers in order that He may preserve them and bless them, and that they may be His and He may be theirs from henceforth for ever.

cards.note: *And (that) all the seed of his sons should be nations, and be reckoned with the nations; but from the sons of Isaac one should become a holy seed, and should not be reckoned among the nations.* (Jubilees 16:17). *But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.* (Matthew 15:26). Abraham's other sons became nations and are reckoned with the nations; from Isaac comes one holy seed that is not reckoned among them. Paul says it the same way: *they are not all Yashar'el (Israel), which are of Yashar'el (Israel) ... In Isaac shall thy seed be called* (Romans 9:6–7). Children and dogs at the table is the same distinction. The seed of promise has a name and a line, and Yahusha (Jesus) does not pretend otherwise; he tells her the bread is the children's. But he was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Matthew 15:24), and the coast of Tyre and Sidon was where the divorced northern house had been swallowed up among the Gentiles (Hosea 8:8). When she answers as one who knows the Master's table and he gives her the bread, he is not crossing the line; he is finding a child of Isaac's holy seed on the far side of her exile.
cards.s_text: But he answered and said, It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.
cards.t_text: And (that) all the seed of his sons should be nations, and be reckoned with the nations; but from the sons of Isaac one should become a holy seed, and should not be reckoned among the nations.

cards.note: *And I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years: but the year thereof have I not told you till you enter the land which you are to possess.* (Jubilees 50:2). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.* (Matthew 15:37). Jubilees counts the land's rest in sevens: Sabbaths of years, and the jubilee at the end of seven sevens, as Moses laid it out, *seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years* (Leviticus 25:8). The two feedings count in the two numbers of Yashar'el (Israel): twelve baskets for the twelve tribes (Matthew 14:20), seven baskets for the Sabbath and the jubilee. A crowd fed and filled with seven baskets over is a picture of the rest the land was promised: enough, more than enough, and the count of the week on top. The bread was real, and so was the number.
cards.s_text: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.
cards.t_text: And I told you of the Sabbaths of the land on Mount Sinai, and I told you of the jubilee years in the sabbaths of years: but the year thereof have I not told you till you enter the land which you are to possess.

cards.note: *Wherefore I have ordained for you the year-weeks and the years and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years and there are yet forty years to come (lit. "distant for learning the commandments of Yahuah (God), until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.* (Jubilees 50:4). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.* (Matthew 15:37). Jubilees counts forty-nine jubilees from Adam to the border of the land, seven sevens of jubilees, with the fiftieth opening as Yashar'el (Israel) crosses Jordan. Seven is the number this book counts the world's history in. When Yahusha (Jesus) feeds the crowd and seven baskets remain, the number lands on ears trained by that count. He had already stood in Nazareth and read *the acceptable year of Yahuah (Lord)* and told them *this day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears* (Luke 4:19, 21); the jubilee had a face. The seven baskets are the full measure left over when the jubilee is proclaimed.
cards.s_text: And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets full.
cards.t_text: Wherefore I have ordained for you the year-weeks and the years and the jubilees: there are forty-nine jubilees from the days of Adam until this day, and one week and two years and there are yet forty years to come (lit. "distant for learning the commandments of Yahuah (God), until they pass over into the land of Canaan, crossing the Jordan to the west.

cards.note: *Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.* (Ecclesiasticus 17:11). *And he said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.* (Matthew 19:17). Sirach calls the law a law of life, given for an heritage along with knowledge. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the young man that if he would enter into life he should keep the commandments. The law of life and entering into life are the same road. Moses set life and good before Yashar'el (Israel) in the commandments, Sirach calls that inheritance by its name, and the King does not amend it when the question is put to him directly.
cards.s_text: And he said unto him, Why callest you me good? there is none good but one, that is, Elohim (God): but if you will enter into life, keep the commandments.
cards.t_text: Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.

cards.note: *And after this they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations, and they will seek Me, so that I shall be found of them, when they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul.* (Jubilees 1:15). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Twelve thrones judging twelve tribes means twelve tribes will be there to be judged. Jubilees says how they get there: they turn to Him from among the nations with all their heart, and He gathers them from among all the nations. That is Ezekiel's two sticks made one, and Isaiah's *outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel)* and *dispersed of Yahudah (Judah)* gathered *from the four corners of the earth* (Isaiah 11:12). The regeneration Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of is a gathered people of Jacob's blood seated under Jacob's sons' names, not a church that has renamed itself Yashar'el (Israel). The scattering was real, the gathering is real, and the thrones are for real tribes.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And after this they will turn to Me from amongst the nations with all their heart and with all their soul and with all their strength, and I shall gather them from amongst all the nations, and they will seek Me, so that I shall be found of them, when they seek Me with all their heart and with all their soul.

cards.note: *And they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They will speak the word of Yahuah (God) in righteousness, And they will judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they will declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Yashar’el (Israel). The blessing of Yahuah (God) will be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved.* (Jubilees 31:15). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Isaac's blessing on Levi at Bethel is a blessing of judgeship: princes and judges and chiefs over all the seed of Jacob's sons, speaking the word of Yahuah (God) and declaring His ways to Jacob. Yahusha (Jesus) seats twelve men on twelve thrones over the same seed. Judging in Yashar'el (Israel) was never only a courtroom; *Yahuah (LORD) raised up judges, which delivered them out of the hand of those that spoiled them* (Judges 2:16). What Levi was blessed to carry at the altar, the twelve are given to carry at the throne, and the people under them are still the seed of the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And they will be princes and judges, and chiefs of all the seed of the sons of Jacob; They will speak the word of Yahuah (God) in righteousness, And they will judge all His judgments in righteousness. And they will declare My ways to Jacob And My paths to Yashar’el (Israel). The blessing of Yahuah (God) will be given in their mouths To bless all the seed of the beloved.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve that in the regeneration, when the Son of Adam sits on the throne of his glory, they will sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). Twelve thrones for twelve tribes means the twelve tribes are there to be judged: gathered, whole, as from the beginning. What Sirach asked for in prayer the King states as the shape of the kingdom when it comes.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). Wisdom says the righteous shall judge the nations; Yahusha (Jesus) tells the twelve they shall sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). These are two views of one kingdom. The gathered twelve tribes sit under the apostles' thrones, and that gathered people is the kingdom of priests the Father promised at Sinai — *ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests* (Exodus 19:6) — who judge and teach the nations left alive in the reign. The priesthood toward the nations begins when the kingdom is set up, not before. Wisdom saw the outer ring; the King named the inner one.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.

cards.note: *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* Testaments XII Joseph 15 (chapter 86 in the corpus enumeration) verse 2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the twelve-harts-feeding-then-dispersed substance — the same scattering-and-restoration-of-the-twelve-tribes architecture the King at Matt 19:28's *judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* presupposes-as-the-completed-gathering-architecture. The framework reads the verse against the King's-statement. The Joseph-testament-substance names the substance directly: twelve-harts (the twelve-tribes) feeding-together-originally, then-dispersed (the nine = the ten-northern-tribes; the three = the southern-house-substance), the substance the prophets had named at Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) 37:15-22's two-sticks-becoming-one. The substance the King-states at Matt 19:28 is the gathering-and-judging-substance the wisdom-stream-Joseph-testament had named the architecture-for. The wisdom-stream, the Tanakh-prophets, and the King's-mouth all hold the same architecture: twelve-tribes-dispersed-and-gathered-and-judged-by-twelve-apostles-at-the-consummated-substance. The framework reads in framework-substance per Red Line #11 — the twelve-tribes are LITERAL twelve-tribes, the paternal-blood remnant the Father-promised-through-the-prophets-and-now-states-at-the-King's-mouth. FRAMEWORK-MAJOR.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.

cards.note: *So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* (Ecclesiasticus 24:8). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Wisdom was commanded by the Creator to pitch her tent in Jacob and take her inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel). Isaiah had already said that the vineyard of Yahuah (God) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and Jeremiah mourned the pastors who destroyed it. When Yahusha (Jesus) opens the parable with a householder hiring labourers into his vineyard, that is the vineyard he means — the covenant people the Father planted and in whom Wisdom made her dwelling. The householder is the Father, and the labourers are the ones he calls into it through the hours of the day.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 24:12). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Wisdom says she took root in an honourable people, in the portion that is Yahuah's (God's) own inheritance. That people is the vineyard of the parable — the householder's own ground, into which he goes out to hire labourers through the day. The vineyard is Yashar'el (Israel), and so are the labourers called into it, whether called early or late: the covenant line from Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and the children of that line who grew up scattered among the nations and are being called home. The honourable people Wisdom rooted in is the inheritance the Father is still gathering.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: And I took root in an honourable people, even in the portion of the inheritance of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:* (2 Esdras 5:23). *For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.* (Matthew 20:1). Ezra, praying, names what the Most High did with the whole earth: out of every wood and every tree he chose one vine. When Yahusha (Jesus) opens the parable of the labourers, the householder's vineyard is not a new field; it is that one vine, the vineyard Isaiah had already named as the house of Yashar'el (Israel) (Isaiah 5:7). Labourers are hired into it at different hours, but the vineyard itself was chosen long before the morning began. Whoever is brought in at the eleventh hour is brought into that same vineyard, not into a different one planted beside it.
cards.s_text: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard.
cards.t_text: And said, O Yahuah (God) that bearest rule, of every wood of the earth, and of all the trees thereof, you have chosen you one only vine:

cards.note: *And after these things shall a star arise to you from Jacob in peace.* Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 37:5 (Testament of Levi 18 / Testament of Yahudah (Judah) 24 cluster, depending on the recension-positioning the parsed-text preserves) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the star-from-Ya'aqov (Jacob) substance — the Davidic-Messianic credential the marginalized two-blind-men at Yericho (Jericho) recognize at Matt 20:30's *thou Son of David, have mercy on us.* The framework reads the verse in continuity with Bamidbar (Numbers) 24:17's *there shall come a Star out of Ya'aqov (Jacob), and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)* the prophet Bila'am (Balaam) had carried at the pre-entry-to-the-Land vision. The wisdom-stream and the Tanakh-prophetic-witness cohere — the star-from-Ya'aqov (Jacob) substance is the same Davidic-Messianic credential the marginalized-substance walks-into-recognizing at the gospel-pivot.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you Son of David.
cards.t_text: Until Yahuah (Lord) visit you, when with perfect heart ye repent and walk in all His commandments, and He bring you up from captivity among the Gentiles.

cards.note: *And from it shall grow up the rod of righteousness unto the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).* Testament of Yahudah (Judah) ch 15 v.6 names the wisdom-stream articulation of the rod-of-righteousness substance the Messianic-King carries-out — the *judge and save all that call upon Yahuah* substance the framework reads carefully. The framework reads the verse against Matt 21:5's King-coming-to-his-city substance. The substance the wisdom-stream names at *all that call upon Yahuah (Lord)* is the substance the King-walks at the marginalized-substance crying *Son of David* (Matt 9:27, 15:22, 20:30-31) now-walked-by-the-multitudes at the entry-substance; the *Gentiles* in the wisdom-stream-language carries the same wisdom-stream-convention as Paul's-letters address — the substance is NOT the categorical-three-categories-nations-as-collective replacing-Yashar'el (Israel) but the substance of the scattered-seed-of-Yashar'el-living-as-Gentiles-among-the-nations per Red Line #7's scattered-seed-coming-home substance + Red Line #11's wild-olive-substance of the descendants-of-the-broken-off-who-hear-when-the-Shepherd-calls. The substance the wisdom-stream had named is the substance the gospel walks-out at the entry.
cards.s_text: Tell you the daughter of Sion, Behold, your King comes unto you, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.
cards.t_text: And from it shall grow a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).

cards.note: *For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:4). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom describes the brood of the ungodly as branches that flourish for a while with nothing under them; the wind shakes them and finally roots them out. Yahusha (Jesus) came to a fig tree in full leaf, found no fruit, and it withered. Leaves without fruit is the same picture as branches without roots — a show of life with nothing feeding it. The tree stands for the religious leadership of that day, which had the look of the covenant and none of its fruit; it does not stand for the people of Yashar'el (Israel) as a whole. What flourishes without a root does not stand when the wind comes.
cards.s_text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
cards.t_text: For though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out.

cards.note: *The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.* (Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). Wisdom is describing branches that flourish for a season, bear nothing worth eating, and are broken off. The fig tree the King met on the road the morning after he cleansed the Temple was all leaves and no fruit, and he spoke its end on the spot. The tree was not the people of Yashar'el (Israel); it was the leadership standing in that Temple with every show of foliage and nothing to feed anyone, the same men he answers with seven woes in Matthew 23 before the week is out. The test he had already given his disciples was fruit, not leaves (Matthew 7:16), and Solomon had written the same verdict long before.
cards.s_text: And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on you henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.
cards.t_text: The imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing.

cards.note: *Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11). *Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.* (Matthew 21:43). Sirach prays for all the tribes of Jacob to be gathered and inherited as from the beginning. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the chief priests the kingdom will be taken from them and given to a nation bringing forth its fruits; a nation, one, not the nations. That one nation is the gathered tribes of Jacob bearing fruit, the very people Sirach prayed for. It is not the church put in the place of Yashar'el (Israel), and it is not whoever keeps Torah regardless of seed; it is Jacob's own tribes, gathered home and bearing the fruit their leaders in that day would not bring.
cards.s_text: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of Elohim (God) shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.
cards.t_text: Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning.

cards.note: *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* Testaments XII Levi (file ch 17, canonical Testament of Levi 16) names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the corrupted-priesthood-substance walking-lawlessly-with-Yashar'el (Israel) — the substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-against at Matt 23:13 (the first-woe — *ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men*). The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's prefiguring of the substance the seven-woes walk-out at the Pharisaic-leadership-system at the first-coming. The veil-of-the-temple-rent substance walks-toward the historical-fulfillment at Matt 27:51 (*the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom*) — the same Tanakh-and-wisdom-stream-and-gospel-substance walks-from-prefiguring-to-fulfillment. The framework reads the substance in continuity with the system-not-people posture — the substance the wisdom-stream names is the leadership-substance walking-lawlessly, NOT the people-of-Yashar'el (Israel) categorically. (FRAMEWORK-MAJOR)
cards.s_text: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for you neither go in yourselves, neither suffer you them that are entering to go in.
cards.t_text: And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.

cards.note: *And in the seventh week shall become priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.* Testaments XII Levi (file ch 20, canonical Testament of Levi 17) names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the corrupted-priesthood-substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-against at Matt 23:15 (the second-woe — *ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of Gehinnom (Gehenna) than yourselves*). The framework reads the verse as FRAMEWORK-MAJOR — the wisdom-stream had named the substance of the priests-as-idolaters-adulterers-lovers-of-money-proud-lawless centuries before the gospel-pivot articulated the same substance at the seven-woes. The proselyte the Pharisaic-leadership-system makes becomes-twofold-the-child-of-Gehinnom (Gehenna) because the leadership-substance the proselyte is-converted-into is the same idolaters-adulterers-lovers-of-money-proud-lawless substance Testaments XII Levi names. The framework reads the substance in continuity with the contrary-to-Torah-test the apostle-Yochanan (John) names at 1 John 2:3-4 — the leadership-substance fails-the-test categorically. The same diagnostic operates in five costumes by the contrary-to-Torah-test: Pharisaic-rabbinic-system through ADDITION, Galatian-agitators through INVERSION, modern-institutional-Christianity through SUBTRACTION, modern-Hebrew-Roots-false-inclusion through COLLAPSE, Islam through TRANSFER. Same flesh-credential gospel. Same voiding of the Torah-substance. Four costumes on one antichrist architecture. (FRAMEWORK-MAJOR)
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, you make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.
cards.t_text: And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.

cards.note: *But do not ye, my children, wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness; but cleave unto goodness only, for Elohim (God) hath his habitation therein.* Testaments XII Asher (file ch 67, canonical Asher 3:1) names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wear-not-two-faces substance — the same substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-against at Matt 23:28 (the outward-appearance-righteous against the within-full-of-hypocrisy-and-iniquity). The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's direct prefiguring of the whited-sepulchres-substance the King names at Matt 23:27-28. The same architecture the prophet-Yechezk'el (Ezekiel) walks at Ezekiel 13:10-12 (*daubed it with untempered morter*) is the substance Testaments XII Asher names directly — the wear-not-two-faces substance is the substance the wisdom-stream walks-from and the King walks-against. The framework reads this in continuity with the contrary-to-Torah-test the apostle-Yochanan (John) names at 1 John 2:3-4 — the two-faces substance is the substance that-fails the test categorically.
cards.s_text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
cards.t_text: But do not ye, my children, wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness; but cleave unto goodness only, for Elohim (God) hath His habitation therein, and men desire it.

cards.note: *For they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin; for they both do the evil thing and they have pleasure in them that do it, following the example of the spirits of deceit.* Testaments XII Asher (file ch 69, canonical Asher 5:2) names the wisdom-stream's articulation of the double-faced-guilty-of-twofold-sin substance — the same substance the King-of-Yashar'el (Israel) walks-against at Matt 23:27 (*ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness*). The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the substance the seven-woes walk-against — the whited-sepulchres-substance the King names is the same double-faced-guilty-of-twofold-sin substance the wisdom-stream had-named.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
