cards.t_text: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 6:4 — *And Yahuah (God) smelt the goodly savour, and He made a covenant with him that there should not be any more a flood to destroy the earth.* Jubilees keeps the same altar-savour and no-more-flood covenant that follows the service of Jasher 6:41.
cards.s_text: And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) smelt the goodly savour, and He made a covenant with him that there should not be any more a flood to destroy the earth; that all the days of the earth seed-time and harvest should never cease; cold and heat, and summer and winter, and day and night should not change their order, nor cease for ever.

cards.note: Jubilees 6:16 — *He set His bow in the cloud for a sign of the eternal covenant that there should not again be a flood on the earth to destroy it all the days of the earth.* Jubilees keeps the bow of the eternal covenant that crowns Noah's going-forth in Jasher 6:41, self-linked.
cards.s_text: And they went and returned every one to his way and to his place, and Noah and his sons dwelt in the land that Elohim had told them, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed Noah and his sons on their going out from the ark.
cards.t_text: He set His bow in the cloud for a sign of the eternal covenant that there should not again be a flood on the earth to destroy it all the days of the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 9:18 — *And the sons of Noah, that went forth of the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan.* The same three brothers Jasher names are the three who came out of the ark in the canon.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Noah, that went forth of the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth: and Ham is the father of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 9:19 — *These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread.* Jasher 7's whole genealogy of the nations is the unfolding of this one verse — from the three, all the earth.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
cards.t_text: These are the three sons of Noah: and of them was the whole earth overspread.

cards.note: Genesis 10:1 — *Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them were sons born after the flood.* Jasher 7:1 is the same heading to the table of nations, the children born after the flood.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
cards.t_text: Now these are the generations of the sons of Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth: and unto them were sons born after the flood.

cards.note: *And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.* (Jubilees 8:10). *And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.* (Jasher 7:1). Jasher names the three sons and says children were born to them after the flood; Jubilees picks up once those families have grown and shows the earth divided into three parts, one for each son, by inheritance. The division was not a scramble for land; one who had been sent, an angel, was present with them as they did it. The brothers of Jasher 7 become the heads of the three portions of the whole earth. What Jasher begins as a family list, Jubilees finishes as a map.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the sons of Noah: Japheth, Ham and Shem; and children were born to them after the flood, for they had taken wives before the flood.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the beginning of the thirty-third jubilee that they divided the earth into three parts, for Shem and Ham and Japheth, according to the inheritance of each, in the first year in the first week, when one of us, who had been sent, was with them.

cards.note: Genesis 10:2 — *The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.* The same seven sons of Japheth Jasher 7:2 names, in the same order.
cards.s_text: These are the sons of Japheth; Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras, seven sons.
cards.t_text: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.

cards.note: Genesis 10:3 — *And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.* Jasher 7:3's Askinaz, Rephath and Tegarmah are these same three sons of Gomer.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Gomer were Askinaz, Rephath and Tegarmah.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Gomer; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.

cards.note: Genesis 10:4 — *And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.* Jasher 7:6's sons of Javan match the canon's line of Javan exactly.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Javan were Elisha, Tarshish, Chittim and Dudonim.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

cards.note: Genesis 10:5 — *By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.* Jasher closing the families of Japheth with their numbers is the same dividing-into-nations the canon records here.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Tiras were Benib, Gera, Lupirion and Gilak; these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, and their numbers in those days were about four hundred and sixty men.
cards.t_text: By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.

cards.note: Genesis 10:6 — *And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.* The same four sons of Ham Jasher 7:10 names — Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Ham; Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan, four sons; and the sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Satecha, and the sons of Raama were Sheba and Dedan.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 10:7 — *And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan.* Jasher 7:10's house of Cush, down to Raama's sons Sheba and Dedan, is the canon's line of Cush.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Ham; Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan, four sons; and the sons of Cush were Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama and Satecha, and the sons of Raama were Sheba and Dedan.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Cush; Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha: and the sons of Raamah; Sheba, and Dedan.

cards.note: Genesis 10:15 — *And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth.* Jasher 7:13 opens Canaan's sons with the same Zidon and Heth the canon names first.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Canaan were Zidon, Heth, Amori, Gergashi, Hivi, Arkee, Seni, Arodi, Zimodi and Chamothi.
cards.t_text: And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth,

cards.note: Genesis 10:17 — *And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite.* Jasher 7:13's Hivi, Arkee and Seni are these same Canaanite families of the table of nations.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Canaan were Zidon, Heth, Amori, Gergashi, Hivi, Arkee, Seni, Arodi, Zimodi and Chamothi.
cards.t_text: And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite,

cards.note: Genesis 10:22 — *The children of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.* The same five sons of Shem Jasher 7:15 names — Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Shem; Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram, five sons; and the sons of Elam were Shushan, Machul and Harmon.
cards.t_text: The children of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.

cards.note: Genesis 10:23 — *And the children of Aram; Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.* Jasher 7:17's sons of Aram — Uz, Chul, Gather and Mash — are the canon's line of Aram.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Lud were Pethor and Bizayon, and the sons of Aram were Uz, Chul, Gather and Mash.
cards.t_text: And the children of Aram; Uz, and Hul, and Gether, and Mash.

cards.note: Genesis 10:21 — *Unto Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born.* Jasher narrowing to Shem's house marks the chosen seed-line — Shem the father of the children of Eber, through whom the promise runs.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Shem; Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram, five sons; and the sons of Elam were Shushan, Machul and Harmon.
cards.t_text: Unto Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born.

cards.note: Genesis 10:25 — *And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother's name was Joktan.* Jasher 7:19 gives the same Peleg, so named because in his days the earth was divided.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.

cards.note: Genesis 10:32 — *These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.* The whole genealogy of Jasher 7 is the dividing of the nations after the flood the canon seals here.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:8 — *When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The dividing in Peleg's day was the Most High apportioning the nations their inheritance.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Acts 17:26 — *And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation.* Paul preaches the same truth Jasher 7 narrates — one blood, the bounds of the nations' habitation set.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: And has made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

cards.note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.* (Jasher 7:19). Both books explain the name the same way: Peleg means division, and he was named for what was happening in his days. Jasher says the sons of men were divided and in the latter days the earth was divided; Jubilees says the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves when he was born. The name is a date stamp. Eber named his son after a world event, and both books kept the reason.
cards.s_text: These are the generations of Shem; Shem begat Arpachshad and Arpachshad begat Shelach, and Shelach begat Eber and to Eber were born two children, the name of one was Peleg, for in his days the sons of men were divided, and in the latter days, the earth was divided.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.

cards.note: Genesis 10:8 — *And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.* Jasher 7:30's Nimrod, son of Cush, grown mighty in the earth, is the very figure the canon introduces here.
cards.s_text: And Nimrod became strong when he put on the garments, and Elohim gave him might and strength, and he was a mighty hunter in the earth, yea, he was a mighty hunter in the field, and he hunted the animals and he built altars, and he offered upon them the animals before Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 10:10 — *And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.* Jasher 7:43 names Nimrod's city Shinar and his great kingdom — the canon's land of Shinar, the beginning of his rebel rule.
cards.s_text: And they found a large valley opposite to the east, and they built him a large and extensive city, and Nimrod called the name of the city that he built Shinar, for Yahuah (the Lord) had vehemently shaken his enemies and destroyed them.
cards.t_text: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

cards.note: Genesis 11:1 — *And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.* Jasher 7:46's earth of one tongue gathered under Nimrod is the Babel generation of one language.
cards.s_text: And all the earth was of one tongue and words of union, but Nimrod did not go in the ways of Yahuah (the Lord), and he was more wicked than all the men that were before him, from the days of the flood until those days.
cards.t_text: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.

cards.note: Micah 5:6 — *And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our borders.* The prophet still calls the kingdom-of-man Nimrod built 'the land of Nimrod' — the rebel power undone in the deliverance.
cards.s_text: And Nimrod dwelt in Shinar, and he reigned securely, and he fought with his enemies and he subdued them, and he prospered in all his battles, and his kingdom became very great.
cards.t_text: And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: thus shall he deliver us from the Assyrian, when he comes into our land, and when he treads within our borders.

cards.note: *For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”* (Jubilees 10:19). *And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so.* (Jasher 7:42). Jasher gives the man: Nimrod, reigning after his heart's desire, advised by his counselors to build a city for his palace. Jubilees gives the place and the boast: they left Ararat eastward to Shinar and built the city and the tower to climb into heaven by it. Put together, the tower was a king's project with a king's ambition, not a village's. "In his days" in Jubilees is Nimrod's days, and Jasher tells you who he was.
cards.s_text: And whilst he was reigning according to his heart’s desire, after having conquered all his enemies around, he advised with his counselors to build a city for his palace, and they did so.
cards.t_text: For they departed from the land of Ararat eastward to Shinar; for in his days they built the city and the tower, saying, “Go to, let us ascend thereby into heaven.”

cards.note: Genesis 5:24 — *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* Jasher 7:25's Enoch 'taken up to Elohim' is the canon's Enoch whom God took.
cards.s_text: For after the death of Adam and his wife, the garments were given to Enoch, the son of Jared, and when Enoch was taken up to Elohim, he gave them to Methuselah, his son.
cards.t_text: And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:5 — *By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased Elohim (God).* The witness names the same translation Jasher 7:25 recalls when Enoch was taken up and passed the garments on.
cards.s_text: For after the death of Adam and his wife, the garments were given to Enoch, the son of Jared, and when Enoch was taken up to Elohim, he gave them to Methuselah, his son.
cards.t_text: By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased Elohim (God).

cards.note: Genesis 11:26 — *And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.* Jasher 7:51 records the same Terah, seventy years old, begetting Abram — the called seed entering the story.
cards.s_text: Terah was seventy years old when he begat him, and Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram, because the king had raised him in those days, and dignified him above all his princes that were with him.
cards.t_text: And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Abram born to Terah inside Nimrod's idolatrous Shinar is the seed called out from fathers who served other gods.
cards.s_text: Terah was seventy years old when he begat him, and Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram, because the king had raised him in those days, and dignified him above all his princes that were with him.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:7 — *And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.* Terah's fear of the people matches Jasher's Terah trembling before Nimrod's threat over his household.
cards.s_text: And the king hearkened to Terah, and he did so and he gave him three days’ time, and Terah went out from the king’s presence, and he came home to his family and spoke to them all the words of the king; and the people were greatly afraid.
cards.t_text: And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.”

cards.note: Jubilees 12:4–5 — *Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth, And does everything upon the earth... Why do you worship things that have no spirit in them?* Jubilees gives the same father — an idolater Abram must rebuke — that Jasher shows bargaining with Nimrod.
cards.s_text: And Terah saw that the anger of the king was kindled against him, and he answered the king, saying, All that I have is in the king’s power; whatever the king desires to do to his servant, that let him do, yea, even my son, he is in the king’s power, without value in exchange, he and his two brothers that are older than he.
cards.t_text: Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth, And does everything upon the earth, And has created everything by His word, And all life is from before His face.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* The canon confirms Jasher's Terah — Nimrod's idol-serving prince — as the house out of which Yahuah calls the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And Terah saw that the anger of the king was kindled against him, and he answered the king, saying, All that I have is in the king’s power; whatever the king desires to do to his servant, that let him do, yea, even my son, he is in the king’s power, without value in exchange, he and his two brothers that are older than he.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Exodus 2:24 — *And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.* The covenant Yahuah keeps in Exodus is the very seed He shields in the cave so Nimrod cannot end it before Abraham.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Terah in this matter, that Nimrod might not cause Abram’s death, and the king took the child from Terah and with all his might dashed his head to the ground, for he thought it had been Abram; and this was concealed from him from that day, and it was forgotten by the king, as it was the will of Providence not to suffer Abram’s death.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

cards.note: Matthew 2:14 — *When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt.* The Messiah-child taken by night and hidden from the murdering king — Yahuah preserving the seed exactly as He hides Abram from Nimrod.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Abram in the cave and he grew up, and Abram was in the cave ten years, and the king and his princes, soothsayers and sages, thought that the king had killed Abram.
cards.t_text: When he arose, he took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt:

cards.note: Exodus 2:2 — *And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.* Moses hidden from Pharaoh's death-edict is the canon's same deliverer-concealed pattern as Abram hidden in the cave from Nimrod.
cards.s_text: And Terah took Abram his son secretly, together with his mother and nurse, and he concealed them in a cave, and he brought them their provisions monthly.
cards.t_text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

cards.note: Jubilees 11:2 — *And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil.* The Jubilees portrait of the kingdoms-of-man rising in Nimrod's generation — the very throne menacing Abram's house.
cards.s_text: And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Noah began to war on each other, to take captive and to slay each other, and to shed the blood of men on the earth, and to eat blood, and to build strong cities, and walls, and towers, and individuals (began) to exalt themselves above the nation, and to found the beginnings of kingdoms, and to go to war people against people, and nation against nation, and city against city, and all (began) to do evil, and to acquire arms, and to teach their sons war, and they began to capture cities, and to sell male and female slaves.

cards.note: Genesis 11:4 — *And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.* The name-making rebellion of Babel is the spirit of Nimrod's kingdom set against the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.
cards.t_text: And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

cards.note: Genesis 10:10 — *And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.* Babel is Nimrod's throne; the king threatening Terah is the founder of the kingdom-of-man.
cards.s_text: And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.
cards.t_text: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

cards.note: Genesis 10:8 — *And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.* The canon's own naming of the tyrant whose murderous reach over Terah's house Jasher dramatizes.
cards.s_text: And it was in the third day that the king sent to Terah, saying, Send me your son for a price as I spoke to you; and should you not do this, I will send and slay all you have in your house, so that you shall not even have a dog remaining.
cards.t_text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 1:16 — *And he said, When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.* The tyrant-king ordering the slaying of the newborn son to crush the seed — the exact menace Nimrod presses on Terah.
cards.s_text: And now therefore give me the child, that we may slay him before his evil springs up against us, and I will give you for his value, your house full of silver and gold.
cards.t_text: And he said, When you do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then you shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.

cards.note: Matthew 2:16 — *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* Herod, warned by stargazers of a King's birth, slays the children — Nimrod's plot against Abram replayed against the Messiah.
cards.s_text: If it seems good to the king to give his father value for this child, we will slay him before he shall grow up and increase in the land, and his evil increase against us, that we and our children perish through his evil.
cards.t_text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.

cards.note: Exodus 1:22 — *And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.* Pharaoh's edict against the Hebrew sons is the same kingdom-of-man move Nimrod makes against the infant Abram.
cards.s_text: And now therefore give me the child, that we may slay him before his evil springs up against us, and I will give you for his value, your house full of silver and gold.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born you shall cast into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:16 — *And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.* The same star-watching Chaldean world that frames Abram's birth in Jasher; Jubilees has Abram himself reading the heavens.
cards.s_text: And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth week, in the fifth year thereof, Abram sat up throughout the night on the new moon of the seventh month to observe the stars from the evening to the morning, in order to see what would be the character of the year with regard to the rains, and he was alone as he sat and observed.

cards.note: Genesis 12:2 — *And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing.* The destiny the magi read in the star is the very covenant Yahuah would speak over Abram.
cards.s_text: And they said to each other, This only betokens the child that has been born to Terah this night, who will grow up and be fruitful, and multiply, and possess all the earth, he and his children for ever, and he and his seed will slay great kings, and inherit their lands.
cards.t_text: And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great; and you shall be a blessing:

cards.note: *And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.* (Jasher 8:2). *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1). On the night Abram is born, Nimrod's wise men look up from Terah's house and see one great star run across the heavens and swallow four others, and they understand its import; before the chapter is out Nimrod is demanding the child's life. On the night Yahusha (Jesus) is born, wise men from the east read the heavens the same way and come to Jerusalem, and Herod moves to kill the child. Twice the sky announces the seed of promise at its birth, and twice the kingdom of man answers by reaching for the infant. What happened to Abram is what happened to the Messiah (Christ), because it is one war against one seed.
cards.s_text: And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.
cards.t_text: Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,

cards.note: Matthew 2:2 — *Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.* The same eastern stargazers reading a King's birth in a star that Jasher sets over Abram's cradle.
cards.s_text: And when all the wise men and conjurors went out from the house of Terah, they lifted up their eyes toward heaven that night to look at the stars, and they saw, and behold one very large star came from the east and ran in the heavens, and he swallowed up the four stars from the four sides of the heavens.
cards.t_text: Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:17 — *All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?* Jubilees records the same reasoning — Abram turning from the host of heaven to the One in whose hand they are (Jasher 9:19).
cards.s_text: And Abram said to himself Surely these are not gods that made the earth and all mankind, but these are the servants of Elohim, and Abram remained in the house of Noah and there knew Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways’ and he served Yahuah (the Lord) all the days of his life, and all that generation forgot Yahuah (the Lord), and served other gods of wood and stone, and rebelled all their days.
cards.t_text: And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 4:19 — *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them,* Moses forbids the host-of-heaven worship that Abram reasons his way out of, finding sun and moon are servants, not gods (Jasher 9:19).
cards.s_text: And Abram said to himself Surely these are not gods that made the earth and all mankind, but these are the servants of Elohim, and Abram remained in the house of Noah and there knew Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways’ and he served Yahuah (the Lord) all the days of his life, and all that generation forgot Yahuah (the Lord), and served other gods of wood and stone, and rebelled all their days.
cards.t_text: And lest you lift up your eyes unto heaven, and when you see the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, should be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has divided unto all nations under the whole heaven.

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:14 — *Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.* the prophet's verdict on the breathless idols Jasher's generation served (Jasher 9:6).
cards.s_text: And Abram was in Noah’s house thirty-nine years, and Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord) from three years old, and he went in the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) until the day of his death, as Noah and his son Shem had taught him; and all the sons of the earth in those days greatly transgressed against Yahuah (the Lord), and they rebelled against him and they served other gods, and they forgot Yahuah (the Lord) who had created them in the earth; and the inhabitants of the earth made to themselves, at that time, every man his god; gods of wood and stone which could neither speak, hear, nor deliver, and the sons of men served them and they became their gods.
cards.t_text: Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

cards.note: Psalm 115:4 — *Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.* the gods of wood and stone that could neither speak nor hear nor deliver (Jasher 9:6) are the very dumb idols the psalm derides.
cards.s_text: And Abram was in Noah’s house thirty-nine years, and Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord) from three years old, and he went in the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) until the day of his death, as Noah and his son Shem had taught him; and all the sons of the earth in those days greatly transgressed against Yahuah (the Lord), and they rebelled against him and they served other gods, and they forgot Yahuah (the Lord) who had created them in the earth; and the inhabitants of the earth made to themselves, at that time, every man his god; gods of wood and stone which could neither speak, hear, nor deliver, and the sons of men served them and they became their gods.
cards.t_text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* the canon names Terah the idolater exactly as Jasher does — the first of the idol-servers (Jasher 9:7).
cards.s_text: And the king and all his servants, and Terah with all his household were then the first of those that served gods of wood and stone.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Joshua 24:3 — *And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.* Yahuah's own testimony that He took Abraham out, the deliverance Jasher shows beginning in the house of Noah and Shem (Jasher 9:5).
cards.s_text: And when Abram came out from the cave, he went to Noah and his son Shem, and he remained with them to learn the instruction of Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways, and no man knew where Abram was, and Abram served Noah and Shem his son for a long time.
cards.t_text: And I took your father Abraham from the other side of the flood, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac.

cards.note: Acts 7:2 — *And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,* Stephen sets the call in Mesopotamia, the land of the idol-houses Jasher describes, before ever Abram reached Haran (Jasher 9:6).
cards.s_text: And Abram was in Noah’s house thirty-nine years, and Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord) from three years old, and he went in the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) until the day of his death, as Noah and his son Shem had taught him; and all the sons of the earth in those days greatly transgressed against Yahuah (the Lord), and they rebelled against him and they served other gods, and they forgot Yahuah (the Lord) who had created them in the earth; and the inhabitants of the earth made to themselves, at that time, every man his god; gods of wood and stone which could neither speak, hear, nor deliver, and the sons of men served them and they became their gods.
cards.t_text: And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,

cards.note: Isaiah 51:2 — *Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.* the prophet names the lone calling that Jasher shows beginning in the hidden boy who knew Yahuah from three years old (Jasher 9:6).
cards.s_text: And Abram was in Noah’s house thirty-nine years, and Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord) from three years old, and he went in the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) until the day of his death, as Noah and his son Shem had taught him; and all the sons of the earth in those days greatly transgressed against Yahuah (the Lord), and they rebelled against him and they served other gods, and they forgot Yahuah (the Lord) who had created them in the earth; and the inhabitants of the earth made to themselves, at that time, every man his god; gods of wood and stone which could neither speak, hear, nor deliver, and the sons of men served them and they became their gods.
cards.t_text: Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.

cards.note: Genesis 9:26 — *And he said, Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.* Abram learns the way of Yahuah in the house of Shem, the blessed line in whose tents the knowledge of the Creator was kept (Jasher 9:5).
cards.s_text: And when Abram came out from the cave, he went to Noah and his son Shem, and he remained with them to learn the instruction of Yahuah (the Lord) and his ways, and no man knew where Abram was, and Abram served Noah and Shem his son for a long time.
cards.t_text: And he said, Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.

cards.note: Genesis 11:29 — *And Abram and Nahor took them wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.* the canon names the same daughters of Haran's house that Jasher records, Milcah and Sarai (Jasher 9:3).
cards.s_text: And she conceived again and bare a daughter, and she called her name Milca; and she again conceived and bare a daughter, and she called her name Sarai.
cards.t_text: And Abram and Nahor took them wives: the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai; and the name of Nahor’s wife, Milcah, the daughter of Haran, the father of Milcah, and the father of Iscah.

cards.note: *And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.* (Jubilees 9:3). *And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.* (Jasher 10:32). Jasher tells of Asshur son of Shem going out with a large company to a distant land, finding a wide valley, and building four cities named after themselves. Jubilees had already allotted him that ground: the second portion of Shem's share, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar to the border of India. Jasher's "distant land that they found" was not stumbled upon; it was his by lot. The walking and the allotment are the same inheritance seen from two sides.
cards.s_text: And Ashur son of Shem and his children and household went forth at that time, a very large body of them, and they went to a distant land that they found, and they met with a very extensive valley in the land that they went to, and they built themselves four cities, and they called them after their own names and occurrences.
cards.t_text: And for Asshur came forth the second portion, all the land of Asshur and Nineveh and Shinar and to the border of India, and it ascends and skirts the river.

cards.note: Genesis 10:11 — *Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,* the same Asshur founding the same cities — Nineveh, Rehoboth, Calah — that Jasher 10:33 names among Asshur's four.
cards.s_text: And these are the names of the cities which the children of Ashur built, Ninevah, Resen, Calach and Rehobother; and the children of Ashur dwell there to this day.
cards.t_text: Out of that land went forth Asshur, and builded Nineveh, and the city Rehoboth, and Calah,

cards.note: Genesis 10:21 — *Unto Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born.* Genesis marks Shem as father of Eber's line — the seed Jasher 10:30 traces as it builds cities after the scattering.
cards.s_text: And some of the children of Shem son of Noah, father of all the children of Eber, also went and built themselves cities in the places wherein they were scattered, and they called their cities after their names.
cards.t_text: Unto Shem also, the father of all the children of Eber, the brother of Japheth the elder, even to him were children born.

cards.note: Genesis 10:22 — *The children of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.* The identical five sons of Shem that Jasher 10:31 names, the father-stock of the chosen line.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Shem were Elam, Ashur, Arpachshad, Lud and Aram, and they built themselves cities and called the names of all their cities after their names.
cards.t_text: The children of Shem; Elam, and Asshur, and Arphaxad, and Lud, and Aram.

cards.note: Genesis 14:2 — *That these made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.* The canon names the same four plain-cities by their kings that Jasher 10:26 records being built and named after their founders.
cards.s_text: And these men built themselves four cities in the land of the plain, and they called the names of their cities after their own names.
cards.t_text: That these made war with Bera king of Sodom, and with Birsha king of Gomorrah, Shinab king of Admah, and Shemeber king of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, which is Zoar.

cards.note: Genesis 10:19 — *And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, as thou comest to Gerar, unto Gaza; as thou goest, unto Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, even unto Lasha.* Genesis sets the Canaanite border at the very four cities of the plain Jasher 10:25 says four men of Ham founded.
cards.s_text: And four men from the family of Ham went to the land of the plain; these are the names of the four men, Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboyim.
cards.t_text: And the border of the Canaanites was from Sidon, as you come to Gerar, unto Gaza; as you go, unto Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Admah, and Zeboim, even unto Lasha.

cards.note: *And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.* (Jubilees 9:1). *And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.* (Jasher 10:19). Jasher names Ham's four sons; Jubilees shows Ham dividing his portion among those same four, laid out from east to west: Cush to the east, then Mizraim, then Put, then Canaan on the sea. One book is the roll call and the other is the map. Canaan's lot on the sea matters later, because Canaan did not keep to it but settled in Shem's portion, and the land that bears his name was never his by right.
cards.s_text: And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.
cards.t_text: And Ham divided amongst his sons, and the first portion came forth for Cush towards the east, and to the west of him for Mizraim, and to the west . of him for Put, and to the west of him and to the west thereof on the sea for Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 10:14 — *And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (out of whom came Philistim,) and Caphtorim.* Genesis names the same Philistine origin that Jasher 10:23 records as the Pelishtim going forth from Pathros and Casloch.
cards.s_text: And the children of Pathros and Casloch intermarried together, and from them went forth the Pelishtim, the Azathim, and the Gerarim, the Githim and the Ekronim, in all five families; these also built themselves cities, and they called their cities after the names of their fathers to this day.
cards.t_text: And Pathrusim, and Casluhim, (out of whom came Philistim,) and Caphtorim.

cards.note: Genesis 10:13 — *And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,* the identical Egyptian families Jasher 10:21 lists as the children of Mitzraim.
cards.s_text: And the children of Mitzraim are the Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuchim, Pathrusim, Casluchim and Caphturim, seven families.
cards.t_text: And Mizraim begat Ludim, and Anamim, and Lehabim, and Naphtuhim,

cards.note: Genesis 10:6 — *And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.* The same four sons of Ham that Jasher 10:19 names according to their generation and cities.
cards.s_text: And the children of Ham were Cush, Mitzraim, Phut and Canaan according to their generation and cities.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Ham; Cush, and Mizraim, and Phut, and Canaan.

cards.note: *And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.* (Jubilees 9:8). *And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.* (Jasher 10:7). Jasher lists Japheth's seven sons; Jubilees takes the first two of that list and places them on the ground, Gomer's portion east from the north side to the river Tina, Magog's the inner north as far as the sea of Meot. The same names, now with borders. The far north was Magog's lot from the division of the earth, which is worth remembering whenever the prophets speak of Magog and the north.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.
cards.t_text: And the first portion came forth for Gomer to the east from the north side to the river Tînâ; and in the north there came forth for Magog all the inner portions of the north until it reaches to the sea of Mê’at.

cards.note: Genesis 10:5 — *By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.* Genesis records the same division of Japheth's line into lands and languages that Jasher 10:6 recounts as they built cities where they were scattered.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Japheth the son of Noah went and built themselves cities in the places where they were scattered, and they called all their cities after their names, and the sons of Japheth were divided upon the face of the earth into many divisions and languages.
cards.t_text: By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations.

cards.note: Genesis 10:2 — *The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.* The identical roll of Japheth's seven sons that Jasher 10:7 names according to their generations.
cards.s_text: And these are the sons of Japheth according to their families, Gomer, Magog, Medai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech and Tiras; these are the children of Japheth according to their generations.
cards.t_text: The sons of Japheth; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.

cards.note: *For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.* (Jubilees 10:25). *And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.* (Jasher 10:2). Jasher opens with the result: the sons of men scattered for their sin at the tower into the four corners of the earth. Jubilees gives the means and the name: the language confounded at Shinar, so the place is called Babel, and from there they went out each to his own cities according to his language and his nation. Jasher's "many divisions" are Jubilees' languages. The scattering was judgment on the tower, and both books say so.
cards.s_text: And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.
cards.t_text: For this reason the whole land of Shinar is called Babel, because Yahuah (God) did there confound all the language of the children of men, and from thence they were dispersed into their cities, each according to his language and his nation.

cards.note: Acts 17:26 — *And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;* Paul preaches the same divine ordering of the nations and their dwellings that Jasher 10:5 narrates after the tower.
cards.s_text: And some of them built cities in places from which they were afterward extirpated, and they called these cities after their own names, or the names of their children, or after their particular occurrences.
cards.t_text: And has made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:8 — *When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The scattering and city-building of Jasher 10:4 is the Most High bounding the nations around the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And the sons of men built many cities according to their families, in all the places where they went, and throughout the earth where Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered them.
cards.t_text: When the El Elyon (most High) divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 11:9 — *Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because Yahuah (LORD) did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did Yahuah (LORD) scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.* Genesis names the confusion of tongues that Jasher 10:3 describes as each family according to its language.
cards.s_text: And all the families became each according to its language, its land, or its city.
cards.t_text: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because Yahuah (LORD) did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did Yahuah (LORD) scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 11:8 — *So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.* The very scattering Jasher 10:2 recounts as the sons of men dispersed into the four corners of the earth.
cards.s_text: And when Yahuah (the Lord) had scattered the sons of men on account of their sin at the tower, behold they spread forth into many divisions, and all the sons of men were dispersed into the four corners of the earth.
cards.t_text: So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.

cards.note: *And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.* (Jubilees 8:8). *And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.* (Jasher 10:1). Jasher 10 opens with Peleg's death in Abram's forty-eighth year, at two hundred and thirty-nine years old; Jubilees gives his birth and the reason for his name. The man whose name means division was born as the earth was being divided and died in the days of the man through whom it would be gathered into one seed. Two books tell the two ends of Peleg's life. The name given at his birth was the headline of his generation.
cards.s_text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year thereof, she bare him a son, and he called his name Peleg; for in the days when he was born the children of Noah began to divide the earth amongst themselves: for this reason he called his name Peleg.

cards.note: Genesis 11:17 — *And Eber lived after he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.* The chosen line is kept generation by generation, the same chain Jasher 10:1 measures by Peleg's two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.s_text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.t_text: And Eber lived after he begat Peleg four hundred and thirty years, and begat sons and daughters.

cards.note: Genesis 11:16 — *And Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg:* the canon's lifespan register carrying the seed-line Shem-Eber-Peleg that Jasher 10:1 is counting toward Abram.
cards.s_text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.t_text: And Eber lived four and thirty years, and begat Peleg:

cards.note: Genesis 10:25 — *And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.* Jasher 10:1 dates Peleg's death in Abram's lifetime; Genesis names him for the very dividing of the earth this chapter recounts.
cards.s_text: And Peleg the son of Eber died in those days, in the forty-eighth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, and all the days of Peleg were two hundred and thirty-nine years.
cards.t_text: And unto Eber were born two sons: the name of one was Peleg; for in his days was the earth divided; and his brother’s name was Joktan.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:7 — *And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.* Jubilees gives the fearful father where Jasher gives the fearless son before Nimrod — the same idol-people who would slay the witness of truth.
cards.s_text: And the king said to Abram, What is this that you have done to your father and to his gods? And Abram answered the king in the words that he spoke to his father, and he said, The large god that was with them in the house did to them what you have heard.
cards.t_text: And if I tell them the truth, they will slay me; for their soul cleaves to them to worship them and honour them. Keep silent, my son, lest they slay you.”

cards.note: Genesis 11:8 — *So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.* Abram's closing word that Yahuah sees and judges the wicked is the same judgment that scattered Nimrod's Babel.
cards.s_text: And when Abram had ceased speaking before the king and princes, Abram lifted up his eyes to the heavens, and he said, Yahuah (the Lord) sees all the wicked, and he will judge them.
cards.t_text: So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.

cards.note: Genesis 7:23 — *And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.* Abram warns Nimrod by the flood that destroyed the whole earth — the very judgment Genesis records standing against the kingdom of man.
cards.s_text: Dost you not know, or have you not heard, that this evil which you do, our ancestors sinned in it in days of old, and the eternal Elohim brought the waters of the flood upon them and destroyed them all, and also destroyed the whole earth on their account? And will you and your people rise up now and do like to this work, in order to bring down the anger of Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) of the universe, and to bring evil upon you and the whole earth?
cards.t_text: And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground, both man, and cattle, and the creeping things, and the fowl of the heaven; and they were destroyed from the earth: and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:12 — *Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it.* Jubilees tells the same deed Jasher tells with the hatchet — the called seed destroying his father's gods, a second witness to the legend.
cards.s_text: And when Abram saw all these things his anger was kindled against his father, and he hastened and took a hatchet in his hand, and came to the chamber of the gods, and he broke all his father’s gods.
cards.t_text: And in the sixtieth year of the life of Abram, that is, in the fourth week, in the fourth year thereof, Abram arose by night, and burned the house of the idols, and he burned all that was in the house, and no man knew it.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:17 — *And the residue thereof he maketh a god, even his graven image: he falleth down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and saith, Deliver me; for thou art my god.* Abram mocks idols that cannot hear prayer or deliver — the very cry Isaiah shows the maker raising to dead wood.
cards.s_text: And Abram answered his father and said to him, And how can you then serve these idols in whom there is no power to do any thing? Can those idols in which you trust deliver you? can they hear your prayers when you call upon them? can they deliver you from the hands of your enemies, or will they fight your battles for you against your enemies, that you should serve wood and stone which can neither speak nor hear?
cards.t_text: And the residue thereof he makes a god, even his graven image: he falls down unto it, and worshippeth it, and prayeth unto it, and says, Deliver me; for you are my god.

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:14 — *Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.* Abram breaking the breathless idols confounds the founder exactly as Jeremiah says — there is no breath in them.
cards.s_text: And when Abram saw all these things his anger was kindled against his father, and he hastened and took a hatchet in his hand, and came to the chamber of the gods, and he broke all his father’s gods.
cards.t_text: Every man is brutish in his knowledge: every founder is confounded by the graven image: for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

cards.note: Habakkuk 2:18 — *What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?* Abram asking what power is in idols that cannot deliver is Habakkuk's exact charge against the dumb, profitless image.
cards.s_text: And Abram answered his father and said to him, And how can you then serve these idols in whom there is no power to do any thing? Can those idols in which you trust deliver you? can they hear your prayers when you call upon them? can they deliver you from the hands of your enemies, or will they fight your battles for you against your enemies, that you should serve wood and stone which can neither speak nor hear?
cards.t_text: What profiteth the graven image that the maker thereof has graven it; the molten image, and a teacher of lies, that the maker of his work trusts therein, to make dumb idols?

cards.note: Jeremiah 10:3 — *For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe.* Abram's idols of wood, like them are those that made them, is Jeremiah's tree cut and shaped by the workman's axe.
cards.s_text: And he called out and said, Wo to my father and this wicked generation, whose hearts are all inclined to vanity, who serve these idols of wood and stone which can neither eat, smell, hear nor speak, who have mouths without speech, eyes without sight, ears without hearing, hands without feeling, and legs which cannot move; like them are those that made them and that trust in them.
cards.t_text: For the customs of the people are vain: for one cutteth a tree out of the forest, the work of the hands of the workman, with the axe.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:9 — *They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.* The gods that cannot stretch a hand to eat are Isaiah's blind, profitless graven images.
cards.s_text: And Abram saw on the day when he was sitting amongst them, that they had no voice, no hearing, no motion, and not one of them could stretch forth his hand to eat.
cards.t_text: They that make a graven image are all of them vanity; and their delectable things shall not profit; and they are their own witnesses; they see not, nor know; that they may be ashamed.

cards.note: Psalm 115:6 — *They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not:* Jasher's ears without hearing and idols that can neither smell carries the same line of the Psalm's rebuke.
cards.s_text: And he called out and said, Wo to my father and this wicked generation, whose hearts are all inclined to vanity, who serve these idols of wood and stone which can neither eat, smell, hear nor speak, who have mouths without speech, eyes without sight, ears without hearing, hands without feeling, and legs which cannot move; like them are those that made them and that trust in them.
cards.t_text: They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not:

cards.note: Psalm 115:5 — *They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not:* Abram's cry that the idols have mouths without speech and eyes without sight is the Psalmist's idol-polemic exactly.
cards.s_text: And he called out and said, Wo to my father and this wicked generation, whose hearts are all inclined to vanity, who serve these idols of wood and stone which can neither eat, smell, hear nor speak, who have mouths without speech, eyes without sight, ears without hearing, hands without feeling, and legs which cannot move; like them are those that made them and that trust in them.
cards.t_text: They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not:

cards.note: Jubilees 12:17 — *All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God).* Jubilees has the same Abram turning from the host of heaven to the Maker, the elect heart that Jasher shows knowing Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord), and he went in his ways and instructions, and Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) was with him.
cards.t_text: And a word came into his heart and he said: "All the signs of the stars, and the signs of the moon and of the sun are all in the hand of Yahuah (God). Why do I search (them) out?

cards.note: Acts 7:2 — *And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran.* Stephen places Abram's call in idolatrous Mesopotamia — exactly where Jasher has him come forth knowing Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And in the fiftieth year of the life of Abram son of Terah, Abram came forth from the house of Noah, and went to his father’s house.
cards.t_text: And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,

cards.note: Isaiah 51:2 — *Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.* Abram knowing Yahuah amid idols is the elect seed Isaiah names — called alone, not a church, the covenant line kept and chosen.
cards.s_text: And Abram knew Yahuah (the Lord), and he went in his ways and instructions, and Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) was with him.
cards.t_text: Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Jasher's Terah serving strange gods is the very idolatry Joshua names — the house Abram is called out of.
cards.s_text: And Terah his father was in those days, still captain of the host of king Nimrod, and he still followed strange gods.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Genesis 14:4 — *Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.* Jasher's twelve-year tax to Chedorlaomer is the exact servitude Genesis names, the seed of the war of kings that Abram will enter.
cards.s_text: And they served him twelve years, and they gave him a yearly tax.
cards.t_text: Twelve years they served Chedorlaomer, and in the thirteenth year they rebelled.

cards.note: Romans 1:22 — *Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,* — Nimrod teaching wickedness to the sons of men is Paul's whole-earth idolatry diagnosis, the kingdom of man rebelling against its Maker.
cards.s_text: And notwithstanding this, Nimrod did not return to Yahuah (the Lord), and he continued in wickedness and teaching wickedness to the sons of men; and Mardon, his son, was worse than his father, and continued to add to the abominations of his father.
cards.t_text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

cards.note: Genesis 11:8 — *So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.* Jasher names Babel for this confounding and dispersing — the cities are monuments to the judgment Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And he called the first Babel, saying, Because Yahuah (the Lord) there confounded the language of the whole earth; and the name of the second he called Erech, because from there Elohim (God) dispersed them.
cards.t_text: So Yahuah (LORD) scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.

cards.note: Genesis 10:10 — *And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.* Jasher names the same four cities (Babel, Erech, Eched, Calnah) after the tower's fall, expanding the canon's bare list.
cards.s_text: And he called the first Babel, saying, Because Yahuah (the Lord) there confounded the language of the whole earth; and the name of the second he called Erech, because from there Elohim (God) dispersed them.
cards.t_text: And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Accad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar.

cards.note: Genesis 10:8 — *And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.* Jasher's Nimrod reigning and building in Shinar is the same mighty one Genesis names — the kingdom-of-man founder.
cards.s_text: And Nimrod son of Cush was still in the land of Shinar, and he reigned over it and dwelt there, and he built cities in the land of Shinar.
cards.t_text: And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:2–4 — *What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself? For there is no spirit in them, For they are dumb forms, and a misleading of the heart. Worship them not: Worship the Elohim (God) of heaven, Who causes the rain and the dew to descend on the earth...* Abram's idol-polemic to his father, the same plea Jasher gives him to cast away the vain things and serve Yahuah (Jasher 12:68).
cards.s_text: Now therefore hearken to my voice, and let us arise and go to the land of Canaan, out of the reach of injury from Nimrod; and serve you Yahuah (the Lord) who created you in the earth and it will be well with you; and cast away all the vain things which you pursue.
cards.t_text: And he said, "What help and profit have we from those idols which you do worship, And before which you do bow yourself?

cards.note: Jubilees 12:9 — *And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.* The same marriage of Abram to Sarai that Jasher records alongside Nahor's to Milca (Jasher 12:44).
cards.s_text: And at that time Nahor and Abram took to themselves wives, the daughters of their brother Haran; the wife of Nahor was Milca and the name of Abram’s wife was Sarai. And Sarai, wife of Abram, was barren; she had no offspring in those days.
cards.t_text: And in the fortieth jubilee, in the second week, in the seventh year thereof, Abram took to himself a wife, and her name was Sarai, the daughter of his father, and she became his wife.

cards.note: Jubilees 12:14 — *And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees...* The same death of Haran by fire in the Chaldees that Jasher records, his heart not perfect with Yahuah (Jasher 12:26).
cards.s_text: And Haran died when they had cast him into the fire, and he was burned to ashes, for his heart was not perfect with Yahuah (the Lord); and those men who cast him into the fire, the flame of the fire spread over them, and they were burned, and twelve men of them died.
cards.t_text: And Haran hasted to save them, but the fire flamed over him, and he was burnt in the fire, and he died in Ur of the Chaldees before Terah his father, and they buried him in Ur of the Chaldees.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:8 — *By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.* The faith that walked in Yahuah's ways and followed His law all Abram's days (Jasher 12:42) is the faith that obeyed the call.
cards.s_text: And Abram returned on that day and went to his father’s house, he and the men that followed him, and Abram served Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) all the days of his life, and he walked in his ways and followed his law.
cards.t_text: By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went.

cards.note: Genesis 12:1 — *Now Yahuah (LORD) had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto a land that I will shew thee.* The canon call that Jasher dramatizes as Abram's plea to leave the land of Nimrod and go to Canaan (Jasher 12:68).
cards.s_text: Now therefore hearken to my voice, and let us arise and go to the land of Canaan, out of the reach of injury from Nimrod; and serve you Yahuah (the Lord) who created you in the earth and it will be well with you; and cast away all the vain things which you pursue.
cards.t_text: Now Yahuah (LORD) had said unto Abram, Get you out of your country, and from your kindred, and from your father’s house, unto a land that I will shew you:

cards.note: Acts 7:2 — *And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran.* Stephen sets the call in Mesopotamia before Haran, the same flight from Nimrod's reach toward Canaan that Abram urges on Terah (Jasher 12:68).
cards.s_text: Now therefore hearken to my voice, and let us arise and go to the land of Canaan, out of the reach of injury from Nimrod; and serve you Yahuah (the Lord) who created you in the earth and it will be well with you; and cast away all the vain things which you pursue.
cards.t_text: And he said, Men, brethren, and fathers, hearken; The Elohim (God) of glory appeared unto our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,

cards.note: Isaiah 51:2 — *Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.* Called alone — election before confession, the same Abram who from that day served Yahuah all his days and inclined men's hearts to Him (Jasher 12:42-43).
cards.s_text: And Abram returned on that day and went to his father’s house, he and the men that followed him, and Abram served Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) all the days of his life, and he walked in his ways and followed his law.
cards.t_text: Look unto Abraham your father, and unto Sarah that bare you: for I called him alone, and blessed him, and increased him.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* The idolatrous land Abram begs Terah to leave for Canaan (Jasher 12:65) is the very world Joshua names — the fathers served other gods beyond the river.
cards.s_text: Now whom have you here and what have you in this land? Arise, let us go together to the land of Canaan, that we may be delivered from his hand, lest you perish also through him in the latter days.
