cards.note: Genesis 28:13 — *And, behold, Yahuah (LORD) stood above it, and said, I am Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham thy father, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac: the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed;* The same covenant word Jasher 30:1 puts in Yahuah's mouth over Jacob at Luz.
cards.s_text: And Jacob went forth continuing his road to Haran, and he came as far as mount Moriah, and he tarried there all night near the city of Luz; and Yahuah (the Lord) appeared there to Jacob on that night, and he said to him, I am Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of Abraham and the Elohim (God) of Isaac your father; the land upon which you lie I will give to you and your seed.
cards.t_text: And, behold, Yahuah (LORD) stood above it, and said, I am Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac: the land whereon you lie, to you will I give it, and to your seed;

cards.note: Genesis 29:23 — *And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.* The canon's terse wedding-night line is the scene Jasher 31:4 expands with the extinguished lamps and the unwitting Jacob.
cards.s_text: And afterward Laban took his daughter Leah, and he brought her to Jacob, and he came to her and Jacob did not know that she was Leah.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.

cards.note: Genesis 29:25 — *And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this thou hast done unto me? did not I serve with thee for Rachel? wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?* Jacob's morning protest in Jasher 31:11 is the same charge of deceit lodged in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Jacob called to Laban, and said to him, What is this that you did to me? Surely I served you for Rachel, and why did you deceive me and did give me Leah?
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, that in the morning, behold, it was Leah: and he said to Laban, What is this you have done unto me? did not I serve with you for Rachel? wherefore then have you beguiled me?

cards.note: Genesis 29:26 — *And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.* Laban's elder-before-younger custom in Jasher 31:12 quotes the canon's defense almost verbatim.
cards.s_text: And Laban answered Jacob, saying, Not so is it done in our place to give the younger before the elder now therefore if you desire to take her sister likewise, take her to you for the service which you will serve me for another seven years.
cards.t_text: And Laban said, It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:4 — *And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: “Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah?* Jubilees narrates the same deceived wedding night that Jasher 31:4 tells, the two extra-canon witnesses agreeing with Genesis.
cards.s_text: And afterward Laban took his daughter Leah, and he brought her to Jacob, and he came to her and Jacob did not know that she was Leah.
cards.t_text: And he went in to her, and behold, she was Leah; and Jacob was angry with Laban, and said to him: “Why have you dealt thus with me? Did not I serve you for Rachel and not for Leah? Why have you wronged me? Take your daughter, and I will go; for you have done evil to me.”

cards.note: Genesis 29:31 — *And when Yahuah (LORD) saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.* Jasher 31:14 retells this opening of Leah's womb that begins the tribal births.
cards.s_text: And when Yahuah (the Lord) saw that Leah was hated, Yahuah (the Lord) opened her womb, and she conceived and bare Jacob four sons in those days.
cards.t_text: And when Yahuah (LORD) saw that Leah was hated, he opened her womb: but Rachel was barren.

cards.note: Genesis 30:21 — *And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.* The sister named in Jasher 31:18 alongside Issachar and Zebulon is the canon's Dinah.
cards.s_text: And Leah again conceived and bare Jacob in those days two sons and one daughter, and these are their names, Issachar, Zebulon, and their sister Dinah.
cards.t_text: And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

cards.note: Exodus 1:1 — *Now these are the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.* The sons Jasher 31:15 begins naming are the very tribes that become the nation in Egypt.
cards.s_text: And these are their names, Reuben Simeon, Levi, and Judah, and she afterward left bearing.
cards.t_text: Now these are the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:11 — *And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.* Jubilees dates the first of the sons Jasher 31:15 lists, the same tribal beginning.
cards.s_text: And these are their names, Reuben Simeon, Levi, and Judah, and she afterward left bearing.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) opened the womb of Leah, and she conceived and bare Jacob a son, and he called his name Reuben, on the fourteenth day of the ninth month, in the first year of the third week.

cards.note: Genesis 30:22 — *And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.* Rachel's answered supplication in Jasher 31:19-21 is the canon's remembering of Rachel.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) heard her and opened her womb, and Rachel conceived and bare a son, and she said, Yahuah (the Lord) has taken away my reproach, and she called his name Joseph, saying, May Yahuah (the Lord) add to me another son; and Jacob was ninety-one years old when she bare him.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

cards.note: Genesis 30:23 — *And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, Elohim (God) hath taken away my reproach.* The exact words Jasher 31:21 puts in Rachel's mouth at Joseph's naming.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) heard her and opened her womb, and Rachel conceived and bare a son, and she said, Yahuah (the Lord) has taken away my reproach, and she called his name Joseph, saying, May Yahuah (the Lord) add to me another son; and Jacob was ninety-one years old when she bare him.
cards.t_text: And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, Elohim (God) has taken away my reproach:

cards.note: Jubilees 28:24 — *And Yahuah (God) was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week.* Jubilees dates the birth that answers Rachel's prayer in Jasher 31:19.
cards.s_text: And Rachel was still barren in those days, and Rachel prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) at that time, and she said, O Yahuah Elohim (O Lord God) remember me and visit me, I beseech you, for now my husband will cast me off, for I have borne him no children.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) was gracious to Rachel, and opened her womb, and she conceived, and bare a son, and she called his name Joseph, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the sixth year in this fourth week.

cards.note: Genesis 30:32 — *I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.* The very wage-terms Jacob names in Jasher 31:26.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to him, This is what you shall give me for wages, that I shall this day pass through all your flock and take away from them every lamb that is speckled and spotted and such as are brown amongst the sheep, and amongst the goats, and if you will do this thing for me I will return and feed your flock and keep them as at first.
cards.t_text: I will pass through all your flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled and spotted cattle, and all the brown cattle among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats: and of such shall be my hire.

cards.note: Genesis 30:43 — *And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses.* Jasher 31:31 closes the flock account with the canon's identical inventory of Jacob's increase.
cards.s_text: And Jacob served Laban six years longer, and when the sheep brought forth, Jacob removed from them such as were speckled and spotted, as he had determined with Laban, and Jacob did so at Laban’s for six years, and the man increased abundantly and he had cattle and maid servants and men servants, camels, and asses.
cards.t_text: And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and menservants, and camels, and asses.

cards.note: Genesis 31:1 — *And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's; and of that which was our father's hath he gotten all this glory.* The envy of Laban's sons in Jasher 31:35 is quoted nearly word for word from the canon.
cards.s_text: And in the course of time he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s, and of that which was our father’s has he acquired all this glory.
cards.t_text: And he heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s; and of that which was our father’s has he gotten all this glory.

cards.note: Jubilees 28:29–30 — *And Jacob's possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maidservants. And Laban and his sons envied Jacob.* Jubilees joins the same multiplying-and-envy Jasher 31:31-35 records.
cards.s_text: And Jacob served Laban six years longer, and when the sheep brought forth, Jacob removed from them such as were speckled and spotted, as he had determined with Laban, and Jacob did so at Laban’s for six years, and the man increased abundantly and he had cattle and maid servants and men servants, camels, and asses.
cards.t_text: And Jacob’s possessions multiplied exceedingly, and he possessed oxen and sheep and asses and camels, and menservants and maidservants.

cards.note: Genesis 31:3 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred; and I will be with thee.* The departure command of Jasher 31:37 is the canon's call to return, with the same “I will be with thee.”
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob at the expiration of the six years, and said to him, Arise, go forth out of this land, and return to the land of your birthplace and I will be with you.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of your fathers, and to your kindred; and I will be with you.

cards.note: Genesis 31:19 — *And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father's.* Rachel's theft of the teraphim in Jasher 31:40 retells this canon line, sheep-shearing and all.
cards.s_text: And Rachel stole her father’s images, and she took them and she concealed them upon the camel upon which she sat, and she went on.
cards.t_text: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images that were her father’s.

cards.note: Jubilees 29:2 — *And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.* Jubilees narrates the same shearing-day flight Jasher 31:37-40 sets up.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob at the expiration of the six years, and said to him, Arise, go forth out of this land, and return to the land of your birthplace and I will be with you.
cards.t_text: And Jacob saw that Laban was going to shear his sheep, and Jacob called Leah and Rachel, and spake kindly to them that they should come with him to the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 31:50 — *If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, Elohim (God) is witness betwixt me and thee.* The exact covenant condition Laban lays on Jacob in Jasher 31:51.
cards.s_text: And Laban said to Jacob, We will make a covenant together and it shall be a testimony between me and you; if you shall afflict my daughters, or shall take other wives besides my daughters, even Elohim shall be a witness between me and you in this matter.
cards.t_text: If you shall afflict my daughters, or if you shall take other wives beside my daughters, no man is with us; see, Elohim (God) is witness betwixt me and you.

cards.note: Genesis 31:44 — *Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou; and let it be for a witness between me and thee.* Jasher 31:52's heap-as-witness is the canon's covenant of witness between Laban and Jacob.
cards.s_text: And they took stones and made a heap, and Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you, therefore he called the name of it Gilead.
cards.t_text: Now therefore come you, let us make a covenant, I and you; and let it be for a witness between me and you.

cards.note: Jubilees 29:8 — *And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.* Jubilees names the same Gilead heap-of-witness Jacob and Laban raise in Jasher 31:52.
cards.s_text: And they took stones and made a heap, and Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you, therefore he called the name of it Gilead.
cards.t_text: And he made there a heap for a witness; wherefore the name of that place is called: “The Heap of Witness,” after this heap.

cards.note: Genesis 25:23 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.* Esau's burning hatred in Jasher 31:64 stands against the womb-oracle that chose the younger Jacob.
cards.s_text: And Esau heard all the words of Laban’s messengers, and his anger was greatly kindled against Jacob, and he remembered his hatred, and his anger burned within him.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto her, Two nations are in your womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from your bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

cards.note: Romans 9:11 — *(For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of Elohim (God) according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth;)* Paul reads Jacob-over-Esau, the very rivalry erupting in Jasher 31:64-65, as election before works.
cards.s_text: And Esau heard all the words of Laban’s messengers, and his anger was greatly kindled against Jacob, and he remembered his hatred, and his anger burned within him.
cards.t_text: (For the children being not yet born, neither having done any good or evil, that the purpose of Elohim (God) according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calls;)

cards.note: Hebrews 12:16 — *Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.* The Esau who arms four hundred men in Jasher 31:65 is the profane brother who despised his birthright.
cards.s_text: And Esau hastened and took his children and servants and the souls of his household, being sixty men, and he went and assembled all the children of Seir the Horite and their people, being three hundred and forty men, and took all this number of four hundred men with drawn swords, and he went to Jacob to smite him.
cards.t_text: Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.

cards.note: Hosea 12:3 — *He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with Elohim (God):* The prophet recalls the heel-grasping Jacob whose host-of-Elohim camp Jasher 31:72 names Machnayim.
cards.s_text: And these messengers went on the road to meet Jacob, and they met him in the road of the brook on the opposite side of the brook Jabuk, and Jacob said when he saw them, This camp is destined to me from Elohim, and Jacob called the name of that place Machnayim.
cards.t_text: He took his brother by the heel in the womb, and by his strength he had power with Elohim (God):

cards.note: *And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.* (Jubilees 29:13). *And Esau hearkened to the voice of Jacob, and Esau returned with the four hundred men that were with him on their road to Seir, and Jacob and all belonging to him went that day as far as the extremity of the land of Canaan in its borders, and he remained there some time.* (Jasher 32:73). Jubilees dates the crossing of the Jabbok and puts the meeting with Esau on the same day: reconciled, and then parted, Esau to Seir and Jacob to his tents. Jasher tells the parting from the road: Esau heard Jacob's voice and turned back with his four hundred men toward Seir while Jacob went on to the edge of Canaan. Peace between the brothers did not make them one house. Esau went his way with his army and Jacob stayed a dweller in tents, and the two lines stayed two lines.
cards.s_text: And Esau hearkened to the voice of Jacob, and Esau returned with the four hundred men that were with him on their road to Seir, and Jacob and all belonging to him went that day as far as the extremity of the land of Canaan in its borders, and he remained there some time.
cards.t_text: And he passed over the Jabbok in the ninth month, on the eleventh thereof. And on that day Esau, his brother, came to him, and he was reconciled to him, and departed from him to the land of Seir, but Jacob dwelt in tents.

cards.note: Genesis 33:10 — *And Jacob said, Nay, I pray thee, if now I have found grace in thy sight, then receive my present at my hand: for therefore I have seen thy face, as though I had seen the face of Elohim (God), and thou wast pleased with me.* Jasher 32:64's 'as though I had seen a god-like face, because you were pleased with me' is the canon's face-of-Elohim word.
cards.s_text: And Esau refused to take the present, and Jacob said to him, I beseech you my Lord, if now I have found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, for I have therefore seen your face, as though I had seen a god-like face, because you were pleased with me.
cards.t_text: And Jacob said, Nay, I pray you, if now I have found grace in your sight, then receive my present at my hand: for therefore I have seen your face, as though I had seen the face of Elohim (God), and you were pleased with me.

cards.note: Genesis 33:3 — *And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.* Jasher 32:54's 'he bowed down seven times until he approached his brother' matches the canon's sevenfold bowing.
cards.s_text: And he passed before his children and wives to meet his brother, and he bowed down to the ground, yea he bowed down seven times until he approached his brother, and Elohim caused Jacob to find grace and favor in the sight of Esau and his men, for Elohim had heard the prayer of Jacob.
cards.t_text: And he passed over before them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

cards.note: Genesis 33:4 — *And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.* Jasher 32:56's 'he ran toward him and he embraced him, and he fell upon his neck, and they kissed and they wept' is the canon reunion verbatim.
cards.s_text: And when Esau saw Jacob running toward him, he also ran toward him and he embraced him, and he fell upon his neck, and they kissed and they wept.
cards.t_text: And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.

cards.note: Hosea 12:4 — *Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Beth-el, and there he spake with us.* The prophet reads Jasher 32:48's all-night wrestling as Israel's defining 'power over the angel,' the nation's own name carried in the grip.
cards.s_text: And when he passed all belonging to him over the brook, Jacob was left by himself, and a man met him, and he wrestled with him that night until the breaking of the day, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint through wrestling with him.
cards.t_text: Yea, he had power over the angel, and prevailed: he wept, and made supplication unto him: he found him in Beth-el, and there he spake with us;

cards.note: Genesis 32:30 — *And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen Elohim (God) face to face, and my life is preserved.* Jasher 32:50's sun rising as he passed the brook follows the canon's Peniel — 'I have seen Elohim face to face.'
cards.s_text: And the sun rose upon him when he had passed the brook, and he came up to the place of his cattle and children.
cards.t_text: And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel: for I have seen Elohim (God) face to face, and my life is preserved.

cards.note: Genesis 32:28 — *And he said, Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Yashar'el (Israel): for as a prince hast thou power with Elohim (God) and with men, and hast prevailed.* Jasher 32:49's blessing at the break of day is the canon's renaming — the name Israel born of this wrestling.
cards.s_text: And at the break of day the man left Jacob there, and he blessed him and went away, and Jacob passed the brook at the break of day, and he halted upon his thigh.
cards.t_text: And he said, Your name shall be called no more Jacob, but Yashar'el (Israel): for as a prince have you power with Elohim (God) and with men, and have prevailed.

cards.note: Genesis 32:24 — *And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.* Jasher 32:48's 'Jacob was left by himself, and a man met him, and he wrestled with him that night until the breaking of the day' is the canon scene verbatim.
cards.s_text: And when he passed all belonging to him over the brook, Jacob was left by himself, and a man met him, and he wrestled with him that night until the breaking of the day, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was out of joint through wrestling with him.
cards.t_text: And Jacob was left alone; and there wrestled a man with him until the breaking of the day.

cards.note: Genesis 32:20 — *And say ye moreover, Behold, thy servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goeth before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.* Jasher 32:46's 'I will appease him with the present... and after this I will see his face, peradventure he will accept of me' is the canon's reasoning nearly word for word.
cards.s_text: And if they shall say to you, Why does he delay behind you, from coming to meet his brother and to see his face, then you shall say to them, Surely he comes joyfully behind us to meet his brother, for he said, I will appease him with the present that goes to him, and after this I will see his face, peradventure he will accept of me.
cards.t_text: And say you moreover, Behold, your servant Jacob is behind us. For he said, I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face; peradventure he will accept of me.

cards.note: Genesis 32:17 — *And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth thee, and asketh thee, saying, Whose art thou? and whither goest thou? and whose are these before thee?* Jasher 32:44's instruction for when Esau asks 'Whose are you, and whither do you go' matches the canon's commanded answer.
cards.s_text: And he commanded them, and said to them, Keep yourselves at a distance from each other, and put a space between the droves, and when Esau and those who are with him shall meet you and ask you, saying, Whose are you, and whither do you go, and to whom belongs all this before you, you shall say to them, We are the servants of Jacob, and we come to meet Esau in peace, and behold Jacob comes behind us.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the foremost, saying, When Esau my brother meeteth you, and asks you, saying, Whose are you? and whither go you? and whose are these before you?

cards.note: Genesis 32:16 — *And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.* Jasher 32:43-44's ten droves 'each sort by itself' with 'a space between the droves' is the canon staging verbatim.
cards.s_text: And he put them all in ten droves, and he placed each sort by itself, and he delivered them into the hands of ten of his servants, each drove by itself.
cards.t_text: And he delivered them into the hand of his servants, every drove by themselves; and said unto his servants, Pass over before me, and put a space betwixt drove and drove.

cards.note: Genesis 32:8 — *And said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the other company which is left shall escape.* Jasher 32:25's two-camp safeguard ('if Esau come to one camp and slay it, the other camp... will escape') matches the canon plan exactly, the deliverance of Jasher 32:27 answering it.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the prayer of Jacob on that day, and Yahuah (the Lord) then delivered Jacob from the hands of his brother Esau.
cards.t_text: And said, If Esau come to the one company, and smite it, then the other company which is left shall escape.

cards.note: Genesis 32:2 — *And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is Elohim's (God's) host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.* Jasher 32:29's angel camps 'divided into four camps' carry the 'host of Elohim' and the Mahanaim ('two camps') the canon names.
cards.s_text: And these angels appeared to Esau and his people as two thousand men, riding upon horses furnished with all sorts of war instruments, and they appeared in the sight of Esau and all his men to be divided into four camps, with four chiefs to them.
cards.t_text: And when Jacob saw them, he said, This is Elohim's (God’s) host: and he called the name of that place Mahanaim.

cards.note: Genesis 32:1 — *And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of Elohim (God) met him.* Jasher 32:28's 'Yahuah sent three angels of the angels of heaven' to go before Esau expands the canon's bare meeting of the angels of Elohim.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent three angels of the angels of heaven, and they went before Esau and came to him.
cards.t_text: And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of Elohim (God) met him.

cards.note: Genesis 32:12 — *And thou saidst, I will surely do thee good, and make thy seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.* Jasher 32:17's 'I will make your seed as the stars of heaven... in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed' is the covenant-seed oath the canon prayer leans on.
cards.s_text: I am Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of your father Abraham and the Elohim of Isaac, to you do I give this land and your seed after you, and I will make your seed as the stars of heaven, and you shall spread forth to the four sides of heaven, and in you and in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.
cards.t_text: And you saidst, I will surely do you good, and make your seed as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.

cards.note: Genesis 32:11 — *Deliver me, I pray thee, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.* Jasher 32:21's 'deliver me from the hands of my brother Esau, for I am greatly afraid of him' is the canon plea word for word.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, O Yahuah Elohim, deliver me, I pray you, also from the hands of my brother Esau, for I am greatly afraid of him.
cards.t_text: Deliver me, I pray you, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau: for I fear him, lest he will come and smite me, and the mother with the children.

cards.note: Genesis 32:9 — *And Jacob said, O Elohim (God) of my father Abraham, and Elohim (God) of my father Isaac, Yahuah (LORD) which saidst unto me, Return unto thy country, and to thy kindred, and I will deal well with thee.* Jasher 32:16's invocation of 'the Elohim of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac' is the canon prayer Jasher unfolds at length.
cards.s_text: And Jacob prayed to Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God), and he said, O Yahuah Elohim (O Lord God) of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac, you did say to me when I went away from my father’s house, saying,
cards.t_text: And Jacob said, O Elohim (God) of my father Abraham, and Elohim (God) of my father Isaac, Yahuah (LORD) which saidst unto me, Return unto your country, and to your kindred, and I will deal well with you:

cards.note: Genesis 32:7 — *Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands.* Jasher 32:15's 'Jacob was greatly afraid and he was distressed' and the two-camp division (Jasher 32:24) are the canon's same fear and division.
cards.s_text: And when he heard the words of his brother which he had spoken to the messengers of Jacob, Jacob was greatly afraid and he was distressed.
cards.t_text: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed: and he divided the people that was with him, and the flocks, and herds, and the camels, into two bands;

cards.note: Genesis 32:6 — *And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and also he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.* Jasher 32:13's returning messengers reporting Esau 'comes to meet you with four hundred men' is the canon's dread report unchanged.
cards.s_text: And the messengers returned and came to Jacob and said to him, We came to your brother, to Esau, and we told him all your words, and thus has he answered us, and behold he comes to meet you with four hundred men.
cards.t_text: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to your brother Esau, and also he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him.

cards.note: Genesis 32:5 — *And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and menservants, and womenservants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in thy sight.* Jasher 32:5's list of oxen, asses, cattle and servants 'to find favor in the sight of my Lord' is the same message Genesis records verbatim.
cards.s_text: And I afterward through Elohim’s great mercy and kindness acquired oxen and asses and cattle, and men servants and maid servants.
cards.t_text: And I have oxen, and asses, flocks, and menservants, and womenservants: and I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find grace in your sight.

cards.note: Genesis 32:3 — *And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the country of Edom.* Jasher 32:1's embassy 'toward the land of Seir' is the same canon sending to Esau in Edom.
cards.s_text: And at that time Jacob sent messengers to his brother Esau toward the land of Seir, and he spoke to him words of supplication.
cards.t_text: And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the country of Edom.

cards.note: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* The Levitical zeal that Jasher 33:52 calls 'from Yahuah' is the same zeal Numbers later vindicates in Phinehas of Levi's house.
cards.s_text: And they circumcised Shechem and Hamor his father, and the five brothers of Shechem, and then every one rose up and went home, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) against the city of Shechem, and from Yahuah (the Lord) was Simeon’s counsel in this matter, in order that Yahuah (the Lord) might deliver the city of Shechem into the hands of Jacob’s two sons.
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: Genesis 49:5 — *Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.* The two brothers who resolve to slay the city in Jasher 33:39 are the Simeon and Levi Jacob names together in his blessing.
cards.s_text: And Simeon’s advice pleased them, and Simeon and Levi resolved to do to them as it was proposed.
cards.t_text: Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.

cards.note: Genesis 49:7 — *Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel).* Jacob's blessing answers the slaughter of Jasher 33:52 with a curse on the brothers' fierce anger.
cards.s_text: And they circumcised Shechem and Hamor his father, and the five brothers of Shechem, and then every one rose up and went home, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) against the city of Shechem, and from Yahuah (the Lord) was Simeon’s counsel in this matter, in order that Yahuah (the Lord) might deliver the city of Shechem into the hands of Jacob’s two sons.
cards.t_text: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 30:18 — *And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar'el (Israel).* Jubilees reads Levi's resolve in Jasher 33:39 as the zeal that won him the priesthood.
cards.s_text: And Simeon’s advice pleased them, and Simeon and Levi resolved to do to them as it was proposed.
cards.t_text: And the seed of Levi was chosen for the priesthood, and to be Levites, that they might minister before Yahuah (God), as we, continually, and that Levi and his sons may be blessed for ever; for he was zealous to execute righteousness and judgment and vengeance on all those who arose against Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 30:6 — *And Yahuah (God) delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob that they might exterminate them with the sword and execute judgment upon them, and that it might not thus again be done in Yashar'el (Israel) that a virgin of Yashar'el (Israel) should be defiled.* Jubilees names the same hand that Jasher 33:52 names — Yahuah delivering Shechem into the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: And they circumcised Shechem and Hamor his father, and the five brothers of Shechem, and then every one rose up and went home, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) against the city of Shechem, and from Yahuah (the Lord) was Simeon’s counsel in this matter, in order that Yahuah (the Lord) might deliver the city of Shechem into the hands of Jacob’s two sons.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) delivered them into the hands of the sons of Jacob that they might exterminate them with the sword and execute judgment upon them, and that it might not thus again be done in Yashar’el (Israel) that a virgin of Yashar’el (Israel) should be defiled.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:5 — *And thus let it not again be done from henceforth that a daughter of Yashar'el (Israel) be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them that they should destroy with the sword all the men of the Shechemites because they had wrought shame in Yashar'el (Israel).* Jubilees draws from this scene the same standing judgment Jasher 33:34 invokes against the city.
cards.s_text: And when they had gone, the sons of Jacob said to their father, saying, Behold, we know that death is due to these wicked ones and to their city, because they transgressed that which Elohim (God) had commanded to Noah and his children and his seed after them.
cards.t_text: And thus let it not again be done from henceforth that a daughter of Yashar’el (Israel) be defiled; for judgment is ordained in heaven against them that they should destroy with the sword all the men of the Shechemites because they had wrought shame in Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 22:21 — *Then they shall bring out the damsel to the door of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones that she die: because she hath wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel), to play the whore in her father's house: so shalt thou put evil away from among you.* The Torah names sexual defilement folly in Israel, the same charge the brothers raise in Jasher 33:35.
cards.s_text: And also because Shechem did this thing to our sister Dinah in defiling her, for such vileness shall never be done amongst us.
cards.t_text: Then they shall bring out the damsel to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones that she die: because she has wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel), to play the whore in her father’s house: so shall you put evil away from among you.

cards.note: Genesis 34:7 — *And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob's daughter; which thing ought not to be done.* Jasher 33:35's 'such vileness shall never be done amongst us' is this same folly-in-Israel that ought not be done.
cards.s_text: And also because Shechem did this thing to our sister Dinah in defiling her, for such vileness shall never be done amongst us.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Jacob came out of the field when they heard it: and the men were grieved, and they were very wroth, because he had wrought folly in Yashar'el (Israel) in lying with Jacob’s daughter; which thing ought not to be done.

cards.note: Genesis 9:6 — *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man.* Jasher 33:21 grounds the death-verdict in this very charge that Yahuah commanded Noah and his children.
cards.s_text: And they came and sat before their father and they spoke to him kindled with wrath, saying, Surely death is due to this man and to his household, because Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of the whole earth commanded Noah and his children that man shall never rob, nor commit adultery; now behold Shechem has both ravaged and committed fornication with our sister, and not one of all the people of the city spoke a word to him.
cards.t_text: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The pretext in Jasher 33:44 rests on the Torah's standing separation of the seed from the nations.
cards.s_text: But herein will we consent to you, to give you our daughter, and we will also take to ourselves your daughters, and will dwell amongst you and be one people as you have spoken, if you will hearken to us, and consent to be like us, to circumcise every male belonging to you, as we are circumcised.
cards.t_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.

cards.note: Genesis 34:15 — *But in this will we consent unto you: If ye will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised;* Jasher 33:37 is Simeon's counsel to make them circumcise every male as the condition.
cards.s_text: And Simeon said to them, Here is a proper advice for you: tell them to circumcise every male amongst them as we are circumcised, and if they do not wish to do this, we shall take our daughter from them and go away.
cards.t_text: But in this will we consent unto you: If you will be as we be, that every male of you be circumcised;

cards.note: Genesis 34:14 — *And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us:* Jasher 33:43 echoes that giving the daughter to an uncircumcised man is a disgrace.
cards.s_text: Now we have made known to you all our ways that our father spoke to us, for we cannot do this of which you spoke to us, to give our daughter to an uncircumcised man, for it is a disgrace to us.
cards.t_text: And they said unto them, We cannot do this thing, to give our sister to one that is uncircumcised; for that were a reproach unto us:

cards.note: Genesis 34:13 — *And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister:* Jasher 33:29 has Simeon and Levi answering Hamor and Shechem deceitfully in the very same words.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi answered Hamor and Shechem his son deceitfully, saying, All you have spoken to us we will do for you.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully, and said, because he had defiled Dinah their sister:

cards.note: Jubilees 30:2 — *And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years.* Jubilees, like Jasher 33:11, has Dinah carried into Shechem's house and defiled.
cards.s_text: And he sent and had her taken by force, and Dinah came to the house of Shechem and he seized her forcibly and lay with her and humbled her, and he loved her exceedingly and placed her in his house.
cards.t_text: And there they carried off Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, into the house of Shechem, the son of Hamor, the Hivite, the prince of the land, and he lay with her and defiled her, and she was a little girl, a child of twelve years.

cards.note: Genesis 34:1 — *And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.* Jasher 33:6 has Dinah going out to see the daughters of the city, the very going-forth Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And Dinah the daughter of Jacob also went along with them and saw the daughters of the city, and they remained there before these daughters whilst all the people of the city were standing by them to behold their rejoicings, and all the great people of the city were there.
cards.t_text: And Dinah the daughter of Leah, which she bare unto Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

cards.note: Genesis 34:2 — *And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.* Jasher 33:11 expands the seizing and defiling of Dinah by Shechem the prince.
cards.s_text: And he sent and had her taken by force, and Dinah came to the house of Shechem and he seized her forcibly and lay with her and humbled her, and he loved her exceedingly and placed her in his house.
cards.t_text: And when Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, prince of the country, saw her, he took her, and lay with her, and defiled her.

cards.note: Genesis 34:3 — *And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.* Jasher 33:10's 'his soul became fixed upon Dinah' is the same clinging of Shechem's soul to her.
cards.s_text: And Shechem beheld Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and when he looked at her his soul became fixed upon Dinah.
cards.t_text: And his soul clave unto Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the damsel, and spake kindly unto the damsel.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:1 — *And in the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.* Jubilees fixes Jacob's coming to Shalem/Shechem in its calendar, the same scene Jasher 33:1 opens with.
cards.s_text: And in some time after Jacob went away from the borders of the land, and he came to the land of Shalem, that is the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, and he rested in front of the city.
cards.t_text: And in the first year of the sixth week he went up to Salem, to the east of Shechem, in peace, in the fourth month.

cards.note: Genesis 33:17 — *And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him an house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.* Jasher 33:3 names Succoth from the same booths Jacob made for his cattle.
cards.s_text: And Jacob there built himself a house, and he pitched his tent there, and he made booths for his cattle, therefore he called the name of that place Succoth.
cards.t_text: And Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built him an house, and made booths for his cattle: therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.

cards.note: Genesis 33:19 — *And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem's father, for an hundred pieces of money.* Jasher 33:2 retells the purchase of the field from the children of Hamor.
cards.s_text: And he bought a parcel of the field which was there, from the children of Hamor the people of the land, for five shekels.
cards.t_text: And he bought a parcel of a field, where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for an hundred pieces of money.

cards.note: Genesis 33:18 — *And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-aram; and pitched his tent before the city.* Jasher 33:1 is this same arrival at Shechem, resting before the city.
cards.s_text: And in some time after Jacob went away from the borders of the land, and he came to the land of Shalem, that is the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, and he rested in front of the city.
cards.t_text: And Jacob came to Shalem, a city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Padan-aram; and pitched his tent before the city.

cards.note: Genesis 48:22 — *Moreover I have given to thee one portion above thy brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.* Jacob's deathbed word recalls the very Amorite war of Jasher 34, the portion taken by the sword and bow Judah bids each man gird on (34:60).
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob and their servants went toward these kings, and they trusted in Yahuah their Elohim, and whilst they were going, Jacob their father also prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) and said, O Yahuah Elohim, powerful and exalted Elohim, who has reigned from days of old, from there till now and forever;
cards.t_text: Moreover I have given to you one portion above your brethren, which I took out of the hand of the Amorite with my sword and with my bow.

cards.note: Genesis 22:17 — *That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.* The sworn promise Isaac leans on in Jasher 34:65 even names the seed possessing the gate of its enemies — exactly the war at hand.
cards.s_text: And Isaac the son of Abraham prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) for his sons, and he said, O Yahuah (O Lord) Elohim, you did promise my father, saying, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and you did also promise me, and establish you your word, now that the kings of Canaan are coming together, to make war with my children because they committed no violence.
cards.t_text: That in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and your seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

cards.note: Genesis 15:5 — *And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if thou be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall thy seed be.* The 'seed as the stars of heaven' Isaac pleads in Jasher 34:65 is this word first spoken to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And Isaac the son of Abraham prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) for his sons, and he said, O Yahuah (O Lord) Elohim, you did promise my father, saying, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and you did also promise me, and establish you your word, now that the kings of Canaan are coming together, to make war with my children because they committed no violence.
cards.t_text: And he brought him forth abroad, and said, Look now toward heaven, and tell the stars, if you be able to number them: and he said unto him, So shall your seed be.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 20:15 — *And he said, Hearken ye, all Yahudah (Judah), and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but Elohim's (God’s).* Judah's call to cast away fear and trust Yahuah in Jasher 34:56 is the same word later spoken to all Judah.
cards.s_text: Now be tranquil about them and cast away your fears, but trust in Yahuah our Elohim (the Lord our God), and pray to him to assist us and deliver us, and deliver our enemies into our hands.
cards.t_text: And he said, Hearken you, all Yahudah (Judah), and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you king Jehoshaphat, Thus says Yahuah (LORD) unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but Elohim's (God’s).

cards.note: Joshua 2:9 — *And she said unto the men, I know that Yahuah (LORD) hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.* Rahab voices from the other side the very terror Judah trusts will fall on the kings in Jasher 34:55.
cards.s_text: Surely our Elohim who delivered into their hand the city of Shechem and its people, he will also deliver into our hands all the Canaanitish kings who are coming against us, and we will do to them as my brothers did to Shechem.
cards.t_text: And she said unto the men, I know that Yahuah (LORD) has given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 11:25 — *There shall no man be able to stand before you: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that ye shall tread upon, as he hath said unto you.* The dread Judah expects to fall on the Canaanite kings (Jasher 34:55) is the laid-on fear Moses promises the land.
cards.s_text: Surely our Elohim who delivered into their hand the city of Shechem and its people, he will also deliver into our hands all the Canaanitish kings who are coming against us, and we will do to them as my brothers did to Shechem.
cards.t_text: There shall no man be able to stand before you: for Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall lay the fear of you and the dread of you upon all the land that you shall tread upon, as he has said unto you.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 20:1 — *When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.* Judah's 'do not fear them' in Jasher 34:59-60 is the Torah's own war-law before the battle.
cards.s_text: Stand forth each man, girt with his weapons of war, his bow and his sword, and we will go and fight against these uncircumcised men; Yahuah (the Lord) is our Elohim, He will save us.
cards.t_text: When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, and chariots, and a people more than you, be not afraid of them: for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) is with you, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 23:27 — *I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.* The terror Judah counts on in Jasher 34:55-60 is the conquest-promise Yahuah will keep before Israel.
cards.s_text: Stand forth each man, girt with his weapons of war, his bow and his sword, and we will go and fight against these uncircumcised men; Yahuah (the Lord) is our Elohim, He will save us.
cards.t_text: I will send my fear before you, and will destroy all the people to whom you shall come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs unto you.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:26 — *And the dread of Yahuah (God) was upon all the cities which are around about Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue after the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them.* Jubilees turns the surrounding cities' terror into the same shield over the sons of Jacob that blunts the seven kings of Jasher 34:50.
cards.s_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled with all their armies, about ten thousand men with drawn swords, and they came to fight against the sons of Jacob; and Jacob heard that the kings of the Amorites had assembled to fight against his sons, and Jacob was greatly afraid, and it distressed him.
cards.t_text: And the dread of Yahuah (God) was upon all the cities which are around about Shechem, and they did not rise to pursue after the sons of Jacob; for terror had fallen upon them.

cards.note: Genesis 35:5 — *And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.* The canon's reason the gathered Amorite kings of Jasher 34:50 never overrun Jacob's household — the dread of Elohim guards the seed.
cards.s_text: And the seven kings of the Amorites assembled with all their armies, about ten thousand men with drawn swords, and they came to fight against the sons of Jacob; and Jacob heard that the kings of the Amorites had assembled to fight against his sons, and Jacob was greatly afraid, and it distressed him.
cards.t_text: And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:25 — *And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword; for he feared those who dwelt in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.* Jacob's reproach and fear of the Canaanites and Perizzites in Jasher 34:33 stands word-for-word in Jubilees.
cards.s_text: And now you have done to make me obnoxious to the inhabitants of the land, amongst the Canaanites and the Perizzites, and I am but of a small number, and they will all assemble against me and slay me when they hear of your work with their brethren, and I and my household will be destroyed.
cards.t_text: And he reproached them because they had put the city to the sword; for he feared those who dwelt in the land, the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

cards.note: Jubilees 30:24 — *And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father.* The same flocks and captives Jasher 34:31 leads home to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And they took away their sheep and their oxen and their cattle, and also the remainder of the women and little ones, and they led all these away, and they opened a gate and went out and came to their father Jacob with vigor.
cards.t_text: And they brought Dinah, their sister, out of the house of Shechem, and they took captive everything that was in Shechem, their sheep and their oxen and their asses, and all their wealth, and all their flocks, and brought them all to Jacob their father.

cards.note: Genesis 34:30 — *And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, Ye have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.* Jacob's fear in Jasher 34:33 — few in number, the land assembling — is this canon verse retold.
cards.s_text: And now you have done to make me obnoxious to the inhabitants of the land, amongst the Canaanites and the Perizzites, and I am but of a small number, and they will all assemble against me and slay me when they hear of your work with their brethren, and I and my household will be destroyed.
cards.t_text: And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, You have troubled me to make me to stink among the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites: and I being few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me, and slay me; and I shall be destroyed, I and my house.

cards.note: Genesis 34:28 — *They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field.* The catalogue of spoil Jasher 34:31 leads out of the gate is Moses' own list.
cards.s_text: And they took away their sheep and their oxen and their cattle, and also the remainder of the women and little ones, and they led all these away, and they opened a gate and went out and came to their father Jacob with vigor.
cards.t_text: They took their sheep, and their oxen, and their asses, and that which was in the city, and that which was in the field,

cards.note: Jubilees 30:4 — *And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah.* The same scene Jasher 34:25 tells, read in Jubilees as judgment for the defiled seed.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi continued to go about in the city, and they killed all the people of the city at the edge of the sword, and they left none remaining.
cards.t_text: And Simeon and Levi came unexpectedly to Shechem and executed judgment on all the men of Shechem, and slew all the men whom they found in it, and left not a single one remaining in it: they slew all in torments because they had dishonoured their sister Dinah.

cards.note: Genesis 49:5 — *Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.* Jacob's later blessing-oracle names the very zeal Jasher 34:23 records as an oath.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi swore and said, As Yahuah (the Lord) lives, the Elohim (God) of the whole earth, by this time tomorrow, there shall not be a remnant left in the whole city.
cards.t_text: Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.

cards.note: Genesis 34:31 — *And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?* The brothers' closing retort in Jasher 34:34 quotes this canon line almost exactly — the defilement of the covenant seed is the grievance.
cards.s_text: And Simeon and Levi and all their brothers with them answered their father Jacob and said to him, Behold we live in the land, and shall Shechem do this to our sister? why are you silent at all that Shechem has done? and shall he deal with our sister as with a harlot in the streets?
cards.t_text: And they said, Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?

cards.note: Genesis 34:26 — *And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went out.* The same two deaths and the same rescue of Dinah stand word-for-word behind Jasher 34:28.
cards.s_text: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son at the edge of the sword, and they brought away Dinah from the house of Shechem and they went from there.
cards.t_text: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went out.

cards.note: Genesis 34:25 — *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* Moses' verse is the bare event Jasher 34:23-28 expands into the oath, the hidden young men, and the house-to-house sweep.
cards.s_text: And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son at the edge of the sword, and they brought away Dinah from the house of Shechem and they went from there.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

cards.note: Genesis 35:5 — *And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.* That the kings' restraint proceeded from Yahuah in Jasher 35:24 is the canon's same statement that the terror of Elohim, not the sons' strength, stayed the cities.
cards.s_text: For this proceeded from Yahuah (the Lord) to them, for he heard the prayers of his servants Isaac and Jacob, for they trusted in him; and all these kings returned with their camps on that day, each to his own city, and they did not at that time fight with the sons of Jacob.
cards.t_text: And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

cards.note: Joshua 2:9 — *And she said unto the men, I know that Yahuah (LORD) hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.* The Amorite kings' melting hearts in Jasher 35:23 are Rahab's confession in advance — the inhabitants faint before the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And the kings turned and refrained from the sons of Jacob, for they durst not approach them to make war with them, for they were greatly afraid of them, and their hearts melted within them from their fear of them.
cards.t_text: And she said unto the men, I know that Yahuah (LORD) has given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.

cards.note: Exodus 23:27 — *I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.* The kings warring against Israel's Elohim in Jasher 35:19 face the very dread Yahuah promises to send before His people.
cards.s_text: Surely you know and understand that you do not come to fight with them, but you come to war with their Elohim who made choice of them, and you have therefore all come this day to be destroyed.
cards.t_text: I will send my fear before you, and will destroy all the people to whom you shall come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs unto you.

cards.note: Genesis 33:1 — *And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.* The deliverance from Esau's hand that Jasher 35:15 cites is the canon's encounter where the four hundred do no harm.
cards.s_text: And he went to meet him when he came from Syria, to smite the mother with the children, and who delivered him from his hands but his Elohim in whom he trusted? he delivered him from the hand of his brother and also from the hands of his enemies, and surely he again will protect them.
cards.t_text: And Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau came, and with him four hundred men. And he divided the children unto Leah, and unto Rachel, and unto the two handmaids.

cards.note: Genesis 32:6 — *And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to thy brother Esau, and also he cometh to meet thee, and four hundred men with him.* The four hundred men coming with Esau in Jasher 35:14 is the canon's own report to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And behold, we ourselves saw with our eyes that Esau, the brother of Jacob, came to him with four hundred men, with the intention of slaying him, for he called to mind that he had taken away from him his father’s blessing.
cards.t_text: And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying, We came to your brother Esau, and also he comes to meet you, and four hundred men with him.

cards.note: Genesis 20:17 — *So Abraham prayed unto Elohim (God): and Elohim (God) healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bare children.* The judgment on Abimelech's people that Jasher 35:13 alludes to is the canon's affliction lifted only by Abraham's prayer.
cards.s_text: And have you not heard what their Elohim did to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to Abimelech king of Gerar, through taking Abraham’s wife, who said of her, She is my sister, lest they might slay him on account of her, and think of taking her for a wife? and Elohim did to them and their people all that you heard of.
cards.t_text: So Abraham prayed unto Elohim (God): and Elohim (God) healed Abimelech, and his wife, and his maidservants; and they bare children.

cards.note: Genesis 20:2 — *And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.* The 'she is my sister' and the king of Gerar named in Jasher 35:13 are taken straight from Genesis.
cards.s_text: And have you not heard what their Elohim did to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to Abimelech king of Gerar, through taking Abraham’s wife, who said of her, She is my sister, lest they might slay him on account of her, and think of taking her for a wife? and Elohim did to them and their people all that you heard of.
cards.t_text: And Abraham said of Sarah his wife, She is my sister: and Abimelech king of Gerar sent, and took Sarah.

cards.note: Genesis 12:17 — *And Yahuah (LORD) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram's wife.* Jasher 35:13's memory of what Elohim did to Pharaoh over Abraham's wife is the canon's plague-judgment on Egypt's house.
cards.s_text: And have you not heard what their Elohim did to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to Abimelech king of Gerar, through taking Abraham’s wife, who said of her, She is my sister, lest they might slay him on account of her, and think of taking her for a wife? and Elohim did to them and their people all that you heard of.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.

cards.note: Jubilees 17:16 — *And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before Elohim (God), "Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything wherein You do try him."* Jasher 35:11's love-driven offering of the only son is the same trial Jubilees frames as the testing of Abraham's faithfulness.
cards.s_text: And behold through his love toward his Elohim, Abraham took his only and precious son and intended to bring him up as a burnt offering to his Elohim, and had it not been for Elohim who prevented him from doing this, he would then have done it through his love to his Elohim.
cards.t_text: And the prince Mastêmâ came and said before Elohim (God), “Behold, Abraham loves Isaac his son, and he delights in him above all things else; bid him offer him as a burnt-offering on the altar, and You will see if he will do this command, and You will know if he is faithful in everything wherein You do try him.”

cards.note: Genesis 22:17 — *That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies.* The promise to deliver Abraham's seed from every trouble in Jasher 35:12 is the canon's sworn blessing on the akedah.
cards.s_text: And Elohim saw all his works, and swore to him, and promised him that he would deliver his sons and all his seed from every trouble that would befall them, because he had done this thing, and through his love to his Elohim stifled his compassion for his child.
cards.t_text: That in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and your seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

cards.note: Genesis 22:12 — *And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest Elohim (God), seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.* Jasher 35:11's note that Elohim prevented the offering matches the canon's stayed hand and tested fear of Elohim.
cards.s_text: And behold through his love toward his Elohim, Abraham took his only and precious son and intended to bring him up as a burnt offering to his Elohim, and had it not been for Elohim who prevented him from doing this, he would then have done it through his love to his Elohim.
cards.t_text: And he said, Lay not your hand upon the lad, neither do you any thing unto him: for now I know that you fearest Elohim (God), seeing you have not withheld your son, your only son from me.

cards.note: Genesis 14:16 — *And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.* Jasher 35:8-9 names the rescued kinsman in Sodom and his restored property exactly as Genesis records of Lot.
cards.s_text: And who else can do the like? surely it was Abraham who slew the five kings of Elam, when they had touched his brother’s son who in those days dwelt in Sodom.
cards.t_text: And he brought back all the goods, and also brought again his brother Lot, and his goods, and the women also, and the people.

cards.note: Genesis 14:14 — *And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.* The few faithful men of Abraham's house pursuing by night in Jasher 35:9 is the canon's own account of the war on the kings.
cards.s_text: And took his servant that was faithful in his house and a few of his men, and they pursued the kings of Elam in one night and killed them, and restored to his brother’s son all his property which they had taken from him.
cards.t_text: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* The canon frames Abraham's call as the seed drawn out of Nimrod's idolatry that Jasher 35:6 recalls.
cards.s_text: Surely he delivered their father Abraham, the Hebrew, from the hand of Nimrod, and from the hand of all his people who had many times sought to slay him.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Jasher 12:24 — *And Yahuah (the Lord) loved Abram and he had compassion over him, and Yahuah (the Lord) came down and delivered Abram from the fire and he was not burned.* The deliverance the counsellors cite in Jasher 35:7 is the very rescue Jasher's own earlier chapter narrates.
cards.s_text: He delivered him also from the fire in which king Nimrod had cast him, and his Elohim delivered him from it.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) loved Abram and he had compassion over him, and Yahuah (the Lord) came down and delivered Abram from the fire and he was not burned.

cards.note: Exodus 23:27 — *I will send my fear before thee, and will destroy all the people to whom thou shalt come, and I will make all thine enemies turn their backs unto thee.* The fear Yahuah pours into the kings' advisers in Jasher 35:2 is the same covenant weapon He promises Israel.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the prayers of Isaac and Jacob, and he filled the hearts of all these kings’ advisers with great fear and terror that they unanimously exclaimed,
cards.t_text: I will send my fear before you, and will destroy all the people to whom you shall come, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs unto you.

cards.note: Genesis 35:5 — *And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.* The canon supplies exactly the dread Jasher 35:1-2 narrates the Amorite kings consulting under — the cities round about do not pursue.
cards.s_text: And all the kings of the Amorites came and took their stand in the field to consult with their counsellors what was to be done with the sons of Jacob, for they were still afraid of them, saying, Behold, two of them slew the whole of the city of Shechem.
cards.t_text: And they journeyed: and the terror of Elohim (God) was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 35:1 — *And Elohim (God) said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto Elohim (God), that appeared unto thee when thou fleddest from the face of Esau thy brother.* The canon command Jasher 36:1 retells word for word.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) said unto Jacob, Arise, go up to Beth-el, and dwell there: and make there an altar unto Elohim (God), that appeared unto you when you fleddest from the face of Esau your brother.

cards.note: Genesis 35:6 — *So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Beth-el, he and all the people that were with him.* The same Luz/Bethel arrival where Jasher 36:3 has Jacob remain six months.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was ninety-nine years old when he went up to Bethel, and Jacob and his sons and all the people that were with him, remained in Bethel in Luz, and he there built an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appeared to him, and Jacob and his sons remained in Bethel six months.
cards.t_text: So Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan, that is, Beth-el, he and all the people that were with him.

cards.note: Genesis 35:7 — *And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el: because there Elohim (God) appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.* The altar Jasher 36:3 records Jacob building to Yahuah who appeared to him.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was ninety-nine years old when he went up to Bethel, and Jacob and his sons and all the people that were with him, remained in Bethel in Luz, and he there built an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appeared to him, and Jacob and his sons remained in Bethel six months.
cards.t_text: And he built there an altar, and called the place El-beth-el: because there Elohim (God) appeared unto him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

cards.note: *And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed Yahuah (God).* (Jubilees 32:1). *At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.* (Jasher 36:1). Jasher records the command to go up to Bethel and build an altar to the One who delivered him; Jubilees records what happened the night Jacob was there: Levi dreamed he had been ordained priest of the Most High, he and his sons for ever, and woke and blessed Yahuah (God). The altar Jacob was sent to build needed a priesthood, and the priesthood was given at Bethel in a dream long before Sinai named Levi. Jasher gives the summons to Bethel and Jubilees gives what Bethel produced.
cards.s_text: At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to Jacob saying, Arise, go to Bethel and remain there, and make there an altar to Yahuah (the Lord) who appears to you, who delivered you and your sons from affliction.
cards.t_text: And he abode that night at Bethel, and Levi dreamed that they had ordained and made him the priest of the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), him and his sons for ever; and he awoke from his sleep and blessed Yahuah (God).

cards.note: Genesis 35:8 — *But Deborah Rebekah's nurse died, and she was buried beneath Beth-el under an oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bachuth.* The same nurse, oak and name Jasher 36:4,6 retells.
cards.s_text: At that time died Deborah the daughter of Uz, the nurse of Rebecca, who had been with Jacob; and Jacob buried her beneath Bethel under an oak that was there.
cards.t_text: But Deborah Rebekah’s nurse died, and she was buried beneath Beth-el under an oak: and the name of it was called Allon-bachuth.

cards.note: *And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, “The river of Deborah,” and the oak, “The oak of the mourning of Deborah.”* (Jubilees 32:30). *And the life of Rebecca was one hundred and thirty-three years, and she died and when Jacob heard that his mother Rebecca was dead he wept bitterly for his mother, and made a great mourning for her, and for Deborah her nurse beneath the oak, and he called the name of that place Allon-bachuth.* (Jasher 36:6). Both books bury Deborah, Rebecca's nurse, under an oak and name the place for the mourning. Jubilees dates it to the twenty-third of the month and gives the names, the river of Deborah and the oak of the mourning of Deborah; Jasher calls the oak Allon-bachuth and sets it beside Jacob's weeping for his mother Rebecca, dead at a hundred and thirty-three. A nurse received a named oak and a dated grave. The books remembered the servants, not only the patriarchs.
cards.s_text: And the life of Rebecca was one hundred and thirty-three years, and she died and when Jacob heard that his mother Rebecca was dead he wept bitterly for his mother, and made a great mourning for her, and for Deborah her nurse beneath the oak, and he called the name of that place Allon-bachuth.
cards.t_text: And in the night, on the twenty-third of this month, Deborah Rebecca’s nurse died, and they buried her beneath the city under the oak of the river, and he called the name of this place, “The river of Deborah,” and the oak, “The oak of the mourning of Deborah.”

cards.note: Genesis 35:10 — *Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Yashar'el (Israel) shall be thy name: and he called his name Yashar'el (Israel).* The renaming Jasher 36:8 records as the hundred-year-old Jacob being blessed and called Israel.
