cards.note: Matthew 26:15 — *And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.* The brother bartered for silver in Jasher 42:24 prefigures the greater Joseph delivered up for thirty — the Messiah-type sold by his own.
cards.s_text: And they did so, and they reached the Ishmaelites, and the Midianites sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver which they had given for him to his brethren.
cards.t_text: And said unto them, What will you give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.

cards.note: Psalm 105:17 — *He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:* The pit-cry of Jasher 42:6 read as Yahuah sending Joseph ahead — the affliction is the errand.
cards.s_text: And these Midianites ran to the pit to drink water, for they thought that it contained water, and on coming before the pit they heard the voice of Joseph crying and weeping in the pit, and they looked down into the pit, and they saw and behold there was a youth of comely appearance and well favored.
cards.t_text: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The brethren's disposal of Joseph in Jasher 42:4 is later named the means by which much people were kept alive — the Messiah-type who saves those who sold him.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, come let us dispose of him to them, and let not our hand be upon him, and they will lead him along with them, and he will be lost amongst the people of the land, and we will not put him to death with our own hands. And the proposal pleased his brethren and they did according to the word of Judah.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,* Stephen reads the sale Jasher 42:3 narrates as the brethren's envy overruled by the God who stayed with the rejected one.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to them, What gain will it be to us if we slay our brother? peradventure Elohim (God) will require him from us; this then is the counsel proposed concerning him, which you shall do to him: Behold this company of Ishmaelites going down to Egypt,
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Genesis 37:27 — *Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.* The very 'let not our hand be upon him' counsel that Jasher 42:4 records the brethren accepting at Judah's word.
cards.s_text: Now therefore, come let us dispose of him to them, and let not our hand be upon him, and they will lead him along with them, and he will be lost amongst the people of the land, and we will not put him to death with our own hands. And the proposal pleased his brethren and they did according to the word of Judah.
cards.t_text: Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.

cards.note: Genesis 37:26 — *And Yahudah (Judah) said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?* The canon's terse line that Jasher 42:3 expands into Judah's full speech against shedding a brother's blood.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to them, What gain will it be to us if we slay our brother? peradventure Elohim (God) will require him from us; this then is the counsel proposed concerning him, which you shall do to him: Behold this company of Ishmaelites going down to Egypt,
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?

cards.note: Hebrews 11:22 — *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* The long mourning of Jasher 43:48 gives way to Joseph's faith in the coming departure of Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was still crying aloud and weeping for Joseph day after day, and he mourned for his son many days.
cards.t_text: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.

cards.note: Genesis 50:24 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.* The son mourned as lost in Jasher 43:48 will live to pledge the visitation and the sworn inheritance.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was still crying aloud and weeping for Joseph day after day, and he mourned for his son many days.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

cards.note: Romans 8:28 — *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.* The persecuted-righteous pattern of Jasher 43:42 is the gospel's own promise of all things working for good.
cards.s_text: And you did devour my son for naught, because he committed no violence, and did thereby render me culpable on his account, therefore Elohim will require him that is persecuted.
cards.t_text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The innocent blood required in Jasher 43:42 is the evil Elohim turns to good to save much people alive.
cards.s_text: And you did devour my son for naught, because he committed no violence, and did thereby render me culpable on his account, therefore Elohim will require him that is persecuted.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Genesis 45:5 — *Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.* The persecuted son of Jasher 43:42 becomes the deliverer who reads the crime as Elohim's sending.
cards.s_text: And you did devour my son for naught, because he committed no violence, and did thereby render me culpable on his account, therefore Elohim will require him that is persecuted.
cards.t_text: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him.* Stephen names the envy behind the crime Jasher 43:42 grieves — Joseph the innocent kept by Elohim.
cards.s_text: And you did devour my son for naught, because he committed no violence, and did thereby render me culpable on his account, therefore Elohim will require him that is persecuted.
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Hebrews 11:21 — *By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.* The father whose head Yahudah lifts in Jasher 43:32 will yet bless the seed in faith.
cards.s_text: And Judah rose up and lifted his father’s head from the ground, and placed it upon his lap, and he wiped his father’s tears from his cheeks, and Judah wept an exceeding great weeping, whilst his father’s head was reclining upon his lap, still as a stone.
cards.t_text: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The Shiloh-Messianic sceptre rests on the very Yahudah who comforts his father in Jasher 43:32.
cards.s_text: And Judah rose up and lifted his father’s head from the ground, and placed it upon his lap, and he wiped his father’s tears from his cheeks, and Judah wept an exceeding great weeping, whilst his father’s head was reclining upon his lap, still as a stone.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.* Jasher 43:32 lifts up Yahudah to bear the father's head — the brother the blessing will exalt.
cards.s_text: And Judah rose up and lifted his father’s head from the ground, and placed it upon his lap, and he wiped his father’s tears from his cheeks, and Judah wept an exceeding great weeping, whilst his father’s head was reclining upon his lap, still as a stone.

cards.note: Jubilees 34:18 — *For this reason it is ordained for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month–on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father–that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son.* Jubilees binds the kid's blood of Jasher 43:13 to the Day of Atonement — Torah and the appointed times stand, it ain't new.
cards.s_text: And they hastened and took Joseph’s coat and tore it, and they killed a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in the blood of the kid, and then trampled it in the dust, and they sent the coat to their father Jacob by the hand of Naphtali, and they commanded him to say these words:
cards.t_text: For this reason it is ordained for the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that they should afflict themselves on the tenth of the seventh month–on the day that the news which made him weep for Joseph came to Jacob his father–that they should make atonement for themselves thereon with a young goat on the tenth of the seventh month, once a year, for their sins; for they had grieved the affection of their father regarding Joseph his son.

cards.note: *And they dealt treacherously with him, and formed a plot against him to slay him, but changing their minds, they sold him to Ishmaelite merchants, and they brought him down into Egypt, and they sold him to Potiphar, the eunuch of Pharaoh, the chief of the cooks, priest of the city of ’Êlêw. And the sons of Jacob slaughtered a kid, and dipped the coat of Joseph in the blood, and sent (it) to Jacob their father on the tenth of the seventh month.* (Jubilees 34:11–12). *And they hastened and took Joseph’s coat and tore it, and they killed a kid of the goats and dipped the coat in the blood of the kid, and then trampled it in the dust, and they sent the coat to their father Jacob by the hand of Naphtali, and they commanded him to say these words:* (Jasher 43:13). Jubilees folds the whole betrayal into two breaths: the plot to kill him, the change of heart, the sale to the Ishmaelites, the house of Potiphar, and then the kid slaughtered and the coat dipped in its blood and sent to Jacob. Jasher opens that second moment wider, the coat torn, the blood of the kid, the coat trampled in the dust and carried to their father by the hand of Naphtali with words the brothers put in his mouth. Both witnesses agree on the order: the sale came first, and the blood on the coat was a lie told afterward to cover it. Jubilees even dates the lie, the tenth of the seventh month, and goes on to say that this is why Yashar'el (Israel) afflicts itself on that day each year; the day a kid's blood was sent to deceive a father became the day of atonement.

cards.note: *And the Egyptian saw the garment of Joseph and the broken door, and heard the words of his wife, and cast Joseph into prison into the place where the prisoners were kept whom the king imprisoned. And he was there in the prison; and Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour in the sight of the chief of the prison guards and compassion before him, for he saw that Yahuah (God) was with him, and that Yahuah (God) made all that he did to prosper.* (Jubilees 39:11–12). *And Potiphar heard their words, and he placed him in the prison house, the place where the king’s prisoners are confined, and Joseph was in the house of confinement twelve years.* (Jasher 44:76). Both witnesses put Joseph in the same place, not a common jail but the prison where the king's own prisoners were kept, and Jasher adds that he was there twelve years. Jubilees adds what Jasher's one line does not, that Yahuah (God) was with him inside the prison, giving him favour with the chief of the guards and prospering everything he did. A master's anger chose the place, yet it was the one prison where Pharaoh's butler and baker would be sent, the only prison from which a road ran to the throne. Twelve years is a long time to be favoured in a cell, but the favour inside the walls was the same favour that would open them.
cards.s_text: And Potiphar heard their words, and he placed him in the prison house, the place where the king’s prisoners are confined, and Joseph was in the house of confinement twelve years.

cards.note: Genesis 39:20 — *And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.* Jasher 44:76 names the same 'house of confinement, the place where the king's prisoners are confined.'

cards.note: *And Joseph was afraid of her at her doing this thing, and he rose up to flee from her, and she seized the front of his garments, and in the terror of his flight the garment which Zelicah seized was torn, and Joseph left the garment in the hand of Zelicah, and he fled and got out, for he was in fear.* (Jasher 44:54). *But she embraced him and held him fast in the house in order to force him to lie with her, and closed the doors of the house and held him fast; but he left his garment in her hands and broke through the door and fled without from her presence.* (Jubilees 39:9). Jubilees and Jasher keep the same ending to the same scene: the garment left in her hands and Joseph fleeing from her presence. Jubilees has her close the doors and hold him fast until he breaks through and runs; Jasher has her seize the front of his garments so that it tears in the terror of his flight. Both put the torn garment in her hand, which is the very thing she will turn into a false witness against him in the verses that follow. The evidence of his innocence becomes the tool of his accusation.

cards.note: 1 Corinthians 6:18 — *Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.* Joseph's flat refusal to sin against Elohim in Jasher 44:45 is the very flight Paul commands the assembly.
cards.s_text: For he has also greatly honored me in his house, and he has also made me overseer over his house, and he has exalted me, and there is no one greater in this house than I am, and my master has refrained nothing from me, excepting you who are his wife, how then can you speak these words to me, and how can I do this great evil and sin to Elohim and to your husband?
cards.t_text: Flee fornication. Every sin that a man does is without the body; but he that commits fornication sins against his own body.

cards.note: *But he did not surrender his soul, and he remembered Yahuah (God) and the words which Jacob, his father, used to read from amongst the words of Abraham, that no man should commit fornication with a woman who has a husband; that for him the punishment of death has been ordained in the heavens before the El Elyon (Most High) Elohim (God), and the sin will be recorded against him in the eternal books continually before Yahuah (God). And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.* (Jubilees 39:6–7). *And Joseph answered her, saying, It is better for me to remain in this house than to hearken to your words, to sin against Elohim; and she said to him, If you will not perform my wish, I will pluck out your eyes, add fetters to your feet, and will deliver you into the hands of them whom you did not know before.* (Jasher 44:78). Joseph's refusal did not come out of nowhere. Jubilees says he remembered the words of Abraham that his father Jacob used to read aloud, that a man who takes another man's wife has a death sentence written against him in heaven and a sin recorded in the eternal books, and because he remembered he refused. Jasher gives the same refusal in Joseph's own mouth, that he would rather stay in the house than sin against Elohim (God), and it cost him the threat of his eyes and fetters. Adultery was sin in Egypt long before there was a mountain called Sinai, because the commandment was older than the stone it was later written on. Joseph kept Torah because his fathers had kept it and read it to him.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.* (Jasher 44:12). *And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.* (Genesis 39:5). Jasher retells the Genesis verse in a sentence: Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph, he prospered, and the house of Potiphar was blessed for his sake. Genesis spells out the reach of it, upon all that Potiphar had in the house and in the field, from the day Joseph was made overseer. The blessing does not stop at the man Yahuah (the Lord) is with; it spills over onto the house that holds him, even the house of a stranger that holds him as a slave.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) was with Joseph and he became a prosperous man, and Yahuah (the Lord) blessed the house of Potiphar for the sake of Joseph.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass from the time that he had made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, that Yahuah (LORD) blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of Yahuah (LORD) was upon all that he had in the house, and in the field.

cards.note: Genesis 39:2 — *And Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.* Jasher 44:12 quotes the canon's own claim that Yahuah was with the sold-away son.

cards.note: *And he set Joseph over all his house, and the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the house of the Egyptian on account of Joseph, and Yahuah (God) prospered him in all that he did.* (Jubilees 39:3). *And Potiphar took Joseph and brought him to his house that he might serve him, and Joseph found favor in the sight of Potiphar, and he placed confidence in him, and made him overseer over his house, and all that belonged to him he delivered over into his hand.* (Jasher 44:11). Jasher tells how Joseph came into Potiphar's house and found favour there until he was made overseer and everything was put in his hand. Jubilees tells what that meant for the house: the blessing of Yahuah (God) came upon the Egyptian's household on Joseph's account, and everything Potiphar did prospered. A slave sold out of Canaan carried the blessing of Abraham's house into a stranger's house, which is the promise to Abraham working in miniature, that in his seed the families of the earth would be blessed. Potiphar was blessed for the sake of the man he owned.

cards.note: Numbers 26:20 — *And the sons of Yahudah (Judah) after their families were; of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites: of Pharez, the family of the Pharzites: of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites.* The census enrolls Shelah, Perez and Zarah as the families of Judah, the sons named across Jasher 45:27-32.
cards.s_text: And when Onan died, Judah said to Tamar, Remain in your father’s house until my son Shiloh shall have grown up, and Judah did no more delight in Tamar, to give her to Shiloh, for he said, Peradventure he will also die like his brothers.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Yahudah (Judah) after their families were; of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites: of Pharez, the family of the Pharzites: of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites.

cards.note: Matthew 1:3 — *And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram.* The Messiah's genealogy names Tamar and the twins Perez and Zarah of Jasher 45:32 in the royal line of Judah.
cards.s_text: And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.
cards.t_text: And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;

cards.note: Ruth 4:12 — *And let thy house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Yahudah (Judah), of the seed which Yahuah (LORD) shall give thee of this young woman.* Bethlehem blesses Boaz by the very house of Perez that Tamar bears at the close of Jasher 45:32, the line that runs to David.
cards.s_text: And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.
cards.t_text: And let your house be like the house of Pharez, whom Tamar bare unto Yahudah (Judah), of the seed which Yahuah (LORD) shall give you of this young woman.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The Perez born in Jasher 45:32 carries the sceptre of Judah toward the promised Shiloh.
cards.s_text: And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: *And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged, and said: “Tamar is more righteous than I am. And therefore let them burn her not.”* (Jubilees 41:19). *And Tamar rose up and put off the garments of her widowhood, and she put a vail upon her, and she entirely covered herself, and she went and sat in the public thoroughfare, which is upon the road to Timnah.* (Jasher 45:31). These two verses are the beginning and the end of one story. Jasher shows Tamar putting off her widow's garments, veiling herself and sitting on the road to Timnah; Jubilees shows Yahudah (Judah) at the end of it, confessing that she is more righteous than he and refusing to let her be burned. She was not on that road for harlotry. The seed of her dead husband's house was owed to her, Yahudah (Judah) had withheld Shelah, and she went and claimed what Torah gave her by the only door left open. When he saw the pledge he owned it, and the line that runs to Messiah (Christ) passes through the son she bore him.
cards.s_text: And Tamar rose up and put off the garments of her widowhood, and she put a vail upon her, and she entirely covered herself, and she went and sat in the public thoroughfare, which is upon the road to Timnah.
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged, and said: “Tamar is more righteous than I am. And therefore let them burn her not.”

cards.note: Genesis 38:27 — *And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.* Genesis records the twin birth Jasher 45:32 names as Perez and Zarah.
cards.s_text: And Judah passed and saw her and took her and he came to her, and she conceived by him, and at the time of being delivered, behold, there were twins in her womb, and he called the name of the first Perez, and the name of the second Zarah.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the time of her travail, that, behold, twins were in her womb.

cards.note: Genesis 38:14 — *And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.* Genesis gives the veiling at the Timnath road that Jasher 45:31 retells almost word for word.
cards.s_text: And Tamar rose up and put off the garments of her widowhood, and she put a vail upon her, and she entirely covered herself, and she went and sat in the public thoroughfare, which is upon the road to Timnah.
cards.t_text: And she put her widow’s garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.

cards.note: Numbers 26:19 — *The sons of Yahudah (Judah) were Er and Onan: and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.* The wilderness census remembers the deaths Jasher 45:24-26 narrates, the two sons of Judah who perished in Canaan.
cards.s_text: And Er came to his wife Tamar, and she became his wife, and when he came to her he outwardly destroyed his seed, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and Yahuah (the Lord) slew him.
cards.t_text: The sons of Yahudah (Judah) were Er and Onan: and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: *And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother’s only, and he went into the house of his brother’s wife, and spilt the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him.* (Jubilees 41:5). *And Onan took Tamar for a wife and he came to her, and Onan also did like to the work of his brother, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he slew him also.* (Jasher 45:26). Both witnesses say the same thing in almost the same words: Onan's work was evil in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him. Jubilees tells why it was evil. Onan knew the seed would not be counted his but his dead brother's, and he spilled it on the ground rather than raise a name for his brother. Jasher adds only that he did as his brother had done, which is to say the house of Yahudah (Judah) lost two sons to the same refusal. The judgment did not fall on lust; it fell on a man who took his brother's wife and would not give his brother a seed.
cards.s_text: And Onan took Tamar for a wife and he came to her, and Onan also did like to the work of his brother, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he slew him also.
cards.t_text: And Onan knew that the seed would not be his, (but) his brother’s only, and he went into the house of his brother’s wife, and spilt the seed on the ground, and he was wicked in the eyes of Yahuah (God), and He slew him.

cards.note: Genesis 38:7 — *And Er, Yahudah's (Judah's) firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) slew him.* Genesis records the death of Er that Jasher 45:24 narrates word for word, Judah's evil firstborn slain by Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And Er came to his wife Tamar, and she became his wife, and when he came to her he outwardly destroyed his seed, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and Yahuah (the Lord) slew him.
cards.t_text: And Er, Yahudah's (Judah’s) firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) slew him.

cards.note: Genesis 38:9 — *And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.* Genesis gives the very deed Jasher 45:26 calls 'the work of his brother,' for which Yahuah slew Onan.
cards.s_text: And Onan took Tamar for a wife and he came to her, and Onan also did like to the work of his brother, and his work was evil in the sight of Yahuah (the Lord), and he slew him also.
cards.t_text: And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother’s wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.

cards.note: Genesis 46:23 — *And the sons of Dan; Hushim.* Genesis records Dan's single son, the very child Jasher 45:8 says Elohim gave the barren Aphlaleth when He remembered her.
cards.s_text: And Aphlaleth was barren, she had no offspring, and Elohim (God) afterward remembered Aphlaleth the wife of Dan, and she conceived and bare a son, and she called his name Chushim.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Dan; Hushim.

cards.note: Exodus 1:1 — *Now these are the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.* Exodus reopens with the same households Jasher 45 has just enumerated, the twelve tribes about to become a nation.
cards.s_text: And Eliuram the wife of Reuben conceived and bare him Hanoch, Palu, Chetzron and Carmi, four sons; and Simeon his brother took his sister Dinah for a wife, and she bare to him Memuel, Yamin, Ohad, Jachin and Zochar, five sons.
cards.t_text: Now these are the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 46:27 — *And the sons of Joseph, which were born him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.* The household whose offspring Jasher 45 itemizes is the seventy souls Genesis numbers going down into Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Aridah bare to Issachar Tola, Puvah, Job and Shomron, four sons; and Dan went to the land of Moab and took for a wife Aphlaleth, the daughter of Chamudan the Moabite, and he brought her to the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Joseph, which were born him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.

cards.note: Genesis 46:11 — *And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.* The three sons of Levi that Jasher 45:6 names for Adinah are exactly the Levitical line Genesis counts among the seventy.
cards.s_text: And Levi took Adinah, and Issachar took Aridah, and they came to the land of Canaan, to their father’s house, and Adinah bare to Levi, Gershon, Kehath and Merari; three sons.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

cards.note: Genesis 46:9 — *And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.* Genesis registers Reuben's four sons by the same names Jasher 45:2 records for Reuben's house.
cards.s_text: And Eliuram the wife of Reuben conceived and bare him Hanoch, Palu, Chetzron and Carmi, four sons; and Simeon his brother took his sister Dinah for a wife, and she bare to him Memuel, Yamin, Ohad, Jachin and Zochar, five sons.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Reuben; Hanoch, and Phallu, and Hezron, and Carmi.

cards.note: Genesis 39:20 — *And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.* Genesis names the same dungeon Jasher 46:1 keeps Joseph confined in.
cards.s_text: In those days Joseph was still confined in the prison house in the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison.

cards.note: Genesis 39:21 — *But Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.* Behind Jasher's bare 'still confined' the canon shows Yahuah with the righteous one in his bonds.
cards.s_text: In those days Joseph was still confined in the prison house in the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

cards.note: Psalms 105:17 — *He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:* the Psalm reads Joseph's descent of Jasher 46:1 as Elohim sending a man ahead to preserve the seed.
cards.s_text: In those days Joseph was still confined in the prison house in the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:

cards.note: Psalms 105:18 — *Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:* the Psalm puts the irons on the prisoner Jasher 46:1 leaves confined.
cards.s_text: In those days Joseph was still confined in the prison house in the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:

cards.note: Genesis 40:5 — *And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.* The Genesis source of the one-night double dream Jasher 46:6 retells.
cards.s_text: And at the end of the year, they both dreamed dreams in one night, in the place of confinement where they were, and in the morning Joseph came to them to attend upon them as usual, and he saw them, and behold their countenances were dejected and sad.
cards.t_text: And they dreamed a dream both of them, each man his dream in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the butler and the baker of the king of Egypt, which were bound in the prison.

cards.note: Genesis 40:8 — *And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to Elohim (God)? tell me them, I pray you.* Joseph credits Elohim with the answer in both Jasher 46:7 and its Genesis source.
cards.s_text: And Joseph asked them, Why are your countenances sad and dejected this day? and they said to him, We dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it; and Joseph said to them, Relate, I pray you, your dream to me, and Elohim (God) shall give you an answer of peace as you desire.
cards.t_text: And they said unto him, We have dreamed a dream, and there is no interpreter of it. And Joseph said unto them, Do not interpretations belong to Elohim (God)? tell me them, I pray you.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:15 — *And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them.* Jubilees gives the same prison-attendant setting Jasher 46:6 places Joseph in among the two officers.
cards.s_text: And at the end of the year, they both dreamed dreams in one night, in the place of confinement where they were, and in the morning Joseph came to them to attend upon them as usual, and he saw them, and behold their countenances were dejected and sad.
cards.t_text: And the chief of the prison guards appointed Joseph to serve them; and he served before them.

cards.note: Genesis 40:10 — *And in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:* the same vine and three branches the butler describes in Jasher 46:8.
cards.s_text: And the butler related his dream to Joseph, and he said, I saw in my dream, and behold a large vine was before me, and upon that vine I saw three branches, and the vine speedily blossomed and reached a great height, and its clusters were ripened and became grapes.
cards.t_text: And in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:

cards.note: Genesis 40:12 — *And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days:* Joseph's reading of the three branches in Jasher 46:9 is the Genesis word.
cards.s_text: And I took the grapes and pressed them in a cup, and placed it in Pharaoh’s hand and he drank; and Joseph said to him, The three branches that were upon the vine are three days.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto him, This is the interpretation of it: The three branches are three days:

cards.note: Genesis 40:13 — *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thine head, and restore thee unto thy place: and thou shalt deliver Pharaoh's cup into his hand, after the former manner when thou wast his butler.* the restoration in three days Joseph foretells in Jasher 46:10.
cards.s_text: Yet within three days, the king will order you to be brought out and he will restore you to your office, and you shall give the king his wine to drink as at first when you were his butler; but let me find favor in your sight, that you shall remember me to Pharaoh when it will be well with you, and do kindness to me, and get me brought forth from this prison, for I was stolen away from the land of Canaan and was sold for a slave in this place.
cards.t_text: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up your head, and restore you unto your place: and you shall deliver Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, after the former manner when you were his butler.

cards.note: Genesis 40:14 — *But think on me when it shall be well with thee, and shew kindness, I pray thee, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:* Joseph's 'remember me when it is well with you' of Jasher 46:10.
cards.s_text: Yet within three days, the king will order you to be brought out and he will restore you to your office, and you shall give the king his wine to drink as at first when you were his butler; but let me find favor in your sight, that you shall remember me to Pharaoh when it will be well with you, and do kindness to me, and get me brought forth from this prison, for I was stolen away from the land of Canaan and was sold for a slave in this place.
cards.t_text: But think on me when it shall be well with you, and shew kindness, I pray you, unto me, and make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:

cards.note: Genesis 40:15 — *For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.* the same 'stolen away, here for naught' protest Joseph makes in Jasher 46:10-11.
cards.s_text: Yet within three days, the king will order you to be brought out and he will restore you to your office, and you shall give the king his wine to drink as at first when you were his butler; but let me find favor in your sight, that you shall remember me to Pharaoh when it will be well with you, and do kindness to me, and get me brought forth from this prison, for I was stolen away from the land of Canaan and was sold for a slave in this place.
cards.t_text: For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.

cards.note: Genesis 39:9 — *There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?* the purity that makes the 'false' charge of Jasher 46:11 false — the seed kept clean.
cards.s_text: And also that which was told you concerning my master’s wife is false, for they placed me in this dungeon for naught; and the butler answered Joseph, saying, If the king deal well with me as at first, as you last interpreted to me, I will do all that you desire, and get you brought out of this dungeon.
cards.t_text: There is none greater in this house than I; neither has he kept back any thing from me but you, because you are his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?

cards.note: 1 Corinthians 6:18 — *Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.* the apostle commands the very fleeing Joseph chose, vindicating his protest in Jasher 46:11.
cards.s_text: And also that which was told you concerning my master’s wife is false, for they placed me in this dungeon for naught; and the butler answered Joseph, saying, If the king deal well with me as at first, as you last interpreted to me, I will do all that you desire, and get you brought out of this dungeon.
cards.t_text: Flee fornication. Every sin that a man does is without the body; but he that commits fornication sins against his own body.

cards.note: Jubilees 39:7 — *And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.* Jubilees records the refusal that made the wife's accusation false, the 'false' charge Joseph names in Jasher 46:11.
cards.s_text: And also that which was told you concerning my master’s wife is false, for they placed me in this dungeon for naught; and the butler answered Joseph, saying, If the king deal well with me as at first, as you last interpreted to me, I will do all that you desire, and get you brought out of this dungeon.
cards.t_text: And Joseph remembered these words and refused to lie with her.

cards.note: Genesis 40:16 — *When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head:* the same three white baskets the baker tells in Jasher 46:13.
cards.s_text: And he said to him, In my dream I saw and behold three white baskets upon my head, and I looked, and behold there were in the upper-most basket all manner of baked meats for Pharaoh, and behold the birds were eating them from off my head.
cards.t_text: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said unto Joseph, I also was in my dream, and, behold, I had three white baskets on my head:

cards.note: Genesis 40:17 — *And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.* the bakemeats and birds of the baker's dream in Jasher 46:13.
cards.s_text: And he said to him, In my dream I saw and behold three white baskets upon my head, and I looked, and behold there were in the upper-most basket all manner of baked meats for Pharaoh, and behold the birds were eating them from off my head.
cards.t_text: And in the uppermost basket there was of all manner of bakemeats for Pharaoh; and the birds did eat them out of the basket upon my head.

cards.note: *And Joseph said to him, The three baskets which you did see are three days, yet within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you, as you saw in your dream.* (Jasher 46:14). *Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up thy head from off thee, and shall hang thee on a tree; and the birds shall eat thy flesh from off thee.* (Genesis 40:19). Joseph's verdict on the baker runs the same in both records: within three days Pharaoh will take his head, hang him on a tree, and the birds will eat his flesh. Jasher adds only the reading of the three baskets as three days, which Genesis gives in the verse before. The dream that promised the butler his place promised the baker a tree, and Joseph told each man the truth of his own dream without softening it.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to him, The three baskets which you did see are three days, yet within three days Pharaoh will take off your head, and hang you upon a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh from off you, as you saw in your dream.
cards.t_text: Yet within three days shall Pharaoh lift up your head from off you, and shall hang you on a tree; and the birds shall eat your flesh from off you.

cards.note: Genesis 40:23 — *Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.* the same forgetting Jasher 46:19 records, which it reads as Yahuah's discipline for trusting in man.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

cards.note: Genesis 41:9 — *Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:* the delayed remembering that follows the butler's forgetting in Jasher 46:19.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: Then spake the chief butler unto Pharaoh, saying, I do remember my faults this day:

cards.note: Psalms 105:19 — *Until the time that his word came: the word of Yahuah (LORD) tried him.* the Psalm names the forgetting of Jasher 46:19 as Yahuah trying the righteous one until his hour.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: Until the time that his word came: the word of Yahuah (LORD) tried him.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,* Stephen reads the whole prison ordeal of Jasher 46:19 as Elohim being with the rejected one.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Jubilees 39:18 — *But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although he had informed him what would befall him, and did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him for he forgot.* Jubilees tells the same forgetting Jasher 46:19 attributes to Yahuah's hand.
cards.s_text: And the butler, to whom Joseph had interpreted his dream, forgot Joseph, and he did not mention him to the king as he had promised, for this thing was from Yahuah (the Lord) in order to punish Joseph because he had trusted in man.
cards.t_text: But the chief butler forgot Joseph in the prison, although he had informed him what would befall him, and did not remember to inform Pharaoh how Joseph had told him for he forgot.

cards.note: Genesis 45:5 — *Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.* the prison years of Jasher 46:20 are the path by which the rejected one is kept to preserve life.
cards.s_text: And Joseph remained after this in the prison house two years, until he had completed twelve years.
cards.t_text: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* the Messiah-type verdict over Joseph's whole ordeal, including the dungeon years of Jasher 46:20.
cards.s_text: And Joseph remained after this in the prison house two years, until he had completed twelve years.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Romans 8:28 — *And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.* the apostle gathers Joseph's 'meant for good' prison years of Jasher 46:20 into the promise over all the called.
cards.s_text: And Joseph remained after this in the prison house two years, until he had completed twelve years.
cards.t_text: And we know that all things work together for good to them that love Elohim (God), to them who are the called according to his purpose.

cards.note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:14 — *And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.* reads the completed prison years of Jasher 46:20 as the road from bonds to the sceptre, the accusers shown to be liars.
cards.s_text: And Joseph remained after this in the prison house two years, until he had completed twelve years.
cards.t_text: And left him not in bonds, till she brought him the sceptre of the kingdom, and power against those that oppressed him: as for them that had accused him, she shewed them to be liars, and gave him perpetual glory.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 44:23 — *And made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.* Sirach sums the very outcome of Jasher 47:33 — the heritage resting on Jacob and parted among the twelve tribes.
cards.s_text: And the whole land of Canaan became an inheritance to the children of Israel for an everlasting inheritance, and Esau with all his children inherited the mountain of Seir.
cards.t_text: And made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing, and gave him an heritage, and divided his portions; among the twelve tribes did he part them.

cards.note: Acts 7:8 — *And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so Abraham begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.* Stephen traces the same kept seed-line — Abraham to Isaac to Jacob to the twelve — whose deed Jacob seals for his children in Jasher 47:29.
cards.s_text: And Jacob took the book of purchase and the signature, the command and the statutes and the revealed book, and he placed them in an earthen vessel in order that they should remain for a long time, and he delivered them into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And he gave him the covenant of circumcision: and so Abraham begat Isaac, and circumcised him the eighth day; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:9 — *By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:* The everlasting inheritance Jacob secures for Israel in Jasher 47:33 is the land of promise the fathers held by faith as joint heirs.
cards.s_text: And the whole land of Canaan became an inheritance to the children of Israel for an everlasting inheritance, and Esau with all his children inherited the mountain of Seir.
cards.t_text: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob, the heirs with him of the same promise:

cards.note: Genesis 27:39 — *And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;* Esau's portion away from Canaan in Jasher 47:33 fulfills the very dwelling Isaac had spoken over him.
cards.s_text: And the whole land of Canaan became an inheritance to the children of Israel for an everlasting inheritance, and Esau with all his children inherited the mountain of Seir.
cards.t_text: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, your dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above;

cards.note: Genesis 36:8 — *Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.* Genesis records the same end Jasher 47:33 gives — Esau and his children inheriting the mountain of Seir while Canaan goes to Israel.
cards.s_text: And the whole land of Canaan became an inheritance to the children of Israel for an everlasting inheritance, and Esau with all his children inherited the mountain of Seir.
cards.t_text: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:11–12 — *I say and testify to you, my sons, according to the judgment which will come upon the man who wishes to injure his brother." And he divided all his possessions between the two on that day, and he gave the larger portion to him that was the first-born, and the tower and all that was about it, and all that Abraham possessed at the Well of the Oath.* Jubilees has Isaac himself divide the estate between the brothers, the same partition Jacob and Esau settle in Jasher 47:15-19.
cards.s_text: If you desire the whole land take it for you and your children forever, and I will take this riches, and it you desire the riches take it to you, and I will take this land for me and for my children to inherit it forever.
cards.t_text: And he divided all his possessions between the two on that day, and he gave the larger portion to him that was the first-born, and the tower and all that was about it, and all that Abraham possessed at the Well of the Oath.

cards.note: Genesis 36:6 — *And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance, which he had got in the land of Canaan; and went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob.* Genesis already records Esau taking his goods and departing from Jacob to Seir, just as Jasher 47:31 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Esau took all this, and he and his children went home to the land of Seir the Horite, away from his brother Jacob and his children.
cards.t_text: And Esau took his wives, and his sons, and his daughters, and all the persons of his house, and his cattle, and all his beasts, and all his substance, which he had got in the land of Canaan; and went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 17:7 — *And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a Elohim (God) unto thee, and to thy seed after thee.* The everlasting possession Jacob secures in Jasher 47:24 rests on the everlasting covenant to Abraham's seed.
cards.s_text: And Esau rose up and returned to Jacob, and did all that Nebayoth the son of Ishmael had advised; and Esau took all the riches that Isaac had left, the souls, the beasts, the cattle and the property, and all the riches; he gave nothing to his brother Jacob; and Jacob took all the land of Canaan, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates, and he took it for an everlasting possession, and for his children and for his seed after him forever.
cards.t_text: And I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a Elohim (God) unto you, and to your seed after you.

cards.note: Genesis 15:18 — *In the same day Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto thy seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates:* The exact boundary Jacob takes for his seed forever in Jasher 47:24 is the covenant land-grant Yahuah cut with Abram.
cards.s_text: And Esau rose up and returned to Jacob, and did all that Nebayoth the son of Ishmael had advised; and Esau took all the riches that Isaac had left, the souls, the beasts, the cattle and the property, and all the riches; he gave nothing to his brother Jacob; and Jacob took all the land of Canaan, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates, and he took it for an everlasting possession, and for his children and for his seed after him forever.
cards.t_text: In the same day Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with Abram, saying, Unto your seed have I given this land, from the river of Egypt unto the great river, the river Euphrates:

cards.note: Jubilees 36:2 — *Wherefore bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham purchased a sepulchre to bury in; in the sepulchre which I digged for myself, there bury me.* Isaac's request to be laid in Abraham's purchased cave matches the Machpelah burial of Jasher 47:9-10.
cards.s_text: And when Isaac had finished commanding Jacob and his children, he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: Wherefore bury me near Abraham my father, in the double cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite, where Abraham purchased a sepulchre to bury in; in the sepulchre which I digged for myself, there bury me.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:18 — *And Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.* Jubilees gives the same death at one hundred and eighty years, buried by Esau and Jacob, that Jasher 47:9 narrates.
cards.s_text: And when Isaac had finished commanding Jacob and his children, he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: And Isaac slept on his bed that day rejoicing; and he slept the eternal sleep, and died one hundred and eighty years old. He completed twenty-five weeks and five years; and his two sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

cards.note: Genesis 23:17 — *And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders round about, were made sure* The cave Abraham bought from the children of Heth, where Isaac is buried in Jasher 47:10, is the field of Machpelah secured here.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and Esau fell upon the face of their father Isaac, and they wept, and Isaac was one hundred and eighty years old when he died in the land of Canaan, in Hebron, and his sons carried him to the cave of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought from the children of Heth for a possession of a burial place.
cards.t_text: And the field of Ephron, which was in Machpelah, which was before Mamre, the field, and the cave which was therein, and all the trees that were in the field, that were in all the borders round about, were made sure

cards.note: Genesis 35:28 — *And the days of Isaac were an hundred and fourscore years.* Genesis records the same one hundred and eighty years that Jasher 47:10 gives for Isaac at his death.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and Esau fell upon the face of their father Isaac, and they wept, and Isaac was one hundred and eighty years old when he died in the land of Canaan, in Hebron, and his sons carried him to the cave of Machpelah, which Abraham had bought from the children of Heth for a possession of a burial place.
cards.t_text: And the days of Isaac were an hundred and fourscore years.

cards.note: Genesis 35:29 — *And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.* Jasher 47:9 retells this verse almost verbatim — Isaac gathered to his people, buried by his two sons.
cards.s_text: And when Isaac had finished commanding Jacob and his children, he gave up the ghost and died, and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: And Isaac gave up the ghost, and died, and was gathered unto his people, being old and full of days: and his sons Esau and Jacob buried him.

cards.note: Jubilees 36:3 — *And this I command you, my sons, that you practise righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that Yahuah (God) may bring upon you all that Yahuah (God) said that he would do to Abraham and to his seed.* Jubilees gives the same dying charge to walk in righteousness so the promise to Abraham's seed may come, paralleling Jasher 47:8.
cards.s_text: Now therefore my son, teach your children and your children’s children to fear Yahuah (the Lord), and to go in the good way which will please Yahuah your Elohim (the Lord your God), for if you keep the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his statutes Yahuah (the Lord) will also keep to you his covenant with Abraham, and will do well with you and your seed all the days.
cards.t_text: And this I command you, my sons, that you practise righteousness and uprightness on the earth, so that Yahuah (God) may bring upon you all that Yahuah (God) said that he would do to Abraham and to his seed.

cards.note: *And Isaac called Jacob and his sons, and they all came and sat before Isaac, and Isaac said to Jacob, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of the whole earth said to me, To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and I will perform to them the oath which I swore to your father Abraham.* (Jasher 47:7). *Sojourn in this land, and I will be with thee, and will bless thee; for unto thee, and unto thy seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham thy father;* (Genesis 26:3). The word Isaac passes to Jacob and his sons in Jasher is the word Yahuah (the Lord) first spoke to Isaac himself in Genesis: to your seed I will give this land, and I will perform the oath I swore to Abraham your father. Isaac does not hand it on as a bare deed; he hands it on with its condition in the open, if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and in the next verse he tells Jacob to teach his children and his children's children to fear Yahuah (the Lord). The land, the oath, and the keeping of his ways are passed down together from Abraham to Isaac to Jacob.
cards.s_text: And Isaac called Jacob and his sons, and they all came and sat before Isaac, and Isaac said to Jacob, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of the whole earth said to me, To your seed will I give this land for an inheritance if your children keep my statutes and my ways, and I will perform to them the oath which I swore to your father Abraham.
cards.t_text: Sojourn in this land, and I will be with you, and will bless you; for unto you, and unto your seed, I will give all these countries, and I will perform the oath which I sware unto Abraham your father;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:7 — *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* Isaac's charge to teach the children to fear Yahuah in Jasher 47:8 is the Shema's own command, kept by the fathers before Sinai.
cards.s_text: Now therefore my son, teach your children and your children’s children to fear Yahuah (the Lord), and to go in the good way which will please Yahuah your Elohim (the Lord your God), for if you keep the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his statutes Yahuah (the Lord) will also keep to you his covenant with Abraham, and will do well with you and your seed all the days.
cards.t_text: And you shall teach them diligently unto your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you risest up.

cards.note: Ecclesiasticus 44:22 — *With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant,* Sirach's praise of the fathers confirms that the blessing Isaac hands on in Jasher 47:5 was first established with him for Abraham's sake.
cards.s_text: And Isaac placed his hands upon all the sons of Jacob, and he took hold of them and embraced them, and kissed them one by one, and Isaac blessed them on that day, and he said to them, May the Elohim (God) of your fathers bless you and increase your seed like the stars of heaven for number.
cards.t_text: With Isaac did he establish likewise for Abraham his father’s sake the blessing of all men, and the covenant,

cards.note: Jubilees 36:6 — *Remember you, my sons, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and how I too worshipped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, that He might multiply you and increase your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness which will not be rooted out to all the generations for ever.* Jubilees keeps the same deathbed scene of Isaac invoking the star-seed that Jasher 47:5 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Isaac placed his hands upon all the sons of Jacob, and he took hold of them and embraced them, and kissed them one by one, and Isaac blessed them on that day, and he said to them, May the Elohim (God) of your fathers bless you and increase your seed like the stars of heaven for number.
cards.t_text: Remember you, my sons, Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham your father, and how I too worshipped Him and served Him in righteousness and in joy, that He might multiply you and increase your seed as the stars of heaven in multitude, and establish you on the earth as the plant of righteousness which will not be rooted out to all the generations for ever.

cards.note: Genesis 26:4 — *And I will make thy seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto thy seed all these countries; and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;* The same promise was renewed to Isaac himself, which is why he can pass the star-blessing to his grandsons in Jasher 47:5.
cards.s_text: And Isaac placed his hands upon all the sons of Jacob, and he took hold of them and embraced them, and kissed them one by one, and Isaac blessed them on that day, and he said to them, May the Elohim (God) of your fathers bless you and increase your seed like the stars of heaven for number.
cards.t_text: And I will make your seed to multiply as the stars of heaven, and will give unto your seed all these countries; and in your seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed;

cards.note: Genesis 22:17 — *That in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;* The star-seed Isaac speaks over Jacob's sons in Jasher 47:5 is the very oath Yahuah swore to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And Isaac placed his hands upon all the sons of Jacob, and he took hold of them and embraced them, and kissed them one by one, and Isaac blessed them on that day, and he said to them, May the Elohim (God) of your fathers bless you and increase your seed like the stars of heaven for number.
cards.t_text: That in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the sea shore; and your seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;

cards.note: Daniel 2:28 — *But there is a Elohim (God) in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these.* The sign that vindicates Joseph's word in Jasher 48:62 rests on the same heaven-given revelation Daniel later names before another king.
cards.s_text: And the king answered and said to Joseph, Who says and who knows that your words are correct? And he said to the king, This shall be a sign for you respecting all my words, that they are true and that my advice is good for you.
cards.t_text: But there is a Elohim (God) in heaven that revealeth secrets, and makes known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head upon your bed, are these;

cards.note: Genesis 41:13 — *And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto mine office, and him he hanged.* The canon's witness that Joseph's prison interpretations came true is the ground for the confirming sign Jasher 48:62-64 adds — his word does not fall.
cards.s_text: And Joseph finished speaking these words to the king, and he bowed down to the king and he went out, and when Joseph had gone out from the king’s presence, those signs which Joseph had spoken to the king came to pass on that day.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, as he interpreted to us, so it was; me he restored unto my office, and him he hanged.

cards.note: *And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: “Seven years will come (in which there will be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.* (Jubilees 40:3). *Behold the seven years that are coming there will be a great plenty throughout the land, and after that the seven years of famine will follow them, a very grievous famine; and all the plenty will be forgotten from the land, and the famine will consume the inhabitants of the land.* (Jasher 48:55). Joseph gave Pharaoh one reading for two dreams, and both witnesses carry the same reading word for word: seven years of plenty over the land, and after them seven years of famine such as had never been. Jasher's telling adds what the famine would do, that all the plenty would be forgotten and the famine would eat the inhabitants of the land. Jubilees says the two dreams were one, which is why the king needed a Hebrew and not a magician; the doubling was not two messages but one message fixed. The plenty was given so that the famine could be survived, and only one man in Egypt could see that.
cards.s_text: Behold the seven years that are coming there will be a great plenty throughout the land, and after that the seven years of famine will follow them, a very grievous famine; and all the plenty will be forgotten from the land, and the famine will consume the inhabitants of the land.
cards.t_text: And he said before Pharaoh that his two dreams were one, and he said to him: “Seven years will come (in which there will be) plenty over all the land of Egypt, and after that seven years of famine, such a famine as has not been in all the land.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The famine-counsel of Jasher 48:57 is God's design behind the brothers' evil — meant unto good to save much people alive.
cards.s_text: Now therefore I will give you counsel and deliver your soul and the souls of the inhabitants of the land from the evil of the famine, that you seek throughout your kingdom for a man very discreet and wise, who knows all the affairs of government, and appoint him to superintend over the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Genesis 45:5 — *Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.* The deliverance of souls Joseph offers in Jasher 48:57 is the very purpose he later confesses — Elohim sent him to preserve life.
cards.s_text: Now therefore I will give you counsel and deliver your soul and the souls of the inhabitants of the land from the evil of the famine, that you seek throughout your kingdom for a man very discreet and wise, who knows all the affairs of government, and appoint him to superintend over the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.

cards.note: Genesis 41:33 — *Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.* Joseph's counsel to appoint a discreet man, which Jasher 48:57 records in the same breath.
cards.s_text: Now therefore I will give you counsel and deliver your soul and the souls of the inhabitants of the land from the evil of the famine, that you seek throughout your kingdom for a man very discreet and wise, who knows all the affairs of government, and appoint him to superintend over the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 41:26 — *The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.* The single interpretation of the doubled dream that Jasher 48:54 gives in the same words.
cards.s_text: The seven good kine and ears of corn are seven years, and the seven bad kine and ears of corn are also seven years; it is one dream.
cards.t_text: The seven good kine are seven years; and the seven good ears are seven years: the dream is one.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”* (Jubilees 40:5). *And Joseph was then clothed with the spirit of Elohim before the king, and he knew all the things that would befall the king from that day forward, and he knew the proper interpretation of the king’s dream, and he spoke before the king.* (Jasher 48:52). Jasher shows the inside of the thing, Joseph clothed with the spirit of Elohim (God) before the king and knowing what would befall him from that day forward. Jubilees shows the outside, Pharaoh turning to his servants and saying out loud that the spirit of Yahuah (God) was with this man. A heathen king confessed what the court magicians could not produce. The wisdom was not Joseph's own, and Pharaoh knew it, which is why he did not look for a wiser Egyptian; there was none to find.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was then clothed with the spirit of Elohim before the king, and he knew all the things that would befall the king from that day forward, and he knew the proper interpretation of the king’s dream, and he spoke before the king.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”

cards.note: Genesis 41:38 — *And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) is?* Pharaoh's recognition of the Spirit that Jasher 48:52 says clothed Joseph before the king.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was then clothed with the spirit of Elohim before the king, and he knew all the things that would befall the king from that day forward, and he knew the proper interpretation of the king’s dream, and he spoke before the king.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) is?

cards.note: Genesis 41:16 — *And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: Elohim (God) shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.* Joseph's same disclaimer in Jasher 48:51 — the interpretation belongs to Elohim, not to the man.
cards.s_text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, Let Pharaoh relate his dreams that he dreamed; surely the interpretations belong to Elohim (God); and Pharaoh related his dreams to Joseph, the dream of the kine, and the dream of the ears of corn, and the king left off speaking.
cards.t_text: And Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, It is not in me: Elohim (God) shall give Pharaoh an answer of peace.

cards.note: *And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spake of him to the king, and he brought him forth from the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.* (Jubilees 40:2). *And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.* (Jasher 48:33). Jubilees gives the hinge in one verse, the chief butler remembering Joseph and speaking of him to the king, and Joseph brought up out of the prison. Jasher gives the butler's actual words, a Hebrew servant of the captain of the guard, put in the house of confinement by an angry master, who attended us there. The man who brought Joseph before Pharaoh was a man Joseph had served in a cell. The service he gave in confinement was the road that carried him out of it, and the one who had forgotten him was the one Yahuah (God) used to remember him.
cards.s_text: And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.
cards.t_text: And then the chief butler remembered Joseph and spake of him to the king, and he brought him forth from the prison, and he told his two dreams before him.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him.* Stephen names the rejected-but-kept Hebrew servant of the prison whom Jasher 48:33 sets in confinement — the Messiah type, sold yet sustained.
cards.s_text: And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Psalms 105:20 — *The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.* The king's sending that frees Joseph from the dungeon in Jasher 48:41 — the cast-down one lifted up.
cards.s_text: And the servants of the king went to Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon, and the king’s servants shaved him, and he changed his prison garment and he came before the king.
cards.t_text: The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.

cards.note: Psalms 105:18 — *Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron.* The house of confinement Jasher 48:33 names — the righteous one in irons before he is exalted.
cards.s_text: And there was with us a Hebrew servant belonging to the captain of the guard, his name was Joseph, for his master had been angry with him and placed him in the house of confinement, and he attended us there.
cards.t_text: Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:

cards.note: Genesis 41:14 — *Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.* The hasty raising from the dungeon, the shaving, the changed garment that Jasher 48:41 retells exactly.
cards.s_text: And the servants of the king went to Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon, and the king’s servants shaved him, and he changed his prison garment and he came before the king.
cards.t_text: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon: and he shaved himself, and changed his raiment, and came in unto Pharaoh.

cards.note: Daniel 2:28 — *But there is a Elohim (God) in heaven that revealeth secrets, and maketh known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Thy dream, and the visions of thy head upon thy bed, are these.* The same pattern Jasher 48:25 names — Yahuah frustrating Egypt's wise men so His chosen interpreter alone holds the secret.
