cards.s_text: And the king knew in his wisdom that they did not altogether speak correctly in all these words, for this was from Yahuah (the Lord) to frustrate the words of the wise men of Egypt, in order that Joseph might go forth from the house of confinement, and in order that he should become great in Egypt.
cards.t_text: But there is a Elohim (God) in heaven that revealeth secrets, and makes known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what shall be in the latter days. Your dream, and the visions of your head upon your bed, are these;

cards.note: Genesis 41:8 — *And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.* The summoning Jasher 48:6 expands into two failed companies of interpreters.
cards.s_text: And in the morning the king remembered his dreams, and his spirit was sadly troubled on account of his dreams, and the king hastened and sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and the wise men, and they came and stood before Pharaoh.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.

cards.note: *And in those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning a famine which was to be in all the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams that were in Egypt, and magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they were not able to declare (them).* (Jubilees 40:1). *At that time Pharaoh king of Egypt was sitting upon his throne in the land of Egypt, and lay in his bed and dreamed dreams, and Pharaoh saw in his dream that he was standing by the side of the river of Egypt.* (Jasher 48:2). Jasher sets the scene, Pharaoh on his bed in the land of Egypt, dreaming that he stood by the river. Jubilees tells what the dreams were about and what came of them: two dreams in one night concerning a famine, and all the interpreters and magicians of Egypt called in and unable to say what they meant. Yahuah (God) spoke to a heathen king in his sleep and shut the meaning from every wise man in his court, so that the only door left open was a Hebrew slave in the king's prison. The famine was coming either way; the dream was mercy, and the silence of the magicians was the thing that got Joseph out.
cards.s_text: At that time Pharaoh king of Egypt was sitting upon his throne in the land of Egypt, and lay in his bed and dreamed dreams, and Pharaoh saw in his dream that he was standing by the side of the river of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And in those days Pharaoh dreamed two dreams in one night concerning a famine which was to be in all the land, and he awoke from his sleep and called all the interpreters of dreams that were in Egypt, and magicians, and told them his two dreams, and they were not able to declare (them).

cards.note: Genesis 41:7 — *And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.* The second dream of the ears that Jasher 48:5 records as the king waking.
cards.s_text: And he awoke, and he slept again and he dreamed a second time, and he saw and behold seven ears of corn came up upon one stalk, rank and good, and seven thin ears blasted with the east wind sprang, up after them, and the thin ears swallowed up the full ones, and Pharaoh awoke out of his dream.
cards.t_text: And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears. And Pharaoh awoke, and, behold, it was a dream.

cards.note: Genesis 41:4 — *And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.* The lean kine swallowing the fat that Jasher 48:4 retells word for scene.
cards.s_text: And seven other kine, lean fleshed and ill favored, came up after them, and the seven ill favored ones swallowed up the well favored ones, and still their appearance was ill as at first.
cards.t_text: And the ill favoured and leanfleshed kine did eat up the seven well favoured and fat kine. So Pharaoh awoke.

cards.note: Genesis 41:1 — *And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.* The very dream by the river that Jasher 48:2 sets at the throne of Egypt.
cards.s_text: At that time Pharaoh king of Egypt was sitting upon his throne in the land of Egypt, and lay in his bed and dreamed dreams, and Pharaoh saw in his dream that he was standing by the side of the river of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass at the end of two full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and, behold, he stood by the river.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,* Stephen names the Elohim who was with Joseph from the pit, the same Yahuah Joseph praises in Jasher 49:30.
cards.s_text: And Joseph upon his horse lifted up his eyes to heaven, and called out and said, He raises the poor man from the dust, He lifts up the needy from the dunghill. O Yahuah (O Lord) of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in you.
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Psalm 105:20 — *The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.* The very day Jasher 49:30 celebrates, the king's loosing of Joseph from the prison to the rule, is Psalm 105's word.
cards.s_text: And Joseph upon his horse lifted up his eyes to heaven, and called out and said, He raises the poor man from the dust, He lifts up the needy from the dunghill. O Yahuah (O Lord) of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in you.
cards.t_text: The king sent and loosed him; even the ruler of the people, and let him go free.

cards.note: Psalm 105:18 — *Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:* the dungeon of Jasher 49:13, where Joseph lay the night before his exaltation, is the iron Psalm 105 remembers.
cards.s_text: And on that night Yahuah (the Lord) sent one of his ministering angels, and he came into the land of Egypt to Joseph, and the angel of Yahuah (the Lord) stood over Joseph, and behold Joseph was lying in the bed at night in his master’s house in the dungeon, for his master had put him back into the dungeon on account of his wife.
cards.t_text: Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron:

cards.note: Psalm 105:17 — *He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:* Joseph's praise in Jasher 49:30, that Yahuah raises the poor from the dust, sings the same providence Psalm 105 ascribes to the whole story.
cards.s_text: And Joseph upon his horse lifted up his eyes to heaven, and called out and said, He raises the poor man from the dust, He lifts up the needy from the dunghill. O Yahuah (O Lord) of Hosts, happy is the man who trusts in you.
cards.t_text: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:

cards.note: *And the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.* (Jubilees 40:10). *And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.* (Jasher 49:21). The king gives Joseph a new name, and both books record it. Jubilees writes it as Sĕphânṭîphâns and Jasher writes it as Zaphnath Paaneah; it is one Egyptian name heard through two scribes' ears, the same name Genesis carries. Jasher adds what the name meant in Pharaoh's mouth: second to me, every affair of the government at your word, the people going out and coming in at your word. Jubilees adds the wife, the priest's daughter from Heliopolis. The two books do not compete; each keeps a piece of the same afternoon in Pharaoh's court.
cards.s_text: And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.
cards.t_text: And the king called Joseph’s name Sĕphânṭîphâns, and gave Joseph to wife the daughter of Potiphar, the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis, the chief cook.

cards.note: Genesis 41:46 — *And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.* Jasher 49:38 reckons the identical thirty years at Joseph's standing before Pharaoh.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh, and Joseph went out from before the king, and he became the king’s second in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 41:45 — *And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.* The renaming of Jasher 49:21 and the marriage of 49:36 are Genesis' own record (Zaphnath-paaneah; daughter of the priest of On).
cards.s_text: And your name no more shall be called Joseph, but Zaphnath Paaneah shall be your name; you shall be second to me, and according to your word shall be all the affairs of my government, and at your word shall my people go out and come in.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphnath-paaneah; and he gave him to wife Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On. And Joseph went out over all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 40:8 — *And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.* Jubilees gives the righteous character of the second-to-Pharaoh that Jasher 49:22 establishes.
cards.s_text: Also from under your hand shall my servants and officers receive their salary which is given to them monthly, and to you shall all the people of the land bow down; only in my throne will I be greater than you.
cards.t_text: And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.

cards.note: Genesis 41:43 — *And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.* The second chariot opposite the king's in Jasher 49:24 retells Genesis' very procession.
cards.s_text: And the king commanded his servants, and they made him ride in the second chariot belonging to the king, that went opposite to the king’s chariot, and he caused him to ride upon a great and strong horse from the king’s horses, and to be conducted through the streets of the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And he made him to ride in the second chariot which he had; and they cried before him, Bow the knee: and he made him ruler over all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 41:40 — *Thou shalt be over my house, and according unto thy word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than thou.* Pharaoh's reservation in Jasher 49:22, 'only in my throne will I be greater than you,' is the canon's exact word.
cards.s_text: Also from under your hand shall my servants and officers receive their salary which is given to them monthly, and to you shall all the people of the land bow down; only in my throne will I be greater than you.
cards.t_text: You shall be over my house, and according unto your word shall all my people be ruled: only in the throne will I be greater than you.

cards.note: Genesis 41:42 — *And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;* the investiture of Jasher 49:23 (ring, princely garment, gold chain) is Genesis detail for detail.
cards.s_text: And the king took off his ring from his hand and put it upon the hand of Joseph, and the king dressed Joseph in a princely garment, and he put a golden crown upon his head, and he put a golden chain upon his neck.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh took off his ring from his hand, and put it upon Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in vestures of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck;

cards.note: Acts 7:10 — *And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.* Stephen reads Joseph's elevation in Jasher 49 as Elohim's own deliverance and gift of wisdom.
cards.s_text: Now you did give me counsel to appoint a wise man over the land of Egypt, in order with his wisdom to save the land from the famine; now therefore, since Elohim has made all this known to you, and all the words which you have spoken, there is not throughout the land a discreet and wise man like to you.
cards.t_text: And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.

cards.note: Jubilees 40:5 — *And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”* Jubilees narrates the identical Pharaoh-speech that opens Jasher 49:8.
cards.s_text: And the king said to all the officers: I have thought that since Elohim (God) has made known to the Hebrew man all that he has spoken, there is none so discreet and wise in the whole land as he is; if it seem good in your sight I will place him over the land, for he will save the land with his wisdom.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) gave Joseph favour and mercy in the eyes of Pharaoh, and Pharaoh said to his servants: “We shall not find such a wise and discreet man as this man, for the spirit of Yahuah (God) is with him.”

cards.note: Genesis 41:39 — *And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as Elohim (God) hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art:* the king's words to Joseph in Jasher 49:20 echo Genesis verbatim, 'there is not throughout the land a discreet and wise man like to you.'
cards.s_text: Now you did give me counsel to appoint a wise man over the land of Egypt, in order with his wisdom to save the land from the famine; now therefore, since Elohim has made all this known to you, and all the words which you have spoken, there is not throughout the land a discreet and wise man like to you.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as Elohim (God) has shewed you all this, there is none so discreet and wise as you are:

cards.note: Genesis 41:38 — *And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) is?* Pharaoh's reasoning in Jasher 49:8, that Elohim has made all known to the Hebrew, is the canon's own ground for the elevation.
cards.s_text: And the king said to all the officers: I have thought that since Elohim (God) has made known to the Hebrew man all that he has spoken, there is none so discreet and wise in the whole land as he is; if it seem good in your sight I will place him over the land, for he will save the land with his wisdom.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh said unto his servants, Can we find such a one as this is, a man in whom the Spirit of Elohim (God) is?

cards.note: *And Joseph did all these things, and made these statutes, in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn; and Joseph’s people caused it daily to be proclaimed in Egypt according to these words and statutes which Joseph had commanded.* (Jasher 50:37). *And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.* (Genesis 42:6). Jasher explains why Joseph set up his statutes for the sale of corn: so that he would know the moment his brethren came down to Egypt to buy. Genesis gives the moment itself, Joseph the governor selling to all the people of the land, and his brethren coming in and bowing before him with their faces to the earth. The sheaves of his boyhood dream bow at last, and Jasher shows it was not chance that brought them before him but a net Joseph had spread across all Egypt for that very day.
cards.s_text: And Joseph did all these things, and made these statutes, in order that he might know when his brethren should come to Egypt to buy corn; and Joseph’s people caused it daily to be proclaimed in Egypt according to these words and statutes which Joseph had commanded.
cards.t_text: And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 42:3 — *And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.* The brethren Joseph foresaw and laid his gate-statutes to detect in Jasher 50:32 are the ten who go down in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Joseph knew that his brethren also would come to Egypt to buy corn, for the famine prevailed throughout the earth. And Joseph commanded all his people that they should cause it to be proclaimed throughout the land of Egypt, saying,
cards.t_text: And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 42:5 — *And the sons of Yashar'el (Israel) came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.* The inhabitants of Canaan coming for corn in Jasher 50:30 include the covenant seed — Israel's own sons going down for bread.
cards.s_text: And all the inhabitants of the land of Canaan and the Philistines, and those beyond the Jordan, and the children of the east and all the cities of the lands far and nigh heard that there was corn in Egypt, and they all came to Egypt to buy corn, for the famine prevailed over them.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Yashar'el (Israel) came to buy corn among those that came: for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 41:57 — *And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn; because that the famine was so sore in all lands.* Canaan, the Philistines, those beyond the Jordan and the children of the east coming to Egypt in Jasher 50:30 is Genesis's 'all countries.'
cards.s_text: And all the inhabitants of the land of Canaan and the Philistines, and those beyond the Jordan, and the children of the east and all the cities of the lands far and nigh heard that there was corn in Egypt, and they all came to Egypt to buy corn, for the famine prevailed over them.
cards.t_text: And all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn; because that the famine was so sore in all lands.

cards.note: Genesis 41:56 — *And the famine was over all the face of the earth: and Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.* Joseph opening all his stores and selling to the people of Egypt in Jasher 50:27 is the same act Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And when Joseph heard all the words of the people of Egypt and what had befallen them, Joseph opened all his stores of the produce and he sold it to the people of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And the famine was over all the face of the earth: and Joseph opened all the storehouses, and sold unto the Egyptians; and the famine waxed sore in the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 41:55 — *And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he saith to you, do.* Pharaoh's answer in Jasher 50:25 sending the people to Joseph to do whatever he says is the same command Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And when the king heard all that had befallen the inhabitants of Egypt, the king was greatly afraid on account of the famine, and he was much terrified; and the king answered the people of Egypt, saying, Since all this has happened to you, go to Joseph, do whatever he shall say to you, transgress not his commands.
cards.t_text: And when all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread: and Pharaoh said unto all the Egyptians, Go unto Joseph; what he says to you, do.

cards.note: Genesis 41:54 — *And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.* Jasher 50:18's famine coming 'as Joseph had spoken' matches Genesis's 'according as Joseph had said.'
cards.s_text: And the seven years of plenty that were throughout the land were at an end, and the seven years of famine came after them as Joseph had spoken, and the famine was throughout the land.
cards.t_text: And the seven years of dearth began to come, according as Joseph had said: and the dearth was in all lands; but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

cards.note: Genesis 41:53 — *And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.* Jasher 50:18's seven years of plenty 'at an end' is the same hinge Genesis marks before the dearth.
cards.s_text: And the seven years of plenty that were throughout the land were at an end, and the seven years of famine came after them as Joseph had spoken, and the famine was throughout the land.
cards.t_text: And the seven years of plenteousness, that was in the land of Egypt, were ended.

cards.note: Genesis 41:52 — *And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For Elohim (God) hath caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.* Ephraim, the second son of Jasher 50:15, becomes the great tribe of the northern house — the seed made fruitful in affliction.
cards.s_text: And Joseph’s wife Osnath the daughter of Potiphera bare him two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and Joseph was thirty-four years old when he begat them.
cards.t_text: And the name of the second called he Ephraim: For Elohim (God) has caused me to be fruitful in the land of my affliction.

cards.note: Genesis 41:51 — *And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For Elohim (God), said he, hath made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.* Jasher 50:15 names Manasseh as the elder of the two; Genesis gives the meaning of his name.
cards.s_text: And Joseph’s wife Osnath the daughter of Potiphera bare him two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and Joseph was thirty-four years old when he begat them.
cards.t_text: And Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh: For Elohim (God), said he, has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.

cards.note: Genesis 41:50 — *And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bare unto him.* Jasher 50:15's two sons by Osnath daughter of Potiphera, born before the famine, are the same birth Genesis sets down.
cards.s_text: And Joseph’s wife Osnath the daughter of Potiphera bare him two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, and Joseph was thirty-four years old when he begat them.
cards.t_text: And unto Joseph were born two sons before the years of famine came, which Asenath the daughter of Poti-pherah priest of On bare unto him.

cards.note: *And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.* (Jubilees 40:8). *And at the revolution of the year, in the second year of Joseph’s reigning over Egypt, Yahuah (the Lord) gave great plenty throughout the land for seven years as Joseph had spoken, for Yahuah (the Lord) blessed all the produce of the earth in those days for seven years, and they ate and were greatly satisfied.* (Jasher 50:7). Jasher tells of the second year of Joseph's reign, when Yahuah (the Lord) gave the great plenty for seven years exactly as Joseph had spoken. Jubilees tells what kind of man was reigning while the plenty came: one who walked in uprightness, without pride, with no respect of persons, who took no gifts and judged all the people of the land fairly. That is the judge Torah later requires of Yashar'el (Israel), and here he is, a Hebrew ruling Egypt. The land was fed under a ruler who could not be bought, and the princes and servants loved him for it.
cards.s_text: And at the revolution of the year, in the second year of Joseph’s reigning over Egypt, Yahuah (the Lord) gave great plenty throughout the land for seven years as Joseph had spoken, for Yahuah (the Lord) blessed all the produce of the earth in those days for seven years, and they ate and were greatly satisfied.
cards.t_text: And Joseph ruled over all the land of Egypt, and all the princes of Pharaoh, and all his servants, and all who did the king’s business loved him, for he walked in uprightness, for he was without pride and arrogance, and he had no respect of persons, and did not accept gifts, but he judged in uprightness all the people of the land.

cards.note: Genesis 41:49 — *And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.* Jasher 50:10's corn 'like the sand of the sea for abundance... could not be numbered' is the same numberless store.
cards.s_text: And Joseph did according to this year by year, and he heaped up corn like the sand of the sea for abundance, for his stores were immense and could not be numbered for abundance.
cards.t_text: And Joseph gathered corn as the sand of the sea, very much, until he left numbering; for it was without number.

cards.note: Genesis 41:35 — *And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.* Joseph's officers collecting and heaping the corn year by year in Jasher 50:8 is Joseph's own counsel to Pharaoh in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Joseph at that time had officers under him, and they collected all the food of the good years, and heaped corn year by year, and they placed it in the treasuries of Joseph.
cards.t_text: And let them gather all the food of those good years that come, and lay up corn under the hand of Pharaoh, and let them keep food in the cities.

cards.note: Genesis 41:29 — *Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:* the seven plenteous years Jasher 50:7 says Yahuah gave throughout the land are Joseph's interpreted dream in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And at the revolution of the year, in the second year of Joseph’s reigning over Egypt, Yahuah (the Lord) gave great plenty throughout the land for seven years as Joseph had spoken, for Yahuah (the Lord) blessed all the produce of the earth in those days for seven years, and they ate and were greatly satisfied.
cards.t_text: Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt:

cards.note: Genesis 50:24 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.* The kindness with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob the brothers fear is lost (Jasher 51:50) is the very covenant Joseph confesses Elohim will keep by the visitation.
cards.s_text: And they all said, And where is Yahuah (the Lord)’s kindness with our fathers, with Abraham, Isaac, end Jacob, that Yahuah (the Lord) has this day delivered us into the hands of the king of Egypt to contrive against us?
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The brothers' fearful "what has Elohim done to us?" (Jasher 51:49-50) is the providence Joseph will later name as good for the saving of the covenant seed.
cards.s_text: And they all said, And where is Yahuah (the Lord)’s kindness with our fathers, with Abraham, Isaac, end Jacob, that Yahuah (the Lord) has this day delivered us into the hands of the king of Egypt to contrive against us?
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Genesis 42:28 — *And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that Elohim (God) hath done unto us?* The restored silver and the very cry of Jasher 51:49 are the canon's own inn-scene, word for word.
cards.s_text: And the man was greatly afraid, and he said to his brethren, My money is restored, and lo, it is even in my sack, and the men were greatly afraid, and they said, What is this that Elohim (God) has done to us?
cards.t_text: And he said unto his brethren, My money is restored; and, lo, it is even in my sack: and their heart failed them, and they were afraid, saying one to another, What is this that Elohim (God) has done unto us?

cards.note: Genesis 34:24 — *And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.* The circumcision that left Shechem's men "sore" sets up the very smiting Joseph recalls in Jasher 51:32.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to them, That is the thing which I have spoken to you; you are spies, for you are come to slay the inhabitants of the land, for we heard that two of your brethren smote all the inhabitants of Shechem, in the land of Canaan, on account of your sister, and you now come to do the like in Egypt on account of your brother.
cards.t_text: And unto Hamor and unto Shechem his son hearkened all that went out of the gate of his city; and every male was circumcised, all that went out of the gate of his city.

cards.note: Genesis 34:25 — *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* The "two of your brethren smote Shechem... on account of your sister" that Joseph cites in Jasher 51:32 is this Genesis deed.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to them, That is the thing which I have spoken to you; you are spies, for you are come to slay the inhabitants of the land, for we heard that two of your brethren smote all the inhabitants of Shechem, in the land of Canaan, on account of your sister, and you now come to do the like in Egypt on account of your brother.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:6–7 — *And after that he set them free again, and detained Simeon alone and sent off his nine brothers. And he filled their sacks with corn, and he put their gold in their sacks, and they did not know.* The live Jubilees layer keeps Simeon detained and the gold secretly restored, as Jasher 51:37-45.
cards.s_text: And Joseph went out from them and came into the chamber, and wept a great weeping, for his pity was excited for them, and he washed his face, and returned to them again, and he took Simeon from them and ordered him to be bound, but Simeon was not willing to be done so, for he was a very powerful man and they could not bind him.
cards.t_text: And after that he set them free again, and detained Simeon alone and sent off his nine brothers.

cards.note: Genesis 42:19 — *If ye be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go ye, carry corn for the famine of your houses.* The order to confine one brother in prison while the rest carry corn home (Jasher 51:39, 46) is Joseph's third-day verdict in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to them, Seize this man and confine him in prison until his brethren come to him, and Joseph’s valiant men hastened and they all laid hold of Simeon to bind him, and Simeon gave a loud and terrible shriek and the cry was heard at a distance.
cards.t_text: If you be true men, let one of your brethren be bound in the house of your prison: go you, carry corn for the famine of your houses:

cards.note: Genesis 42:24 — *And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.* Joseph's chamber-weeping and the taking of Simeon in Jasher 51:37 is the canon's own turning-aside to weep.
cards.s_text: And Joseph went out from them and came into the chamber, and wept a great weeping, for his pity was excited for them, and he washed his face, and returned to them again, and he took Simeon from them and ordered him to be bound, but Simeon was not willing to be done so, for he was a very powerful man and they could not bind him.
cards.t_text: And he turned himself about from them, and wept; and returned to them again, and communed with them, and took from them Simeon, and bound him before their eyes.

cards.note: Genesis 37:28 — *Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.* "Having sold our brother" (Jasher 51:51) points back to this selling into Egypt that now stands ruling over them.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to them, Surely we are guilty sinners before Yahuah our Elohim (the Lord our God) in having sold our brother, our own flesh, and therefore do you say, Where is Yahuah’s kindness with our fathers?
cards.t_text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 37:26 — *And Yahudah (Judah) said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?* The sin Judah confesses in Jasher 51:51 was his own earlier counsel to sell rather than slay Joseph.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to them, Surely we are guilty sinners before Yahuah our Elohim (the Lord our God) in having sold our brother, our own flesh, and therefore do you say, Where is Yahuah’s kindness with our fathers?
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?

cards.note: Genesis 42:22 — *And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and ye would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.* Reuben's "said I not... do not sin against the lad" in Jasher 51:52 is verbatim the canon's Reuben.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to them, Said I not to you, do not sin against the lad, and you would not listen to me? now Elohim requires him from us, and how dare you say, Where is Yahuah’s kindness with our fathers, whilst you have sinned to Yahuah (the Lord)?
cards.t_text: And Reuben answered them, saying, Spake I not unto you, saying, Do not sin against the child; and you would not hear? therefore, behold, also his blood is required.

cards.note: Genesis 42:21 — *And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.* Judah's confession in Jasher 51:51 of guilt for selling their own flesh is the canon's own road-side reckoning.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to them, Surely we are guilty sinners before Yahuah our Elohim (the Lord our God) in having sold our brother, our own flesh, and therefore do you say, Where is Yahuah’s kindness with our fathers?
cards.t_text: And they said one to another, We are verily guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the anguish of his soul, when he besought us, and we would not hear; therefore is this distress come upon us.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:5 — *And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him, and he spake to them and questioned them, and he said to them: “Are you not spies, and have you not come to explore the approaches of the land?” And he put them in ward.* The live Jubilees layer carries the same recognition and spy-charge as Jasher 51:20-24.
cards.s_text: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but they knew him not, for Joseph was very great in their eyes, therefore they knew him not.
cards.t_text: And Joseph recognized them, but they did not recognize him, and he spake to them and questioned them, and he said to them: “Are you not spies, and have you not come to explore the approaches of the land?” And he put them in ward.

cards.note: Genesis 42:15 — *Hereby ye shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh ye shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.* The demand that the youngest be brought as proof, sworn by Pharaoh's life, matches Joseph's test in Jasher 51:33.
cards.s_text: Only hereby shall I know that you are true men; if you will send home one from amongst you to fetch your youngest brother from your father, and to bring him here to me, and by doing this thing I will know that you are right.
cards.t_text: Hereby you shall be proved: By the life of Pharaoh you shall not go forth hence, except your youngest brother come hither.

cards.note: Genesis 42:9 — *And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, Ye are spies; to see the nakedness of the land ye are come.* Joseph's spy-charge and "nakedness of the land" in Jasher 51:24 is the canon's own accusation.
cards.s_text: And Joseph again answered them and said, That is the thing which I spoke to you, you have come to spy through the land, therefore you all came through ten gates of the city; you have come to see the nakedness of the land.
cards.t_text: And Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed of them, and said unto them, You are spies; to see the nakedness of the land you are come.

cards.note: Genesis 42:8 — *And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.* Word for word the recognition of Jasher 51:20 — the brother they sold stands ruling, unrecognized.
cards.s_text: And Joseph saw his brethren, and he knew them, but they knew him not, for Joseph was very great in their eyes, therefore they knew him not.
cards.t_text: And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.

cards.note: *(Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)* (Jubilees 42:4). *And Jacob afterward heard that there was corn in Egypt, and he called to his sons to go to Egypt to buy corn, for upon them also did the famine prevail, and he called to his sons, saying,* (Jasher 51:1). Both witnesses put the same scene at the door of the reunion: Jacob hearing that there is food in Egypt and sending his sons down to buy it, because the famine had reached Canaan too. Jubilees adds the detail the whole testing turns on, that he sent ten and kept Benjamin home. The famine that drove the ten down was the same famine Joseph had been set over, so the sons of Jacob were walking toward the brother they had sold without knowing it. Benjamin being withheld is what gave Joseph the lever he would use to find out whether they had changed.
cards.s_text: And Jacob afterward heard that there was corn in Egypt, and he called to his sons to go to Egypt to buy corn, for upon them also did the famine prevail, and he called to his sons, saying,
cards.t_text: (Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)

cards.note: Genesis 42:4 — *But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure mischief befall him.* Jacob's fear in Jasher 51:5 that Benjamin meet the road-mischief of his brother is the very reason Genesis gives for keeping him home.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob went forth and they went to Egypt, and the sons of Jacob did all as their father had commanded them, and Jacob did not send Benjamin, for he said, Lest an accident might befall him on the road like his brother; and ten of Jacob’s sons went forth.
cards.t_text: But Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, Jacob sent not with his brethren; for he said, Lest peradventure mischief befall him.

cards.note: Genesis 42:3 — *And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.* Jasher 51:3-5 numbers the same ten brethren going down to buy corn in Egypt.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob hearkened to the voice of their father, and they rose up to go down to Egypt in order to buy corn amongst the rest that came there.
cards.t_text: And Joseph’s ten brethren went down to buy corn in Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 42:1 — *Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?* The same famine that opens Jasher 51:1 sends Jacob's sons down in the canon's own account.
cards.s_text: And Jacob afterward heard that there was corn in Egypt, and he called to his sons to go to Egypt to buy corn, for upon them also did the famine prevail, and he called to his sons, saying,
cards.t_text: Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do you look one upon another?

cards.note: Genesis 14:14 — *And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.* Abraham smiting the kings with a few men, recalled in Jasher 52:35, is the canon's own account of the rescue of Lot.
cards.s_text: For dost you not know, or have you not heard that which our Elohim did to Pharaoh when he took my mother Sarah, and what he did to Abimelech king of the Philistines on account of her, and also what our father Abraham did to the nine kings of Elam, how he smote them all with a few men that were with him?
cards.t_text: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.

cards.note: Genesis 34:25 — *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* The deed of Simeon and Levi that Jacob recalls in his letter (Jasher 52:36) is the Genesis scene at Shechem.
cards.s_text: And also what my two sons Simeon and Levi did to the eight cities of the Amorites, how they destroyed them on account of their sister Dinah?
cards.t_text: And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.

cards.note: Acts 7:12 — *But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.* Stephen retells the same sending for bread that Jacob commands in Jasher 52:10.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to them, And have you not seen how your children have been weeping over me this day, saying, Give to us bread, and there is none? now therefore return and buy for us a little food.
cards.t_text: But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.

cards.note: Psalm 105:17 — *He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:* The famine that bends the seed toward Egypt in Jasher 52:7 is the providence that set Joseph ahead of them.
cards.s_text: And in those days the famine was sore throughout the land, and all the people of the earth went and came to Egypt to buy food, for the famine prevailed greatly amongst them, and the sons of Jacob remained in Canaan a year and two months until their corn was finished.
cards.t_text: He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant:

cards.note: Psalm 105:16 — *Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.* The psalm reads the famine of Jasher 52:7 as Yahuah's own deliberate act.
cards.s_text: And in those days the famine was sore throughout the land, and all the people of the earth went and came to Egypt to buy food, for the famine prevailed greatly amongst them, and the sons of Jacob remained in Canaan a year and two months until their corn was finished.
cards.t_text: Moreover he called for a famine upon the land: he brake the whole staff of bread.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:4 — *(Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)* Jubilees opens the same famine and sending that drives Jasher 52:7.
cards.s_text: And in those days the famine was sore throughout the land, and all the people of the earth went and came to Egypt to buy food, for the famine prevailed greatly amongst them, and the sons of Jacob remained in Canaan a year and two months until their corn was finished.
cards.t_text: (Now the famine was very sore in the land of Canaan), and Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, and he sent his ten sons that they should procure food for him in Egypt; but Benjamin he did not send, and (the ten sons of Jacob) arrived (in Egypt) among those that went (there.)

cards.note: Genesis 15:14 — *And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.* The affliction Jacob fears in Jasher 52:26 is bounded by the same covenant's promise of judgment and deliverance.
cards.s_text: And Jacob rose up from his sons and spread forth his hands and he prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) on account of his sons, saying, O Yahuah Elohim (O Lord God) of heaven and earth, remember your covenant with our father Abraham, remember it with my father Isaac and deal kindly with my sons and deliver them not into the hands of the king of Egypt; do it I pray you O Elohim (God) for the sake of your mercies and redeem all my children and rescue them from Egyptian power, and send them their two brothers.
cards.t_text: And also that nation, whom they shall serve, will I judge: and afterward shall they come out with great substance.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The covenant Jacob pleads in Jasher 52:26 is the one that already foretold this going-down and the bondage to come.
cards.s_text: And Jacob rose up from his sons and spread forth his hands and he prayed to Yahuah (the Lord) on account of his sons, saying, O Yahuah Elohim (O Lord God) of heaven and earth, remember your covenant with our father Abraham, remember it with my father Isaac and deal kindly with my sons and deliver them not into the hands of the king of Egypt; do it I pray you O Elohim (God) for the sake of your mercies and redeem all my children and rescue them from Egyptian power, and send them their two brothers.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Genesis 43:14 — *And El Shaddai (God Almighty) give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.* Jacob's El Shaddai blessing in Jasher 52:23 is the patriarchal benediction the canon records.
cards.s_text: Now therefore rise up and go to the man, and take for him in your hands a present from what can be obtained in the land and bring it before him, and may El Shaddai (the Almighty God) give you mercy before him that he may send Benjamin and Simeon your brethren with you.
cards.t_text: And El Shaddai (God Almighty) give you mercy before the man, that he may send away your other brother, and Benjamin. If I be bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:18 — *And Reuben said: “Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, slay my two sons instead of his soul.” And he said to him He will not go with you."* Jubilees likewise records the firstborn's rejected surety before Judah's, matching Jasher 52:5.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
cards.t_text: And Reuben said: “Give him into my hand, and if I do not bring him back to you, slay my two sons instead of his soul.” And he said to him He will not go with you."

cards.note: Genesis 42:37 — *And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to thee: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to thee again.* Reuben's pledge of his two sons in Jasher 52:5 is the canon scene, word for word.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
cards.t_text: And Reuben spake unto his father, saying, Slay my two sons, if I bring him not to you: deliver him into my hand, and I will bring him to you again.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* Judah who bears the blame for his brother in Jasher 52:19 is the tribe of the sceptre, foreshadowing the Surety to come.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to Jacob his father, Give the lad into my care and we will rise up and go down to Egypt and buy corn, and then return, and it shall be when we return if the lad be not with us, then let me bear your blame forever.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Jubilees 43:13 — *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever.* Jubilees carries Judah's surety to its climax — offering himself a bondsman — the same pledge first given in Jasher 52:19.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to Jacob his father, Give the lad into my care and we will rise up and go down to Egypt and buy corn, and then return, and it shall be when we return if the lad be not with us, then let me bear your blame forever.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Genesis 43:5 — *But if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.* The condition Judah reports in Jasher 52:11 — no Benjamin, no audience — is the man's word in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Judah answered and said to his father, If you will send our brother with us we will go down and buy corn for you, and if you will not send him then we will not go down, for surely the king of Egypt particularly enjoined us, saying, You shall not see my face unless your brother be with you, for the king of Egypt is a strong and mighty king, and behold if we shall go to him without our brother we shall all be put to death.
cards.t_text: But if you will not send him, we will not go down: for the man said unto us, You shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.

cards.note: Genesis 44:32 — *For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.* Before Joseph's throne Judah makes good the very surety he gives in Jasher 52:19.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to Jacob his father, Give the lad into my care and we will rise up and go down to Egypt and buy corn, and then return, and it shall be when we return if the lad be not with us, then let me bear your blame forever.
cards.t_text: For your servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto you, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.

cards.note: Genesis 43:9 — *I will be surety for him; of my hand shalt thou require him: if I bring him not unto thee, and set him before thee, then let me bear the blame for ever:* Judah's pledge in Jasher 52:19 is the canon's own word, nearly verbatim.
cards.s_text: And Judah said to Jacob his father, Give the lad into my care and we will rise up and go down to Egypt and buy corn, and then return, and it shall be when we return if the lad be not with us, then let me bear your blame forever.
cards.t_text: I will be surety for him; of my hand shall you require him: if I bring him not unto you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame for ever:

cards.note: Jubilees 42:11–12 — *And he said: “My son will not go down with you lest perchance he fall sick; for their mother gave birth to two sons, and one has perished, and this one also you will take from me. If perchance he took a fever on the road, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to death.” For he saw that their money had been returned to every man in his sack, and for this reason he feared to send him.* Jasher 52:4 carries Jacob's same fear of losing the last son of Rachel.
cards.s_text: Now therefore my son shall not go down with you, for his brother is dead and he is left alone, and mischief may befall him by the way in which you go, as it befell his brother.
cards.t_text: And he said: “My son will not go down with you lest perchance he fall sick; for their mother gave birth to two sons, and one has perished, and this one also you will take from me. If perchance he took a fever on the road, you would bring down my old age with sorrow to death.”

cards.note: Jubilees 42:10 — *And Jacob said: “Me have you bereaved of my children! Joseph is not and Simeon also is not, and you will take Benjamin away. On me has your wickedness come.”* Jubilees records the same grieving father at the same moment as Jasher 52:5.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
cards.t_text: And Jacob said: “Me have you bereaved of my children! Joseph is not and Simeon also is not, and you will take Benjamin away. On me has your wickedness come.”

cards.note: Genesis 42:38 — *And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which ye go, then shall ye bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.* Jacob's refusal to send Benjamin in Jasher 52:5 is the same word given to Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Reuben said to his father, You shall slay my two sons if I do not bring your son and place him before you; and Jacob said to his sons, Abide you here and do not go down to Egypt, for my son shall not go down with you to Egypt, nor die like his brother.
cards.t_text: And he said, My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he is left alone: if mischief befall him by the way in the which you go, then shall you bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to the grave.

cards.note: Genesis 42:35 — *And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man’s bundle of money was in his sack: and when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.* The terror over the returned money in Jasher 52:1 is the canon scene retold.
cards.s_text: And they entered their house, and every man opened his sack and they saw and behold every man’s bundle of money was there, at which they and their father were greatly terrified.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass as they emptied their sacks, that, behold, every man’s bundle of money was in his sack: and when both they and their father saw the bundles of money, they were afraid.

cards.note: Jubilees 43:13 — *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever.* Jubilees keeps Judah's surety-plea that Jasher 53:31 begins, the same intercession before Joseph.
cards.s_text: And Judah said, What shall we say to our Lord, what shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves, Elohim has this day found the iniquity of all your servants, therefore has he done this thing to us this day.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* Judah stepping forward to speak and stand surety for his brethren in Jasher 53:31 foreshadows the sceptre-bearing tribe whose line runs to Shiloh the Messiah.
cards.s_text: And Judah said, What shall we say to our Lord, what shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves, Elohim has this day found the iniquity of all your servants, therefore has he done this thing to us this day.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Genesis 44:14 — *And Yahudah (Judah) and his brethren came to Joseph’s house; for he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.* The brethren coming to Joseph's house and standing before his throne in Jasher 53:29 is the canon's same return after the cup was found.
cards.s_text: And the men came to Joseph’s house, and they found Joseph sitting upon his throne, and all the mighty men standing at his right and left.
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) and his brethren came to Joseph’s house; for he was yet there: and they fell before him on the ground.

cards.note: Genesis 44:16 — *And Yahudah (Judah) said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? Elohim (God) hath found out the iniquity of thy servants: behold, we are my lord’s servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.* Judah's confession in Jasher 53:31 is the canon's own word, Elohim finding out the iniquity of the servants.
cards.s_text: And Judah said, What shall we say to our Lord, what shall we speak and how shall we justify ourselves, Elohim has this day found the iniquity of all your servants, therefore has he done this thing to us this day.
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) said, What shall we say unto my lord? what shall we speak? or how shall we clear ourselves? Elohim (God) has found out the iniquity of your servants: behold, we are my lord’s servants, both we, and he also with whom the cup is found.

cards.note: Jubilees 43:1 — *And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks for them with food and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin’s sack.* Jubilees narrates the same hidden cup that Jasher 53:23 sets in Benjamin's sack.
cards.s_text: At that time Joseph commanded his officer to fill their sacks with food, and to put each man’s money into his sack, and to put the cup in the sack of Benjamin, and to give them provision for the road, and they did so to them.
cards.t_text: And he did as Joseph had told him, and filled all their sacks for them with food and put their money in their sacks, and put the cup in Benjamin’s sack.

cards.note: Genesis 44:12 — *And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.* The cup found in Benjamin's bag in Jasher 53:27 is the canon's own discovery, eldest to youngest.
cards.s_text: And they hastened and each man brought down his sack from his ass, and they looked in their bags and the cup was found in Benjamin’s bag, and they all tore their garments and they returned to the city, and they smote Benjamin in the road, continually smiting him until he came into the city, and they stood before Joseph.
cards.t_text: And he searched, and began at the eldest, and left at the youngest: and the cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

cards.note: Genesis 44:2 — *And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.* The hiding of the cup in Benjamin's sack in Jasher 53:23 is the canon's silver-cup test verbatim.
cards.s_text: At that time Joseph commanded his officer to fill their sacks with food, and to put each man’s money into his sack, and to put the cup in the sack of Benjamin, and to give them provision for the road, and they did so to them.
cards.t_text: And put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, and his corn money. And he did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

cards.note: Genesis 44:1 — *And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.* Joseph's command to fill the sacks and return the money in Jasher 53:23 is the canon's same order to his steward.
cards.s_text: At that time Joseph commanded his officer to fill their sacks with food, and to put each man’s money into his sack, and to put the cup in the sack of Benjamin, and to give them provision for the road, and they did so to them.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the steward of his house, saying, Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put every man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:23 — *And they ate before him and he gave them all a portion, but the portion of Benjamin was seven times larger than that of any of theirs.* Jubilees, like Jasher 53:14, marks Benjamin's portion as far greater than his brothers' at Joseph's table.
cards.s_text: And Benjamin went up before Joseph and sat upon the throne, and the men beheld the acts of Joseph, and they were astonished at them; and the men ate and drank at that time with Joseph, and he then gave presents to them, and Joseph gave one gift to Benjamin, and Manasseh and Ephraim saw the acts of their father, and they also gave presents to him, and Osnath gave him one present, and they were five presents in the hand of Benjamin.
cards.t_text: And they ate before him and he gave them all a portion, but the portion of Benjamin was seven times larger than that of any of theirs.

cards.note: Genesis 43:34 — *And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.* Benjamin's heaped gifts in Jasher 53:14 echo the canon's fivefold portion at the same feast.
cards.s_text: And Benjamin went up before Joseph and sat upon the throne, and the men beheld the acts of Joseph, and they were astonished at them; and the men ate and drank at that time with Joseph, and he then gave presents to them, and Joseph gave one gift to Benjamin, and Manasseh and Ephraim saw the acts of their father, and they also gave presents to him, and Osnath gave him one present, and they were five presents in the hand of Benjamin.
cards.t_text: And he took and sent messes unto them from before him: but Benjamin’s mess was five times so much as any of theirs. And they drank, and were merry with him.

cards.note: Genesis 43:33 — *And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.* Joseph seating the brethren by their births in Jasher 53:12 is the canon's own astonishing arrangement.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to the men, I know by this cup that Reuben the first born, Simeon and Levi and Judah, Issachar and Zebulun are children from one mother, seat yourselves to eat according to your births.
cards.t_text: And they sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth: and the men marvelled one at another.

cards.note: Genesis 43:31 — *And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.* The washing of the face and refraining from weeping in Jasher 53:10 is the canon's same gesture before the meal.
cards.s_text: And when Joseph saw his brother, the son of his mother, he again wished to weep, and he entered the chamber, and he wept there, and he washed his face, and went out and refrained from weeping, and he said, Prepare food.
cards.t_text: And he washed his face, and went out, and refrained himself, and said, Set on bread.

cards.note: Genesis 43:30 — *And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.* Jasher 53:10's entering the chamber to weep over Benjamin matches Genesis exactly.
cards.s_text: And when Joseph saw his brother, the son of his mother, he again wished to weep, and he entered the chamber, and he wept there, and he washed his face, and went out and refrained from weeping, and he said, Prepare food.
cards.t_text: And Joseph made haste; for his bowels did yearn upon his brother: and he sought where to weep; and he entered into his chamber, and wept there.

cards.note: Genesis 43:29 — *And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother’s son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom ye spake unto me? And he said, Elohim (God) be gracious unto thee, my son.* Joseph's blessing over Benjamin in Jasher 53:9 is the canon's own line restored.
cards.s_text: And he lifted up his eyes and beheld his brother Benjamin, and he said, Is this your brother of whom you spoke to me? And Benjamin approached Joseph, and Joseph placed his hand upon his head and he said to him, May Elohim (God) be gracious to you my son.
cards.t_text: And he lifted up his eyes, and saw his brother Benjamin, his mother’s son, and said, Is this your younger brother, of whom you spake unto me? And he said, Elohim (God) be gracious unto you, my son.

cards.note: Jubilees 42:21 — *And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them: “Is this your youngest brother?” And they said to him: “It is he.” And he said: “Yahuah (God) be gracious to you, my son!”* Jubilees narrates the same arrival with Benjamin that Jasher 53:1 opens, the parallel patriarchal record.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob rose up and took Benjamin and the whole of the presents, and they went and came to Egypt and they stood before Joseph.
cards.t_text: And they went and stood before Joseph, and he saw Benjamin his brother, and he knew him, and said to them: “Is this your youngest brother?” And they said to him: “It is he.” And he said: “Yahuah (God) be gracious to you, my son!”

cards.note: Genesis 43:26 — *And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.* Judah leading Benjamin to bow before Joseph in Jasher 53:6 is the same obeisance the canon records, the dream fulfilled.
cards.s_text: And Judah took Benjamin by the hand, and they came before Joseph, and they bowed down to him to the ground.
cards.t_text: And when Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves to him to the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 43:15 — *And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.* The canon records the very descent Jasher 53:1 retells, Benjamin and the presents carried down to stand before Joseph.
cards.s_text: And the sons of Jacob rose up and took Benjamin and the whole of the presents, and they went and came to Egypt and they stood before Joseph.
cards.t_text: And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

cards.note: Genesis 14:15 — *And he divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.* The night-victory "in one night" Yahudah cites in Jasher 54:60 is Genesis's own account of Abram smiting the kings by night.
cards.s_text: Dost you not know or have you not heard that our father Abraham with his servant Eliezer smote all the kings of Elam with their hosts in one night, they left not one remaining? and ever since that day our father’s strength was given to us for an inheritance, for us and our seed forever.
cards.t_text: And he divided himself against them, he and his servants, by night, and smote them, and pursued them unto Hobah, which is on the left hand of Damascus.

cards.note: Genesis 14:14 — *And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.* Abraham's rescue Yahudah recalls in Jasher 54:60 is this Genesis muster of the fathers' strength.
cards.s_text: Dost you not know or have you not heard that our father Abraham with his servant Eliezer smote all the kings of Elam with their hosts in one night, they left not one remaining? and ever since that day our father’s strength was given to us for an inheritance, for us and our seed forever.
cards.t_text: And when Abram heard that his brother was taken captive, he armed his trained servants, born in his own house, three hundred and eighteen, and pursued them unto Dan.

cards.note: Genesis 45:28 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.* Jacob's resolve in Jasher 54:105 is the canon's own "It is enough... I will go and see him before I die."
cards.s_text: And Jacob said, It is enough for me that my son Joseph is still living, I will go and see him before I die.
cards.t_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) said, It is enough; Joseph my son is yet alive: I will go and see him before I die.

cards.note: Genesis 45:27 — *And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:* Jacob believing only when he saw what Joseph sent (Jasher 54:103) is the reviving of his spirit Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And Jacob heard all the words of his sons, and his heart palpitated at their words, for he could not believe them until he saw all that Joseph had given them and what he had sent him, and all the signs which Joseph had spoken to them.
cards.t_text: And they told him all the words of Joseph, which he had said unto them: and when he saw the wagons which Joseph had sent to carry him, the spirit of Jacob their father revived:

cards.note: Genesis 45:26 — *And told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob's heart fainted, for he believed them not.* Jacob's heart palpitating and his disbelief in Jasher 54:103 is the canon's own "his heart fainted, for he believed them not."
cards.s_text: And Jacob heard all the words of his sons, and his heart palpitated at their words, for he could not believe them until he saw all that Joseph had given them and what he had sent him, and all the signs which Joseph had spoken to them.
cards.t_text: And told him, saying, Joseph is yet alive, and he is governor over all the land of Egypt. And Jacob’s heart fainted, for he believed them not.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The covenant with Abraham that Yahudah trusts Elohim to remember in Jasher 54:7 is the same covenant that foretold the bondage in Egypt.
cards.s_text: Have you not heard what our Elohim (God) who made choice of us did to Pharaoh on account of Sarah our mother, whom he took away from our father, that he smote him and his household with heavy plagues, that even to this day the Egyptians relate this wonder to each other? so will our Elohim do to you on account of Benjamin whom you have this day taken from his father, and on account of the evils which you this day heap over us in your land; for our Elohim will remember his covenant with our father Abraham and bring evil upon you, because you have grieved the soul of our father this day.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Genesis 12:17 — *And Yahuah (LORD) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram's wife.* The plaguing of Pharaoh "on account of Sarah" that Yahudah cites in Jasher 54:7 is this Genesis scene.
cards.s_text: Have you not heard what our Elohim (God) who made choice of us did to Pharaoh on account of Sarah our mother, whom he took away from our father, that he smote him and his household with heavy plagues, that even to this day the Egyptians relate this wonder to each other? so will our Elohim do to you on account of Benjamin whom you have this day taken from his father, and on account of the evils which you this day heap over us in your land; for our Elohim will remember his covenant with our father Abraham and bring evil upon you, because you have grieved the soul of our father this day.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai Abram’s wife.

cards.note: Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* The crime rehearsed in Jasher 54:24 is the evil Elohim bent to keep the seed alive.
cards.s_text: And Joseph answered and said, There is no false judgment in the word that I spoke on account of your brother Joseph, for all of you sold him to the Midianites for twenty pieces of silver, and you all denied it to your father and said to him, An evil beast has devoured him, Joseph has been torn to pieces.
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Acts 7:9 — *And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,* The selling Joseph throws back at his brothers in Jasher 54:24 is the patriarchs' sin Stephen names.
cards.s_text: And Joseph answered and said, There is no false judgment in the word that I spoke on account of your brother Joseph, for all of you sold him to the Midianites for twenty pieces of silver, and you all denied it to your father and said to him, An evil beast has devoured him, Joseph has been torn to pieces.
cards.t_text: And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but Elohim (God) was with him,

cards.note: Genesis 37:28 — *Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.* Jasher 54:19 names the same twenty pieces of silver Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And Joseph answered, And why did you forsake your brother and sell him for twenty pieces of silver to this day, and why then will you not do the same to this your brother?
cards.t_text: Then there passed by Midianites merchantmen; and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 49:9 — *Yahudah (Judah) is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?* Yahudah roaring like a lion in Jasher 54:46 is the canon's own lion's-whelp blessing made vivid.
cards.s_text: And whilst they were fleeing, Judah and his brethren pursued them to the house of Pharaoh, and they all escaped, and Judah again sat before Joseph and roared at him like a lion, and gave a great and tremendous shriek at him.
cards.t_text: Yahudah (Judah) is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, you are gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?

cards.note: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.* Jasher 54:6 magnifies the very might Jacob blessed onto the sceptre-tribe.
cards.s_text: And I with my strength, who am greater and mightier than both of them, come this day upon you and your land if you are unwilling to send our brother.
cards.t_text: Yahudah (Judah), you are he whom your brethren shall praise: your hand shall be in the neck of your enemies; your father’s children shall bow down before you.

cards.note: Acts 7:13 — *And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph's kindred was made known unto Pharaoh.* Stephen rehearses the very making-known Jasher 54:69 dramatizes.
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph’s kindred was made known unto Pharaoh.
