cards.note: *And Joseph saw that they were all accordant in goodness one with another, and he could not refrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph.* (Jubilees 43:14). *And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.* (Jasher 54:69). Jubilees tells exactly when Joseph broke: when he saw that his brothers were all of one accord in goodness toward one another, he could not hold himself and told them who he was. Jasher gives the words, I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, and the comfort that came with them, that Elohim (God) had sent him ahead of them to keep them alive through the famine. He did not reveal himself to the men who had sold him; he waited until he saw them stand together for Benjamin, which was the opposite of what they had done to him. The test was whether they had changed, and when they had, the hidden brother showed his face.
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: And Joseph saw that they were all accordant in goodness one with another, and he could not refrain himself, and he told them that he was Joseph.

cards.note: Genesis 45:8 — *So now it was not you that sent me hither, but Elohim (God): and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.* Jasher 54:69 names the same hand: not the brothers but Elohim set Joseph before them.
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: So now it was not you that sent me hither, but Elohim (God): and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 45:7 — *And Elohim (God) sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.* The providence Jasher 54:69 confesses — Elohim sent him before them — kept the covenant seed alive through the famine.
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) sent me before you to preserve you a posterity in the earth, and to save your lives by a great deliverance.

cards.note: Genesis 45:3 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; doth my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.* Joseph's self-disclosure in Jasher 54:69 is the canon's own "I am Joseph."
cards.s_text: And Joseph observed all their acts, and said to them, Why do you look here and there? I am Joseph whom you sold to Egypt, now therefore let it not grieve you that you sold me, for as a support during the famine did Elohim send me before you.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I am Joseph; does my father yet live? And his brethren could not answer him; for they were troubled at his presence.

cards.note: *Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."* (Jubilees 43:13). *And Judah answered Joseph, saying, Surely you must know that I was security for the lad to his father, saying, If I brought him not to him I should bear his blame forever.* (Jasher 54:57). Jasher and Jubilees carry Yahudah's (Judah's) plea almost word for word: he had become surety for the lad to his father, and if he did not bring him back he would bear the blame for ever. Jubilees adds the offer that goes with it, let me stay as a bondsman in the boy's place and let the lad go home with his brothers. The brother who once proposed selling Joseph now offers himself as a slave so that Rachel's other son can go free. That is the change Joseph was waiting to see, and it is why the next thing in the story is Joseph weeping and telling them who he is.
cards.s_text: And Judah answered Joseph, saying, Surely you must know that I was security for the lad to his father, saying, If I brought him not to him I should bear his blame forever.
cards.t_text: Now rather let me, your servant, abide instead of the boy as a bondsman to my lord, and let the lad go with his brethren, for I became surety for him at the hand of your servant our father, and if I do not bring him back, your servant will bear the blame to our father for ever."

cards.note: Genesis 44:33 — *Now therefore, I pray thee, let thy servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.* Yahudah's offer in Jasher 54:58 to remain as a substitute for Benjamin is the canon's own substitution plea.
cards.s_text: Therefore have I approached you from amongst all my brethren, for I saw that you were unwilling to suffer him to go from you; now therefore may I find grace in your sight that you shall send him to go with us, and behold I will remain as a substitute for him, to serve you in whatever you desire, for wheresoever you shall send me I will go to serve you with great energy.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, I pray you, let your servant abide instead of the lad a bondman to my lord; and let the lad go up with his brethren.

cards.note: Genesis 44:32 — *For thy servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto thee, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.* The same surety-oath Jasher 54:57 puts in Yahudah's mouth before Joseph.
cards.s_text: And Judah answered Joseph, saying, Surely you must know that I was security for the lad to his father, saying, If I brought him not to him I should bear his blame forever.
cards.t_text: For your servant became surety for the lad unto my father, saying, If I bring him not unto you, then I shall bear the blame to my father for ever.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* While Jasher 55:35 has the seed learning Yahuah's law, the bitter bondage of Exodus is the affliction the elect line is about to enter.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was very aged, advanced in days, and his two sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, remained constantly in the house of Jacob, together with the children of the sons of Jacob their brethren, to learn the ways of Yahuah (the Lord) and his law.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 1:11 — *Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.* The multiplying of Jasher 55:36 is the very growth that draws the taskmasters once Joseph's generation passes.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and his sons dwelt in the land of Egypt in the land of Goshen, and they took possession in it, and they were fruitful and multiplied in it.
cards.t_text: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

cards.note: Acts 7:6 — *And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.* Stephen reads the same sojourn-and-bondage that begins as Jasher 55:36 settles the seed in Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and his sons dwelt in the land of Egypt in the land of Goshen, and they took possession in it, and they were fruitful and multiplied in it.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The Goshen settlement of Jasher 55:36 is the seed becoming the stranger Abraham was forewarned of.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and his sons dwelt in the land of Egypt in the land of Goshen, and they took possession in it, and they were fruitful and multiplied in it.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Exodus 1:7 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.* The fruitful-and-multiplied of Jasher 55:36 is the exact verse that opens Exodus and the bondage.
cards.s_text: And Jacob and his sons dwelt in the land of Egypt in the land of Goshen, and they took possession in it, and they were fruitful and multiplied in it.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

cards.note: Jubilees 45:11–12 — *And this was the first year of the fourth week of the forty-fifth jubilee. And Joseph took of the corn of the harvest the fifth part for the king and left four parts for them for food and for seed, and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt until this day.* Jubilees keeps the same fifth-part ordinance behind Joseph's gathering in Jasher 55:30.
cards.s_text: And Joseph purchased all the lands and fields of Egypt for bread on the account of Pharaoh, and Joseph supplied all Egypt with bread all the days of the famine, and Joseph collected all the silver and gold that came to him for the corn which they bought throughout the land, and he accumulated much gold and silver, besides an immense quantity of onyx stones, bdellium and valuable garments which they brought to Joseph from every part of the land when their money was spent.
cards.t_text: And Joseph took of the corn of the harvest the fifth part for the king and left four parts for them for food and for seed, and Joseph made it an ordinance for the land of Egypt until this day.

cards.note: Genesis 47:26 — *And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth part; except the land of the priests only, which became not Pharaoh's.* The famine purchase Jasher 55:30 narrates is the same Genesis transaction that ends in Pharaoh's fifth.
cards.s_text: And Joseph purchased all the lands and fields of Egypt for bread on the account of Pharaoh, and Joseph supplied all Egypt with bread all the days of the famine, and Joseph collected all the silver and gold that came to him for the corn which they bought throughout the land, and he accumulated much gold and silver, besides an immense quantity of onyx stones, bdellium and valuable garments which they brought to Joseph from every part of the land when their money was spent.
cards.t_text: And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt unto this day, that Pharaoh should have the fifth part; except the land of the priests only, which became not Pharaoh’s.

cards.note: Jubilees 45:6–7 — *And Joseph had given to his father and to his brothers as a gift the right of dwelling in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all the region round about, which he ruled over before Pharaoh. And Yashar'el (Israel) and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt; and Yashar'el (Israel) was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt, And Joseph nourished his father and his brethren and also their possessions with bread as much as sufficed them for the seven years of the famine.* Jubilees carries the same Goshen grant and the same hundred-and-thirtieth year Jasher 55:26 records.
cards.s_text: In the second year, that is in the hundred and thirtieth year of the life of Jacob, Joseph maintained his father and his brethren, and all his father’s household, with bread according to their little ones, all the days of the famine; they lacked nothing.
cards.t_text: And Joseph had given to his father and to his brothers as a gift the right of dwelling in the land of Goshen and in Rameses and all the region round about, which he ruled over before Pharaoh. And Yashar’el (Israel) and his sons dwelt in the land of Goshen, the best part of the land of Egypt; and Yashar’el (Israel) was one hundred and thirty years old when he came into Egypt,

cards.note: Genesis 47:7 — *And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.* Jacob blessing Pharaoh in Jasher 55:25 — the patriarch's blessing over the king of Egypt — stands in Genesis verbatim.
cards.s_text: And Jacob came and bowed down to Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and he then went out; and Jacob and all his sons, and all his household dwelt in the land of Goshen.
cards.t_text: And Joseph brought in Jacob his father, and set him before Pharaoh: and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Place your father and brethren in the best part of the land, withhold not from them all that is good, and cause them to eat of the fat of the land.* (Jasher 55:22). *The land of Egypt is before thee; in the best of the land make thy father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if thou knowest any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.* (Genesis 47:6). Pharaoh's grant in Jasher is the decree Genesis records, and Joseph's answer in the next verse of Jasher names Goshen just as Pharaoh names it here. The best of the land is given to shepherds out of Canaan by the king of Egypt, and it is given because of Joseph. Yahuah (the Lord) had sent him ahead to keep the family alive, and now the family is settled on the fat of the land by the word of the very throne whose successors would enslave their children.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, Place your father and brethren in the best part of the land, withhold not from them all that is good, and cause them to eat of the fat of the land.
cards.t_text: The land of Egypt is before you; in the best of the land make your father and brethren to dwell; in the land of Goshen let them dwell: and if you know any men of activity among them, then make them rulers over my cattle.

cards.note: Genesis 47:1 — *Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.* The report Jasher 55:19 has Joseph plan is Genesis word for word.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to his father and to his brethren, I will go up and tell Pharaoh, saying, My brethren and my father’s household and all belonging to them have come to me, and behold they are in the land of Goshen.
cards.t_text: Then Joseph came and told Pharaoh, and said, My father and my brethren, and their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have, are come out of the land of Canaan; and, behold, they are in the land of Goshen.

cards.note: *And Jacob said to Joseph, Now I will die cheerfully after I have seen your face, that you are still living and with glory.* (Jasher 55:16). *And Yashar'el (Israel) said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen thy face, because thou art yet alive.* (Genesis 46:30). Jacob says the same thing in both books, and he says it for the same reason. The face he had mourned as dead is in front of him, alive and in glory, and there is nothing left for this life to give him. Genesis has him ready to die having seen it; Jasher has him die cheerfully. A father who has his son back has nothing more to ask.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Joseph, Now I will die cheerfully after I have seen your face, that you are still living and with glory.
cards.t_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) said unto Joseph, Now let me die, since I have seen your face, because you are yet alive.

cards.note: *And behold Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept, and Joseph also embraced his father and kissed him, and they wept and all the people of Egypt wept with them.* (Jasher 55:15). *And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.* (Genesis 46:29). Jasher gives the meeting of Genesis in fuller motion: Jacob runs to Joseph and falls on his neck and kisses him, Joseph embraces and kisses his father, and all Egypt weeps with them. Genesis keeps the same falling on the neck and the long weeping, and adds the chariot made ready and the presenting of himself to Yashar'el (Israel) his father in Goshen. Twenty-two years of grief end on a neck in Goshen, and the next verse of Jasher gives Jacob's words, that now he can die cheerfully having seen Joseph's face.
cards.s_text: And behold Jacob ran and hastened to his son Joseph and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept, and Joseph also embraced his father and kissed him, and they wept and all the people of Egypt wept with them.
cards.t_text: And Joseph made ready his chariot, and went up to meet Yashar'el (Israel) his father, to Goshen, and presented himself unto him; and he fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a good while.

cards.note: Genesis 46:28 — *And he sent Yahudah (Judah) before him unto Joseph, to direct his face unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.* Genesis names the same sceptre-tribe Jasher 55:6 sends ahead to ready Goshen.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass when they came near Egypt, Jacob sent Judah before him to Joseph that he might show him a situation in Egypt, and Judah did according to the word of his father, and he hastened and ran and came to Joseph, and they assigned for them a place in the land of Goshen for all his household, and Judah returned and came along the road to his father.
cards.t_text: And he sent Yahudah (Judah) before him unto Joseph, to direct his face unto Goshen; and they came into the land of Goshen.

cards.note: *At that time Jacob commanded his sons and household to go to Egypt according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) to him, and Jacob rose up with his sons and all his household, and he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart, and they went to the land of Egypt.* (Jasher 55:5). *And Yashar’el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* (Jubilees 45:1). Jasher tells the going down: at the word of Yahuah (the Lord), Jacob rose with his sons and all his household and went out from Beersheba with joy and gladness of heart to the land of Egypt. Jubilees fixes the date of that same journey, the new moon of the fourth month in the year 2172, when Yashar'el (Israel) went into Goshen. One witness carries the heart of the old man leaving Canaan; the other carries the calendar, and together they set the beginning of the sojourn in Egypt on a day that can be counted.
cards.s_text: At that time Jacob commanded his sons and household to go to Egypt according to the word of Yahuah (the Lord) to him, and Jacob rose up with his sons and all his household, and he went out from the land of Canaan from Beersheba, with joy and gladness of heart, and they went to the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) went into the country of Egypt, 2172 A M. into the land of Goshen, on the new moon of the fourth month, in the second year of the third week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

cards.note: Genesis 46:4 — *I will go down with thee into Egypt; and I will also surely bring thee up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon thine eyes.* The descent of Jasher 55:2 carries the promise of the bringing-up — the visitation already pledged.
cards.s_text: Behold the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came to him, saying, Go down to Egypt with all your household and remain there, fear not to go down to Egypt for I will there make you a great nation.
cards.t_text: I will go down with you into Egypt; and I will also surely bring you up again: and Joseph shall put his hand upon your eyes.

cards.note: Genesis 46:3 — *And he said, I am Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of thy father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of thee a great nation:* The very word Jasher 55:2 puts on Yahuah's lips — fear not, go down, be made a great nation.
cards.s_text: Behold the word of Yahuah (the Lord) came to him, saying, Go down to Egypt with all your household and remain there, fear not to go down to Egypt for I will there make you a great nation.
cards.t_text: And he said, I am Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of your father: fear not to go down into Egypt; for I will there make of you a great nation:

cards.note: Genesis 47:28 — *And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole age of Jacob was an hundred forty and seven years.* Genesis gives the identical seventeen years and 147-year lifespan that opens Jasher 56:1.
cards.s_text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, and the years of his life were a hundred and forty seven years.
cards.t_text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years: so the whole age of Jacob was an hundred forty and seven years.

cards.note: Genesis 49:1 — *And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.* The gathering of the sons to be blessed in Jasher 56:6 is the deathbed assembly of Genesis 49.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said, Call all your children to me, and all the children of Jacob’s sons came and sat before him, and Jacob blessed them, and he said to them, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of your fathers shall grant you a thousand times as much and bless you, and may he give you the blessing of your father Abraham; and all the children of Jacob’s sons went forth on that day after he had blessed them.
cards.t_text: And Jacob called unto his sons, and said, Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last days.

cards.note: *And Jacob said to Joseph and to his sons, Behold I die, and the Elohim (God) of your ancestors will visit you, and bring you back to the land, which Yahuah (the Lord) sware to give to you and to your children after you, now therefore when I am dead, bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron in the land of Canaan, near my ancestors.* (Jasher 56:3). *And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,* (Genesis 49:29). The charge is the same charge. Jacob will not be buried in Egypt; he binds his sons to carry him to the cave at Machpelah where his fathers already lie. Jasher adds what the dying man says before the charge, that Elohim (God) will visit them and bring them back to the land Yahuah (the Lord) swore to give. The burial is the first step of that return, the father going home ahead of the children.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Joseph and to his sons, Behold I die, and the Elohim (God) of your ancestors will visit you, and bring you back to the land, which Yahuah (the Lord) sware to give to you and to your children after you, now therefore when I am dead, bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron in the land of Canaan, near my ancestors.
cards.t_text: And he charged them, and said unto them, I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite,

cards.note: Genesis 49:33 — *And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.* The death scene of Jasher 56:22, feet drawn into the bed and gathered to his people, is Genesis 49:33.
cards.s_text: And Jacob ceased commanding his sons, and he drew his feet into the bed, he died and was gathered to his people.
cards.t_text: And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.

cards.note: Jubilees 45:13 — *And Yashar'el (Israel) lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the days which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.* Jubilees keeps the same seventeen years and 147-year total that frames Jasher 56:1, with the deathbed blessing of the sons.
cards.s_text: And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, and the years of his life were a hundred and forty seven years.
cards.t_text: And Yashar’el (Israel) lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and all the days which he lived were three jubilees, one hundred and forty-seven years, and he died in the fourth year of the fifth week of the forty-fifth jubilee.

cards.note: Genesis 50:24 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.* The visitation Jacob promises in Jasher 56:3 is the same sworn deliverance Joseph repeats in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Joseph and to his sons, Behold I die, and the Elohim (God) of your ancestors will visit you, and bring you back to the land, which Yahuah (the Lord) sware to give to you and to your children after you, now therefore when I am dead, bury me in the cave which is in Machpelah in Hebron in the land of Canaan, near my ancestors.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.* Jacob's word that Judah shall reign over his brethren (Jasher 56:8) is the Genesis blessing of dominion over Judah.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Judah, I know my son that you are a mighty man for your brethren; reign over them, and your sons shall reign over their sons forever.
cards.t_text: Yahudah (Judah), you are he whom your brethren shall praise: your hand shall be in the neck of your enemies; your father’s children shall bow down before you.

cards.note: Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The everlasting reign Jacob gives Judah in Jasher 56:8 is the undeparting sceptre held until Shiloh.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Judah, I know my son that you are a mighty man for your brethren; reign over them, and your sons shall reign over their sons forever.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: Numbers 24:17 — *I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* The battle-ready ruler over his enemies in Jasher 56:9 is the Sceptre Balaam foresaw rising out of Israel.
cards.s_text: Only teach your sons the bow and all the weapons of war, in order that they may fight the battles of their brother who will rule over his enemies.
cards.t_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.

cards.note: Hebrews 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The forever-reign Jacob speaks over Judah in Jasher 56:8 lands on the Lord sprung from Judah.
cards.s_text: And Jacob said to Judah, I know my son that you are a mighty man for your brethren; reign over them, and your sons shall reign over their sons forever.
cards.t_text: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

cards.note: Genesis 50:2 — *And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Yashar'el (Israel).* Joseph's command to the doctors to embalm Jacob in Jasher 56:29 is the Genesis embalming verbatim.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after this that Joseph commanded his servants the doctors to embalm his father with myrrh and frankincense and all manner of incense and perfume, and the doctors embalmed Jacob as Joseph had commanded them.
cards.t_text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 50:3 — *And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.* The seventy days of weeping in Jasher 56:28 are the threescore and ten days the Egyptians mourned in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And also from the land of Canaan did the women come to Egypt when they heard that Jacob was dead, and they wept for him in Egypt for seventy days.
cards.t_text: And forty days were fulfilled for him; for so are fulfilled the days of those which are embalmed: and the Egyptians mourned for him threescore and ten days.

cards.note: Genesis 50:7 — *And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,* The caravan of Pharaoh's servants and the elders of Egypt going up in Jasher 56:34 is the Genesis burial procession.
cards.s_text: And all Egypt heard of Pharaoh’s proclamation, and they all rose up together, and all the servants of Pharaoh, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt went up with Joseph, and all the officers and nobles of Pharaoh went up as the servants of Joseph, and they went to bury Jacob in the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: And Joseph went up to bury his father: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,

cards.note: Genesis 50:10 — *And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.* The great mourning at the threshing floor of Atad beyond Jordan in Jasher 56:42 is the same Atad lamentation in Genesis.
cards.s_text: And Joseph went up with a heavy camp, and they did after this manner every day until they reached the land of Canaan, and they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which was on the other side of Jordan, and they mourned an exceeding great and heavy mourning in that place.
cards.t_text: And they came to the threshingfloor of Atad, which is beyond Jordan, and there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation: and he made a mourning for his father seven days.

cards.note: Genesis 50:13 — *For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.* Jacob buried by his sons in the cave of Machpelah that Abraham bought (Jasher 56:66) is the Genesis burial.
cards.s_text: And Jacob was buried in Hebron, in the cave of Machpelah which Abraham had bought from the sons of Heth for the possession of a burial place, and he was buried in very costly garments.
cards.t_text: For his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a possession of a buryingplace of Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

cards.note: Genesis 25:23 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto her, Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.* Esau standing against Jacob's sons at the cave (Jasher 56:50) plays out the two-nations division spoken from the womb.
cards.s_text: And they came to Kireath-arba, to the cave, and as they came Esau stood with his sons against Joseph and his brethren as a hindrance in the cave, saying, Jacob shall not be buried in it, for it belongs to us and to our father.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto her, Two nations are in your womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from your bowels; and the one people shall be stronger than the other people; and the elder shall serve the younger.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* Esau's claim on the cave against Jacob (Jasher 56:50) sets the very brothers Malachi distinguishes as loved and not chosen.
cards.s_text: And they came to Kireath-arba, to the cave, and as they came Esau stood with his sons against Joseph and his brethren as a hindrance in the cave, saying, Jacob shall not be buried in it, for it belongs to us and to our father.
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: Obadiah 10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* Esau cut down at the cave by Chushim in Jasher 56:64 prefigures Edom cut off for his violence against his brother Jacob.
cards.s_text: And he asked, saying, Why do you not bury the dead, and what is this great consternation? and they answered him the words of Esau and his sons; and he ran to Esau in the midst of the battle, and he slew Esau with a sword, and he cut off his head, and it sprang to a distance, and Esau fell amongst the people of the battle.
cards.t_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:21 — *By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.* The sons burying Jacob by force despite Esau (Jasher 56:65) carries out the faith of the dying Jacob the New Testament honors.
cards.s_text: And when Chushim did this thing the sons of Jacob prevailed over the sons of Esau, and the sons of Jacob buried their father Jacob by force in the cave, and the sons of Esau beheld it.
cards.t_text: By faith Jacob, when he was a dying, blessed both the sons of Joseph; and worshipped, leaning upon the top of his staff.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The grievous troubles Jacob foresees in the latter days (Jasher 56:20) are the affliction sworn to Abraham at the covenant of the pieces.
cards.s_text: For I know that many and grievous troubles will befall you in the latter days in the land, yea your children and children’s children, only serve Yahuah (the Lord) and he will save you from all trouble.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* The deliverance from affliction Jacob promises in Jasher 56:21 answers the new king of Exodus under whom the bondage begins.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass when you shall go after Elohim to serve him and will teach your children after you, and your children’s children, to know Yahuah (the Lord), then will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant from amongst your children, and Yahuah (the Lord) will deliver you through his hand from all affliction, and bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers to inherit it securely.
cards.t_text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* The servant Yahuah raises to bring them out of Egypt (Jasher 56:21) is Moses, who carries Joseph's bones at the visitation.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass when you shall go after Elohim to serve him and will teach your children after you, and your children’s children, to know Yahuah (the Lord), then will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant from amongst your children, and Yahuah (the Lord) will deliver you through his hand from all affliction, and bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers to inherit it securely.
cards.t_text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and you shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

cards.note: *And it shall come to pass when you shall go after Elohim to serve him and will teach your children after you, and your children’s children, to know Yahuah (the Lord), then will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant from amongst your children, and Yahuah (the Lord) will deliver you through his hand from all affliction, and bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers to inherit it securely.* (Jasher 56:21). *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* (Hebrews 11:22). Jacob dies foreseeing the bringing out of Egypt; Joseph dies foreseeing the same departing and gives commandment about his bones because of it. Hebrews counts Joseph's word as faith, and Jasher shows where the son heard it first: at his father's bed, hearing that Yahuah (the Lord) would raise up a servant from among their children and bring them back to the land of their fathers. Neither man saw it. Both died holding it.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass when you shall go after Elohim to serve him and will teach your children after you, and your children’s children, to know Yahuah (the Lord), then will Yahuah (the Lord) raise up to you and your children a servant from amongst your children, and Yahuah (the Lord) will deliver you through his hand from all affliction, and bring you out of Egypt and bring you back to the land of your fathers to inherit it securely.
cards.t_text: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:6 — *And he made them swear regarding his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring forth and bury him in the land of Canaan...* The latter-day troubles and visitation Jacob foretells in Jasher 56:20 are framed in Jubilees by Joseph's sworn oath over his bones as the affliction nears.
cards.s_text: For I know that many and grievous troubles will befall you in the latter days in the land, yea your children and children’s children, only serve Yahuah (the Lord) and he will save you from all trouble.
cards.t_text: And he made them swear regarding his bones, for he knew that the Egyptians would not again bring forth and bury him in the land of Canaan, for Mâkamârôn, king of Canaan, while dwelling in the land of Assyria, fought in the valley with the king of Egypt and slew him there, and pursued after the Egyptians to the gates of ’Êrmôn.

cards.note: Jubilees 38:14–15 — *And the sons of Edom have not got quit of the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob had imposed on them until this day. And these are the kings that reigned in Edom before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar’el (Israel) until this day in the land of Edom.* Jasher 57:40's vow to take a king 'from a strange land to this day' frames the same Edomite king-list Jubilees opens here.
cards.s_text: Therefore the sons of Esau swore, saying, From that day forward they would not choose a king from their brethren, but one from a strange land to this day.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Edom have not got quit of the yoke of servitude which the twelve sons of Jacob had imposed on them until this day.

cards.note: *And Bâlâq, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danâbâ.* (Jubilees 38:16). *And all the children of Esau took him and anointed him and they crowned him for a king, and they bowed down to him, and they said to him, May the king live, may the king live.* (Jasher 57:42). Jubilees gives the name and the city, Balaq the son of Beor reigning in Edom from Danaba. Jasher shows the crowning itself, the children of Esau anointing a king and bowing to him and shouting that the king should live. Edom had a throne and a shout of loyalty while the sons of Jacob were still a family of shepherds, and long before Yashar'el (Israel) asked for a king of its own. The elder brother built a kingdom first; it did not make him the heir.
cards.s_text: And all the children of Esau took him and anointed him and they crowned him for a king, and they bowed down to him, and they said to him, May the king live, may the king live.
cards.t_text: And Bâlâq, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Danâbâ.

cards.note: Genesis 36:31 — *And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The crowning of Bela in Jasher 57:42 begins the very Edomite kingship Genesis dates before Israel ever had a king.
cards.s_text: And all the children of Esau took him and anointed him and they crowned him for a king, and they bowed down to him, and they said to him, May the king live, may the king live.
cards.t_text: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 36:32 — *And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.* Jasher 57:41 names the same first king of Edom, Bela son of Beor, even fixing his city as Dinhabah exactly as Genesis does.
cards.s_text: And there was a man there from the people of Angeas king of Dinhabah; his name was Bela the son of Beor, who was a very valiant man, beautiful and comely and wise in all wisdom, and a man of sense and counsel; and there was none of the people of Angeas like to him.
cards.t_text: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

cards.note: *And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob.* (Jubilees 38:10). *And it came to pass after the battle, the children of Esau turned back and came home to Seir, and the children of Esau slew those who had remained in the land of the children of Seir; they slew also their wives and little ones, they left not a soul alive except fifty young lads and damsels whom they suffered to live, and the children of Esau did not put them to death, and the lads became their slaves, and the damsels they took for wives.* (Jasher 57:35). These are two layers of the same mountain. Jubilees shows the sons of Jacob pressing the sons of Esau hard in Seir and bowing their necks until they served Jacob's sons. Jasher shows what the sons of Esau did when they came home from battle to Seir: they slaughtered the Horites who were left, wives and little ones, and kept only fifty lads and damsels, the lads as slaves and the damsels as wives. The ones made servants of Jacob turned and made servants of others, and the land of Seir changed hands by the sword twice over. Esau's house was always strong against the weak and bowed before the brother it hated.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the battle, the children of Esau turned back and came home to Seir, and the children of Esau slew those who had remained in the land of the children of Seir; they slew also their wives and little ones, they left not a soul alive except fifty young lads and damsels whom they suffered to live, and the children of Esau did not put them to death, and the lads became their slaves, and the damsels they took for wives.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Jacob pressed hard upon the sons of Esau in the mountains of Seir, and bowed their necks so that they became servants of the sons of Jacob.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 2:22 — *As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day:* The canon's 'even unto this day' matches Jasher 57:37's 'to this day' — Esau possessing Seir in the Horites' stead.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau took all belonging in the land to the children of Seir, also their flocks, their bullocks and their goods, and all belonging to the children of Seir, did the children of Esau take, and the children of Esau dwelt in Seir in the place of the children of Seir to this day, and the children of Esau divided the land into divisions to the five sons of Esau, according to their families.
cards.t_text: As he did to the children of Esau, which dwelt in Seir, when he destroyed the Horims from before them; and they succeeded them, and dwelt in their stead even unto this day:

cards.note: Deuteronomy 2:12 — *The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Yashar'el (Israel) did unto the land of his possession, which Yahuah (LORD) gave unto them.* Moses records the exact dispossession Jasher 57:36 narrates — Esau destroying the Horim and dwelling in their stead in Seir.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau dwelt in Seir in the place of the children of Seir, and they inherited their land and took possession of it.
cards.t_text: The Horims also dwelt in Seir beforetime; but the children of Esau succeeded them, when they had destroyed them from before them, and dwelt in their stead; as Yashar'el (Israel) did unto the land of his possession, which Yahuah (LORD) gave unto them.

cards.note: Genesis 36:21 — *And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.* Jasher 57:37 has Esau seizing all that belonged to these very children of Seir the Horite in the land of Edom.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau took all belonging in the land to the children of Seir, also their flocks, their bullocks and their goods, and all belonging to the children of Seir, did the children of Esau take, and the children of Esau dwelt in Seir in the place of the children of Seir to this day, and the children of Esau divided the land into divisions to the five sons of Esau, according to their families.
cards.t_text: And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.

cards.note: Genesis 36:20 — *These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,* The children of Seir whom Esau dispossesses in Jasher 57:36 are the Horite house Genesis names as the land's first inhabitants.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau dwelt in Seir in the place of the children of Seir, and they inherited their land and took possession of it.
cards.t_text: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,

cards.note: Malachi 1:4 — *Whereas Edom saith, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom Yahuah (LORD) hath indignation for ever.* Esau settled and buried in Seir (Jasher 57:4) is the Edom on whom Yahuah's lasting indignation rests.
cards.s_text: And they came to Mount Seir and they buried Esau in Seir, but they had not brought his head with them to Seir, for it was buried in that place where the battle had been in Hebron.
cards.t_text: Whereas Edom says, We are impoverished, but we will return and build the desolate places; thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), They shall build, but I will throw down; and they shall call them, The border of wickedness, and, The people against whom Yahuah (LORD) has indignation for ever.

cards.note: Malachi 1:3 — *And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.* The flight of Esau's sons to the mountains of Seir with their father's body in Jasher 57:3 leads to the wasted heritage Malachi pronounces on Esau.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass when the sons of Jacob had taken Zepho and his people captive, all those that remained were greatly afraid of their lives from the house of Esau, lest they should also be taken captive, and they all fled with Eliphaz the son of Esau and his people, with Esau’s body, and they went on their road to Mount Seir.
cards.t_text: And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

cards.note: Genesis 36:8 — *Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.* Jasher 57:4 buries Esau in the very mount Seir that Genesis assigns to him as Edom.
cards.s_text: And they came to Mount Seir and they buried Esau in Seir, but they had not brought his head with them to Seir, for it was buried in that place where the battle had been in Hebron.
cards.t_text: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* The Esau-against-Jacob war of Jasher 57:1 stands inside the election divide Malachi names — the two brothers, the two heritages.
cards.s_text: And it was after this that the sons of Esau waged war with the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Esau fought with the sons of Jacob in Hebron, and Esau was still lying dead, and not buried.
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: *And Simeon and Benjamin and Enoch, Reuben’s son, went forth on the west side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father lying slain, as he had fallen on the hill which is in ’Adûrâm.* (Jubilees 38:8). *And the battle was heavy between them, and the sons of Esau were smitten before the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Jacob slew of the sons of Esau eighty men, and not one died of the people of the sons of Jacob; and the hand of Joseph prevailed over all the people of the sons of Esau, and he took Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and fifty of his men captive, and he bound them with chains of iron, and gave them into the hand of his servants to bring them to Egypt.* (Jasher 57:2). Both witnesses tell of the sons of Jacob prevailing over the sons of Esau in the country of Seir, but they are not the same battle. Jubilees tells the one in which Esau himself fell on the hill at Aduram, Simeon and Benjamin and Reuben's son Enoch going out from the west side of the tower and slaying four hundred of Edom and the Horites. Jasher tells the later war, when Joseph's hand prevailed, eighty of Esau's sons fell and not one of Jacob's, and Zepho was taken in iron chains to Egypt. The feud did not end with Esau's death; his grandchildren came back for more and were beaten again. The enmity between the two brothers' houses outlived both brothers.
cards.s_text: And the battle was heavy between them, and the sons of Esau were smitten before the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Jacob slew of the sons of Esau eighty men, and not one died of the people of the sons of Jacob; and the hand of Joseph prevailed over all the people of the sons of Esau, and he took Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and fifty of his men captive, and he bound them with chains of iron, and gave them into the hand of his servants to bring them to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Simeon and Benjamin and Enoch, Reuben’s son, went forth on the west side of the tower, and fifty (men) with them, and they slew of Edom and of the Horites four hundred men, stout warriors; and six hundred fled, and four of the sons of Esau fled with them, and left their father lying slain, as he had fallen on the hill which is in ’Adûrâm.

cards.note: Obadiah 1:18 — *And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for Yahuah (LORD) hath spoken it.* Joseph's hand prevailing over all the people of Esau in Jasher 57:2 is the flame of Joseph that devours Esau for stubble.
cards.s_text: And the battle was heavy between them, and the sons of Esau were smitten before the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Jacob slew of the sons of Esau eighty men, and not one died of the people of the sons of Jacob; and the hand of Joseph prevailed over all the people of the sons of Esau, and he took Zepho, the son of Eliphaz, the son of Esau, and fifty of his men captive, and he bound them with chains of iron, and gave them into the hand of his servants to bring them to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for Yahuah (LORD) has spoken it.

cards.note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* Esau lying dead and his sons smitten at Hebron in Jasher 57:1 is the brother-violence Obadiah indicts against Edom.
cards.s_text: And it was after this that the sons of Esau waged war with the sons of Jacob, and the sons of Esau fought with the sons of Jacob in Hebron, and Esau was still lying dead, and not buried.
cards.t_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.

cards.note: Malachi 1:3 — *And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.* The final answer to Edom's strong and lasting hatred of Jacob that Jasher 58:28 records — Esau set apart from the elect seed.
cards.s_text: But from that day forward the children of Esau hated the sons of Jacob, and the hatred and enmity were very strong between them all the days, to this day.
cards.t_text: And I hated Esau, and laid his mountains and his heritage waste for the dragons of the wilderness.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* Yahuah's word of election standing over the brother-enmity Jasher 58:28 fixes between Esau and Jacob.
cards.s_text: But from that day forward the children of Esau hated the sons of Jacob, and the hatred and enmity were very strong between them all the days, to this day.
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* The prophet's verdict on the very Esau-against-Jacob enmity Jasher 58:28 records as enduring to this day.
cards.s_text: But from that day forward the children of Esau hated the sons of Jacob, and the hatred and enmity were very strong between them all the days, to this day.
cards.t_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.

cards.note: Genesis 27:41 — *And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.* The root of the hatred Jasher 58:28 says grew very strong between Esau's children and Jacob's all the days.
cards.s_text: But from that day forward the children of Esau hated the sons of Jacob, and the hatred and enmity were very strong between them all the days, to this day.
cards.t_text: And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.

cards.note: Genesis 36:31 — *And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The heading over the very king-list — Bela, Jobab, Husham — whose deaths and reigns Jasher 58:20-29 unfolds as war-history.
cards.s_text: And of the people of Esau and the children of the east that were slain, there fell before the sons of Jacob about two hundred thousand men, and their king Bela the son of Beor fell with them in the battle, and when the children of Esau saw that their king had fallen in battle and was dead, their hands became weak in the combat.
cards.t_text: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 36:34 — *And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.* The same third king, Chusham of the land of Teman, whom Jasher 58:29 raises over Edom after Jobab's death.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after this, at the end of ten years, Jobab, the son of Zarach, from Botzrah, died, and the children of Esau took a man whose name was Chusham, from the land of Teman, and they made him king over them instead of Jobab, and Chusham reigned in Edom over all the children of Esau for twenty years.
cards.t_text: And Jobab died, and Husham of the land of Temani reigned in his stead.

cards.note: Genesis 36:33 — *And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.* Genesis names the very succession Jasher 58:26 narrates — Jobab the son of Zarach from Botzrah set up to reign over Edom after Bela's death.
cards.s_text: And when the children of Esau saw that their king had died in battle they hastened and took a man from the people of the children of the east; his name was Jobab the son of Zarach, from the land of Botzrah, and they caused him to reign over them instead of Bela their king.
cards.t_text: And Bela died, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigned in his stead.

cards.note: Genesis 36:32 — *And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.* The same Bela son of Beor, king of the children of Esau, whose fall Jasher 58:20 records in battle against the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: And of the people of Esau and the children of the east that were slain, there fell before the sons of Jacob about two hundred thousand men, and their king Bela the son of Beor fell with them in the battle, and when the children of Esau saw that their king had fallen in battle and was dead, their hands became weak in the combat.
cards.t_text: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:1 — *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* Jubilees tells the same multiplying-and-secure years of Jasher 58:13 — the seed growing into a nation while Joseph lives.
cards.s_text: And also all his brethren the sons of Jacob dwelt securely in the land, all the days of Joseph, and they were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly in the land, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, as their father Jacob had commanded them.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: Exodus 1:7 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.* The very increase Jasher 58:13 records of the sons of Jacob multiplying exceedingly in the land all the days of Joseph.
cards.s_text: And also all his brethren the sons of Jacob dwelt securely in the land, all the days of Joseph, and they were fruitful and multiplied exceedingly in the land, and they served Yahuah (the Lord) all their days, as their father Jacob had commanded them.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

cards.note: Acts 7:10 — *And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.* Stephen names the favor and wisdom and governorship that Jasher 58:11 says Yahuah gave Joseph over all the land.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was successful in all his ways, and Yahuah (the Lord) was with him, and Yahuah (the Lord) gave Joseph additional wisdom, and honor, and glory, and love toward him in the hearts of the Egyptians and throughout the land, and Joseph reigned over the whole country forty years.
cards.t_text: And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.

cards.note: Genesis 39:2 — *And Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.* The same refrain — Yahuah with Joseph, prospering all his ways — that Jasher 58:11 carries into his forty-year reign over Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was successful in all his ways, and Yahuah (the Lord) was with him, and Yahuah (the Lord) gave Joseph additional wisdom, and honor, and glory, and love toward him in the hearts of the Egyptians and throughout the land, and Joseph reigned over the whole country forty years.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees opens the same Egyptian affliction that begins in Jasher 59:28.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Acts 7:6 — *And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.* Stephen preaches the very bondage-foretelling that opens in Jasher 59:28.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years.* The bondage that begins in Jasher 59:28 was sworn to Abraham long before, the affliction foretold and counted.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Exodus 1:11 — *Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.* The rule-over-Israel of Jasher 59:28 hardens into the taskmasters and burdens Exodus names.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

cards.note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* The Egyptians beginning to rule over Israel in Jasher 59:28 is the same turn Exodus marks with the new king who knew not Joseph.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Joseph, all the Egyptians began in those days to rule over the children of Israel, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, who reigned in his father’s stead, took all the laws of Egypt and conducted the whole government of Egypt under his counsel, and he reigned securely over his people.
cards.t_text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:3 — *And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.* Jubilees gives the same hundred-and-ten-year reckoning of Joseph's life that Jasher 59:26 records at his death.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was one hundred and ten years old when he died in the land of Egypt, and all his brethren and all his servants rose up and they embalmed Joseph, as was their custom, and his brethren and all Egypt mourned over him for seventy days.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died being a hundred and ten years old; seventeen years he lived in the land of Canaan, and ten years he was a servant, and three years in prison, and eighty years he was under the king, ruling all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 1:6 — *And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.* Joseph's death in Jasher 59:25 is the hinge Exodus uses to turn from the patriarchs to the bondage.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after this that Joseph died in that year, the seventy-first year of the Israelites going down to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

cards.note: Genesis 50:26 — *So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.* The hundred-and-ten-year death and embalming of Jasher 59:26 is the closing verse of Genesis itself.
cards.s_text: And Joseph was one hundred and ten years old when he died in the land of Egypt, and all his brethren and all his servants rose up and they embalmed Joseph, as was their custom, and his brethren and all Egypt mourned over him for seventy days.
cards.t_text: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:5 — *And he commanded the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* Jubilees records the very bones-charge Joseph swears the seed to in Jasher 59:24.
cards.s_text: And Joseph made the sons of Israel to swear for their seed after them, saying, Elohim will surely visit you and you shall bring up my bones with you from here.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:22 — *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* The dying word and bone-commandment of Jasher 59:22 is the faith the writer of Hebrews honours.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to his brethren and to the whole of his father’s household, Behold I die, and Elohim (God) will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land which he swore to your fathers to give to them.
cards.t_text: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.

cards.note: Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* The charge Joseph gives in Jasher 59:23 is fulfilled when Moses lifts the bones at the Exodus.
cards.s_text: And it shall be when Elohim shall visit you to bring you up from here to the land of your fathers, then bring up my bones with you from here.
cards.t_text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and you shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

cards.note: Genesis 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* The bones-oath Joseph binds in Jasher 59:24 is the same oath Genesis records.
cards.s_text: And Joseph made the sons of Israel to swear for their seed after them, saying, Elohim will surely visit you and you shall bring up my bones with you from here.
cards.t_text: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from hence.

cards.note: Genesis 50:24 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.* Joseph's dying declaration of the visitation in Jasher 59:22 reproduces this Genesis charge nearly word for word.
cards.s_text: And Joseph said to his brethren and to the whole of his father’s household, Behold I die, and Elohim (God) will surely visit you and bring you up from this land to the land which he swore to your fathers to give to them.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

cards.note: Acts 7:14 — *Then sent Joseph, and called his father Jacob to him, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.* Stephen rehearses the very household-of-Jacob that Jasher 59:19 numbers in Egypt.
cards.s_text: And all the souls that went forth from the loins of Jacob, were seventy souls; these are they who came with Jacob their father to Egypt to dwell there: and Joseph and all his brethren dwelt securely in Egypt, and they ate of the best of Egypt all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: *And all the souls that went forth from the loins of Jacob, were seventy souls; these are they who came with Jacob their father to Egypt to dwell there: and Joseph and all his brethren dwelt securely in Egypt, and they ate of the best of Egypt all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jasher 59:19). *And all the souls that came out of the loins of Jacob were seventy souls: for Joseph was in Egypt already.* (Exodus 1:5). Jasher closes its roll of the family with the same seventy souls Exodus opens with, counted the same way, from the loins of Jacob. The number is the seed of promise as it stood going down into Egypt, a household small enough to name one by one. Exodus turns the page and says they multiplied until the land was filled with them; Jasher ends the sentence with them eating of the best of Egypt all the days of Joseph. Both books want the reader to see how few they were before they became a people.

cards.note: Genesis 46:27 — *And the sons of Joseph, which were born him in Egypt, were two souls: all the souls of the house of Jacob, which came into Egypt, were threescore and ten.* The seventy-soul total of Jasher 59:19 is lifted straight from the Genesis census.

cards.note: Exodus 1:1 — *Now these are the names of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which came into Egypt; every man and his household came with Jacob.* Exodus opens its bondage account with the same muster-formula Jasher 59:1 uses to head the chapter.

cards.note: *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* (Jubilees 46:1). *In that year, being the seventy-ninth year of the Israelites going down to Egypt, died Reuben the son of Jacob, in the land of Egypt; Reuben was a hundred and twenty-five years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.* (Jasher 62:1). Jasher counts this season by funerals, and here it is Reuben, dead at a hundred and twenty-five in the seventy-ninth year of the going down, put into a coffin and left in his children's keeping. Jubilees counts the same season by the living: after Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied in Egypt and became a great nation, brother loving brother, for ten weeks of years, all the days of Joseph. The fathers were being laid in coffins one by one while the seed grew into a people in a land that was not theirs. Both things were happening at once, and both had been told to Abram beforehand.

cards.note: Genesis 36:35 — *And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.* Jasher 62 expands this one verse into the full campaign — Hadad son of Bedad smiting Midian in the field of Moab, exactly as Genesis records it.

cards.note: *And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.* (Jubilees 46:8). *And it came to pass at that time that Judah the son of Jacob died in Egypt, in the eighty-sixth year of Jacob’s going down to Egypt, and Judah was a hundred and twenty-nine years old at his death, and they embalmed him and put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.* (Jasher 62:23). Jubilees says it in one breath: Joseph died and was buried in Egypt, and his brethren died after him. Jasher spreads that one breath across a roll of dated deaths, and this entry is Yahudah (Judah), a hundred and twenty-nine years old in the eighty-sixth year of the going down, embalmed and put into a coffin and given to his children. The embalming and the coffin were not Egyptian vanity. The fathers were being kept, not buried, because the family knew they were going home and the bones were going with them.
