cards.note: Exodus 1:6 — *And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.* Jasher 62 unfolds this single verse into a year-by-year roll-call of the brothers' deaths in Egypt.
cards.s_text: In that year, being the seventy-ninth year of the Israelites going down to Egypt, died Reuben the son of Jacob, in the land of Egypt; Reuben was a hundred and twenty-five years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin, and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

cards.note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* The prophetic word over the Edom/Esau line whose kings Jasher 63:16 sets among the nations.
cards.s_text: And Zepho also sent a letter to the land of Edom to Hadad the son of Bedad king of Edom and to all the children of Esau, saying,
cards.t_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* the election that sets apart the children of Esau (Jasher 63:16) from the chosen seed.
cards.s_text: And Zepho also sent a letter to the land of Edom to Hadad the son of Bedad king of Edom and to all the children of Esau, saying,
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: Genesis 36:32 — *And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.* The very 'Bela the first king' of Edom whom Jasher 63:19 names as the founder of Esau's covenant of peace.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau sent a letter to the children of Chittim and to Zepho their king, saying, We cannot fight against Angeas and his people for a covenant of peace has been between us these many years, from the days of Bela the first king, and from the days of Joseph the son of Jacob king of Egypt, with whom we fought on the other side of Jordan when he buried his father.
cards.t_text: And Bela the son of Beor reigned in Edom: and the name of his city was Dinhabah.

cards.note: Genesis 36:31 — *And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The Edomite kingship Jasher 63:19 dates 'from the days of Bela the first king' is the canon's record of Edom's kings before Israel's.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau sent a letter to the children of Chittim and to Zepho their king, saying, We cannot fight against Angeas and his people for a covenant of peace has been between us these many years, from the days of Bela the first king, and from the days of Joseph the son of Jacob king of Egypt, with whom we fought on the other side of Jordan when he buried his father.
cards.t_text: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Jubilees 46:5 — *And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.* The same bones-oath that frames the fathers' burials in Jasher 63:1.
cards.s_text: And in the ninety-third year died Levi, the son of Jacob, in Egypt, and Levi was a hundred and thirty-seven years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And he commanded the children of Yashar’el (Israel) before he died that they should carry his bones with them when they went forth from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:22 — *By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.* The faith that keeps a coffin against the visitation, of which Levi's coffin (Jasher 63:1) is one.
cards.s_text: And in the ninety-third year died Levi, the son of Jacob, in Egypt, and Levi was a hundred and thirty-seven years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: By faith Joseph, when he died, made mention of the departing of the children of Yashar'el (Israel); and gave commandment concerning his bones.

cards.note: Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* The fathers' coffins Jasher 63:1 records are the bones carried up at the visitation.
cards.s_text: And in the ninety-third year died Levi, the son of Jacob, in Egypt, and Levi was a hundred and thirty-seven years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and you shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

cards.note: Genesis 50:26 — *So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.* Joseph's coffin in Egypt mirrors Levi laid in a coffin and given to his children (Jasher 63:1).
cards.s_text: And in the ninety-third year died Levi, the son of Jacob, in Egypt, and Levi was a hundred and thirty-seven years old when he died, and they put him into a coffin and he was given into the hands of his children.
cards.t_text: So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

cards.note: Acts 7:6 — *And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.* The bondage Jasher 63:8 says was 'from Yahuah' to teach Israel His wonders is the sojourn foretold to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And in order to know the signs and mighty wonders which Yahuah (the Lord) would do in Egypt on account of his people Israel, in order that the children of Israel might fear Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of their ancestors, and walk in all his ways, they and their seed after them all the days.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

cards.note: *And this was also from Yahuah (the Lord), for the children of Israel, to benefit them in their latter days, in order that all the children of Israel might know Yahuah their Elohim (the Lord their God).* (Jasher 63:7). *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* (Genesis 50:20). Joseph said it of his brothers' betrayal, that they meant evil and Elohim (God) meant good; Jasher says the same of the bondage itself. The Egyptians embittered the lives of the sons of Jacob out of ingratitude, having forgotten who fed them in the famine, and yet Jasher names the affliction as being from Yahuah (the Lord), set for the good of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in their latter days. The purpose was that they would know him. Hard labor under a king who did not know Joseph was the ground in which a people learned the name of the Elohim (God) of their fathers.
cards.s_text: And this was also from Yahuah (the Lord), for the children of Israel, to benefit them in their latter days, in order that all the children of Israel might know Yahuah their Elohim (the Lord their God).
cards.t_text: But as for you, you thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:13 — *“Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”* The same forgetting-king's counsel to afflict the seed Jasher 63:6 records.
cards.s_text: Therefore all Egypt began from that day forth to embitter the lives of the sons of Jacob, and to afflict them with all manner of hard labor, because they had not known their ancestors who had delivered them in the days of the famine.
cards.t_text: “Behold the people of the children of Yashar’el (Israel) have increased and multiplied more than we. Come and let us deal wisely with them before they become too many, and let us afflict them with slavery before war come upon us and before they too fight against us; else they will join themselves to our enemies and get them up out of our land, for their hearts and faces are towards the land of Canaan.”

cards.note: Acts 7:19 — *The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.* The embittering Jasher 63:6 says began 'from that day forth' against the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: Therefore all Egypt began from that day forth to embitter the lives of the sons of Jacob, and to afflict them with all manner of hard labor, because they had not known their ancestors who had delivered them in the days of the famine.
cards.t_text: The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.

cards.note: Acts 7:18 — *Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.* Stephen names the same risen generation Jasher 63:5 describes as not knowing the sons of Jacob.
cards.s_text: And another generation rose up in their stead, which had not known the sons of Jacob and all the good which they had done to them, and all their might in Egypt.
cards.t_text: Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* Jasher 63:4 names him Melol son of the dead Pharaoh, the generation that knew Joseph having passed.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass in those days, in the hundred and second year of Israel’s going down to Egypt, that Pharaoh king of Egypt died, and Melol his son reigned in his stead, and all the mighty men of Egypt and all that generation which knew Joseph and his brethren died in those days.
cards.t_text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees tells the same affliction after Joseph's generation passed that Jasher 63:3 records.
cards.s_text: And the hand of all Egypt became more grievous in those days against the children of Israel, and the Egyptians injured the Israelites until the children of Israel were wearied of their lives on account of the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* the affliction 'from that day to the day of their going forth' (Jasher 63:2) is the bondage foretold to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Levi, when all Egypt saw that the sons of Jacob the brethren of Joseph were dead, all the Egyptians began to afflict the children of Jacob, and to embitter their lives from that day to the day of their going forth from Egypt, and they took from their hands all the vineyards and fields which Joseph had given to them, and all the elegant houses in which the people of Israel lived, and all the fat of Egypt, the Egyptians took all from the sons of Jacob in those days.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The same embittering Jasher reports that wearied Israel of their lives (Jasher 63:3).
cards.s_text: And the hand of all Egypt became more grievous in those days against the children of Israel, and the Egyptians injured the Israelites until the children of Israel were wearied of their lives on account of the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 1:6 — *And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.* The canon marks the very hinge Jasher names — once the brethren of Joseph were dead, Egypt turned on Israel (Jasher 63:2).
cards.s_text: And it came to pass after the death of Levi, when all Egypt saw that the sons of Jacob the brethren of Joseph were dead, all the Egyptians began to afflict the children of Jacob, and to embitter their lives from that day to the day of their going forth from Egypt, and they took from their hands all the vineyards and fields which Joseph had given to them, and all the elegant houses in which the people of Israel lived, and all the fat of Egypt, the Egyptians took all from the sons of Jacob in those days.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

cards.note: Jude 1:11 — *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.* Jude names the error of Balaam for reward — the hired counsel against the seed that fails in Balaam's hand in Jasher 64:28.
cards.s_text: And Balaam rose up and tried the are of divination, and he was skillful in the knowledge of it, but he was confused and the work was destroyed in his hand.
cards.t_text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

cards.note: 2 Peter 2:15 — *Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness;* The hireling diviner of Jasher 64:28 is the very way of Balaam the NT marks as the road of those who love the wages of unrighteousness.
cards.s_text: And Balaam rose up and tried the are of divination, and he was skillful in the knowledge of it, but he was confused and the work was destroyed in his hand.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 23:5 — *Nevertheless Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) would not hearken unto Balaam; but Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) loved thee.* Yahuah confounding Balaam in Jasher 64:29 is the same love-driven turning the canon records over Israel.
cards.s_text: And he tried it again but it did not succeed, and Balaam despaired of it and left it and did not complete it, for this was from Yahuah (the Lord), in order to cause Zepho and his people to fall into the hand of the children of Israel, who had trusted in Yahuah (the Lord), the Elohim (God) of their ancestors, in their war.

cards.note: Numbers 23:23 — *Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Yashar'el (Israel): according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Yashar'el (Israel), What hath Elohim (God) wrought!* The canon's verdict is Jasher 64:29's whole point — the divination is destroyed in Balaam's hand because no enchantment stands against the seed.
cards.s_text: And he tried it again but it did not succeed, and Balaam despaired of it and left it and did not complete it, for this was from Yahuah (the Lord), in order to cause Zepho and his people to fall into the hand of the children of Israel, who had trusted in Yahuah (the Lord), the Elohim (God) of their ancestors, in their war.
cards.t_text: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Yashar'el (Israel): according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Yashar'el (Israel), What has Elohim (God) wrought!

cards.note: Numbers 22:5 — *He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me:* The same Balaam son of Beor hired against Israel is the diviner Zepho summons in Jasher 64:27.
cards.s_text: And Zepho said to Balaam, Try by divination for us that we may know who will prevail in the battle, we or the Egyptians.

cards.note: Malachi 1:2 — *I have loved you, saith Yahuah (LORD). Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob's brother? saith Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,* As the children of Esau gather to war in Jasher 64:14, Malachi declares the election that set Jacob's line apart from Esau's.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau hearkened to the words of Zepho, and the children of Esau gathered themselves together, a very great people, and they went to assist Zepho and the children of Chittim in battle.
cards.t_text: I have loved you, says Yahuah (LORD). Yet you say, Wherein have you loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? says Yahuah (LORD): yet I loved Jacob,

cards.note: Obadiah 1:10 — *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.* Edom's vow in Jasher 64:13 to avenge his cause against the children of Jacob is the very violence against his brother Obadiah indicts.
cards.s_text: Now then if you are willing to come to me to assist me in fighting against them and Egypt, then shall we avenge the cause of our brethren.
cards.t_text: For your violence against your brother Jacob shame shall cover you, and you shall be cut off for ever.

cards.note: Genesis 36:8 — *Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.* Genesis already set Esau-Edom apart from the elect line, the house whose cause Zepho rises to avenge in Jasher 64:9.
cards.s_text: And Zepho considered to go to fight against them and all Egypt, to avenge the cause of his brethren the children of Esau, whom Joseph with his brethren and all Egypt had smitten in the land of Canaan, when they went up to bury Jacob in Hebron.
cards.t_text: Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 24:13 — *As saith the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceedeth from the wicked: but mine hand shall not be upon thee.* The very proverb Jasher 64:5 quotes over Zepho and the wicked children of Esau is the ancient canon proverb David spoke.
cards.s_text: But Zepho remembered not Yahuah (the Lord) and considered not that Yahuah (the Lord) had helped him in battle, and that he had delivered him and his people from the hand of the king of Africa, but still walked in the ways of the children of Chittim and the wicked children of Esau, to serve other gods which his brethren the children of Esau had taught him; it is therefore said, From the wicked goes forth wickedness.
cards.t_text: As says the proverb of the ancients, Wickedness proceeds from the wicked: but my hand shall not be upon you.

cards.note: *And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.* (Jubilees 46:8). *For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.* (Jasher 64:8). The death of Joseph and his brethren was not only a grief inside Yashar'el (Israel); it was a signal outside it. Jasher shows Zepho, Esau's grandson, hearing that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren were dead, and that only their children remained, and that is when he moved. Jubilees gives the deaths plainly, Joseph in the forty-sixth jubilee and his brethren after him. Enemies wait for the generation of the fathers to pass before they come against the children, and the king who knew not Joseph was of the same mind as Zepho.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died in the forty-sixth jubilee, in the sixth week, in the second year, and they buried him in the land of Egypt, and his brethren died after him.

cards.note: Exodus 1:7 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.* The seed kept and multiplying in Egypt is the canon backdrop to Jasher 64:8's note that all their children remained in Egypt.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

cards.note: Exodus 1:6 — *And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.* Exodus' own seam matches Jasher 64:8 word for word — Joseph and his brethren dead, the generation passed.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph died, and all his brethren, and all that generation.

cards.note: Genesis 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* The oath over Joseph's bones is the canon promise that frames the death Jasher 64:8 records.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from hence.

cards.note: Genesis 50:24 — *And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.* Joseph's dying word of the promised visitation stands behind Jasher 64:8's report that Joseph and his brethren were dead.
cards.s_text: For Zepho heard that the mighty men of Egypt were dead and that Joseph and his brethren the sons at Jacob were dead, and that all their children the children of Israel remained in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Joseph said unto his brethren, I die: and Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land unto the land which he sware to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees carries the same paradox of Jasher 65:38 — rigour breeds growth.
cards.s_text: And all the work wherein the Egyptians made the children of Israel labor, they exacted with rigor, in order to afflict the children of Israel, but the more they afflicted them, the more they increased and grew, and the Egyptians were grieved because of the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: Exodus 1:12 — *But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* the identical reversal of Jasher 65:38: affliction only increases the seed.
cards.s_text: And all the work wherein the Egyptians made the children of Israel labor, they exacted with rigor, in order to afflict the children of Israel, but the more they afflicted them, the more they increased and grew, and the Egyptians were grieved because of the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Acts 7:6 — *And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.* Stephen names the bondage of Jasher 65 as the very thing Elohim had foretold to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And the children of Israel built Pithom and Rameses, and all the children of Israel did the work, some making bricks, and some building, and the children of Israel built and fortified all the land of Egypt and its walls, and the children of Israel were engaged in work for many years, until the time came when Yahuah (the Lord) remembered them and brought them out of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* the affliction Jasher 65:31 says lasted 'many years' was promised to Abraham beforehand.
cards.s_text: And the children of Israel built Pithom and Rameses, and all the children of Israel did the work, some making bricks, and some building, and the children of Israel built and fortified all the land of Egypt and its walls, and the children of Israel were engaged in work for many years, until the time came when Yahuah (the Lord) remembered them and brought them out of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* (Jubilees 46:14). *Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.* (Jasher 65:8). Jasher records the counsel that proposed the work: Pithom and Rameses stood unfortified against battle, and the Egyptians said it behooved them to build and fortify. Jubilees records the work itself: taskmasters set over the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and the strong cities Pithom and Raamses built for Pharaoh, with all the walls and fortifications that had fallen. The one book gives the plan and the other gives the labour, and the same two cities stand at the centre of both. The fortifying Jasher's counsellors called for is the fortification Jubilees says Yashar'el (Israel) raised with their own hands under the taskmasters.
cards.s_text: Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.s_text: And the Egyptians embittered the lives of the children of Israel with hard work, in mortar and bricks, and also in all manner of work in the field.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.s_text: And the hands of the men of Egypt were directed with continued severity against the children of Israel in that work, and the Egyptians made the children of Israel work with rigor.
cards.t_text: And the Egyptians made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to serve with rigour:

cards.note: Exodus 1:11 — *Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.* the same two cities Jasher 65:8 names as the pretext for the bondage.
cards.s_text: Behold in the land are Pithom and Rameses, cities unfortified against battle, it behooves you and us to build them, and to fortify them.

cards.note: *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* (Jubilees 46:15). *And when they ploughed they were unable to hurt the infants of the children of Israel, so the people increased and waxed exceedingly.* (Jasher 67:59). Jubilees gives the rule: the more Egypt dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied. Jasher gives the strangest proof of it, the Egyptians ploughing the ground where the Hebrew women had given birth and finding they could not harm the infants, so the people grew all the more. Rigour, ploughing, and later the river, and every one of them a failure. What was meant to cut off the seed became the thing under which it multiplied, because the one who had promised Abraham a seed like the sand of the sea was the one keeping count.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.* (Jubilees 47:2). *If it please the king let him order all their children which shall be born from this day forward, to be thrown into the water, for by this can you wipe away their name, for none of them, nor of their fathers, were tried in this manner.* (Jasher 67:49). Jubilees gives the decree, Pharaoh commanding that every male child born to them be thrown into the river. Jasher gives where the decree came from: Balaam counselling the king to throw the children into the water, and saying the aim out loud, by this you can wipe away their name. The war was never only about numbers; it was against the name of the seed. The same Balaam would later be hired to curse that seed in the wilderness, and here he is already at work before Moses was born. The order came from a prophet for hire before it came from a king.

cards.note: Matthew 2:16 — *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* As Moses grows safe in Pharaoh's house (Jasher 68:32) while the king slays the male children, so Herod's slaughter repeats the pattern — the kingdom-of-man hunts the chosen child while the true deliverer is preserved.
cards.s_text: And Moses was in Pharaoh’s house, and was to Bathia, Pharaoh’s daughter, as a son, and Moses grew up amongst the king’s children.
cards.t_text: Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:9 — *And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.* The Jubilees parallel to Jasher 68:24, the grown child made the daughter's son and brought into Pharaoh's court.
cards.s_text: And at the end of two years, when the child grew up, she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he was to her as a son, and she called his name Moses, for she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
cards.t_text: And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.

cards.note: Acts 7:22 — *And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.* The Egyptian rearing of Jasher 68:32, Moses grown amongst the king's children, becomes Stephen's 'learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.'
cards.s_text: And Moses was in Pharaoh’s house, and was to Bathia, Pharaoh’s daughter, as a son, and Moses grew up amongst the king’s children.
cards.t_text: And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.

cards.note: Acts 7:21 — *And when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.* Stephen's witness that Pharaoh's daughter raised the cast-out child as her own, matching Jasher 68:32.
cards.s_text: And Moses was in Pharaoh’s house, and was to Bathia, Pharaoh’s daughter, as a son, and Moses grew up amongst the king’s children.
cards.t_text: And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.

cards.note: Exodus 2:10 — *And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.* The naming in Jasher 68:24 is the canon's own, the same 'drew him out of the water.'
cards.s_text: And at the end of two years, when the child grew up, she brought him to the daughter of Pharaoh, and he was to her as a son, and she called his name Moses, for she said, Because I drew him out of the water.
cards.t_text: And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh’s daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.

cards.note: Exodus 2:9 — *And Pharaoh's daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.* The wages-for-nursing of Jasher 68:23 ('two bits of silver daily') is the canon's commission of the child's own mother.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said to Jochebed, Take this child away and suckle it for me, and I will pay you your wages, two bits of silver daily; and the woman took the child and nursed it.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh’s daughter said unto her, Take this child away, and nurse it for me, and I will give you your wages. And the woman took the child, and nursed it.

cards.note: *And in those days Tharmuth, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidens to bring you forth, and they brought you to her.* (Jubilees 47:5). *And Bathia lifted up her eyes to the river, and she saw the ark upon the water, and sent her maid to fetch it.* (Jasher 68:18). Jubilees calls her Tharmuth and Jasher calls her Bathia, but both set the same scene: Pharaoh's daughter at the river, seeing or hearing the child, and sending her maid to bring it up out of the water. The river was the decree; the rescue came out of the very river, and by the hand of Pharaoh's own house. Jubilees tells it to Moses in the second person, she heard your voice crying, because this is the Angel reciting Moses' own life back to him. The king's daughter undid the king's command without knowing it.
cards.s_text: And Bathia lifted up her eyes to the river, and she saw the ark upon the water, and sent her maid to fetch it.
cards.t_text: And in those days Tharmuth, the daughter of Pharaoh, came to bathe in the river, and she heard your voice crying, and she told her maidens to bring you forth, and they brought you to her.

cards.note: Exodus 2:7 — *Then said his sister to Pharaoh's daughter, Shall I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?* The sister's offer in Jasher 68:21 is the canon's word for word.
cards.s_text: And Miriam his sister was at that time amongst the Egyptian women at the river side, and she saw this thing and she said to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and fetch a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?
cards.t_text: Then said his sister to Pharaoh’s daughter, Shall I go and call to you a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for you?

cards.note: Exodus 2:6 — *And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews' children.* Jasher 68:19 carries the same weeping babe, the same compassion, the same words 'one of the Hebrew children.'
cards.s_text: And she opened it and saw the child, and behold the babe wept, and she had compassion on him, and she said, This is one of the Hebrew children.
cards.t_text: And when she had opened it, she saw the child: and, behold, the babe wept. And she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children.

cards.note: Exodus 2:5 — *And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river's side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.* The canon scene of Pharaoh's daughter sending her maid for the ark, retold in Jasher 68:18.
cards.s_text: And Bathia lifted up her eyes to the river, and she saw the ark upon the water, and sent her maid to fetch it.
cards.t_text: And the daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river’s side; and when she saw the ark among the flags, she sent her maid to fetch it.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:4 — *And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.* The Jubilees ark and watching Miriam set beside Jasher 68:13-14.
cards.s_text: And the woman hastened to take away her son before the officers came, and she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child in it, and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
cards.t_text: And she made an ark for you, and covered it with pitch and asphalt, and placed it in the flags on the bank of the river, and she placed you in it seven days, and your mother came by night and suckled you, and by day Miriam, your sister, guarded you from the birds.

cards.note: Exodus 2:4 — *And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.* The watching Miriam of Jasher 68:14 is the sister standing afar off in the canon scene.
cards.s_text: And his sister Miriam stood afar off to know what would be done to him, and what would become of her words.
cards.t_text: And his sister stood afar off, to wit what would be done to him.

cards.note: Exodus 2:3 — *And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river's brink.* The canon ark Jasher 68:13 retells almost verbatim, slime and pitch and the flags by the river.
cards.s_text: And the woman hastened to take away her son before the officers came, and she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child in it, and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.
cards.t_text: And when she could not longer hide him, she took for him an ark of bulrushes, and daubed it with slime and with pitch, and put the child therein; and she laid it in the flags by the river’s brink.

cards.note: Jubilees 47:3 — *And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her.* The Jubilees parallel keeps the same seven-month bondage of casting-in and the three-month hiding behind Jasher 68:5.
cards.s_text: And when the woman saw the child that it was good and pleasing to the sight, she hid it for three months in an inner room.
cards.t_text: And they cast them in for seven months until the day that you were born. And your mother hid you for three months, and they told regarding her.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:23 — *By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.* The hiding in Jasher 68:5 read as faith — the parents unafraid of Pharaoh's edict.
cards.s_text: And when the woman saw the child that it was good and pleasing to the sight, she hid it for three months in an inner room.
cards.t_text: By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king’s commandment.

cards.note: Acts 7:20 — *In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father's house three months:* Stephen's witness to the birth and the three months that Jasher 68:4-5 narrates.
cards.s_text: And at the end of seven months from her conception she brought forth a son, and the whole house was filled with great light as of the light of the sun and moon at the time of their shining.
cards.t_text: In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months:

cards.note: Exodus 2:2 — *And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.* The canon source Jasher 68:5 retells, the mother seeing the child good and hiding him three months.
cards.s_text: And when the woman saw the child that it was good and pleasing to the sight, she hid it for three months in an inner room.
cards.t_text: And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.

cards.note: Revelation 12:4 — *And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.* Pharaoh's slaughter of the male children in Jasher 68:11 is the same kingdom-of-man pattern: the serpent waiting to devour the chosen seed at birth.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.
cards.t_text: And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven, and did cast them to the earth: and the dragon stood before the woman which was ready to be delivered, for to devour her child as soon as it was born.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.* (Jubilees 47:2). *And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.* (Jasher 68:11). Jubilees gives the decree; Jasher shows it in force, Pharaoh's officers sent out to take the children and slay them, and the note that this was done to the Hebrew women all the days. The command was not a single bad night. It was a standing order carried out every day, and that is the Egypt Moses was born into. His mother's ark on the water was an answer to a decree that had been running for years, and it had to be hidden because the officers were still coming.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh, king of Egypt, issued a command regarding them that they should cast all their male children which were born into the river.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The affliction Yahuah foretold to Abraham, now come upon his seed in the bondage Jasher 68 deepens.
cards.s_text: In those days the Egyptians conspired to destroy all the Hebrews there.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Acts 7:19 — *The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.* Stephen's summary of the very conspiracy Jasher 68:6 records, the Egyptians plotting to destroy all the Hebrews.
cards.s_text: In those days the Egyptians conspired to destroy all the Hebrews there.
cards.t_text: The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.

cards.note: Exodus 1:22 — *And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive.* The canon edict that Jasher 68:11 dramatizes as Pharaoh's officers hunting the Hebrew infants house by house.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh sent his officers to take the children and slay them; thus did the Egyptians to the Hebrew women all the days.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born you shall cast into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees names the taskmasters and Pharaoh's building-cities behind the long, daily Egyptian labor of Jasher 69:8.
cards.s_text: And the men of Egypt did so to all the children of Israel day by day, all the days for a long period.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Acts 7:18 — *Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.* Stephen marks the same regime change behind the unending bondage of Jasher 69:8.
cards.s_text: And the men of Egypt did so to all the children of Israel day by day, all the days for a long period.
cards.t_text: Till another king arose, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Exodus 1:10 — *Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.* The relentless daily labor of Jasher 69:8 is the outworking of Pharaoh's 'deal wisely with them' counsel against the multiplying seed.
cards.s_text: And the men of Egypt did so to all the children of Israel day by day, all the days for a long period.
cards.t_text: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falls out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.

cards.note: Exodus 1:8 — *Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.* The Egypt that grinds Israel day by day in Jasher 69:8 is the realm of the new king who knew not Joseph.
cards.s_text: And the men of Egypt did so to all the children of Israel day by day, all the days for a long period.
cards.t_text: Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:15 — *And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.* Jubilees gives the same rigorous bondage Jasher 69:5 decrees, with the same paradox — the seed multiplies under the lash.
cards.s_text: Then Pharaoh commanded in those days that a proclamation should be issued throughout Egypt to the children of Israel, saying, No man shall diminish any thing of his daily labor.
cards.t_text: And they made them serve with rigour, and the more they dealt evilly with them, the more they increased and multiplied.

cards.note: Acts 7:19 — *The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.* The taking of the youngest sons by force in Jasher 69:7 is the same evil-entreating of Israel's young children Stephen recounts.
cards.s_text: And the labor of Egypt strengthened upon the children of Israel in those days, and behold if one brick was deficient in any man’s daily labor, the Egyptians took his youngest boy by force from his mother, and put him into the building in the place of the brick which his father had left wanting.
cards.t_text: The same dealt subtilly with our kindred, and evil entreated our fathers, so that they cast out their young children, to the end they might not live.

cards.note: Exodus 5:8 — *And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our Elohim (God).* Pharaoh's 'no man shall diminish' brick-quota in Jasher 69:6 matches the unyielding 'ye shall not diminish ought' brick decree of Exodus.
cards.s_text: And the man who shall be found deficient in his labor which he performs daily, whether in mortar or in bricks, then his youngest son shall be put in their place.
cards.t_text: And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, you shall lay upon them; you shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our Elohim (God).

cards.note: Exodus 1:11 — *Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.* Pharaoh's daily-labor proclamation in Jasher 69:5 is the taskmaster-burden of the Exodus building decree.
cards.s_text: Then Pharaoh commanded in those days that a proclamation should be issued throughout Egypt to the children of Israel, saying, No man shall diminish any thing of his daily labor.
cards.t_text: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The mortar-and-brick labor strengthened upon Israel in Jasher 69:7 is the very 'morter, and brick... with rigour' of the Exodus bondage.
cards.s_text: And the labor of Egypt strengthened upon the children of Israel in those days, and behold if one brick was deficient in any man’s daily labor, the Egyptians took his youngest boy by force from his mother, and put him into the building in the place of the brick which his father had left wanting.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:1 — *And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar'el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.* Jubilees records the same multiplying nation in Egypt that Jasher 69:4 says Pharaoh's counsel could not stop.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that after Jacob died the children of Yashar’el (Israel) multiplied in the land of Egypt, and they became a great nation, and they were of one accord in heart, so that brother loved brother and every man helped his brother, and they increased abundantly and multiplied exceedingly, ten weeks of years, all the days of the life of Joseph.

cards.note: Acts 7:17 — *But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which Elohim (God) had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,* Stephen names the same growing, multiplying people of Jasher 69:4 as the promise to Abraham drawing near.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: But when the time of the promise drew nigh, which Elohim (God) had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* The bondage Pharaoh is deepening in Jasher 69:4 is the very affliction the LORD foretold to Abraham.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Exodus 1:12 — *But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* This is exactly why Pharaoh's counsel 'did not succeed' in Jasher 69:4 — affliction only multiplied the seed.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 1:7 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.* The fruitful, multiplying, increasing seed of Jasher 69:4 is Exodus' own word for the nation Pharaoh's counsel could not check.
cards.s_text: And when Pharaoh king of Egypt saw that the counsel which Balaam had advised respecting the children of Israel did not succeed, but that still they were fruitful, multiplied and increased throughout the land of Egypt,
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and waxed exceeding mighty; and the land was filled with them.

cards.note: Genesis 36:31 — *And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The dying king of Edom in Jasher 69:1 belongs to this very dynasty of Esau, kings already enthroned while Israel had none.
cards.s_text: And the king of Edom died in those days, in the eighteenth year of his reign, and was buried in his temple which he had built for himself as his royal residence in the land of Edom.
cards.t_text: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And the children of Esau sent to Pethor, which is upon the river, and they fetched from there a young man of beautiful eyes and comely aspect, whose name was Saul, and they made him king over them in the place of Samlah.* (Jasher 69:2). *And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.* (Genesis 36:37). The Torah's list of the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the children of Yashar'el (Israel) names the same Saul, from a city upon the river, succeeding the same Samlah. Genesis calls his city Rehoboth; Jasher calls it Pethor, and tells how the children of Esau went and fetched him, a young man chosen for his looks, and made him king. The two books agree on the man, the order, and the river, and Jasher supplies how he came to the throne.
cards.s_text: And the children of Esau sent to Pethor, which is upon the river, and they fetched from there a young man of beautiful eyes and comely aspect, whose name was Saul, and they made him king over them in the place of Samlah.
cards.t_text: And Samlah died, and Saul of Rehoboth by the river reigned in his stead.

cards.note: Exodus 20:10 — *But the seventh day is the sabbath of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:* The proclamation's seventh-day rest from all work is the Sabbath of the fourth word, here kept before Sinai.
cards.s_text: To you, all the children of Israel, thus says the king, for six days you shall do your work and labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest, and shall not preform any work, thus shall you do all the days, as the king and Moses the son of Bathia have commanded.
cards.t_text: But the seventh day is the sabbath of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): in it you shall not do any work, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your cattle, nor your stranger that is within your gates:

cards.note: Exodus 20:8 — *Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.* The command later graven in stone is the same six-days-labor, seventh-day-rest Jasher shows proclaimed in Goshen.
cards.s_text: To you, all the children of Israel, thus says the king, for six days you shall do your work and labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest, and shall not preform any work, thus shall you do all the days, as the king and Moses the son of Bathia have commanded.
cards.t_text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.

cards.note: Genesis 2:2 — *And on the seventh day Elohim (God) ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.* The seventh-day rest Moses obtains for Israel is the rest set in creation, kept long before Sinai.
cards.s_text: To you, all the children of Israel, thus says the king, for six days you shall do your work and labor, but on the seventh day you shall rest, and shall not preform any work, thus shall you do all the days, as the king and Moses the son of Bathia have commanded.
cards.t_text: And on the seventh day Elohim (God) ended his work which he had made; and he rested on the seventh day from all his work which he had made.

cards.note: Acts 7:25 — *For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that Elohim (God) by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.* The deliverer's heart is already set on his people, the very compassion Jasher narrates before the slaying and the flight.
cards.s_text: And the day arrived when Moses went to Goshen to see his brethren, that he saw the children of Israel in their burdens and hard labor, and Moses was grieved on their account.
cards.t_text: For he supposed his brethren would have understood how that Elohim (God) by his hand would deliver them: but they understood not.

cards.note: Acts 7:23 — *And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Stephen names the heart that turns to visit the brethren — the grief Jasher shows Moses bearing over their hard labor.
cards.s_text: And the day arrived when Moses went to Goshen to see his brethren, that he saw the children of Israel in their burdens and hard labor, and Moses was grieved on their account.
cards.t_text: And when he was full forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 2:11 — *And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.* Jasher's daily going-forth to see the burdens is the going-out Exodus records, the prince claiming the slaves as his brethren.
cards.s_text: And he daily went forth and came into the land of Goshen, where his brethren the children of Israel were, and Moses saw them daily in shortness of breath and hard labor.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in those days, when Moses was grown, that he went out unto his brethren, and looked on their burdens: and he spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew, one of his brethren.

cards.note: *And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.* (Jubilees 47:9). *And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.* (Jasher 70:33). Jasher tells it from the outside: Moses grown in the king's house, Bathia counting him as her son, the household honouring him and all Egypt afraid of him. Jubilees tells it to Moses himself, the Angel reciting his own life back to him in the second person, you became her son, and they brought you into the royal court. But Jubilees keeps one thing Jasher does not: before the court had him, Amram his father taught him writing. The Hebrew father's teaching came first, and then Pharaoh's house. He was raised in the court, but he was taught at home.
cards.s_text: And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.
cards.t_text: And afterwards, when you were grown up, they brought you to the daughter of Pharaoh, and you did become her son, and Amram your father taught you writing, and after you had completed three weeks they brought you into the royal court.

cards.note: Acts 7:22 — *And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.* Stephen names the wisdom Moses gained growing in the king's house, the very upbringing Jasher narrates.
cards.s_text: And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.

cards.note: Exodus 2:10 — *And the child grew, and she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water.* Jasher's Bathia who considers the grown boy a son is Exodus' daughter of Pharaoh who drew Moses out and made him her son.
cards.s_text: And when Moses grew up in the king’s house, Bathia the daughter of Pharaoh considered him as a son, and all the household of Pharaoh honored him, and all the men of Egypt were afraid of him.

cards.note: Acts 7:21 — *And when he was cast out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.* Stephen names the favor that keeps Moses in the king's house — Jasher's *Yahuah was with him* in Pharaoh's hall.
cards.s_text: So the king and princes refrained from slaying the child, so Moses remained in Pharaoh’s house, growing up, and Yahuah (the Lord) was with him.
cards.t_text: And when he was cast out, Pharaoh’s daughter took him up, and nourished him for her own son.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:23 — *By faith Moses, when he was born, was hid three months of his parents, because they saw he was a proper child; and they were not afraid of the king's commandment.* Hebrews reads Moses' preservation as faith that did not fear the king's commandment — the same deliverer Jasher shows kept in Pharaoh's house.
cards.s_text: So the king and princes refrained from slaying the child, so Moses remained in Pharaoh’s house, growing up, and Yahuah (the Lord) was with him.

cards.note: Exodus 2:2 — *And the woman conceived, and bare a son: and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months.* The canon's plain account of the child kept alive stands beneath Jasher's coal-legend of why the king spared him.
cards.s_text: So the king and princes refrained from slaying the child, so Moses remained in Pharaoh’s house, growing up, and Yahuah (the Lord) was with him.

cards.note: Matthew 2:16 — *Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked of the wise men, was exceeding wroth, and sent forth, and slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under, according to the time which he had diligently enquired of the wise men.* Pharaoh seeking the chosen child's blood is the same pattern Herod repeats — the dragon ever seeking to slay the deliverer.

cards.note: *And you were three weeks of years at court until the time when you did go forth from the royal court and did see an Egyptian smiting your friend who was of the children of Yashar’el (Israel), and you did slay him and hide him in the sand.* (Jubilees 47:10). *At that time that the war and the siege were against Cush, Moses fled from Egypt from Pharaoh who sought to kill him for having slain the Egyptian.* (Jasher 72:21). Jubilees gives the deed, told to Moses as his own memory: he went out from the court, saw an Egyptian smiting his friend of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), slew him and hid him in the sand. Jasher gives what followed, Moses fleeing because Pharaoh sought to kill him for it, and sets the flight in the days of the war against Cush. The man raised in the king's house chose the beaten Hebrew over the court that raised him, and it cost him the court. Three weeks of years in Pharaoh's palace ended in a day over one afflicted brother.

cards.s_text: And Moses was eighteen years old when he fled from Egypt from the presence of Pharaoh, and he fled and escaped to the camp of Kikianus, which at that time was besieging Cush.
cards.t_text: And seeing one of them suffer wrong, he defended him, and avenged him that was oppressed, and smote the Egyptian:

cards.note: Exodus 2:15 — *Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.* Exodus, like Jasher 72:21-22, has Pharaoh seek Moses' life and Moses flee Egypt's presence.
cards.s_text: At that time that the war and the siege were against Cush, Moses fled from Egypt from Pharaoh who sought to kill him for having slain the Egyptian.
cards.t_text: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

cards.note: Exodus 2:12 — *And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.* The slaying for which Pharaoh sought Moses' life in Jasher 72:21 is the canon scene Jasher's war-flight expands.
cards.s_text: At that time that the war and the siege were against Cush, Moses fled from Egypt from Pharaoh who sought to kill him for having slain the Egyptian.
cards.t_text: And he looked this way and that way, and when he saw that there was no man, he slew the Egyptian, and hid him in the sand.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:27 — *By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.* The apostle reads Moses' steadfast life by faith — the same fear of Yahuah and unswerving way Jasher 73:37 records.
cards.s_text: And Moses feared Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) all his life, and Moses walked before Yahuah (the Lord) in truth, with all his heart and soul, he turned not from the right way all the days of his life; he declined not from the way either to the right or to the left, in which Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had walked.
cards.t_text: By faith he forsook Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible.

cards.note: Joshua 1:7 — *Only be thou strong and very courageous, that thou mayest observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded thee: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper whithersoever thou goest.* The charge Moses himself laid down — the same 'right or left' walking Jasher 73:37 reports of his own life.
cards.s_text: And Moses feared Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) all his life, and Moses walked before Yahuah (the Lord) in truth, with all his heart and soul, he turned not from the right way all the days of his life; he declined not from the way either to the right or to the left, in which Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had walked.
cards.t_text: Only be you strong and very courageous, that you may observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded you: turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may prosper whithersoever you go.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 5:32 — *Ye shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.* The very measure of walking Jasher 73:37 says Moses kept — declining neither to right nor left from the fathers' way.
cards.s_text: And Moses feared Yahuah his Elohim (the Lord his God) all his life, and Moses walked before Yahuah (the Lord) in truth, with all his heart and soul, he turned not from the right way all the days of his life; he declined not from the way either to the right or to the left, in which Abraham, Isaac and Jacob had walked.
cards.t_text: You shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) has commanded you: you shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

cards.note: Genesis 9:25 — *And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.* Noah's word on Ham's line stands behind Jasher 73:35, which gives Ham and his seed as slaves to Shem and Japheth.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah our Elohim (the Lord our God) gave Ham the son of Noah, and his children and all his seed, as slaves to the children of Shem and to the children of Japheth, and to their seed after them for slaves, forever.
cards.t_text: And he said, Cursed be Canaan; a servant of servants shall he be unto his brethren.

cards.note: Genesis 28:1 — *And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.* This is Isaac's charge to the fleeing Jacob that Jasher 73:34 recalls as Moses' reason to guard the seed-line.
cards.s_text: Also what Isaac did when Jacob had fled from his brother, when he commanded him, saying, You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan, nor make alliance with any of the children of Ham.
cards.t_text: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him, and said unto him, You shall not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan.

cards.note: Genesis 24:3 — *And I will make thee swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that thou shalt not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell.* This is the very oath of Abraham to Eliezer that Jasher 73:33 says Moses remembered when he kept from the Cushite queen.
cards.s_text: For Moses remembered how Abraham had made his servant Eliezer swear, saying to him, You shall not take a woman from the daughters of Canaan for my son Isaac.
cards.t_text: And I will make you swear by Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of heaven, and the Elohim (God) of the earth, that you shall not take a wife unto my son of the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I dwell:

cards.note: 2 Timothy 3:8 — *Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith.* The apostle names the tradition Jasher 73:29 records — the sorcerers who withstood Moses in Egypt.
cards.s_text: They are the sorcerers and magicians who are mentioned in the book of the law, standing against Moses when Yahuah (the Lord) brought the plagues upon Egypt.
cards.t_text: Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these also resist the truth: men of corrupt minds, reprobate concerning the faith.

cards.note: Exodus 7:22 — *And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as Yahuah (LORD) had said.* The magicians match Yahuah's signs awhile, just as Jasher 73:29 names them resisting Moses through the plagues.
cards.s_text: They are the sorcerers and magicians who are mentioned in the book of the law, standing against Moses when Yahuah (the Lord) brought the plagues upon Egypt.
cards.t_text: And the magicians of Egypt did so with their enchantments: and Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, neither did he hearken unto them; as Yahuah (LORD) had said.

cards.note: Exodus 7:11 — *Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.* These are the very sorcerers Jasher 73:29 says stood against Moses when the plagues came upon Egypt.
cards.s_text: They are the sorcerers and magicians who are mentioned in the book of the law, standing against Moses when Yahuah (the Lord) brought the plagues upon Egypt.
cards.t_text: Then Pharaoh also called the wise men and the sorcerers: now the magicians of Egypt, they also did in like manner with their enchantments.

cards.note: Numbers 24:24 — *And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.* Balaam's oracle foresees the very seafaring Chittim that Jasher 74:10 shows coming in ships to make war — the canon named the sea-power before the legend narrated its battles.
cards.s_text: And Latinus assembled all his forces, and they came in ships, and went in it to fight with Azdrubal son of Angeas king of Africa, and they came to Africa and engaged in battle with Azdrubal and his army.
cards.t_text: And ships shall come from the coast of Chittim, and shall afflict Asshur, and shall afflict Eber, and he also shall perish for ever.

cards.note: Genesis 10:4 — *And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.* The children of Chittim whom Latinus reigns over in Jasher 74:7 are the Kittim the Table of Nations already counts among Javan's sons.
cards.s_text: In the twenty-second year of the reign of Moses over the children of Cush, Latinus reigned over the children of Chittim forty-five years.
cards.t_text: And the sons of Javan; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

cards.note: Genesis 36:31 — *And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Jasher 74:4's account of Edom's kings rising and the children of Moab withdrawing allegiance belongs to the same pre-monarchy Edomite king-era the Torah frames here.
cards.s_text: And when Baal Chanan the son of Achbor reigned over Edom, all the children of Moab withdrew their allegiance from Edom.
cards.t_text: And these are the kings that reigned in the land of Edom, before there reigned any king over the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Genesis 36:35 — *And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.* Jasher 74:3 names the same Hadad son of Bedad who smote Midian and subdued Moab — the Torah's note becomes Jasher's backstory for Moab's later revolt.
cards.s_text: In his days Moab rebelled against the power of Edom, having been under Edom since the days of Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote them and Midian, and brought Moab under subjection to Edom.
cards.t_text: And Husham died, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who smote Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his stead: and the name of his city was Avith.

cards.note: 1 Chronicles 1:49 — *And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.* The Chronicler preserves the same handoff Jasher 74:2 dates to the reign of Moses over Cush — Baal Chanan son of Achbor over all the children of Edom.
cards.s_text: In the sixteenth year of the reign of Moses over Cush, Baal Chanan the son of Achbor reigned in the land of Edom over all the children of Edom for thirty-eight years.
cards.t_text: And when Shaul was dead, Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.

cards.note: Genesis 36:38 — *And Saul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.* The Torah's own Edomite king-list names the exact succession Jasher 74:1 records — Saul of Edom dying and Baal Chanan son of Achbor reigning in his place.
cards.s_text: In the end of years died Saul king of Edom, and Baal Chanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.
cards.t_text: And Saul died, and Baal-hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his stead.

cards.note: 1 Chronicles 7:23 — *And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house.* The birth and naming of Beriah in Jasher 75:22 is the canon's own — the wounded seed-line is kept and continued even after the disaster at Gath.
cards.s_text: And he came to his wife and she bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, for she was unfortunate in his house.
cards.t_text: And when he went in to his wife, she conceived, and bare a son, and he called his name Beriah, because it went evil with his house.

cards.note: 1 Chronicles 7:22 — *And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him.* This is the same mourning of Jasher 75:21 — word for word the canon records Ephraim mourning many days while his brethren came to console him.
cards.s_text: And their father Ephraim mourned over them for many days, and his brethren came to console him.
cards.t_text: And Ephraim their father mourned many days, and his brethren came to comfort him.

cards.note: 1 Chronicles 7:21 — *And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle.* The canon preserves the very slaughter of Jasher 75:16 — the sons of Ephraim cut down by the men of Gath for coming down after their cattle.
cards.s_text: And they smote all the children of Ephraim, all who had gone forth from Egypt, none were remaining but ten men who had run away from the engagement.
cards.t_text: And Zabad his son, and Shuthelah his son, and Ezer, and Elead, whom the men of Gath that were born in that land slew, because they came down to take away their cattle.

cards.note: Exodus 12:41 — *And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.* Yahuah delivered His hosts safely OUT in Exodus, the foil to Jasher 75:15 where He delivered the premature host UP into the hands of the Philistines.
