cards.s_text: And these men were engaged in battle with the children of Ephraim, and Yahuah (the Lord) delivered the children of Ephraim into the hands of the Philistines.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 13:17 — *And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that Elohim (God) led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for Elohim (God) said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:* This is the canon's own reason the Philistine road of Jasher 75:6 was deadly — the route toward Gath that destroyed Ephraim is the one Yahuah deliberately steered the true exodus away from.
cards.s_text: And they directed their course toward the land of Gath, and they went down and found the shepherds of Gath feeding the cattle of the children of Gath.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that Elohim (God) led them not through the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for Elohim (God) said, Lest peradventure the people repent when they see war, and they return to Egypt:

cards.note: Psalms 33:17 — *An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.* The great strength on which Ephraim leaned in Jasher 75:3 is named a vain thing for safety — deliverance belongs to Yahuah alone.
cards.s_text: And these men girded themselves, and they put each man his sword at his side, and every man his armor upon him, and they trusted to their strength, and they went out together from Egypt with a mighty hand.
cards.t_text: An horse is a vain thing for safety: neither shall he deliver any by his great strength.

cards.note: Psalms 33:16 — *There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength.* This unmasks the false confidence of the valiant men of Jasher 75:3 who trusted to their strength and went out with a mighty hand of their own.
cards.s_text: And these men girded themselves, and they put each man his sword at his side, and every man his armor upon him, and they trusted to their strength, and they went out together from Egypt with a mighty hand.
cards.t_text: There is no king saved by the multitude of an host: a mighty man is not delivered by much strength.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 32:30 — *How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?* The Song of Moses shows the very arithmetic of Jasher 75:5 reversed when the Rock sells His people up — which is exactly what befell Ephraim trusting their strength.
cards.s_text: And these men were very mighty and valiant men, one man could pursue a thousand and two could rout ten thousand, so they trusted to their strength and went together as they were.
cards.t_text: How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, except their Rock had sold them, and Yahuah (LORD) had shut them up?

cards.note: Leviticus 26:8 — *And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.* The Ephraimite boast in Jasher 75:5 that one could pursue a thousand quotes the covenant blessing, but claims it apart from the obedience that secures it.
cards.s_text: And these men were very mighty and valiant men, one man could pursue a thousand and two could rout ten thousand, so they trusted to their strength and went together as they were.
cards.t_text: And five of you shall chase an hundred, and an hundred of you shall put ten thousand to flight: and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

cards.note: *And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: “Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they will bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.* (Jubilees 14:13). *For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.* (Jasher 75:2). Jubilees gives the word to Abram in the darkness: his seed would be strangers in a land not theirs, brought into bondage and afflicted four hundred years. Jasher shows what happened when that word was reckoned wrongly. The children of Ephraim said the period Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed was complete, and went out of Egypt before the time, and the chapter that follows tells of their slaughter. A true word misreckoned kills as surely as a false one. The years were fixed, but they were Yahuah's (God's) to count, and the ones who counted for Him died at the hands of the Philistines.
cards.s_text: For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when the sun had set, that an ecstasy fell upon Abram, and lo! an horror of great darkness fell upon him, and it was said to Abram: “Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land (that is) not theirs, and they will bring them into bondage, and afflict them four hundred years.

cards.note: Exodus 12:41 — *And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.* The true exodus came on the selfsame appointed day, vindicating the verdict of Jasher 75:17 that Ephraim transgressed by going forth before the period had arrived.
cards.s_text: For this evil was from Yahuah (the Lord) against the children of Ephraim, for they transgressed the word of Yahuah (the Lord) in going forth from Egypt, before the period had arrived which Yahuah (the Lord) in the days of old had appointed to Israel.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass at the end of the four hundred and thirty years, even the selfsame day it came to pass, that all the hosts of Yahuah (LORD) went out from the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Genesis 15:16 — *But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.* The exodus is fixed to a fourth-generation reckoning, so the Ephraimites of Jasher 75:1 who marched out in the 180th year ran ahead of the covenant timetable.
cards.s_text: For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.
cards.t_text: But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again: for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full.

cards.note: Genesis 15:13 — *And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;* This is the very "period... which he had spoken to Abraham" that the Ephraimites in Jasher 75:2 claimed was completed before its time.
cards.s_text: For they said the period was completed which Yahuah (the Lord) had appointed to the children of Israel in the times of old, which he had spoken to Abraham.
cards.t_text: And he said unto Abram, Know of a surety that your seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years;

cards.note: Acts 7:30 — *And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of Yahuah (Lord) in a flame of fire in a bush.* The death that closes Jasher 76 sets the stage for the burning-bush call Stephen narrates next.
cards.s_text: And at the end of three years, the king died, in shame, disgrace, and disgust, and his servants carried him and buried him in the sepulcher of the kings of Egypt in Zoan Mizraim.
cards.t_text: And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of Yahuah (Lord) in a flame of fire in a bush.

cards.note: Exodus 4:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought thy life.* Because Yahuah requited the Pharaoh evil for his evil in Jasher 76:61, the men who sought Moses' life are dead and the way back to Egypt is opened.
cards.s_text: For this evil was from Yahuah (the Lord) to him, for Yahuah (the Lord) had requited him evil for the evil which in his days he had done to Israel.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses in Midian, Go, return into Egypt: for all the men are dead which sought your life.

cards.note: Exodus 2:23 — *And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.* The death of the king of Egypt that Jasher 76:59 narrates is the canon's own turning-point toward deliverance.
cards.s_text: And at the end of three years, the king died, in shame, disgrace, and disgust, and his servants carried him and buried him in the sepulcher of the kings of Egypt in Zoan Mizraim.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:7–8 — *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar'el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* The bodily plague on Pharaoh in Jasher 76:34 foreshadows the ten covenant-judgments Jubilees records on Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh was ten years afflicted with that plague, still the heart of Pharaoh was more hardened against the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The embittered lives and increased yoke of Jasher 76:27 are Exodus's own words for the bondage.
cards.s_text: Still his anger did not turn from them, and the hand of Pharaoh was still stretched out against the children of Israel, and Pharaoh hardened his neck before Yahuah (the Lord), and he increased his yoke over the children of Israel, and embittered their lives with all manner of hard work.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 2:25 — *And Elohim (God) looked upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and Elohim (God) had respect unto them.* Even as Pharaoh hardens his neck and increases the yoke in Jasher 76:27, Yahuah is already regarding the afflicted seed.
cards.s_text: Still his anger did not turn from them, and the hand of Pharaoh was still stretched out against the children of Israel, and Pharaoh hardened his neck before Yahuah (the Lord), and he increased his yoke over the children of Israel, and embittered their lives with all manner of hard work.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) looked upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and Elohim (God) had respect unto them.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:25 — *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.* Moses' choice by faith to side with the afflicted people of Jasher 76:24 rather than Egypt's throne.
cards.s_text: And all the children of Israel were yet in the land of Egypt serving the Egyptians in all manner of hard work, and the hand of Egypt continued in severity over the children of Israel in those days.
cards.t_text: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

cards.note: Exodus 2:24 — *And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.* The covenant remembered is why Yahuah hearkens to the people's prayer in Jasher 76:26.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (the Lord) had hearkened to the prayer of his people the children of Israel, and their cry reached him on account of their hard work.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

cards.note: Exodus 2:23 — *And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.* Israel's cry reaching Elohim is the very prayer Jasher 76:26 says Yahuah hearkened to.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (the Lord) had hearkened to the prayer of his people the children of Israel, and their cry reached him on account of their hard work.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The same severity of hard work over Israel that Jasher 76:24 describes.
cards.s_text: And all the children of Israel were yet in the land of Egypt serving the Egyptians in all manner of hard work, and the hand of Egypt continued in severity over the children of Israel in those days.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 2:21 — *And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.* Jasher's Zipporah who sustains Moses with bread and water is the same daughter of Reuel the canon gives him to wife.
cards.s_text: And they took and put him into the prison house, and Moses was in prison ten years, and whilst Moses was in the prison house, Zipporah the daughter of Reuel took pity over him, and supported him with bread and water all the time.
cards.t_text: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

cards.note: *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* (Jubilees 48:1). *So Moses went to Midian, for he was afraid to return to Egypt on account of Pharaoh, and he went and sat at a well of water in Midian.* (Jasher 76:13). Jasher gives the first scene of the Midian years, Moses afraid to go back to Egypt, sitting down at a well. Jubilees gives their length, five weeks of years and one year, and the date he went in and the date he came out, down to the week and the jubilee. The one who would stand before Pharaoh spent the better part of his life first as a fugitive at a well. The years are counted so carefully because none of them were wasted; the man who returned in the fiftieth jubilee was not the man who fled in the forty-ninth.
cards.s_text: So Moses went to Midian, for he was afraid to return to Egypt on account of Pharaoh, and he went and sat at a well of water in Midian.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Exodus 2:20 — *And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that ye have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.* Reuel's reproach and summons to eat bread is the same line Jasher 76:19-20 puts in his mouth.
cards.s_text: And Reuel said to his daughters, And where is he? therefore have you left the man?
cards.t_text: And he said unto his daughters, And where is he? why is it that you have left the man? call him, that he may eat bread.

cards.note: Exodus 2:17 — *And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.* The same shepherds, the same rescue, the same watered flock as Jasher 76:16.
cards.s_text: So the shepherds of Midian came and drove them away, and Moses rose up and helped them and watered the flock.
cards.t_text: And the shepherds came and drove them away: but Moses stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.

cards.note: Exodus 2:16 — *Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father's flock.* The seven daughters drawing water for the flock are the very women Jasher 76:14-15 names as Reuel's seven daughters.
cards.s_text: And they came to the well and drew water to water their father’s flock.
cards.t_text: Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

cards.note: Exodus 2:15 — *Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.* Jasher's Moses sits at the same Midian well, fleeing the same Pharaoh.
cards.s_text: So Moses went to Midian, for he was afraid to return to Egypt on account of Pharaoh, and he went and sat at a well of water in Midian.
cards.t_text: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

cards.note: *So Moses went forth from the land of Cush, and went home and ceased to reign over Cush, and Moses was sixty-six years old when he went out of the land of Cush, for the thing was from Yahuah (the Lord), for the period had arrived which he had appointed in the days of old, to bring forth Israel from the affliction of the children of Ham.* (Jasher 76:12). *Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.* (Acts 7:29). Stephen moves Moses from the flight out of Egypt straight to Midian; Jasher fills the years between with a reign over Cush that ends only when Moses is sixty-six and the appointed period has come. Both agree on the shape of the thing: a long stretch away from his brethren, a stranger, before the call. Jasher says why the Cush years end when they do, because the thing was from Yahuah (the Lord), who had fixed the time in the days of old to bring Yashar'el (Israel) out from the affliction of the children of Ham. The deliverer's waiting was on a schedule he did not set.
cards.s_text: So Moses went forth from the land of Cush, and went home and ceased to reign over Cush, and Moses was sixty-six years old when he went out of the land of Cush, for the thing was from Yahuah (the Lord), for the period had arrived which he had appointed in the days of old, to bring forth Israel from the affliction of the children of Ham.
cards.t_text: Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.

cards.note: Exodus 4:20 — *And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of Elohim (God) in his hand.* The stick Moses plucks in Jasher 77:41 is the canon's rod of Elohim he carries back to Egypt for the signs.
cards.s_text: And he read it and stretched forth his hand and he plucked it like a forest tree from the thicket, and the stick was in his hand.
cards.t_text: And Moses took his wife and his sons, and set them upon an ass, and he returned to the land of Egypt: and Moses took the rod of Elohim (God) in his hand.

cards.note: Genesis 27:36 — *And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing. And he said, Hast thou not reserved a blessing for me?* Esau's complaint that Jacob took birthright and blessing is the 'force' by which Jasher 77:47 says the stick passed to Jacob.
cards.s_text: Also when he went down to Egypt he took it into his hand and gave it to Joseph, one portion above his brethren, for Jacob had taken it by force from his brother Esau.
cards.t_text: And he said, Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he has supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he has taken away my blessing. And he said, Have you not reserved a blessing for me?

cards.note: Genesis 25:34 — *Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.* Jacob taking the staff 'by force from his brother Esau' in Jasher 77:47 rests on the despised birthright Genesis records.
cards.s_text: Also when he went down to Egypt he took it into his hand and gave it to Joseph, one portion above his brethren, for Jacob had taken it by force from his brother Esau.
cards.t_text: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and pottage of lentiles; and he did eat and drink, and rose up, and went his way: thus Esau despised his birthright.

cards.note: Genesis 3:23 — *Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.* Jasher 77:43 takes up this exile, saying Adam carried the stick as he went to till the ground from which he was taken.
cards.s_text: And when Elohim had driven Adam from the garden of Eden, he took the stick in his hand and went and tilled the ground from which he was taken.
cards.t_text: Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:1 — *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* Jubilees dates Moses' Midian dwelling, the same sojourn in Reuel's house Jasher 77:26 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Moses the son of Amram was still confined in the dungeon in those days, in the house of Reuel the Midianite, and Zipporah the daughter of Reuel did support him with food secretly day by day.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:25 — *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.* Moses imprisoned yet faithful in Jasher 77:26 embodies the faith Hebrews praises — affliction with God's people over Pharaoh's pleasures.
cards.s_text: And Moses the son of Amram was still confined in the dungeon in those days, in the house of Reuel the Midianite, and Zipporah the daughter of Reuel did support him with food secretly day by day.
cards.t_text: Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of Elohim (God), than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;

cards.note: Exodus 2:21 — *And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.* The canon's gift of Zipporah to Moses is the very marriage Jasher 77:51 records when Reuel sees the stick in Moses' hand.
cards.s_text: And when Reuel saw the stick in the hand of Moses, he wondered at it, and he gave him his daughter Zipporah for a wife.
cards.t_text: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

cards.note: Exodus 2:15 — *Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.* Jasher 77:26 places Moses in the house of Reuel the Midianite, the same Midian refuge Exodus says he fled to from Pharaoh's sword.
cards.s_text: And Moses the son of Amram was still confined in the dungeon in those days, in the house of Reuel the Midianite, and Zipporah the daughter of Reuel did support him with food secretly day by day.
cards.t_text: Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.

cards.note: Exodus 3:8 — *And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey...* The determination to deliver in Jasher 77:25 is the very 'I am come down to deliver' the bush declares.
cards.s_text: And Elohim saw the burden of the children of Israel, and their heavy work in those days, and he determined to deliver them.
cards.t_text: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

cards.note: Exodus 2:25 — *And Elohim (God) looked upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and Elohim (God) had respect unto them.* God's seeing of the burden and respect for His people matches Jasher 77:25, where Elohim sees the heavy work and determines to deliver them.
cards.s_text: And Elohim saw the burden of the children of Israel, and their heavy work in those days, and he determined to deliver them.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) looked upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and Elohim (God) had respect unto them.

cards.note: Exodus 2:24 — *And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.* Jasher 77:24 names the same remembered covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the seed kept by promise.
cards.s_text: And Elohim heard the voice of the children of Israel and their cry, in those days, and Elohim remembered to them his covenant which he had made with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

cards.note: Exodus 2:23 — *And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.* The sighing under hard labor and the cry rising to Elohim in Jasher 77:23 is the very groan Exodus says came up to God.
cards.s_text: But they increased the latter work more than the former, and the children of Israel sighed at this and their cry ascended to Elohim (God) on account of their labor.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass in process of time, that the king of Egypt died: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) sighed by reason of the bondage, and they cried, and their cry came up unto Elohim (God) by reason of the bondage.

cards.note: Jubilees 46:14 — *And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.* Jubilees narrates the same Egyptian taskmasters and forced building that Jasher 77:11 says Adikam intensified over Goshen.
cards.s_text: And he placed over them a measure of bricks for them to do according to that number, day by day, and he turned back and went to Egypt.
cards.t_text: And he set over them taskmasters to afflict them with slavery; and they built strong cities for Pharaoh, Pithom and Raamses, and they built all the walls and all the fortifications which had fallen in the cities of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 5:7 — *Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.* The Pharaoh of Exodus tightens the brick-quota exactly as Adikam does in Jasher 77:13, demanding the full tale without easing the work.
cards.s_text: Thus says Pharaoh, Do your work each day, and finish your task, and observe the daily measure of bricks; diminish not anything.
cards.t_text: You shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* Jasher 77:13's daily measure of bricks 'diminish not anything' is the same brick-and-mortar rigour Exodus names.
cards.s_text: Thus says Pharaoh, Do your work each day, and finish your task, and observe the daily measure of bricks; diminish not anything.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 1:11 — *Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.* The canon's taskmasters and imposed burdens are the very yoke Jasher 77:11 says Adikam strengthened with a fixed daily measure of bricks.
cards.s_text: And he placed over them a measure of bricks for them to do according to that number, day by day, and he turned back and went to Egypt.
cards.t_text: Therefore they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens. And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.

cards.note: *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* (Jubilees 48:7–8). *And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Israel, and saw the oppression with which the Egyptians oppressed them.* (Jasher 78:15). Jasher gives the hearing and the seeing: Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) and saw the oppression. Jubilees gives what came of it, ten great and terrible judgments on Egypt, and says plainly what they were for, vengeance for Yashar'el (Israel) according to the covenant Yahuah (God) had ordained with Abraham. The plagues were not random wrath against a nation; they were a Father keeping an oath sworn four hundred years earlier, that the nation which brought Abraham's seed into bondage by force would be judged for it. He heard, He saw, and then He struck, and every one of the ten came according to the word of Moses.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) heard the cries of the children of Israel, and saw the oppression with which the Egyptians oppressed them.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 6:8 — *And I will bring you in unto the land, concerning the which I did swear to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for an heritage: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The land of Canaan for a possession that Jasher 78:16 names is the sworn inheritance.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) was jealous of his people and his inheritance, and heard their voice, and he resolved to take them out of the affliction of Egypt, to give them the land of Canaan for a possession.
cards.t_text: And I will bring you in unto the land, concerning the which I did swear to give it to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will give it you for an heritage: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Exodus 3:8 — *And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.* Yahuah's resolve to take them out and give them Canaan, the same purpose Jasher 78:16 declares.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) was jealous of his people and his inheritance, and heard their voice, and he resolved to take them out of the affliction of Egypt, to give them the land of Canaan for a possession.
cards.t_text: And I am come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians, and to bring them up out of that land unto a good land and a large, unto a land flowing with milk and honey; unto the place of the Canaanites, and the Hittites, and the Amorites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites.

cards.note: Exodus 2:24 — *And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.* The cry of Jasher 78:14 heard and answered by the remembered covenant.
cards.s_text: And the children of Israel heard this, and they mourned and sighed, and they cried to Yahuah (the Lord) on account of the bitterness of their souls.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) heard their groaning, and Elohim (God) remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The bitter brick-bondage and heavier yoke Jasher 78:11 says Pharaoh increased.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh king of Egypt greatly increased the labor of the children of Israel in those days, and continued to make his yoke heavier upon the children of Israel.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Exodus 5:8 — *And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, ye shall lay upon them; ye shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our Elohim (God).* The undiminished tale of bricks and the idle-charge that Jasher 78:13 records.
cards.s_text: Also the tale of bricks which they shall make let them give each day, and diminish nothing from them, for they are idle in their work.
cards.t_text: And the tale of the bricks, which they did make heretofore, you shall lay upon them; you shall not diminish ought thereof: for they be idle; therefore they cry, saying, Let us go and sacrifice to our Elohim (God).

cards.note: Exodus 5:7 — *Ye shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.* Pharaoh's no-straw decree, the source of Jasher 78:12's proclamation word for word.
cards.s_text: And he ordered a proclamation to be made in Egypt, saying, Give no more straw to the people to make bricks with, let them go and gather themselves straw as they can find it.
cards.t_text: You shall no more give the people straw to make brick, as heretofore: let them go and gather straw for themselves.

cards.note: *And she conceived again and bare a son, but circumcised his foreskin, and called his name Eliezer, for Moses said, Because the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.* (Jasher 78:10). *This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did Elohim (God) send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.* (Acts 7:35). Eliezer's name is Moses' own confession that the Elohim (God) of his fathers was his help and delivered him from the sword of Pharaoh. Stephen says the same of him from the other side: the man his brethren refused is the one Elohim (God) sent back as ruler and deliverer. The one delivered becomes the deliverer. Jasher has Moses name the rescue over his son in Midian, years before the bush, and Acts has the rescue become the sending.
cards.s_text: And she conceived again and bare a son, but circumcised his foreskin, and called his name Eliezer, for Moses said, Because the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
cards.t_text: This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made you a ruler and a judge? the same did Elohim (God) send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.

cards.note: Acts 7:32 — *Saying, I am the Elohim (God) of thy fathers, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.* The Elohim of the fathers whom Jasher 78:10 names Eliezer to honor is the same who speaks from the bush.
cards.s_text: And she conceived again and bare a son, but circumcised his foreskin, and called his name Eliezer, for Moses said, Because the Elohim (God) of my fathers was my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.
cards.t_text: Saying, I am the Elohim (God) of your fathers, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob. Then Moses trembled, and durst not behold.

cards.note: *And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.* (Jubilees 48:1). *In those days Moses, the son of Amram, in Midian, took Zipporah, the daughter of Reuel the Midianite, for a wife.* (Jasher 78:7). Jubilees gives the Midian years in a date, from the forty-ninth jubilee to the fiftieth, five weeks of years and one year. Jasher puts a marriage inside those years, Moses taking Zipporah the daughter of Reuel the Midianite for a wife. The deliverer of Yashar'el (Israel) married outside the camp and kept sheep for a stranger before he ever lifted a rod, and the years are not written as a gap in his story. They are dated to the week because Yahuah (God) was counting them as the preparation of the man.
cards.s_text: In those days Moses, the son of Amram, in Midian, took Zipporah, the daughter of Reuel the Midianite, for a wife.
cards.t_text: And in the sixth year of the third week of the forty-ninth jubilee you did depart and dwell in the land of Midian five weeks and one year. And you did return into Egypt in the second week in the second year in the fiftieth jubilee.

cards.note: Acts 7:29 — *Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.* Stephen counts the two Midian-born sons (Jasher's Gershom of 78:9 and Eliezer of 78:10), the same exile household.
cards.s_text: And Zipporah conceived and bare a son and he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land; but he circumcised not his foreskin, at the command of Reuel his father-in-law.
cards.t_text: Then fled Moses at this saying, and was a stranger in the land of Madian, where he begat two sons.

cards.note: *And Zipporah conceived and bare a son and he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land; but he circumcised not his foreskin, at the command of Reuel his father-in-law.* (Jasher 78:9). *And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.* (Exodus 2:22). The naming of Gershom is the same in both books, nearly word for word: a stranger in a foreign land. Jasher adds something Exodus does not say here, that the boy was not circumcised, and gives the reason, Reuel's command to the son-in-law living under his roof. The next verse of Jasher has the second son circumcised and named for deliverance, so the two births mark the two halves of Moses' time in Midian, the stranger first and then the man Elohim (God) had helped.
cards.s_text: And Zipporah conceived and bare a son and he called his name Gershom, for he said, I was a stranger in a foreign land; but he circumcised not his foreskin, at the command of Reuel his father-in-law.
cards.t_text: And she bare him a son, and he called his name Gershom: for he said, I have been a stranger in a strange land.

cards.note: Exodus 2:21 — *And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.* The Exodus source for Jasher 78:7's marriage of Moses to Zipporah, daughter of Reuel/Jethro the Midianite.
cards.s_text: In those days Moses, the son of Amram, in Midian, took Zipporah, the daughter of Reuel the Midianite, for a wife.
cards.t_text: And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

cards.note: Exodus 3:2 — *And the angel of Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.* The canon scene Jasher 79:3 retells — the bush burns yet the fire has no power to consume it.
cards.s_text: And when he came to Horeb, Yahuah (the Lord) appeared there to him in the bush, and he found the bush burning with fire, but the fire had no power over the bush to consume it.
cards.t_text: And the angel of Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto him in a flame of fire out of the midst of a bush: and he looked, and, behold, the bush burned with fire, and the bush was not consumed.

cards.note: Exodus 3:6 — *Moreover he said, I am the Elohim (God) of thy father, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon Elohim (God).* The One who calls Moses out of the fire in Jasher 79:4 is the covenant Elohim of the fathers, not a new god.
cards.s_text: And Moses was greatly astonished at this sight, therefore the bush was not consumed, and he approached to see this mighty thing, and Yahuah (the Lord) called to Moses out of the fire and commanded him to go down to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to send the children of Israel from his service.
cards.t_text: Moreover he said, I am the Elohim (God) of your father, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob. And Moses hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon Elohim (God).

cards.note: Acts 7:30 — *And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of Yahuah (Lord) in a flame of fire in a bush.* Stephen recounts the same Horeb fire and commission to Egypt that Jasher 79:4 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Moses was greatly astonished at this sight, therefore the bush was not consumed, and he approached to see this mighty thing, and Yahuah (the Lord) called to Moses out of the fire and commanded him to go down to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, to send the children of Israel from his service.
cards.t_text: And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of Yahuah (Lord) in a flame of fire in a bush.

cards.note: Acts 7:34 — *I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send thee into Egypt.* The word that returns Moses to Egypt in Jasher 79:5 is the I AM come down to deliver the chosen people.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) said to Moses, Go, return to Egypt, for all those men who sought your life are dead, and you shall speak to Pharaoh to send forth the children of Israel from his land.
cards.t_text: I have seen, I have seen the affliction of my people which is in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and am come down to deliver them. And now come, I will send you into Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 3:20 — *And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.* The signs and wonders Yahuah shows Moses in Jasher 79:6 are the wonders by which Egypt will be smitten and the seed set free.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) showed him to do signs and wonders in Egypt before the eyes of Pharaoh and the eyes of his subjects, in order that they might believe that Yahuah (the Lord) had sent him.
cards.t_text: And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.

cards.note: Exodus 4:24 — *And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that Yahuah (LORD) met him, and sought to kill him.* The terse canon verse that Jasher 79:8 unfolds — the angel meeting Moses at the inn to take his life.
cards.s_text: And Moses rose up to go to Egypt, and he took his wife and sons with him, and he was at an inn in the road, and an angel of Elohim came down, and sought an occasion against him.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that Yahuah (LORD) met him, and sought to kill him.

cards.note: Exodus 4:25 — *Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband art thou to me.* Zipporah's sharp-rock circumcision in Jasher 79:12 is the canon act that delivers husband and son from the angel.
cards.s_text: And Zipporah hastened and took of the sharp rock stones that were there, and she circumcised her son, and delivered her husband and her son from the hand of the angel of Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: Then Zipporah took a sharp stone, and cut off the foreskin of her son, and cast it at his feet, and said, Surely a bloody husband are you to me.

cards.note: Genesis 17:14 — *And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he hath broken my covenant.* The covenant of Abraham that Jasher 79:9 says Moses transgressed by leaving Gershom uncircumcised.
cards.s_text: And he wished to kill him on account of his first born son, because he had not circumcised him, and had transgressed the covenant which Yahuah (the Lord) had made with Abraham.
cards.t_text: And the uncircumcised man child whose flesh of his foreskin is not circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people; he has broken my covenant.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:2 — *And you yourself know what He spake to you on Mount Sinai, and what prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place.* Jubilees names the very lodging-place attack of Jasher 79:8 as the work of Mastêmâ against the returning deliverer.
cards.s_text: And Moses rose up to go to Egypt, and he took his wife and sons with him, and he was at an inn in the road, and an angel of Elohim came down, and sought an occasion against him.
cards.t_text: And you yourself know what He spake to you on Mount Sinai, and what prince Mastêmâ desired to do with you when you were returning into Egypt on the way when you did meet him at the lodging-place.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:3 — *Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?* The deliverance from the inn-angel in Jasher 79:12 is Jubilees' account of Moses rescued from the one who sought to slay him.
cards.s_text: And Zipporah hastened and took of the sharp rock stones that were there, and she circumcised her son, and delivered her husband and her son from the hand of the angel of Yahuah (the Lord).
cards.t_text: Did he not with all his power seek to slay you and deliver the Egyptians out of your hand when he saw that you were sent to execute judgment and vengeance on the Egyptians?

cards.note: Exodus 4:27 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mount of Elohim (God), and kissed him.* The very meeting at the mountain of Elohim that Jasher 79:14 narrates, kiss and all.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him in that place, and he said to him, Go now toward Moses in the wilderness, and he went and met him in the mountain of Elohim, and he kissed him.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said to Aaron, Go into the wilderness to meet Moses. And he went, and met him in the mount of Elohim (God), and kissed him.

cards.note: Exodus 4:28 — *And Moses told Aaron all the words of Yahuah (LORD) who had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him.* The words of Yahuah that Moses and Aaron speak to Israel in Jasher 79:19 are the words and signs Moses received at the bush.
cards.s_text: And Moses and Aaron came to Egypt to the community of the children of Israel, and they spoke to them all the words of Yahuah (the Lord), and the people rejoiced an exceeding great rejoicing.
cards.t_text: And Moses told Aaron all the words of Yahuah (LORD) who had sent him, and all the signs which he had commanded him.

cards.note: Exodus 4:31 — *And the people believed: and when they heard that Yahuah (LORD) had visited the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.* The exceeding great rejoicing of the people in Jasher 79:19 is the canon's believing, head-bowed worship of the chosen nation.
cards.s_text: And Moses and Aaron came to Egypt to the community of the children of Israel, and they spoke to them all the words of Yahuah (the Lord), and the people rejoiced an exceeding great rejoicing.
cards.t_text: And the people believed: and when they heard that Yahuah (LORD) had visited the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and that he had looked upon their affliction, then they bowed their heads and worshipped.

cards.note: Exodus 7:10 — *And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as Yahuah (LORD) had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.* The exact rod-into-serpent sign Aaron performs before Pharaoh in Jasher 79:36.
cards.s_text: And Aaron hastened and threw the rod out of his hand before Pharaoh and before his servants, and the rod turned into a serpent.
cards.t_text: And Moses and Aaron went in unto Pharaoh, and they did so as Yahuah (LORD) had commanded: and Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh, and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

cards.note: Exodus 7:12 — *For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.* The swallowing of the sorcerers' rods in Jasher 79:42 is the canon's own verdict — the counterfeit is consumed.
cards.s_text: And when they were restored to rods, the rod of Aaron swallowed up their rods.
cards.t_text: For they cast down every man his rod, and they became serpents: but Aaron’s rod swallowed up their rods.

cards.note: Exodus 4:3 — *And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.* The rod of Elohim wielded in Jasher 79:36 is the same staff first turned serpent before Moses at Horeb.
cards.s_text: And Aaron hastened and threw the rod out of his hand before Pharaoh and before his servants, and the rod turned into a serpent.
cards.t_text: And he said, Cast it on the ground. And he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses fled from before it.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:9 — *And the prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you.* The sorcerers who cast their rods in Jasher 79:37 are, in Jubilees, helped by Mastêmâ to work before Moses.
cards.s_text: And the sorcerers saw this and they cast each man his rod upon the ground and they became serpents.
cards.t_text: And the prince of the Mastêmâ stood up against you, and sought to cast you into the hands of Pharaoh, and he helped the Egyptian sorcerers, and they stood up and wrought before you.

cards.note: Exodus 5:2 — *And Pharaoh said, Who is Yahuah (LORD), that I should obey his voice to let Yashar'el (Israel) go? I know not Yahuah (LORD), neither will I let Yashar'el (Israel) go.* Pharaoh's 'I know not Yahuah' in Jasher 79:46 is the canon's defining refusal of the I AM.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh turned to Moses and Aaron and said to them, I know not Yahuah (the Lord) whom you have declared, neither will I send his people.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh said, Who is Yahuah (LORD), that I should obey his voice to let Yashar'el (Israel) go? I know not Yahuah (LORD), neither will I let Yashar'el (Israel) go.

cards.note: Exodus 5:1 — *And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.* The 'send forth my people that they may serve me' of Jasher 79:25 is Exodus' own demand to let the nation go and keep the feast.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh said to Moses, What do you require? and they answered him, saying, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) of the Hebrews has sent us to you, to say, Send forth my people that they may serve me.
cards.t_text: And afterward Moses and Aaron went in, and told Pharaoh, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.

cards.note: Exodus 5:3 — *And they said, The Elohim (God) of the Hebrews hath met with us: let us go, we pray thee, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God); lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.* The three-days' journey to sacrifice in Jasher 79:48 is the canon's same plea, with the same warning of plague and sword.
cards.s_text: Now therefore send us, that we may take a journey for three days in the wilderness, and there may sacrifice to him, for from the days of our going down to Egypt, he has not taken from our hands either burnt offering, oblation or sacrifice, and if you will not send us, his anger will be kindled against you, and he will smite Egypt either with the plague or with the sword.
cards.t_text: And they said, The Elohim (God) of the Hebrews has met with us: let us go, we pray you, three days’ journey into the desert, and sacrifice unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God); lest he fall upon us with pestilence, or with the sword.

cards.note: Exodus 3:15 — *And Elohim (God) said moreover unto Moses... Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of your fathers, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.* The Name proclaimed from the days of the ancestors in Jasher 79:47 is the everlasting memorial-name given at the bush.
cards.s_text: And they answered and said to the king, Yahuah Elohim of elohim (of Gods) is his name, and he proclaimed his name over us from the days of our ancestors, and sent us, saying, Go to Pharaoh and say to him, Send my people that they may serve me.
cards.t_text: And Elohim (God) said moreover unto Moses, Thus shall you say unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of your fathers, the Elohim (God) of Abraham, the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob, has sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.

cards.note: Exodus 5:9 — *Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.* Pharaoh's harsher labor in Jasher 79:52 is the canon's straw-and-bricks decree to crush the people's hope.
cards.s_text: And he drove them from him, and he ordered the labor upon Israel to be more severe than it was yesterday and before.
cards.t_text: Let there more work be laid upon the men, that they may labour therein; and let them not regard vain words.

cards.note: Exodus 3:20 — *And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.* Yahuah's promise of an outstretched hand and heavy plagues in Jasher 79:55 is the canon's own pledge to smite Egypt and free the people.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) said to Moses, Behold you will see that with an outstretched hand and heavy plagues, Pharaoh will send the children of Israel from his land.
cards.t_text: And I will stretch out my hand, and smite Egypt with all my wonders which I will do in the midst thereof: and after that he will let you go.

cards.note: Exodus 12:12 — *For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The heavy plagues foretold in Jasher 79:55 are Yahuah's judgment on the gods of Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) said to Moses, Behold you will see that with an outstretched hand and heavy plagues, Pharaoh will send the children of Israel from his land.
cards.t_text: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Jubilees 48:5 — *And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies... and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.* The plagues that begin to be promised in Jasher 79:55 are Jubilees' great covenant vengeance on Egypt and her idols.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) said to Moses, Behold you will see that with an outstretched hand and heavy plagues, Pharaoh will send the children of Israel from his land.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.

cards.note: Exodus 7:16 — *And thou shalt say unto him, Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of the Hebrews hath sent me unto thee, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto thou wouldest not hear.* The same charge Jasher 80:1 retells — Moses sent again to bring Israel out.
cards.s_text: And at the end of two years, Yahuah (the Lord) again sent Moses to Pharaoh to bring forth the children of Israel, and to send them out of the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And you shall say unto him, Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of the Hebrews has sent me unto you, saying, Let my people go, that they may serve me in the wilderness: and, behold, hitherto you would not hear.

cards.note: Exodus 7:17 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), In this thou shalt know that I am Yahuah (LORD): behold, I will smite with the rod that is in mine hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.* Pharaoh's refusal to hearken to the voice of Yahuah in Jasher 80:2 is the refusal to know the Name.
cards.s_text: And Moses went and came to the house of Pharaoh, and he spoke to him the words of Yahuah (the Lord) who had sent him, but Pharaoh would not hearken to the voice of Yahuah (the Lord), and Elohim (God) roused his might in Egypt upon Pharaoh and his subjects, and Elohim smote Pharaoh and his people with very great and sore plagues.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), In this you shall know that I am Yahuah (LORD): behold, I will smite with the rod that is in my hand upon the waters which are in the river, and they shall be turned to blood.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:4 — *And I delivered you out of his hand, and you did perform the signs and wonders which you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.* Jubilees names the same sending against Pharaoh and his subjects that Jasher 80:2 records.
cards.s_text: And Moses went and came to the house of Pharaoh, and he spoke to him the words of Yahuah (the Lord) who had sent him, but Pharaoh would not hearken to the voice of Yahuah (the Lord), and Elohim (God) roused his might in Egypt upon Pharaoh and his subjects, and Elohim smote Pharaoh and his people with very great and sore plagues.
cards.t_text: And I delivered you out of his hand, and you did perform the signs and wonders which you were sent to perform in Egypt against Pharaoh, and against all his house, and against his servants and his people.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (the Lord) sent by the hand of Aaron and turned all the waters of Egypt into blood, with all their streams and rivers.* (Jasher 80:3). *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take thy rod, and stretch out thine hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.* (Exodus 7:19). Jasher gives the first plague in one line and Exodus gives the command behind it, but both put the hand on Aaron. Yahuah (the Lord) sends by Aaron's hand, Aaron stretches out the rod, and every stream and river of Egypt turns to blood. Jasher's next verses follow the plague into the pitcher and the cup, which is what Exodus means by vessels of wood and vessels of stone. The plagues begin where Egypt drinks.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent by the hand of Aaron and turned all the waters of Egypt into blood, with all their streams and rivers.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Take your rod, and stretch out your hand upon the waters of Egypt, upon their streams, upon their rivers, and upon their ponds, and upon all their pools of water, that they may become blood; and that there may be blood throughout all the land of Egypt, both in vessels of wood, and in vessels of stone.

cards.note: Exodus 8:3 — *And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into thine house, and into thy bedchamber, and upon thy bed, and into the house of thy servants, and upon thy people, and into thine ovens, and into thy kneadingtroughs:* The frogs filling the Egyptians' houses in Jasher 80:6 match Exodus' second plague.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent again and caused all their waters to bring forth frogs, and all the frogs came into the houses of the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And the river shall bring forth frogs abundantly, which shall go up and come into your house, and into your bedchamber, and upon your bed, and into the house of your servants, and upon your people, and into your ovens, and into your kneadingtroughs:

cards.note: Exodus 8:16 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out thy rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.* The dust turned to lice in Jasher 80:10 is Exodus' third plague.
cards.s_text: And he sent and smote their dust to lice, and the lice became in Egypt to the height of two cubits upon the earth.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out your rod, and smite the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Psalm 105:30 — *Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, in the chambers of their kings.* The Psalmist recites the same frog-plague Jasher 80:6 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent again and caused all their waters to bring forth frogs, and all the frogs came into the houses of the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: Their land brought forth frogs in abundance, in the chambers of their kings.

cards.note: Exodus 8:22 — *And I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end thou mayest know that I am Yahuah (LORD) in the midst of the earth.* The swarms loosed on all Egypt in Jasher 80:13 are Exodus' swarm-plague, with Goshen kept apart.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent all kinds of beasts of the field into Egypt, and they came and destroyed all Egypt, man and beast, and trees, and all things that were in Egypt.
cards.t_text: And I will sever in that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwell, that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end you may know that I am Yahuah (LORD) in the midst of the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 9:4 — *And Yahuah (LORD) shall sever between the cattle of Yashar'el (Israel) and the cattle of Egypt: and there shall nothing die of all that is the children's of Yashar'el (Israel).* Jasher 80:26's Goshen herds untouched while Egypt's perish is Exodus' own severing — election kept.
cards.s_text: And there remained of the cattle of the Egyptians only one in ten, and of the cattle belonging to Israel in Goshen not one died.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) shall sever between the cattle of Yashar'el (Israel) and the cattle of Egypt: and there shall nothing die of all that is the children’s of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 9:9 — *And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.* The burning inflammation bursting the Egyptians' skin in Jasher 80:27 is the plague of boils.
cards.s_text: And Elohim sent a burning inflammation in the flesh of the Egyptians, which burst their skins, and it became a severe itch in all the Egyptians from the soles of their feet to the crowns of their heads.
cards.t_text: And it shall become small dust in all the land of Egypt, and shall be a boil breaking forth with blains upon man, and upon beast, throughout all the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:5 — *And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.* Jubilees catalogs the same plague-sequence — pestilence on the cattle included — that Jasher 80:24-27 narrates.
cards.s_text: And Elohim sent the pestilence, and the pestilence pervaded Egypt, in the horses and asses, and in the camels, in herds of oxen and sheep and in man.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) executed a great vengeance on them for Yashar’el’s (Israel’s) sake, and smote them through (the plagues of) blood and frogs, lice and dog-flies, and malignant boils breaking forth in blains; and their cattle by death; and by hail-stones, thereby He destroyed everything that grew for them; and by locusts which devoured the residue which had been left by the hail, and by darkness; and (by the death) of the first-born of men and animals, and on all their idols Yahuah (God) took vengeance and burned them with fire.

cards.note: Exodus 9:24 — *So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.* The mingling fire amidst the hail of Jasher 80:31 is Exodus' seventh plague exactly.
cards.s_text: Also every green herb became dry and perished, for a mingling fire descended amidst the hail, therefore the hail and the fire consumed all things.
cards.t_text: So there was hail, and fire mingled with the hail, very grievous, such as there was none like it in all the land of Egypt since it became a nation.

cards.note: Exodus 10:19 — *And Yahuah (LORD) turned a mighty strong west wind, which took away the locusts, and cast them into the Red sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.* The sea-wind thrusting the locusts into the Red Sea in Jasher 80:35 is Exodus' own ending of the locust-plague.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) turned a mighty wind of the sea which took away all the locusts, even those that were salted, and thrust them into the Red Sea; not one locust remained within the boundaries of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) turned a mighty strong west wind, which took away the locusts, and cast them into the Red sea; there remained not one locust in all the coasts of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 10:22 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:* The three days of darkness over Egypt and Pathros in Jasher 80:36 is the ninth plague.
cards.s_text: And Elohim sent darkness upon Egypt, that the whole land of Egypt and Pathros became dark for three days, so that a man could not see his hand when he lifted it to his mouth.
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand toward heaven; and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt three days:

cards.note: Psalm 78:47 — *He destroyed their vines with hail, and their sycomore trees with frost.* The hail smiting the Egyptians' vines and fruit trees in Jasher 80:30 is the judgment Asaph rehearses.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (the Lord) sent a very heavy hail, which smote their vines and broke their fruit trees and dried them up that they fell upon them.
cards.t_text: He destroyed their vines with hail, and their sycomore trees with frost.

cards.note: Exodus 12:13 — *And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where ye are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.* The 'make your Passover... I will pass over you' of Jasher 80:41 is the very ordinance of Exodus 12.
cards.s_text: And the days of darkness passed away, and Yahuah (the Lord) sent Moses and Aaron to the children of Israel, saying, Celebrate your feast and make your Passover, for behold I come in the midst of the night amongst all the Egyptians, and I will smite all their first born, from the first born of a man to the first born of a beast, and when I see your Passover, I will pass over you.
cards.t_text: And the blood shall be to you for a token upon the houses where you are: and when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and the plague shall not be upon you to destroy you, when I smite the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 12:14 — *And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.* Torah stands — the feast Jasher 80:41 commands Israel to celebrate is kept for ever.
cards.s_text: And the days of darkness passed away, and Yahuah (the Lord) sent Moses and Aaron to the children of Israel, saying, Celebrate your feast and make your Passover, for behold I come in the midst of the night amongst all the Egyptians, and I will smite all their first born, from the first born of a man to the first born of a beast, and when I see your Passover, I will pass over you.
cards.t_text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and you shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

cards.note: Exodus 12:29 — *And it came to pass, that at midnight Yahuah (LORD) smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.* The midnight smiting of the firstborn in Jasher 80:43 is Exodus' tenth plague word for word.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass in the middle of the night, that Yahuah (the Lord) went forth in the midst of Egypt, and smote all the first born of the Egyptians, from the first born of man to the first born of beast.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, that at midnight Yahuah (LORD) smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh that sat on his throne unto the firstborn of the captive that was in the dungeon; and all the firstborn of cattle.

cards.note: *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry throughout Egypt in that night, for there was not a house in which there was not a corpse.* (Jasher 80:44). *And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.* (Exodus 12:30). Jasher 80:44 is Exodus 12:30 nearly word for word: the king rising in the night, the servants, all the Egyptians, the cry, and not a house without its dead. Jasher adds in the next verse that even the carved likenesses of the firstborn fell from the walls, so that the judgment reached the images as well as the sons. The night Yahuah (the Lord) passed through Egypt is told in both books with the same breath.
cards.s_text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he and all his servants and all the Egyptians, and there was a great cry throughout Egypt in that night, for there was not a house in which there was not a corpse.
cards.t_text: And Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt; for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

cards.note: Jubilees 49:3 — *And this is the sign which Yahuah (God) gave them: Into every house on the lintels of which they saw the blood of a lamb of the first year, into (that) house they should not enter to slay, but should pass by (it), that all those should be saved that were in the house because the sign of the blood was on its lintels.* Jubilees keeps the same blood-sign Passover Jasher 80:41 commands.
cards.s_text: And the days of darkness passed away, and Yahuah (the Lord) sent Moses and Aaron to the children of Israel, saying, Celebrate your feast and make your Passover, for behold I come in the midst of the night amongst all the Egyptians, and I will smite all their first born, from the first born of a man to the first born of a beast, and when I see your Passover, I will pass over you.
cards.t_text: And this is the sign which Yahuah (God) gave them: Into every house on the lintels of which they saw the blood of a lamb of the first year, into (that) house they should not enter to slay, but should pass by (it), that all those should be saved that were in the house because the sign of the blood was on its lintels.

cards.note: Exodus 12:12 — *For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The ten plagues Moses counts in Jasher 80:51 are Yahuah's judgment on the gods of Egypt.
cards.s_text: And Moses said to her, Surely ten plagues did Yahuah (the Lord) bring upon Egypt; did any evil accrue to you from any of them? did one of them affect you? and she said, No.
cards.t_text: For I will pass through the land of Egypt this night, and will smite all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and beast; and against all the gods of Egypt I will execute judgment: I am Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Numbers 33:4 — *For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which Yahuah (LORD) had smitten among them: upon their gods also Yahuah (LORD) executed judgments.* The same verdict on Egypt's gods stands behind the ten plagues of Jasher 80:51.
cards.s_text: And Moses said to her, Surely ten plagues did Yahuah (the Lord) bring upon Egypt; did any evil accrue to you from any of them? did one of them affect you? and she said, No.
cards.t_text: For the Egyptians buried all their firstborn, which Yahuah (LORD) had smitten among them: upon their gods also Yahuah (LORD) executed judgments.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:7–8 — *And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar'el (Israel). And Yahuah (God) did everything for Yashar'el's (Israel's) sake, and according to His covenant, which He had ordained with Abraham that He would take vengeance on them as they had brought them by force into bondage.* Jubilees counts the same ten judgments Moses tallies in Jasher 80:51.
cards.s_text: And Moses said to her, Surely ten plagues did Yahuah (the Lord) bring upon Egypt; did any evil accrue to you from any of them? did one of them affect you? and she said, No.
cards.t_text: And everything took place according to your words; ten great and terrible judgments came on the land of Egypt that you might execute vengeance on it for Yashar’el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 12:36 — *And Yahuah (LORD) gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.* The vessels of silver and gold and the stripping of Egypt in Jasher 80:61 is Exodus' spoiling.
cards.s_text: And the children of Israel asked of the Egyptians, vessels of silver, and vessels of gold, and garments, and the children of Israel stripped the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.

cards.note: Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* Moses bringing up Joseph's coffin in Jasher 80:62 is the keeping of this oath.
cards.s_text: And Moses hastened and rose up and went to the river of Egypt, and brought up from there the coffin of Joseph and took it with him.
cards.t_text: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and you shall carry up my bones away hence with you.

cards.note: Genesis 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* The deathbed oath Moses fulfills in Jasher 80:62 was sworn here, generations before.
cards.s_text: And Moses hastened and rose up and went to the river of Egypt, and brought up from there the coffin of Joseph and took it with him.
cards.t_text: And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from hence.
