Judith's Yashar'el (Israel) hears that the invader is coming and does two things: they hold the narrow passes into Judea, and they fast and cry to Yahuah (God) (Judith 4:9–13). Daniel describes the king such a people will keep facing, one whose indignation is against the holy covenant itself and who has intelligence with those inside who forsake it. The Maccabees would meet that king in Antiochus, and the pattern does not end there. The war is never only about the land; it is a war on the covenant, with help from the covenant's own deserters, and the people who keep it answer at the passes and on their knees.
cards.s_text: Charging them to keep the passages of the hill country: for by them there was an entrance into Judea, and it was easy to stop them that would come up, because the passage was straight, for two men at the most.
cards.t_text: For the ships of Chittim shall come against him: therefore he shall be grieved, and return, and have indignation against the holy covenant: so shall he do; he shall even return, and have intelligence with them that forsake the holy covenant.

cards.note: Ezra 6:16 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel), the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) with joy,* the same return-and-rededication that Judith 4:3 names as 'sanctified after the profanation.'
cards.s_text: For they were newly returned from the captivity, and all the people of Judea were lately gathered together: and the vessels, and the altar, and the house, were sanctified after the profanation.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel), the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) with joy,

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Achior's Chaldea-and-idols opening is the very credo Joshua sets before the tribes.
cards.s_text: And they sojourned heretofore in Mesopotamia, because they would not follow the gods of their fathers, which were in the land of Chaldea.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* Holofernes trusts the power of his horses against a nation "that came out of Egypt" — the very nation whose song is that Yahuah threw horse and rider into the sea.
cards.s_text: He will send his power, and will destroy them from the face of the earth, and their Elohim (God) shall not deliver them: but we his servants will destroy them as one man; for they are not able to sustain the power of our horses.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:15 — *And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.* Bethulia's people falling down before Yahuah against the king who claimed to be Yahuah is Hizqiyahu answering Assyria's blasphemy with "thou alone."
cards.s_text: Then the people fell down and worshipped Yahuah (God), and cried to Yahuah (God). saying,
cards.t_text: And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: Isaiah 37:23 — *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).* Judith 9:14 prays that every nation acknowledge the One the Assyrian blasphemed, the sole protector of Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: And make every nation and tribe to acknowledge that you are Yahuah (God) of all power and might, and that there is none other that protecteth the people of Yashar'el (Israel) but you.
cards.t_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Isaiah 37:23 — *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).* The Assyrian purpose to defile the sanctuary in Judith 9:8 is the same blasphemy lifted against the Holy One.
cards.s_text: Throw down their strength in your power, and bring down their force in your wrath: for they have purposed to defile your sanctuary, and to pollute the tabernacle where your glorious name resteth and to cast down with sword the horn of your altar.
cards.t_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Isaiah 31:1 — *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!* The Assyrians' trust in horse and spear of Judith 9:7 is the same condemned reliance on flesh over the Holy One.
cards.s_text: For, behold, the Assyrians are multiplied in their power; they are exalted with horse and man; they glory in the strength of their footmen; they trust in shield, and spear, and bow, and sling; and know not that you are Yahuah (God) that breakest the battles: Yahuah (God) is your name.
cards.t_text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!

cards.note: Exodus 15:3 — *Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war: Yahuah (LORD) is his name.* Judith 9:7 names Him the One that breaketh the battles, the same warrior-name Yashar'el sang at the Red Sea.
cards.s_text: For, behold, the Assyrians are multiplied in their power; they are exalted with horse and man; they glory in the strength of their footmen; they trust in shield, and spear, and bow, and sling; and know not that you are Yahuah (God) that breakest the battles: Yahuah (God) is your name.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) is a man of war: Yahuah (LORD) is his name.

cards.note: Judith 13:18 — *Then said Ozias to her, O daughter, blessed art you of the most high Yahuah (God) above all the women upon the earth; and blessed be Yahuah (God), which has created the heavens and the earth, which has directed you to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.* Her "my life is magnified this day" is answered when Yashar'el blesses her "above all the women upon the earth" — the lowly handmaid called blessed by all.
cards.s_text: So Judith said, I will drink now, my lord, because my life is magnified in me this day more than all the days since I was born.
cards.t_text: Then said Ozias to her, O daughter, blessed art you of the most high Yahuah (God) above all the women upon the earth; and blessed be Yahuah (God), which has created the heavens and the earth, which has directed you to the cutting off of the head of the chief of our enemies.

cards.note: Judith 13:7 — *And approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), this day.* What she announces in 12:4 — that Yahuah works "by my hand" — comes to pass the next night when she takes Holofernes by the hair and asks for strength.
cards.s_text: Then said Judith to him As your soul lives, my lord, yours handmaid shall not spend those things that I have, before Yahuah (God) work by my hand the things that he has determined.
cards.t_text: And approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), this day.

cards.note: Exodus 23:25 — *And ye shall serve Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and he shall bless thy bread, and thy water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of thee.* Judith serves the Elohim of Yashar'el alone and pleads for the "raising up" of her people — the covenant service that brings deliverance, not the worship of Nabuchodonosor.
cards.s_text: And when she came out, she besought Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) to direct her way to the raising up of the children of her people.
cards.t_text: And you shall serve Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and he shall bless your bread, and your water; and I will take sickness away from the midst of you.

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* As Israel sang to Yahuah at the overthrow of Pharaoh, so the people worship Yahuah who has brought the enemies of His people to nought.
cards.s_text: Then all the people were wonderfully astonished, and bowed themselves and worshipped Yahuah (God), and said with one accord, Blessed be you, O our Elohim (God), which have this day brought to nought the enemies of your people.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 17:45 — *Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom thou hast defied.* Judith's plea, *Strengthen me, O Yahuah... this day*, leans on the same name of Yahuah of hosts in which David met Goliath.
cards.s_text: And approached to his bed, and took hold of the hair of his head, and said, Strengthen me, O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), this day.
cards.t_text: Then said David to the Philistine, You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to you in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have defied.

cards.note: Exodus 14:25 — *And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Yashar'el (Israel); for Yahuah (LORD) fighteth for them against the Egyptians.* Israel pursuing and overthrowing the fleeing host in Judith 14:4 is Yahuah fighting for them, as the Egyptians confessed when they fled the face of Israel.
cards.s_text: So you, and all that inhabit the coast of Yashar'el (Israel), shall pursue them, and overthrow them as they go.
cards.t_text: And took off their chariot wheels, that they drave them heavily: so that the Egyptians said, Let us flee from the face of Yashar'el (Israel); for Yahuah (LORD) fighteth for them against the Egyptians.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 18:6 — *And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Yashar'el (Israel), singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.* The women running together with dance to honor the one who slew the enemy's champion is the same answering-song that hails Judith (Judith 15:12).
cards.s_text: Then all the women of Yashar'el (Israel) ran together to see her, and blessed her, and made a dance among them for her: and she took branches in her hand, and gave also to the women that were with her.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass as they came, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine, that the women came out of all cities of Yashar'el (Israel), singing and dancing, to meet king Saul, with tabrets, with joy, and with instruments of musick.

cards.note: Judges 4:23 — *So Elohim (God) subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* As Yahuah subdued Canaan's king after a woman drove the nail, so He breaks Assur before Israel after a woman takes the head (Judith 15:5).
cards.s_text: Now when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) heard it, they all fell upon them with one consent, and slew them to Chobai: likewise also they that came from Jerusalem, and from all the hill country, (for men had told them what things were done in the camp of their enemies) and they that were in Galaad, and in Galilee, chased them with a great slaughter, until they were past Damascus and the borders thereof.
cards.t_text: So Elohim (God) subdued on that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.* (Judith 16:6). *But Elohim (God) hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;* (1 Corinthians 1:27). The Almighty Yahuah (God) brought a whole army to nothing by the hand of one widow, and Judith's song says so without apology. Paul tells the Corinthians this is how Elohim (God) works on purpose: he chooses the weak things to confound the mighty and the foolish things to confound the wise, so that no flesh can glory in his presence (1 Corinthians 1:29). Holofernes bragged of what he would do to Yashar'el (Israel); the next verse of the song says the mighty one did not fall by young men or giants but by a woman. The hand of a woman is the weak thing, and the weak thing is what he chose.
cards.s_text: But the Almighty Yahuah (God) has disappointed them by the hand of a woman.
cards.t_text: But Elohim (God) has chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and Elohim (God) has chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty;

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* Judith's whole nation sings after her exactly as Israel sang after Moses at the Red Sea — the same redeemed-people chorus.
cards.s_text: Then Judith began to sing this thanksgiving in all Yashar'el (Israel), and all the people sang after her this song of praise.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: Psalm 124:3 — *Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:* Without the hand that delivered them from all those evils (The Rest of Esther 10:9), the assembled nations would have swallowed Yashar'el alive.
cards.s_text: And my nation is this Yashar'el (Israel), which cried to Yahuah (God), and were saved: for Yahuah (God) has saved his people, and Yahuah (God) has delivered us from all those evils, and Yahuah (God) has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
cards.t_text: Then they had swallowed us up quick, when their wrath was kindled against us:

cards.note: Psalm 124:1 — *If it had not been Yahuah (LORD) who was on our side, now may Yashar'el (Israel) say;* The very confession of The Rest of Esther 10:9, that it was Yahuah and not the sword who saved His people.
cards.s_text: And my nation is this Yashar'el (Israel), which cried to Yahuah (God), and were saved: for Yahuah (God) has saved his people, and Yahuah (God) has delivered us from all those evils, and Yahuah (God) has wrought signs and great wonders, which have not been done among the Gentiles.
cards.t_text: If it had not been Yahuah (LORD) who was on our side, now may Yashar'el (Israel) say;

cards.note: Deuteronomy 25:17 — *Remember what Amalek did unto thee by the way, when ye were come forth out of Egypt;* The nations assembled to destroy the Name of the Yahudim (The Rest of Esther 10:8) are the standing order of Amalek that Torah commands Yashar'el never to forget.
cards.s_text: And the nations were those that were assembled to destroy the name of the Yahudim (Jews):
cards.t_text: Remember what Amalek did unto you by the way, when you were come forth out of Egypt;

cards.note: Exodus 17:8 — *Then came Amalek, and fought with Yashar'el (Israel) in Rephidim.* Aman the Agagite, the second dragon of The Rest of Esther 10:7, is the seed of the Amalek that first warred against Yashar'el at Rephidim.
cards.s_text: And the two dragons are I and Aman.
cards.t_text: Then came Amalek, and fought with Yashar'el (Israel) in Rephidim.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 15:2 — *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.* Haman the Agagite of Rest of Esther 12:6 is the line of Agag king of Amalek, carrying forward the ancient enmity Yahuah remembers.
cards.s_text: Howbeit Aman the son of Amadathus the Agagite, who was in great honour with the king, sought to molest Mardocheus and his people because of the two eunuchs of the king.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:23 — *Sing, O ye heavens; for Yahuah (LORD) hath done it: shout, ye lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, ye mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for Yahuah (LORD) hath redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Yashar'el (Israel).* The Maker of heaven and earth in Mordecai's prayer is the same who, having made all things, redeems Jacob — creation and salvation in one hand.
cards.s_text: For you have made heaven and earth, and all the wondrous things under the heaven.
cards.t_text: Sing, O you heavens; for Yahuah (LORD) has done it: shout, you lower parts of the earth: break forth into singing, you mountains, O forest, and every tree therein: for Yahuah (LORD) has redeemed Jacob, and glorified himself in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Psalm 83:4 — *They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yashar'el (Israel) may be no more in remembrance.* Haman's plot to send a people "in one day" into the grave is one episode of the recurring confederate vow to erase Israel from the earth.
cards.s_text: That they, who of old and now also are malicious, may in one day with violence go into the grave, and so ever hereafter cause our affairs to be well settled, and without trouble.
cards.t_text: They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Yashar'el (Israel) may be no more in remembrance.

cards.note: *From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.* (The Rest of Esther 14:5). *For thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.* (Deuteronomy 7:6). Esther says she heard it in her youth, in the tribe of her family: Yahuah (God) took Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people for a perpetual inheritance. She is quoting Moses from memory in a Persian palace. Moses had said it to the whole people: chosen above all people on the face of the earth, a special people to himself. Esther is in exile, her people scattered under a foreign king and marked for slaughter, and nothing about that has cancelled what she heard in her tribe. A chosen people stays chosen in the lands of their scattering, and the inheritance is perpetual because the one who gave it does not take it back.
cards.s_text: From my youth up I have heard in the tribe of my family that you, O Yahuah (God), tookest Yashar'el (Israel) from among all people, and our fathers from all their predecessors, for a perpetual inheritance, and you have performed whatsoever you did promise them.
cards.t_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has chosen you to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.

cards.note: *For your power stands not in multitude nor your might in strong men: for you are a Yahuah (God) of the afflicted, an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.* (Judith 9:11). *But deliver us with yours hand, and help me that am desolate, and which have no other help but you.* (The Rest of Esther 14:14). Two women, two prayers, the same confession. Judith says Yahuah (God) is the helper of the oppressed and the saviour of those without hope, that his power never stood in numbers or strong men. Esther says it as a plea rather than a creed: deliver us with your hand, help me that am desolate, I have no other help but you. Each one stands alone in front of a power that means to wipe out her people, and each one knows the only hand that can turn it. The strength of Yashar'el (Israel) in both books is a woman on her knees who has run out of every other help.
cards.s_text: But deliver us with yours hand, and help me that am desolate, and which have no other help but you.
cards.t_text: For your power stands not in multitude nor your might in strong men: for you are a Yahuah (God) of the afflicted, an helper of the oppressed, an upholder of the weak, a protector of the forlorn, a saviour of them that are without hope.

cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* Baruch 2:31's promise 'I will give them an heart, and ears to hear' is Jeremiah's new-covenant law written on the inward heart.
cards.s_text: And shall know that I am Yahuah (God), their Elohim (God): for I will give them an heart, and ears to hear:
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: Daniel 9:7 — *O Yahuah (Lord), righteousness belongeth unto thee, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Yahudah (Judah), and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Yashar'el (Israel), that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.* Baruch 2:6's 'to Yahuah appertaineth righteousness: but to us... open shame' is Daniel's confession in the same words.
cards.s_text: To Yahuah (God), our Elohim (God) appertaineth righteousness: but to us and to our fathers open shame, as appears this day.
cards.t_text: O Adonai (Lord), righteousness belongs unto you, but unto us confusion of faces, as at this day; to the men of Yahudah (Judah), and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Yashar'el (Israel), that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither you have driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against you.

cards.note: Daniel 9:11 — *Yea, all Yashar'el (Israel) have transgressed thy law, even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of Elohim (God), because we have sinned against him.* Daniel, in the same exile, names the law of Moses as the bond whose curse Baruch 2:2 says is now fulfilled in Jerusalem.
cards.s_text: To bring upon us great plagues, such as never happened under the whole heaven, as it came to pass in Jerusalem, according to the things that were written in the law of Moses;
cards.t_text: Yea, all Yashar'el (Israel) have transgressed your law, even by departing, that they might not obey your voice; therefore the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of Elohim (God), because we have sinned against him.

cards.note: Sirach 24:8 — *So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).* Sirach's Wisdom given to dwell in Jacob is the very Wisdom Baruch 3:36 says was given to Jacob his servant.
cards.s_text: He has found out all the way of knowledge, and has given it to Jacob his servant, and to Yashar'el (Israel) his beloved.
cards.t_text: So the Creator of all things gave me a commandment, and he that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:21 — *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* Baruch 5:5's children gathered from west to east are Ezekiel's children of Israel gathered on every side and brought back to their land.
cards.s_text: Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand on high, and look about toward the east, and behold your children gathered from the west to the east by the word of the Holy One, rejoicing in the remembrance of Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: Psalm 115:9 — *O Yashar'el (Israel), trust thou in Yahuah (LORD): he is their help and their shield.* The idol shows no mercy to widow or fatherless (Baruch 6:38); Yahuah alone is the help and shield Israel is to trust.
cards.s_text: They can shew no mercy to the widow, nor do good to the fatherless.
cards.t_text: O Yashar'el (Israel), trust you in Yahuah (LORD): he is their help and their shield.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:6 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).* The redeemer who is first and last is the answer to Baruch 6:36 — beside Him there is no god to save.
cards.s_text: They can save no man from death, neither deliver the weak from the mighty.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).

cards.note: *And it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of Yahuah (God) in them.* (Baruch 6:51). *And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.* (Deuteronomy 4:28). Moses told Yashar'el (Israel) ahead of time what exile would look like: scattered among the nations, they would serve gods that were the work of men's hands, blind and deaf and lifeless. The letter in Baruch is written from inside that exile, in Babylon, where the gods are exactly what Moses described, wood overlaid with silver and gold. What Deuteronomy gave as the curse for forsaking the covenant, Baruch watches play out, and he points at the idols and says what Moses said: there is no work of Yahuah (God) in them. The exile was never only a change of address; it was being handed over to the very idols that cannot see or hear, until the people would know the difference and come home.
cards.s_text: And it shall manifestly appear to all nations and kings that they are no gods, but the works of men’s hands, and that there is no work of Yahuah (God) in them.
cards.t_text: And there you shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.

cards.note: Isaiah 37:16 — *O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth.* Hezekiah's prayer over Assyria confesses the same "thou alone" that Azariah prays over Babylon (Song of the Three 1:22).
cards.s_text: And let them know that you are Yahuah (God), the only Yahuah (God), and glorious over the whole world.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:6 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).* The 'beside me there is no Elohim' that grounds Daniel's worship in Bel and the Dragon 1:25 is Isaiah's first-and-last King.
cards.s_text: Then said Daniel to the king, I will worship Yahuah (God), my Elohim (God): for he is the living Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 33:9 — *So Manasseh made Yahudah (Judah) and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom Yahuah (LORD) had destroyed before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The abominations and multiplied offences Manasseh confesses in 1:10 are the historical sins the Chronicler records of this same king.
cards.s_text: I am bowed down with many iron bands, that I cannot lift up my head, neither have any release: for I have provoked your wrath, and done evil before you: I did not your will, neither kept I your commandments: I have set up abominations, and have multiplied offences.
cards.t_text: So Manasseh made Yahudah (Judah) and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to err, and to do worse than the heathen, whom Yahuah (LORD) had destroyed before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The everlasting priesthood granted for Phinehas' zeal is the covenant Mattathias the priest is acting in when he is inflamed with zeal in 1 Maccabees 2:26.
cards.s_text: Thus dealt he zealously for the law of Yahuah (God) like as Phinees did to Zambri the son of Salom.
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* The delivered army's song in 1 Maccabees 4:24 is the song of the sea sung again after a like deliverance.
cards.s_text: After this they went home, and sung a song of thanksgiving, and praised Yahuah (God) in heaven: because it is good, because his mercy endureth forever.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 17:45 — *Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom thou hast defied.* Judas appeals to this very deliverance by the hand of David in 1 Maccabees 4:30.
cards.s_text: And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;
cards.t_text: Then said David to the Philistine, You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to you in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have defied.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 17:47 — *And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD'S, and he will give you into our hands.* David's confession that the battle is Yahuah's matches Judas' aim in 1 Maccabees 4:11, that all the heathen may know there is one who saves Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: That so all the heathen may know that there is one who delivers and saves Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saves not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’S, and he will give you into our hands.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:30 — *And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;* Deliverance comes by the chosen hand — David's, Jonathan's, Judas' — not by men who came not of that seed.
cards.s_text: Moreover these men came not of the seed of those, by whose hand deliverance was given to Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;

cards.note: Exodus 17:11 — *And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Yashar'el (Israel) prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.* Judas prevailing as he cried with prayer is the lifted hands of Moses over Amalek again — the victory flows from heaven, not the arm.
cards.s_text: So he went forth behind them in three companies, who sounded their trumpets, and cried with prayer.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Yashar'el (Israel) prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

cards.note: Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* The dispersed brethren of Galaad assembled from the least to the greatest foreshadow the assembling of the outcasts from the four corners.
cards.s_text: Then Judas gathered together all the Israelites that were in the country of Galaad, from the least to the greatest, even their wives, and their children, and their stuff, a very great host, to the end they might come into the land of Judea.
cards.t_text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:21 — *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.* The heathen assembling to destroy the Israelites only sets the stage for the LORD's own promise to take His children from among the heathen.
cards.s_text: Then the heathen that were at Galaad assembled themselves together against the Israelites that were in their quarters, to destroy them; but they fled to the fortress of Dathema.
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: Jeremiah 31:10 — *Hear the word of Yahuah (LORD), O ye nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Yashar'el (Israel) will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd doth his flock.* Simon bringing those of Galilee with their wives and children into Judea with great joy is the Shepherd gathering His flock.
cards.s_text: And those that were in Galilee, and in Arbattis, with their wives and their children, and all that they had, took he away with him, and brought them into Judea with great joy.
cards.t_text: Hear the word of Yahuah (LORD), O you nations, and declare it in the isles afar off, and say, He that scattered Yashar'el (Israel) will gather him, and keep him, as a shepherd does his flock.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 9:5 — *But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts.* The sister book names the heaven-sent stroke behind the grief that wasted Antiochus many days until he made account that he should die in 1 Maccabees 6:9.
cards.s_text: And there he continued many days: for his grief was ever more and more, and he made account that he should die.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:30 — *And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;* The Saviour of Israel who felled Goliath, not the senate of 1 Maccabees 8:20, is Israel's deliverer.
cards.s_text: Judas Maccabeus with his brothers, and the people of the Yahudim (Jews), have sent us to you, to make a confederacy and peace with you, and that we might be registered your confederates and friends.
cards.t_text: And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;

cards.note: *And to intreat them that they would take the yoke from them; for they saw that the kingdom of the Grecians did oppress Yashar'el (Israel) with servitude.* (1 Maccabees 8:18). *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!* (Isaiah 31:1). Judas sent to Rome asking them to take the Greek yoke off Yashar'el (Israel). Isaiah had pronounced woe on those who go down to Egypt for help and trust in horses and chariots because they are many, instead of looking to the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel). Rome was many and very strong, and the league was made, and in time the yoke of Rome lay heavier on the land than the yoke of the Greeks ever had. The verse in 1 Maccabees does not condemn the embassy, but Isaiah does, and the reader who has both in front of him can see what the arm of flesh bought.
cards.s_text: And to intreat them that they would take the yoke from them; for they saw that the kingdom of the Grecians did oppress Yashar'el (Israel) with servitude.
cards.t_text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The Maccabean zeal that purges Israel is rewarded as Phinehas's was, the covenant kept through the zealous seed.
cards.s_text: Thus the sword ceased from Yashar'el (Israel): but Jonathan dwelt at Machmas, and began to govern the people; and he destroyed the ungodly men out of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* Jonathan destroying the ungodly out of Israel carries forward Phinehas's zeal that turns away wrath and keeps the people.
cards.s_text: Thus the sword ceased from Yashar'el (Israel): but Jonathan dwelt at Machmas, and began to govern the people; and he destroyed the ungodly men out of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: 2 Samuel 3:38 — *And the king said unto his servants, Know ye not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Yashar'el (Israel)?* As David named the loss of a great man in Israel, so Jonathan and Simon bury their brother and Israel mourns a prince fallen.
cards.s_text: Moreover they bewailed him, and all Yashar'el (Israel) made great lamentation for him, and mourned many days, saying,
cards.t_text: And the king said unto his servants, Know you not that there is a prince and a great man fallen this day in Yashar'el (Israel)?

cards.note: 2 Samuel 1:19 — *The beauty of Yashar'el (Israel) is slain upon thy high places: how are the mighty fallen!* David's opening lament over Saul and Jonathan supplies the very cry Israel raises over Judas, the valiant man fallen that delivered Israel.
cards.s_text: How is the valiant man fallen, that delivered Yashar'el (Israel)!
cards.t_text: The beauty of Yashar'el (Israel) is slain upon your high places: how are the mighty fallen!

cards.note: Leviticus 23:2 — *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* The feasts and solemn days the king frees for the Yahudim are the very feasts Yahuah claims as His own holy convocations.
cards.s_text: Furthermore I will that all the feasts, and sabbaths, and new moons, and solemn days, and the three days before the feast, and the three days after the feast shall be all of immunity and freedom for all the Yahudim (Jews) in my realm.
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* Jonathan's ordination to the high priesthood is the covenant of an everlasting priesthood given to the zealous, kept alive in the house of Mattathias.
cards.s_text: Wherefore now this day we ordain you to be the high priest of your nation, and to be called the king’s friend; (and therewithal he sent him a purple robe and a crown of gold:) and require you to take our part, and keep friendship with us.
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* The Maccabean priesthood Jonathan now wears descends from Phinehas' zeal — the same fire for the covenant that turns away wrath.
cards.s_text: So in the seventh month of the hundred and sixtieth year, at the feast of the tabernacles, Jonathan put on the holy robe, and gathered together forces, and provided much armour.
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: Exodus 17:11 — *And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Yashar’el (Israel) prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.* That Jonathan prevails only after he prays (1 Maccabees 11:72) echoes Amalek’s defeat hanging on uplifted hands of intercession rather than the sword alone.
cards.s_text: Afterwards turning again to battle, he put them to flight, and so they ran away.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Moses held up his hand, that Yashar'el (Israel) prevailed: and when he let down his hand, Amalek prevailed.

cards.note: 1 Samuel 7:8 — *And the children of Yashar’el (Israel) said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.* Jonathan’s prayer in the dust (1 Maccabees 11:71) follows Israel’s pattern: deliverance comes through the cry to Yahuah, not the strength of the host.
cards.s_text: Then Jonathan rent his clothes, and cast earth upon his head, and prayed.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.

cards.note: Joshua 7:6 — *And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of Yahuah (LORD) until the eventide, he and the elders of Yashar’el (Israel), and put dust upon their heads.* Jonathan rending his clothes and casting earth on his head when the battle failed (1 Maccabees 11:71) is the very mourning-before-Yahuah of Joshua at Ai.
cards.s_text: Then Jonathan rent his clothes, and cast earth upon his head, and prayed.
cards.t_text: And Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of Yahuah (LORD) until the eventide, he and the elders of Yashar'el (Israel), and put dust upon their heads.

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar’el (Israel).* The priesthood confirmed to Jonathan (1 Maccabees 11:27) descends from the everlasting priesthood Yahuah covenanted to zealous Phinehas, the same zeal the Maccabean house carries.
cards.s_text: And confirmed him in the high priesthood, and in all the honours that he had before, and gave him preeminence among his chief friends.
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* The brothers slain for Israel's sake in 1 Maccabees 13:4 carry the priestly zeal of Phinehas, who stood for the covenant.
cards.s_text: By reason of which all my brothers are slain for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake, and I am left alone.
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:59 — *Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.* The sanctuary Simon beautifies in 1 Maccabees 14:15 is the one Judas first rededicated, founding the eight-day feast kept year by year.
cards.s_text: He beautified the sanctuary, and multiplied vessels of the temple.
cards.t_text: Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.

cards.note: Micah 4:6 — *In that day, saith Yahuah (LORD), will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted.* Simon establishing Yashar'el and strengthening the brought-low in 1 Maccabees 14:26 mirrors Yahuah's own promise to assemble the afflicted and driven-out.
cards.s_text: For he and his brothers and the house of his father have established Yashar'el (Israel), and chased away in fight their enemies from them, and confirmed their liberty.
cards.t_text: In that day, says Yahuah (LORD), will I assemble her that halteth, and I will gather her that is driven out, and her that I have afflicted;

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The house confirmed to Simon and his sons in 1 Maccabees 14:26 stands in the line of Phinehas, whose zeal won the covenant of an everlasting priesthood for his seed.
cards.s_text: For he and his brothers and the house of his father have established Yashar'el (Israel), and chased away in fight their enemies from them, and confirmed their liberty.
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: 1 Kings 4:25 — *And Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.* Simon's quiet land in 1 Maccabees 14:12 is Solomon's golden peace recovered, a sign of the greater Son of David's reign.
cards.s_text: For every man sat under his vine and his fig tree, and there was none to fray them:
cards.t_text: And Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) dwelt safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan even to Beer-sheba, all the days of Solomon.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 31:7 — *And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Yashar'el (Israel), Be strong and of a good courage: for thou must go with this people unto the land which Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn unto their fathers to give them; and thou shalt cause them to inherit it.* John made high priest *after his father* is the Torah handing-on of office — the line kept unbroken from Mattathias' house through the treachery to the next high priest.
cards.s_text: Behold, these are written in the chronicles of his priesthood, from the time he was made high priest after his father.
cards.t_text: And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Yashar'el (Israel), Be strong and of a good courage: for you must go with this people unto the land which Yahuah (LORD) has sworn unto their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 31:23 — *And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge, and said, Be strong and of a good courage: for thou shalt bring the children of Yashar'el (Israel) into the land which I sware unto them: and I will be with thee.* Simon's recital of *my father's house* that *delivered Yashar'el (Israel) often* is the same chain of deliverance entrusted, generation to generation, with the promise *I will be with thee*.
cards.s_text: Wherefore Simon called his two eldest sons, Judas and John, and said to them, I, and my brothers, and my father’s house, have ever from my youth to this day fought against the enemies of Yashar'el (Israel); and things have prospered so well in our hands, that we have delivered Yashar'el (Israel) often.
cards.t_text: And he gave Joshua the son of Nun a charge, and said, Be strong and of a good courage: for you shall bring the children of Yashar'el (Israel) into the land which I sware unto them: and I will be with you.

cards.note: Deuteronomy 31:7 — *And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Yashar'el (Israel), Be strong and of a good courage: for thou must go with this people unto the land which Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn unto their fathers to give them; and thou shalt cause them to inherit it.* Simon handing the war to Judas and John echoes Moses charging Joshua — the covenant commission passes from the dying captain to the young.
cards.s_text: But now I am old, and you, by the mercy of Yahuah (God), are of a sufficient age: be you instead of me and my brother, and go and fight for our nation, and the help from heaven be with you.
cards.t_text: And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Yashar'el (Israel), Be strong and of a good courage: for you must go with this people unto the land which Yahuah (LORD) has sworn unto their fathers to give them; and you shall cause them to inherit it.

cards.note: Psalms 147:2 — *Yahuah (LORD) doth build up Jerusalem: he gathereth together the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel).* The same gathering God whom Neemias entreats to bring home the scattered and despised in 2 Maccabees 1:27.
cards.s_text: Gather those together that are scattered from us, deliver them that serve among the heathen, look upon them that are despised and abhorred, and let the heathen know that you are our Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) does build up Jerusalem: he gathers together the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:21 — *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.* The two-house regathering from the heathen that Neemias prays for the scattered in 2 Maccabees 1:27.
cards.s_text: Gather those together that are scattered from us, deliver them that serve among the heathen, look upon them that are despised and abhorred, and let the heathen know that you are our Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:59 — *Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.* The companion record of the very feast of dedication the letter of 2 Maccabees 1:18 urges Egypt to keep.
cards.s_text: Therefore whereas we are now purposed to keep the purification of the temple upon the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, we thought it necessary to certify you thereof, that you also might keep it, as the feast of the tabernacles, and of the fire, which was given us when Neemias offered sacrifice, after that he had builded the temple and the altar.
cards.t_text: Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.

cards.note: Jeremiah 3:18 — *In those days the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.* The prophet who hid the ark names the gathering as Judah and Israel walking home together — the time the cave is opened.
cards.s_text: Which when Jeremy perceived, he blamed them, saying, As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that Yahuah (God) gather his people again together, and receive them to mercy.
cards.t_text: In those days the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.

cards.note: Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* Jeremy's regathered people are the two scattered houses Yahuah re-gathers, not a replacement people.
cards.s_text: Which when Jeremy perceived, he blamed them, saying, As for that place, it shall be unknown until the time that Yahuah (God) gather his people again together, and receive them to mercy.
cards.t_text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 9:5 — *But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;* The treasurer Heliodorus is felled and spared at a priest's prayer in 2 Maccabees 3:27, but the unrepentant Antiochus who likewise raged against the sanctuary is struck without remedy.
cards.s_text: And Heliodorus fell suddenly to the ground, and was compassed with great darkness: but they that were with him took him up, and put him into a litter.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (God) Almighty, Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), struck him with an incurable and invisible plague: or as soon as he had spoken these words, a pain of the bowels that was remediless came upon him, and sore torments of the inner parts;

cards.note: Ezekiel 34:2 — *Son of Adam, prophesy against the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel), prophesy, and say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel) that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?* The Woe over shepherds who feed themselves falls squarely on Menelaus, the beast-tempered high priest who devours rather than tends the flock.
cards.s_text: So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.
cards.t_text: Son of Adam, prophesy against the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel), prophesy, and say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) unto the shepherds; Woe be to the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel) that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 20:3 — *And shall say unto them, Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel), ye approach this day unto battle against your enemies: let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be ye terrified because of them.* Judas exhorting his men "not to be stricken with terror" and made "ready to die for the law" follows the very encouragement Torah commands before war.
cards.s_text: Thus when he had made them bold with these words, and ready to die for the law and the country, he divided his army into four parts;
cards.t_text: And shall say unto them, Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel), you approach this day unto battle against your enemies: let not your hearts faint, fear not, and do not tremble, neither be you terrified because of them;

cards.note: Isaiah 31:1 — *Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!* The heathen "trust in their weapons," exactly the misplaced confidence Isaiah condemns, while the faithful look to the Holy One alone.
cards.s_text: For they, said he, trust in their weapons and boldness; but our confidence is in the Almighty who at a beck can cast down both them that come against us, and also all the world.
cards.t_text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong; but they look not unto the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), neither seek Yahuah (LORD)!

cards.note: Exodus 15:1 — *Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.* The psalms and thanksgiving with which the people praise Yahuah for the victory in 2 Maccabees 10:38 reprise the song Moses sang when the LORD overthrew horse and rider.
cards.s_text: When this was done, they praised Yahuah (God) with psalms and thanksgiving, who had done so great things for Yashar'el (Israel), and given them the victory.
cards.t_text: Then sang Moses and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) this song unto Yahuah (LORD), and spake, saying, I will sing unto Yahuah (LORD), for he has triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider has he thrown into the sea.

cards.note: Numbers 25:13 — *And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* The everlasting covenant given for Phinehas' zeal is the inheritance the zealous Maccabean house claims as it burns out the blasphemers in 2 Maccabees 10:36.
cards.s_text: Others likewise ascending after them, whiles they were busied with them that were within, burnt the towers, and kindling fires burnt the blasphemers alive; and others broke open the gates, and, having received in the rest of the army, took the city,
cards.t_text: And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God), and made an atonement for the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.* (2 Maccabees 10:35). *Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.* (Numbers 25:11). The men inside the city trusted their walls and blasphemed from them, and on the fifth day twenty of Judas's young men, inflamed by the blasphemies, went up the wall. The book names the cause of their anger: not the siege, not the plunder, but the blasphemies. That is the zeal of Phinehas. Yahuah (God) said Phinehas turned his wrath away from Yashar'el (Israel) because he was zealous for his sake, and for that zeal gave him a covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12–13). Zeal for the name of Yahuah (God) when his name is mocked is the thread that runs from Phinehas's javelin to Judas's twenty.
cards.s_text: Nevertheless upon the fifth day early twenty young men of Maccabeus’ company, inflamed with anger because of the blasphemies, assaulted the wall manly, and with a fierce courage killed all that they met withal.
cards.t_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:59 — *Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.* The brother book records the same eight-day statute on the twenty-fifth of Casleu that 2 Maccabees 10:8 decrees for the whole nation.
cards.s_text: They ordained also by a common statute and decree, That every year those days should be kept of the whole nation of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Moreover Judas and his brothers with the whole congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) ordained, that the days of the dedication of the altar should be kept in their season from year to year by the space of eight days, from the five and twentieth day of the month Casleu, with mirth and gladness.

cards.note: Joshua 7:12 — *Therefore the children of Yashar'el could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except ye destroy the accursed from among you.* This is why the slain fell — like Achan's Israel, they *could not stand* while the accursed thing was carried among them.
cards.s_text: Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Yahudim (Jews) by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
cards.t_text: Therefore the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stand before their enemies, but turned their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed: neither will I be with you any more, except you destroy the accursed from among you.

cards.note: Joshua 7:11 — *Yashar'el hath sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.* The idol-tokens hidden *under the coats* are Achan's accursed thing hidden among the stuff — the same covenant breach by the same concealment.
cards.s_text: Now under the coats of every one that was slain they found things consecrated to the idols of the Jamnites, which is forbidden the Yahudim (Jews) by the law. Then every man saw that this was the cause wherefore they were slain.
cards.t_text: Yashar'el (Israel) has sinned, and they have also transgressed my covenant which I commanded them: for they have even taken of the accursed thing, and have also stolen, and dissembled also, and they have put it even among their own stuff.

cards.note: 1 Maccabees 4:30 — *And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;* The sister-book shows the same Maccabean rule — prayer before the mighty army — that frames the fasting of 2 Maccabees 13:12.
cards.s_text: So when they had all done this together, and besought the merciful Yahuah (God) with weeping and fasting, and lying flat upon the ground three days long, Judas, having exhorted them, commanded they should be in a readiness.
cards.t_text: And when he saw that mighty army, he prayed and said, Blessed art you, O Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel), who did quell the violence of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and gavest the host of strangers into the hands of Jonathan the son of Saul, and his armourbearer;

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:22 — *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).* Nicanor's hand raised against the temple at 2 Maccabees 14:33 is Sennacherib's exalted voice all over again — the reproach falls not on Israel but on the Holy One who defends His house.
cards.s_text: He stretched out his right hand toward the temple, and made an oath in this manner: If you will not deliver me Judas as a prisoner, I will lay this temple of Yahuah (God) even with the ground, and I will break down the altar, and erect a notable temple to Bacchus.
cards.t_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Deuteronomy 20:1 — *When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for Yahuah (LORD) thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.* The Torah Judas reads to his men is the same word of war that bids Yashar'el not to fear the multitude in 2 Maccabees 15:9.
cards.s_text: And so comforting them out of the law and the prophets, and withal putting them in mind of the battles that they won afore, he made them more cheerful.
cards.t_text: When you go out to battle against your enemies, and see horses, and chariots, and a people more than you, be not afraid of them: for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) is with you, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: Exodus 31:16 — *Wherefore the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.* The seventh-day rest the Yahudim confess before Nicanor is the perpetual sign of the covenant given at Sinai, not a yoke to be set aside under threat.
cards.s_text: And when they said, There is in heaven a living Yahuah (God), and mighty, who commanded the seventh day to be kept:
cards.t_text: Wherefore the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.

cards.note: Exodus 12:15 — *Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel).* The seven days of sweet bread in 1 Esdras 1:19 keep the Torah's own count for the feast of unleavened bread.
cards.s_text: So the children of Yashar'el (Israel) which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.
cards.t_text: Seven days shall you eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 35:18 — *And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.* The Samuel-measure of 1 Esdras 1:20 is the Chronicler's own superlative for Josiah's feast.
cards.s_text: And such a passover was not kept in Yashar'el (Israel) since the time of the prophet Samuel.
cards.t_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 35:17 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present kept the passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.* The seven-day keeping in 1 Esdras 1:19 is the Chronicler's same record of Israel present at the feast.
cards.s_text: So the children of Yashar'el (Israel) which were present held the passover at that time, and the feast of sweet bread seven days.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present kept the passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days.

cards.note: 2 Chronicles 35:3 — *And said unto the Levites that taught all Yashar'el (Israel), which were holy unto Yahuah (LORD), Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Yashar'el (Israel) did build; it shall not be a burden upon your shoulders: serve now Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and his people Yashar'el (Israel),* The Chronicler's charge to house the ark is the very speech 1 Esdras 1:3 retells.
cards.s_text: And he spoke to the Levites, the holy ministers of Yashar'el (Israel), that they should hallow themselves to Yahuah (God), to set the holy ark of Yahuah (God) in the house that king Solomon the son of David had built:
cards.t_text: And said unto the Levites that taught all Yashar'el (Israel), which were holy unto Yahuah (LORD), Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Yashar'el (Israel) did build; it shall not be a burden upon your shoulders: serve now Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), and his people Yashar'el (Israel),

cards.note: Exodus 12:6 — *And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall kill it in the evening.* The Torah ordinance fixes the fourteenth day that Josiah keeps in 1 Esdras 1:1.
cards.s_text: And Josias held the feast of the passover in Jerusalem to his Elohim (God), and offered the passover the fourteenth day of the first month;
cards.t_text: And you shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall kill it in the evening.

cards.note: Ezra 1:3 — *Who is there among you of all his people? his Elohim (God) be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah), and build the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), (he is the Elohim (God),) which is in Jerusalem.* The summons to go up and build, matching 1 Esdras 2:5 phrase for phrase down to Elohim being with him.
cards.s_text: If therefore there be any of you that are of his people, let Yahuah (God), even his Elohim (God), be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem that is in Judea, and build the house of Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel): for he is Yahuah (God) that dwells in Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: Who is there among you of all his people? his Elohim (God) be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah), and build the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), (he is the Elohim (God),) which is in Jerusalem.

cards.note: Ezra 4:3 — *But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), said unto them, Ye have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our Elohim (God); but we ourselves together will build unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), as king Cyrus the king of Persia hath commanded us.* the canon's word-for-word twin of 1 Esdras 5:71, the remnant refusing a mingled temple.
cards.s_text: We ourselves alone will build to Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), according as Cyrus the king of the Persians has commanded us.
cards.t_text: But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), said unto them, You have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our Elohim (God); but we ourselves together will build unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), as king Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.

cards.note: Ezra 3:11 — *And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Yashar'el (Israel). And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised Yahuah (LORD), because the foundation of the house of Yahuah (LORD) was laid.* the same thanksgiving and great shout at the foundation that 1 Esdras 5:62 records for the rearing of the house.
cards.s_text: And all the people sounded trumpets, and shouted with a loud voice, singing songs of thanksgiving to Yahuah (God) for the rearing up of the house of Yahuah (God).

cards.note: Leviticus 23:34 — *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD).* the very statute of Sukkot the returnees keep in 1 Esdras 5:51, the moed written in Moses' book.

cards.s_text: And so dwelt the priests and the Levites and the people in Jerusalem, and in the country, the singers also and the porters; and all Yashar'el (Israel) in their villages.

And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.* The finishing that Darius commands in 1 Esdras 6:28 comes, the canon says, through the prophesying of Haggai and Zechariah by the commandment of Elohim and the kings.

cards.note: Ezra 5:11 — *And thus they returned us answer, saying, We are the servants of the Elohim (God) of heaven and earth, and build the house that was builded these many years ago, which a great king of Yashar'el (Israel) builded and set up.* The same verse that adds the house was builded long ago by a great king of Yashar'el, as 1 Esdras 6:14 says it was builded many years ago by a king of Yashar'el great and strong.
