cards.note: Ezra 5:1 — *Then the prophets, Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied unto the Yahudim (Jews) that were in Yahudah (Judah) and Jerusalem in the name of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), even unto them.* The canon names the very prophets 1 Esdras 6:1 calls Aggeus and Zacharias the son of Addo, prophesying in that same second year of Darius.
cards.s_text: Now in the second year of the reign of Darius Aggeus and Zacharias the son of Addo, the prophets, prophesied to the Yahudim (Jews) in Jewry and Jerusalem in the name of Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which was upon them.

cards.s_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that came out of the captivity did eat, even all they that had separated themselves from the abominations of the people of the land, and sought Yahuah (God).

cards.t_text: And kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.s_text: And to the dedication of the temple of Yahuah (God) they offered an hundred bullocks two hundred rams, four hundred lambs;

And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.* The same Haggai and Zechariah prophesying, the same kings named, the same commandment of Elohim that 1 Esdras 7:3-4 records word for word.
cards.s_text: And so the holy works prospered, when Aggeus and Zacharias the prophets prophesied.

And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.

cards.note: Ezra 10:1 — *Now when Ezra had prayed, and when he had confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of Elohim (God), there assembled unto him out of Yashar'el (Israel) a very great congregation of men and women and children: for the people wept very sore.* The canon's weeping congregation gathered before the house is the same multitude 1 Esdras 8:91 describes.
cards.s_text: And as Esdras in his prayer made his confession, weeping, and lying flat upon the ground before the temple, there gathered to him from Jerusalem a very great multitude of men and women and children: for there was great weeping among the multitude.
cards.t_text: Now when Ezra had prayed, and when he had confessed, weeping and casting himself down before the house of Elohim (God), there assembled unto him out of Yashar'el (Israel) a very great congregation of men and women and children: for the people wept very sore.

cards.note: *O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), you are true: for we are left a root this day.* (1 Esdras 8:89). *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), thou art righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before thee in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before thee because of this.* (Ezra 9:15). These are the same prayer told twice, once by Ezra and once by Esdras. In both, the man kneels with torn garments and confesses that Yahuah (God) is righteous and the people are not, that they are a root left this day, a remnant yet escaped, and that they cannot stand before him because of what they have done. The confession does not plead the people's merit; it pleads his faithfulness, you are true. A root left and a remnant escaped is how Yahuah (God) keeps his word to the fathers when the sons have broken theirs.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), you are true: for we are left a root this day.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), you are righteous: for we remain yet escaped, as it is this day: behold, we are before you in our trespasses: for we cannot stand before you because of this.

cards.note: *For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.* (1 Esdras 8:70). *But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.* (Isaiah 6:13). Both verses call the people the holy seed, and both mean a bloodline. Esdras rends his garment because the seed of Yashar'el (Israel) has been mixed with the strange people of the land, and the rulers led the way in it. Isaiah had already said what would become of that seed: the tree is cut down to a stump, a tenth returns, and the holy seed is what remains alive in the stump when everything else is eaten away. The grief in Esdras and the promise in Isaiah are about the same seed, and the promise is that Yahuah (God) keeps it through the cutting.
cards.s_text: For both they and their sons have married with their daughters, and the holy seed is mixed with the strange people of the land; and from the beginning of this matter the rulers and the great men have been partakers of this iniquity.
cards.t_text: But yet in it shall be a tenth, and it shall return, and shall be eaten: as a teil tree, and as an oak, whose substance is in them, when they cast their leaves: so the holy seed shall be the substance thereof.

cards.note: Ezra 9:1 — *Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Yashar'el (Israel), and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.* The canon's report of the unseparated people is the same news brought to Ezra in 1 Esdras 8:69.
cards.s_text: The nation of Yashar'el (Israel), the princes, the priests and Levites, have not put away from them the strange people of the land, nor the pollutions of the Gentiles to wit, of the Canaanites, Hittites, Pheresites, Jebusites, and the Moabites, Egyptians, and Edomites.
cards.t_text: Now when these things were done, the princes came to me, saying, The people of Yashar'el (Israel), and the priests, and the Levites, have not separated themselves from the people of the lands, doing according to their abominations, even of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites, the Ammonites, the Moabites, the Egyptians, and the Amorites.

cards.note: Ezra 7:28 — *And hath extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellors, and before all the king's mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God) was upon me, and I gathered together out of Yashar'el (Israel) chief men to go up with me.* The mercy shown before king and counsellors in Ezra 7:28 is the very favour 1 Esdras 8:26 records.
cards.s_text: And has honoured me in the sight of the king, and his counsellors, and all his friends and nobles.
cards.t_text: And has extended mercy unto me before the king, and his counsellors, and before all the king’s mighty princes. And I was strengthened as the hand of Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God) was upon me, and I gathered together out of Yashar'el (Israel) chief men to go up with me.

cards.note: Ezra 7:15 — *And to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counsellors have freely offered unto the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), whose habitation is in Jerusalem.* The freely-offered silver and gold borne to Jerusalem in Ezra 7:15 is the vowed gold and silver of 1 Esdras 8:13.
cards.s_text: And carry the gifts to Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) to Jerusalem, which I and my friends have vowed, and all the gold and silver that in the country of Babylon can be found, to Yahuah (God) in Jerusalem,
cards.t_text: And to carry the silver and gold, which the king and his counsellors have freely offered unto the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), whose habitation is in Jerusalem,

cards.note: Ezra 7:13 — *I make a decree, that all they of the people of Yashar'el (Israel), and of his priests and Levites, in my realm, which are minded of their own freewill to go up to Jerusalem, go with thee.* The canon's freewill decree to go up to Jerusalem is the same commission 1 Esdras 8:10 records.
cards.s_text: Having determined to deal graciously, I have given order, that such of the nation of the Yahudim (Jews), and of the priests and Levites being within our realm, as are willing and desirous should go with you to Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: I make a decree, that all they of the people of Yashar'el (Israel), and of his priests and Levites, in my realm, which are minded of their own freewill to go up to Jerusalem, go with you.

cards.note: Ezra 7:10 — *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.* The seek-do-teach heart of Ezra 7:10 is exactly the man who omitted nothing of the law in 1 Esdras 8:7.
cards.s_text: For Esdras had very great skill, so that he omitted nothing of the law and commandments of Yahuah (God), but taught all Yashar'el (Israel) the ordinances and judgments.
cards.t_text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.

cards.note: Ezra 7:6 — *This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) upon him.* The canon names the same ready scribe going up from Babylon with the law of Moses that 1 Esdras 8:3 retells.
cards.s_text: This Esdras went up from Babylon, as a scribe, being very ready in the law of Moses, that was given by Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: This Ezra went up from Babylon; and he was a ready scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) had given: and the king granted him all his request, according to the hand of Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) upon him.

cards.note: Nehemiah 8:1 — *And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel).* The whole multitude gathering with one accord and calling for the Law in 1 Esdras 9:38-39 is the same assembly at the water gate.
cards.s_text: And the whole multitude came together with one accord into the broad place of the holy porch toward the east:
cards.t_text: And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Ezra 9:4 — *Then were assembled unto me every one that trembled at the words of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), because of the transgression of those that had been carried away; and I sat astonied until the evening sacrifice.* Esdras' mourning over the great iniquities in 1 Esdras 9:2 gathers, as Ezra's did, all who tremble at the word of Elohim.
cards.s_text: And remained there, and did eat no meat nor drink water, mourning for the great iniquities of the multitude.
cards.t_text: Then were assembled unto me every one that trembled at the words of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), because of the transgression of those that had been carried away; and I sat astonied until the evening sacrifice.

cards.note: Hosea 1:10 — *Yet the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God).* The believing people of 2 Esdras 1:35 are the not-my-people made sons — Yashar'el restored, the two houses regathered, not replaced.
cards.s_text: Your houses will I give to a people that shall come; which not having heard of me yet shall believe me; to whom I have shewed no signs, yet they shall do that I have commanded them.
cards.t_text: Yet the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, You are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, You are the sons of the living Elohim (God).

cards.note: Romans 11:1 — *I say then, Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.* The turning to other nations in 2 Esdras 1:24 is no casting-away of Yashar'el — Elohim forbid; the seed of Abraham stands.
cards.s_text: What shall I do to you, O Jacob? you, Juda, wouldest not obey me: I will turn me to other nations, and to those will I give my name, that they may keep my statutes.
cards.t_text: I say then, Has Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:12 — *Moreover thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar; and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way wherein they should go.* The pillar of fire of 2 Esdras 1:14 is the very mercy the Levites confess Yashar'el forgot.
cards.s_text: I gave you light in a pillar of fire, and great wonders have I done among you; yet have you forgotten me, says Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Moreover you leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar; and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way wherein they should go.

cards.note: Romans 11:2 — *Elohim (God) hath not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to Elohim (God) against Yashar'el (Israel), saying,* The 'Fear not... for I have chosen you' of 2 Esdras 2:17 is Paul's own guard against supersession: election stands, the people are not cast away.
cards.s_text: Fear not, you mother of the children: for I have chosen you, says Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: Elohim (God) has not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot you not what the scripture says of Elias? how he makes intercession to Elohim (God) against Yashar'el (Israel), saying,

cards.note: Isaiah 54:5 — *For thy Maker is thine husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel); The Elohim (God) of the whole earth shall he be called.* The 'I have chosen you' that lifts the widow in 2 Esdras 2:15 names Yahuah himself as the husband of the once-forsaken mother.
cards.s_text: Mother, embrace your children, and bring them up with gladness, make their feet as fast as a pillar: for I have chosen you, says Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: For your Maker is your husband; Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name; and your Redeemer the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel); The Elohim (God) of the whole earth shall he be called.

cards.note: Romans 11:29 — *For the gifts and calling of Elohim (God) are without repentance.* The Maker who loves Yashar'el better than Esdras ever could has a calling that cannot be revoked (2 Esdras 5:33).
cards.s_text: And I said, Speak on, my Elohim (God). Then said he to me, You are sore troubled in mind for Yashar'el (Israel)’s sake: lovest you that people better than he that made them?
cards.t_text: For the gifts and calling of Elohim (God) are without repentance.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:21 — *Remember these, O Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel); for thou art my servant: I have formed thee; thou art my servant: O Yashar'el (Israel), thou shalt not be forgotten of me.* The firstborn people given into hands yet not forgotten (2 Esdras 6:58) is the servant Yashar'el the prophet vows never to forget — Israel is not cast away.
cards.s_text: But we your people, whom you have called your firstborn, your only begotten, and your fervent lover, are given into their hands.
cards.t_text: Remember these, O Jacob and Yashar'el (Israel); for you are my servant: I have formed you; you are my servant: O Yashar'el (Israel), you shall not be forgotten of me.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:5 — *One shall say, I am the LORD'S; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto Yahuah (LORD), and surname himself by the name of Yashar'el (Israel).* The name of Jacob taken up by the hand answers the heel-grasping hand of Jacob in 2 Esdras 6:8.
cards.s_text: And he said to me, From Abraham to Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau.
cards.t_text: One shall say, I am the LORD’S; and another shall call himself by the name of Jacob; and another shall subscribe with his hand unto Yahuah (LORD), and surname himself by the name of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Hebrews 8:10 — *For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) after those days, saith Yahuah (Lord); I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a Elohim (God), and they shall be to me a people:* That the law *perishes not, but remains in his force* in 2 Esdras 9:37 is confirmed where the covenant writes the same law on mind and heart.
cards.s_text: Notwithstanding the law perishes not, but remains in his force.
cards.t_text: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel) after those days, says Yahuah (Lord); I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a Elohim (God), and they shall be to me a people:

cards.note: Jeremiah 31:33 — *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* The law *sown in you* that brings fruit forever in 2 Esdras 9:31 is the same law written upon the inward parts in the new covenant.
cards.s_text: For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and you shall be honoured in it for ever.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: Isaiah 5:7 — *For the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the men of Yahudah (Judah) his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.* The *plant of a great people* kept in 2 Esdras 9:21 is Isaiah's pleasant plant, the two houses of Yashar'el and Yahudah.
cards.s_text: And I saw, and spared it greatly, and have kept me a grape of the cluster, and a plant of a great people.
cards.t_text: For the vineyard of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the men of Yahudah (Judah) his pleasant plant: and he looked for judgment, but behold oppression; for righteousness, but behold a cry.

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:* The rest of the people the Anointed makes joyful in 2 Esdras 12:34 are the two sticks joined into one nation under one King.
cards.s_text: For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.
cards.t_text: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:

cards.note: Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* The mercy shown to the rest of the people in 2 Esdras 12:34 gathers both houses — outcast Israel and dispersed Judah — from the four corners.
cards.s_text: For the rest of my people shall he deliver with mercy, those that have been pressed upon my borders, and he shall make them joyful until the coming of the day of judgment, of which I have spoken to you from the beginning.
cards.t_text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.

cards.note: Hosea 1:10 — *Yet the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living Elohim (God).* Those found within his borders, defended in that day, are the once-disowned reclaimed as sons of the living Elohim.
cards.s_text: But those that be left behind of your people are they that are found within my borders.
cards.t_text: Yet the number of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, You are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, You are the sons of the living Elohim (God).

cards.note: Hosea 1:11 — *Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.* The peaceable multitude gathered to the Son is Judah and Israel gathered together under one head.
cards.s_text: And whereas you sawest that he gathered another peaceable multitude to him;
cards.t_text: Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

cards.note: Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.* The ten tribes led captive by Assyria are the divided kingdom Ezekiel sees made one nation under one king.
cards.s_text: Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.
cards.t_text: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:

cards.note: Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* The peaceable multitude returning with peace is the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah assembled from the four corners.
cards.s_text: The Highest shall stay the springs of the stream again, that they may go through: therefore sawest you the multitude with peace.
cards.t_text: And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.

cards.note: Exodus 3:10 — *Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Yashar'el (Israel) out of Egypt.* The sending and leading of the people out of Egypt that Esdras recalls is the commission given at the bush.
cards.s_text: And I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up to the mount of where I held him by me a long season,
cards.t_text: Come now therefore, and I will send you unto Pharaoh, that you may bring forth my people the children of Yashar'el (Israel) out of Egypt.

cards.note: Jeremiah 25:15 — *For thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.* The woe and plagues poured on the commandment-breakers in Ezra are this cup of fury Yahuah causes all the nations to drink.
cards.s_text: Woe to them that sin, and keep not my commandments! says Yahuah (God).
cards.t_text: For thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) unto me; Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send you, to drink it.

cards.note: Jasher 1:2 — *And Elohim formed man from the ground, and he blew into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul endowed with speech.* The very speech by which Adam named and ruled the beasts in 1 Adam and Eve 7:4 is the breath of life Jasher records at his forming.
cards.s_text: Your grace was then on me; and I named every one according to Your mind; and you made them all subject to me.
cards.t_text: And Elohim formed man from the ground, and he blew into his nostrils the breath of life, and man became a living soul endowed with speech.

cards.note: Ezekiel 33:11 — *Say unto them, As I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)?* Adam confesses the very mercy Yahuah will later swear by — that He does not want anyone to perish (25:5).
cards.s_text: And thereby it will be made known that You are a merciful Elohim (God), who does not want anyone to perish; who loves not that one should fall; and who does not condemn any one cruelly, badly, and by whole destruction."
cards.t_text: Say unto them, As I live, says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn you, turn you from your evil ways; for why will you die, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)?

cards.note: Deuteronomy 6:4 — *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD).* Adam's question whether there is *another god besides You* in 1 Adam and Eve 27:10 is the Shema confessed at the cave generations before it was spoken to Israel.
cards.s_text: "O Yahuah (Lord), is there in the world another god besides You, who created angels and filled them with light, and sent them to keep us, who would come with them?
cards.t_text: Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD):

cards.note: Exodus 14:19 — *And the angel of Elohim (God), which went before the camp of Yashar'el (Israel), removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them:* the same angel of Elohim posts himself as a guard, as around the cave in 1 Adam and Eve 43:16.
cards.s_text: But by the mercy of Elohim (God) he could not burn the cave, for Elohim (God) sent His angel around the cave to guard it from such a fire, until it went out.
cards.t_text: And the angel of Elohim (God), which went before the camp of Yashar'el (Israel), removed and went behind them; and the pillar of the cloud went from before their face, and stood behind them:

cards.note: Exodus 14:22 — *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.* As Israel walked through the parted sea on dry ground, Adam goes through the parted fire by the order of the Word.
cards.s_text: There is no way for you at present to come from this life to rest, not until My Word comes, who is My Word. Then He will make a way for you, and you shall have rest." Then Elohim (God) called with His Word to the fire that burned around the cave, that it split itself in half, until Adam had gone through it. Then the fire parted itself by Elohim's (God's) order, and a way was made for Adam*.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground: and the waters were a wall unto them on their right hand, and on their left.

cards.note: Jubilees 48:15 — *And on the fourteenth day and on the fifteenth and on the sixteenth and on the seventeenth and on the eighteenth the prince of the Mastêmâ was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that he might not accuse them.* The shamed and thwarted Satan of 1 Adam & Eve 62:6 is the prince of Mastema bound behind the covenant children at the Exodus.
cards.s_text: Then Satan went away ashamed because he hadn't thought his plans all the way through.
cards.t_text: And on the fourteenth day and on the fifteenth and on the sixteenth and on the seventeenth and on the eighteenth the prince of the Mastêmâ was bound and imprisoned behind the children of Yashar’el (Israel) that he might not accuse them.

cards.note: Psalm 78:25 — *Man did eat angels’ food: he sent them meat to the full.* The figs into which Elohim put *a mixture as of savory bread and blood* (64:7) are angels' food given to the full, as the manna was to Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: Then Adam and Eve took the figs and began to eat of them. But Elohim (God) had put into them a mixture as of savory bread and blood.
cards.t_text: Man did eat angels’ food: he sent them meat to the full.

cards.note: Exodus 16:31 — *And the house of Yashar'el (Israel) called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.* The manna on the tree in 1-adam-eve 68:8 bears the same heaven-given name later called Manna by the house of Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: There they saw a tree, and found on it solid manna; and wondered at Elohim's (God's) power. And the angels commanded them to eat of the manna when they were hungry.
cards.t_text: And the house of Yashar'el (Israel) called the name thereof Manna: and it was like coriander seed, white; and the taste of it was like wafers made with honey.

cards.note: Exodus 16:4 — *Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.* The solid manna Adam and Eve find in 1-adam-eve 68:8 prefigures the bread from heaven Yahuah rains on Yashar'el in the wilderness.
cards.s_text: There they saw a tree, and found on it solid manna; and wondered at Elohim's (God's) power. And the angels commanded them to eat of the manna when they were hungry.
cards.t_text: Then said Yahuah (LORD) unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven for you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day, that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.

cards.note: Jasher 1:16 — *And to Cain and his offering Yahuah (the Lord) did not turn, and he did not incline to it, for he had brought from the inferior fruit of the ground before Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain was jealous against his brother Abel on account of this, and he sought a pretext to slay him.* Jasher names the jealousy and sought pretext that 1 Adam and Eve 76:12 says Satan kept alive in Cain's heart.
cards.s_text: And Satan departed from him. But the devil remained behind in Cain's heart, and frequently aspired to kill his brother.
cards.t_text: And to Cain and his offering Yahuah (the Lord) did not turn, and he did not incline to it, for he had brought from the inferior fruit of the ground before Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain was jealous against his brother Abel on account of this, and he sought a pretext to slay him.

cards.note: Jasher 1:17 — *And in some time after, Cain and Abel his brother, went one day into the field to do their work; and they were both in the field, Cain tilling and ploughing his ground, and Abel feeding his flock; and the flock passed that part which Cain had ploughed in the ground, and it sorely grieved Cain on this account.* The brothers going together into the field in 78:36 matches Jasher's account of the fatal day in the field.
cards.s_text: Then Abel consented to go with his brother Cain into the field.
cards.t_text: And in some time after, Cain and Abel his brother, went one day into the field to do their work; and they were both in the field, Cain tilling and ploughing his ground, and Abel feeding his flock; and the flock passed that part which Cain had ploughed in the ground, and it sorely grieved Cain on this account.

cards.note: Jasher 1:16 — *And to Cain and his offering Yahuah (the Lord) did not turn, and he did not incline to it, for he had brought from the inferior fruit of the ground before Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain was jealous against his brother Abel on account of this, and he sought a pretext to slay him.* Cain laying wait to kill his brother in 78:33 is the very pretext-seeking jealousy Jasher records.
cards.s_text: When Cain heard these words of Satan, he was filled with rage; and he let no one know. But he was laying wait to kill his brother, until he brought him into the cave, and then said to him:--
cards.t_text: And to Cain and his offering Yahuah (the Lord) did not turn, and he did not incline to it, for he had brought from the inferior fruit of the ground before Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain was jealous against his brother Abel on account of this, and he sought a pretext to slay him.

cards.note: Jasher 1:15 — *And it was at the expiration of a few years, that they brought an approximating offering to Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain brought from the fruit of the ground, and Abel brought from the firstlings of his flock from the fat of it, and Elohim turned and inclined to Abel and his offering, and a fire came down from Yahuah (the Lord) from heaven and consumed it.* Jasher names the same heavenly fire that descends and consumes Abel's offering in 78:22.
cards.s_text: And Abel prayed to Elohim (God) to accept his offering. Then a divine fire came down and consumed his offering. And Elohim (God) smelled the sweet savor of his offering; because Abel loved Him and rejoice in Him.
cards.t_text: And it was at the expiration of a few years, that they brought an approximating offering to Yahuah (the Lord), and Cain brought from the fruit of the ground, and Abel brought from the firstlings of his flock from the fat of it, and Elohim turned and inclined to Abel and his offering, and a fire came down from Yahuah (the Lord) from heaven and consumed it.

cards.note: Jasher 1:22 — *And Abel answered Cain, saying, Surely Elohim who has made us in the earth, he will avenge my cause, and he will require my blood from you should you slay me, for Yahuah (the Lord) is the judge and arbiter...* Jasher gives righteous Abel's own confession of the avenging Judge, the same righteousness for which the ground would not receive him in 1 Adam & Eve 79:14.
cards.s_text: The muddy ground threw him up the first time, because he was not the first creation; and it threw him up the second time and would not receive him, because he was righteous and good, and was killed without a cause; and the ground threw him up the third time and would not receive him, that there might remain before his brother a witness against him.
cards.t_text: And Abel answered Cain, saying, Surely Elohim who has made us in the earth, he will avenge my cause, and he will require my blood from you should you slay me, for Yahuah (the Lord) is the judge and arbiter, and it is he who will requite man according to his evil, and the wicked man according to the wickedness that he may do upon earth.

cards.note: Jasher 1:25 — *And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth...* Jasher keeps the weapon and the spilt blood that 1 Adam & Eve 79:7 shows oozing before Cain.
cards.s_text: Then Cain, the hard-hearted, and cruel murderer, took a large stone, and beat his brother's head with it, until his brains oozed out, and he wallowed in his blood, before him.
cards.t_text: And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth, and the blood of Abel streamed upon the earth before the flock.

cards.note: Jasher 1:25 — *And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth, and the blood of Abel streamed upon the earth before the flock.* Jasher streams the same blood upon the earth that the family finds in 2 Adam and Eve 1:3.
cards.s_text: And they found him lying on the earth, killed, and beasts around him; while they wept and cried because of this just one. From his body, by reason of its purity, went forth a smell of sweet spices.
cards.t_text: And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth, and the blood of Abel streamed upon the earth before the flock.

cards.note: Jasher 2:16 — *And these are the names of the children of Cainan; the name of the first born Mahlallel, the second Enan, and the third Mered, and their sisters were Adah and Zillah; these are the five children of Cainan that were born to him.* Jasher names Mahalaleel as Cainan's firstborn, confirming the begetting 2 Adam and Eve 7:8 records.
cards.s_text: Cainan also grew up, married, and begat Mahalaleel.
cards.t_text: And these are the names of the children of Cainan; the name of the first born Mahlallel, the second Enan, and the third Mered, and their sisters were Adah and Zillah; these are the five children of Cainan that were born to him.

cards.note: Jasher 2:1 — *And it was in the hundred and thirtieth year of the life of Adam upon the earth, that he again knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bare a son in his likeness and in his image, and she called his name Seth, saying, Because Elohim (God) has appointed me another seed in the place of Abel, for Cain has slain him.* Jasher tells the same appointing that 2 Adam & Eve 10:4 commands Seth to guard — the seed set in Abel's place, kept apart from Cain.
cards.s_text: "But as to thy father Adam, keep thou the commandment he gave thee; and sever thy seed from that of Cain thy brother."
cards.t_text: And it was in the hundred and thirtieth year of the life of Adam upon the earth, that he again knew Eve his wife, and she conceived and bare a son in his likeness and in his image, and she called his name Seth, saying, Because Elohim (God) has appointed me another seed in the place of Abel, for Cain has slain him.

cards.note: Jasher 2:27 — *And Tubal Cain told his father to draw his bow, and with the arrows he smote Cain, who was yet far off, and he slew him, for he appeared to them to be an animal.* Jasher shows the violence still running in Cain's valley-line below, the fellowship 2 Adam and Eve 15:2 forbids the children on the mountain.
cards.s_text: Then when he had lived nine hundred and ten years, suffering and affliction came upon him. And when he was about to enter into rest, all the fathers with their wives and children came to him, and he blessed them, and adjured them by the blood of Abel, the just, saying to them, "Let not one among you go down from this Holy Mountain; and make no fellowship with the children of Cain the murderer."
cards.t_text: And Tubal Cain told his father to draw his bow, and with the arrows he smote Cain, who was yet far off, and he slew him, for he appeared to them to be an animal.

cards.note: Genesis 50:2 — *And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Yashar'el (Israel).* Mahalaleel's charge to be embalmed in 16:9 keeps the same patriarchal burial Joseph renders to Jacob.
cards.s_text: Mahalaleel said, moreover, to his son Jared, "When I die, embalm my body and lay it in the Cave of Treasures, by the bodies of my fathers; then stand thou by my body and pray to Elohim (God); and take care of them, and fulfil thy ministry before them, until thou enterest into rest thyself."
cards.t_text: And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father: and the physicians embalmed Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *In whom ye also trusted, after that ye heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that ye believed, ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,* (Ephesians 1:13). Paul names the same sealing to the Ephesians: *ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise.* To Corinth he writes that Elohim (God) *hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts* (2 Corinthians 1:22). The seal of the Spirit marks the gathered as the Father's own; it is the *holy Spirit of promise,* the down-payment of the inheritance, the same earnest given to believing Yashar'el (Israel) and the grafted-in.
cards.s_text: Who has also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
cards.t_text: In whom you also trusted, after that you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation: in whom also after that you believed, you were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise,

cards.note: *Now I say that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:* (Romans 15:8). Paul writes elsewhere that the Messiah came *to confirm the promises made unto the fathers.* It is the same word he gives to Corinth: *all the promises of Elohim (God) in him are yea, and in him Amen* (2 Corinthians 1:20). The Formed Son does not bring a new and rival set of promises; he confirms the promises made to the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), and in him they are made yea — the covenant of old established, not abolished.
cards.s_text: For all the promises of Elohim (God) in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory of Elohim (God) by us.
cards.t_text: Now I say that Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers:

cards.note: *Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for Yahuah (LORD) hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.* (Isaiah 49:13). Paul blesses *the Father of mercies, and the Elohim (God) of all comfort* (2 Corinthians 1:3) — the very God Isaiah names, who *hath comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.* The comfort poured out on the afflicted assembly at Corinth is the same covenant mercy spoken over Yashar'el (Israel); the Elohim (God) of all comfort is not a new God but the One who from of old comforts his people in their affliction.
cards.s_text: Blessed be Elohim (God), even the Father of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the Father of mercies, and the Elohim (God) of all comfort;
cards.t_text: Sing, O heavens; and be joyful, O earth; and break forth into singing, O mountains: for Yahuah (LORD) has comforted his people, and will have mercy upon his afflicted.

cards.note: *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses' face shone: and Moses put the vail upon his face again, until he went in to speak with him.* (Exodus 34:35). Moses unveiled his face *when [he] went in before Yahuah (LORD) to speak with him* (Exodus 34:34) and veiled it again before the people. Paul makes this the figure of the whole reading: the vail remains *in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Messiah (Christ)* (2 Corinthians 3:14), and *when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart* (3:15) — but *when it shall turn to Yahuah (Lord), the vail shall be taken away* (3:16), as Moses' own vail came off when he turned in to Yahuah (LORD).
cards.s_text: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw the face of Moses, that the skin of Moses’ face shone: and Moses put the vail upon his face again, until he went in to speak with him.

cards.note: *And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a vail on his face.* (Exodus 34:33). Moses *put a vail on his face* after speaking the words of Yahuah (LORD) to the people. Paul reads the vail: *And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished* (2 Corinthians 3:13). The vail belongs to the fading-glory ministration — what is *abolished* is that fading administration of condemnation, not the commandment of Yahuah (LORD); and the vail now lies *upon their heart* (3:15) in the reading, until it is turned to the Lord.
cards.s_text: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:
cards.t_text: And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a vail on his face.

cards.note: *And when Aaron and all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.* (Exodus 34:30). The children of Yashar'el (Israel) *were afraid to come nigh* because of the shining of Moses' face — they *could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance* (2 Corinthians 3:7). The glory was so weighty they could not look on it. Paul names this to set the contrast: under the new covenant *we all, with open face beholding... the glory of Yahuah (Lord), are changed into the same image from glory to glory* (3:18) — no longer afraid, no longer veiled, but transformed by the glory they now behold.
cards.s_text: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:
cards.t_text: And when Aaron and all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.

cards.note: *And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.* (Exodus 34:29). The glory on Moses' face was real and from Yahuah (LORD): *the skin of his face shone* because he had spoken with Yahuah (LORD). Paul grants it fully — *the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance* (2 Corinthians 3:7). The point is not that the Sinai glory was false but that it was a fading glory; the glory of the ministration of the spirit *exceed[s] in glory* (3:9).
cards.s_text: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:
cards.t_text: And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses’ hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him.

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* (Jeremiah 31:33). Paul is *made... able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life* (2 Corinthians 3:6). The *spirit that giveth life* is the very thing Jeremiah promised — the law *written in their hearts.* The *letter that killeth* is that same law graven only on stone, an external code without the inward writing — it condemns a people whose heart is unchanged; the law put *in their inward parts* gives life. The Torah is not the death; the death is the commandment on stone without the heart of flesh.
cards.s_text: Who also has made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* (Jeremiah 31:33). This is the new covenant Paul ministers. When he says the assembly is *the epistle of Messiah (Christ)... written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living Elohim (God); not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart* (2 Corinthians 3:3), he is naming exactly Jeremiah's promise: the SAME law, no longer only graven on stone but now *put in their inward parts* and *written in their hearts.* The new place of the writing is the heart, and the One who writes is the Spirit of the living Elohim (God).
cards.s_text: Forasmuch as you are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Messiah (Christ) ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living Elohim (God); not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *And when she saw that she bare no children she took her handmaid Hagar, whom Pharaoh had given her, and she gave her to Abram her husband for a wife.* (Jasher 16:24). The restored chronicle tells the same act — *Sarai Abram's wife took Hagar her maid the Egyptian... and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife* (Genesis 16:3) — and remembers that this Egyptian maid was the one *whom Pharaoh had given her*, the spoil of the Egypt-sojourn now turned into the instrument of the flesh-scheme.
cards.s_text: And Sarai Abram’s wife took Hagar her maid the Egyptian, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Canaan, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife.
cards.t_text: And when she saw that she bare no children she took her handmaid Hagar, whom Pharaoh had given her, and she gave her to Abram her husband for a wife.

cards.note: *And when Hagar saw that she had conceived she rejoiced greatly, and her mistress was despised in her eyes, and she said within herself, This can only be that I am better before Elohim than Sarai my mistress...* (Jasher 16:29). The restored chronicle opens the heart of *when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes* (Genesis 16:4): the maid, made fruitful by the scheme, exalts herself over the barren mistress. The flesh-plan does not produce peace but contempt and rivalry in the house.
cards.s_text: And he went in unto Hagar, and she conceived: and when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes.
cards.t_text: And when Hagar saw that she had conceived she rejoiced greatly, and her mistress was despised in her eyes, and she said within herself, This can only be that I am better before Elohim than Sarai my mistress, for all the days that my mistress has been with my Lord, she did not conceive, but me Yahuah (the Lord) has caused in so short a time to conceive by him.

cards.note: *And Abram said to Sarai, Behold your handmaid is in your hand, do to her as it may seem good in your eyes; and Sarai afflicted her, and Hagar fled from her to the wilderness.* (Jasher 16:33). The restored chronicle keeps the scene whole with *thy maid is in thy hand; do to her as it pleaseth thee. And when Sarai dealt hardly with her, she fled from her face* (Genesis 16:6) — the bitter fruit of the flesh-scheme, the mistress afflicting and the maid fleeing into the wilderness.
cards.s_text: But Abram said unto Sarai, Behold, your maid is in your hand; do to her as it pleaseth you. And when Sarai dealt hardly with her, she fled from her face.
cards.t_text: And Abram said to Sarai, Behold your handmaid is in your hand, do to her as it may seem good in your eyes; and Sarai afflicted her, and Hagar fled from her to the wilderness.

cards.note: *And an angel of Yahuah (the Lord) found her in the place where she had fled, by a well, and he said to her, Do not fear, for I will multiply your seed, for you shall bear a son and you shall call his name Ishmael; now then return to Sarai your mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.* (Jasher 16:34). The restored chronicle gathers the whole encounter — *the angel of Yahuah found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness* (Genesis 16:7), the multiply-seed oath, the naming of Ishmael, and *Return to thy mistress, and submit thyself under her hands* (Genesis 16:9) — the Formed Son speaking the first-person divine promise to the fleeing maid.
cards.s_text: And the angel of Yahuah (LORD) found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.
cards.t_text: And an angel of Yahuah (the Lord) found her in the place where she had fled, by a well, and he said to her, Do not fear, for I will multiply your seed, for you shall bear a son and you shall call his name Ishmael; now then return to Sarai your mistress, and submit thyself under her hands.

cards.note: *Thou shalt be perfect with Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Deuteronomy 18:13). What the Almighty commands the one man — *walk before me, and be thou perfect* (Genesis 17:1) — Mosheh (Moses) lays on the whole nation that came of his seed: *Thou shalt be perfect with Yahuah Elohayka*. The covenant-walk asked of Abraham is the covenant-walk asked of all Yashar'el; it is inheritance, never abolished.
cards.s_text: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the El Shaddai (Almighty God); walk before me, and be you perfect.
cards.t_text: You shall be perfect with Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God).

cards.note: *At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him and he said to him, I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will greatly multiply your seed* (Jasher 17:17). The restored witness keeps the covenant-word of Genesis 17:2 — *I will make my covenant between me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly* — the same establishing of the covenant and multiplying of the seed spoken when Abram was ninety-nine years old (Jasher 17:16).
cards.s_text: And I will make my covenant between me and you, and will multiply you exceedingly.
cards.t_text: At that time Yahuah (the Lord) appeared to him and he said to him, I will make my covenant between me and you, and I will greatly multiply your seed, and this is the covenant which I make between me and you, that every male child be circumcised, you and your seed after you.

cards.note: *For I will bless you both, and I will multiply your seed after you that you shall become a great nation, and kings shall come forth from you* (Jasher 17:20). The restored witness keeps the promise of Genesis 17:6 — *I will make nations of thee, and kings shall come out of thee* — the multiplied seed becoming a great nation, and kings coming forth from Abraham's loins.
cards.s_text: And I will make you exceeding fruitful, and I will make nations of you, and kings shall come out of you.
cards.t_text: For I will bless you both, and I will multiply your seed after you that you shall become a great nation, and kings shall come forth from you.

cards.note: *And I will walk among you, and will be your Elohim (God), and ye shall be my people* (Leviticus 26:12). The covenant formula given to Abraham — *and I will be their Elohim* (Genesis 17:8) — is the standing covenant bond, repeated over Yashar'el: *I will be your Elohim, and ye shall be my people*. To be their Elohim and they His people is the everlasting heart of the covenant established here.
cards.s_text: And I will give unto you, and to your seed after you, the land wherein you are a stranger, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession; and I will be their Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: And I will walk among you, and will be your Elohim (God), and you shall be my people.

cards.note: *And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised* (Leviticus 12:3). The eighth-day command given to Abraham — *he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you* (Genesis 17:12) — is written again into the standing law of Yashar'el: *in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised*. What was commanded to one household becomes the perpetual ordinance of the whole people.
cards.s_text: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of your seed.
cards.t_text: And in the eighth day the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

cards.note: *At eight days old shall it be circumcised, and this covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant* (Jasher 17:18). The restored witness carries the eighth-day command and the everlasting word of Genesis 17:12-13 — *he that is eight days old shall be circumcised... and my covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant* — the sign in the flesh sworn as everlasting.
cards.s_text: And he that is eight days old shall be circumcised among you, every man child in your generations, he that is born in the house, or bought with money of any stranger, which is not of your seed.
cards.t_text: At eight days old shall it be circumcised, and this covenant shall be in your flesh for an everlasting covenant.

cards.note: *And Abraham rose and did all that Elohim (God) had ordered him, and he took the men of his household and those bought with his money, and he circumcised them as Yahuah (the Lord) had commanded him* (Jasher 18:1). The restored witness keeps the selfsame-day obedience of Genesis 17:23 — *Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house... and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as Elohim had said unto him* — Abraham doing all that he was commanded, the whole household sealed with the sign.
cards.s_text: And Abraham took Ishmael his son, and all that were born in his house, and all that were bought with his money, every male among the men of Abraham’s house; and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the selfsame day, as Elohim (God) had said unto him.
cards.t_text: And Abraham rose and did all that Elohim (God) had ordered him, and he took the men of his household and those bought with his money, and he circumcised them as Yahuah (the Lord) had commanded him.

cards.note: *Art not thou our Elohim (God), who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Yashar'el (Israel), and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?* (2 Chronicles 20:7). Yehoshaphat pleads on the ground of *the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever* — the friendship first shown when Yahuah would not hide His purpose from him: *Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do?* (Genesis 18:17). The Friend of Elohim and his seed inherit the land by that very friendship.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;
cards.t_text: Are not you our Elohim (God), who did drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Yashar'el (Israel), and gave it to the seed of Abraham your friend for ever?

cards.note: *But thou, Yashar'el (Israel), art my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend* (Isaiah 41:8). The whole nation is named for the friendship begun here — *the seed of Abraham my friend* — the friend from whom Yahuah would not hide His doing: *Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do?* (Genesis 18:17). And the friendship is bound to a walk: Abraham *will command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of Yahuah, to do justice and judgment* (Genesis 18:19).
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said, Shall I hide from Abraham that thing which I do;
cards.t_text: But you, Yashar'el (Israel), are my servant, Jacob whom I have chosen, the seed of Abraham my friend.

cards.note: *And the angels rose up from the door of Abraham's tent, after they had eaten and drunk, and they reached Sodom in the evening, and Lot was then sitting in the gate of Sodom, and when he saw them he rose to meet them, and he bowed down to the ground* (Jasher 19:46). The restored witness keeps the scene whole — the angels reaching Sodom *in the evening*, Lot in the gate, rising and bowing — matching *there came two angels to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot seeing them rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground* (Genesis 19:1). Lot greets the stranger; the city will assault him.
cards.s_text: And there came two angels to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot seeing them rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground;
cards.t_text: And the angels rose up from the door of Abraham’s tent, after they had eaten and drunk, and they reached Sodom in the evening, and Lot was then sitting in the gate of Sodom, and when he saw them he rose to meet them, and he bowed down to the ground.

cards.note: *And he pressed them greatly and brought them into his house, and he gave them victuals which they ate, and they abode all night in his house* (Jasher 19:47). The hospitality of *he pressed upon them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat* (Genesis 19:3) is carried in the restored witness — Lot pressing the strangers in, feeding them, sheltering them through the night, the very opposite of the city's violence at the door.
cards.s_text: And he pressed upon them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.
cards.t_text: And he pressed them greatly and brought them into his house, and he gave them victuals which they ate, and they abode all night in his house.

cards.note: *Then Yahuah (the Lord) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah and upon all these cities brimstone and fire from Yahuah (the Lord) out of heaven* (Jasher 19:51). The restored witness keeps the doubling exact — *brimstone and fire from Yahuah... out of heaven* — matching *Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven* (Genesis 19:24): the One who rains, raining from Yahuah out of heaven, the Formed executing the judgment of the Formless.
cards.s_text: Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;
cards.t_text: Then Yahuah (the Lord) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah and upon all these cities brimstone and fire from Yahuah (the Lord) out of heaven.

cards.note: *And when she looked back she became a pillar of salt, and it is yet in that place to this day* (Jasher 19:53). The restored witness keeps the moment whole — the looking back, the becoming salt, the pillar standing *to this day* — matching *his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt* (Genesis 19:26). She was brought out of the overthrow, yet her heart stayed in Sodom, and there she was fixed.
cards.s_text: But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
cards.t_text: And when she looked back she became a pillar of salt, and it is yet in that place to this day.

cards.note: *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah* (Isaiah 1:9). The overthrow of *all the inhabitants of the cities* (Genesis 19:25) is the fate Yashar'el escapes only by the remnant: *except Yahuah Tseva'ot had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom*. The cities the next verse calls *ye rulers of Sodom* (Isaiah 1:10) are spared the overthrow only by grace.
cards.s_text: And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.
cards.t_text: Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

cards.note: *And that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor beareth, nor any grass groweth therein, like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, which Yahuah (LORD) overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath* (Deuteronomy 29:23). Mosheh (Moses) sets the overthrow of *that which grew upon the ground* (Genesis 19:25) — now *brimstone, and salt, and burning... nor any grass groweth therein* — as the covenant warning to Yashar'el: the land that forsakes the covenant becomes *like the overthrow of Sodom*.
cards.s_text: And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain, and all the inhabitants of the cities, and that which grew upon the ground.
cards.t_text: And that the whole land thereof is brimstone, and salt, and burning, that it is not sown, nor bears, nor any grass grows therein, like the overthrow of Sodom, and Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboim, which Yahuah (LORD) overthrew in his anger, and in his wrath:

cards.note: *And they both lay with their father, and they conceived and bare sons, and the first born called the name of her son Moab, saying, From my father did I conceive him; he is the father of the Moabites to this day* (Jasher 19:58). The restored witness carries the origin of Moab — *the first born called the name of her son Moab... the father of the Moabites to this day* — matching *the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day* (Genesis 19:37).
cards.s_text: And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
cards.t_text: And they both lay with their father, and they conceived and bare sons, and the first born called the name of her son Moab, saying, From my father did I conceive him; he is the father of the Moabites to this day.

cards.note: *And the younger also called her son Benami; he is the father of the children of Ammon to this day* (Jasher 19:59). The restored witness keeps the origin of Ammon — *the younger also called her son Benami; he is the father of the children of Ammon to this day* — matching *the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day* (Genesis 19:38).
cards.s_text: And the younger, she also bare a son, and called his name Ben-ammi: the same is the father of the children of Ammon unto this day.
cards.t_text: And the younger also called her son Benami; he is the father of the children of Ammon to this day.

cards.note: *Therefore as I live, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation* (Zephaniah 2:9). The two nations born in the cave above the overthrow — Moab and *the children of Ammon* (Genesis 19:37-38) — are sworn by the prophet to the very fate of the cities their fathers fled: *Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah*, with *saltpits* echoing the pillar of salt. What came out of Sodom's shadow returns to Sodom's judgment.
cards.s_text: And the firstborn bare a son, and called his name Moab: the same is the father of the Moabites unto this day.
cards.t_text: Therefore as I live, says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.

cards.note: Jasher 11:16 — *And Abram came to his father's house and saw twelve gods standing there in their temples, and the anger of Abram was kindled when he saw these images in his father's house.* Jasher tells the identical temple scene — Abraham finding his father's idols and burning with zeal against them.
cards.s_text: On the day when I planed the gods of my father Terah and the gods of Nahor his brother, when I was searching as to who the Mighty Elohim (God) in truth is — I, Abraham, at the time when it fell to my lot, when I fulfilled the services (the sacrifices) of my father Terah to his gods of wood and stone, gold and silver, brass and iron, having entered into their temple for service, I found the god whose name was Merumath (which was) hewn out of stone, fallen forward at the feet of the iron god Nahon.
cards.t_text: And Abram came to his father’s house and saw twelve gods standing there in their temples, and the anger of Abram was kindled when he saw these images in his father’s house.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Scripture names the very house Abraham serves in — Terah's gods of wood and stone are the "other gods" out of which Abraham is called.
cards.s_text: On the day when I planed the gods of my father Terah and the gods of Nahor his brother, when I was searching as to who the Mighty Elohim (God) in truth is — I, Abraham, at the time when it fell to my lot, when I fulfilled the services (the sacrifices) of my father Terah to his gods of wood and stone, gold and silver, brass and iron, having entered into their temple for service, I found the god whose name was Merumath (which was) hewn out of stone, fallen forward at the feet of the iron god Nahon.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Jasher 11:36 — *And Terah entered the room and found all the idols fallen down and broken, and the hatchet in the hand of the largest, which was not broken, and the savory meat which Abram his son had made was still before them.* Jasher's Abraham deliberately does what the camel's groan begins — fells and breaks Terah's gods to prove they cannot save themselves.
cards.s_text: And one of their camels uttered a groan, and the ass took fright and sprang away and upset the gods, and three of them were smashed, and two were preserved.
cards.t_text: And Terah entered the room and found all the idols fallen down and broken, and the hatchet in the hand of the largest, which was not broken, and the savory meat which Abram his son had made was still before them.

cards.note: Hosea 8:6 — *For from Yashar'el (Israel) was it also: the workman made it; therefore it is not Elohim (God): but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.* What a workman made is no Elohim and shall be broken — exactly the fate of the three gods smashed when the ass bolts.
cards.s_text: And one of their camels uttered a groan, and the ass took fright and sprang away and upset the gods, and three of them were smashed, and two were preserved.
cards.t_text: For from Yashar'el (Israel) was it also: the workman made it; therefore it is not Elohim (God): but the calf of Samaria shall be broken in pieces.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Terah, who hands the boy the gods to sell here, is named by Joshua as an idol-server — the very house Abraham is called out of.
cards.s_text: And he made five other gods, and gave them to me, and commanded me to sell them outside in the street of the town.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Joshua names Terah by name as the idol-server, the very father whose evil deed Abraham questions in his heart at 3:2.
cards.s_text: And I said in my heart: "What evil deed is this that my father is doing?
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Joshua 24:2 — *And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.* Joshua names Terah by name as an idolater — the very father whose gods Abraham rebukes (Apocalypse of Abraham 4:6).
