cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel); Yahuah Eloheinu (The Lord our God) is one Yahuah (Lord)* (Mark 12:29). When the scribe asked which is the first commandment of all, Yahusha named the Shema verbatim. *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)* (Deuteronomy 6:4) is not abolished by the Formed Son — it is the very confession he ranks above every other word.
cards.s_text: Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD):
cards.t_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel); Yahuah Eloheinu (The Lord our God) is one Yahuah (Lord):

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Yahuah (LORD), and his name one* (Zechariah 14:9). The Shema's *Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)* (Deuteronomy 6:4) reaches forward to the day the whole earth confesses what Yashar'el confesses now — one Yahuah, his Name one. The echad of the Father and the Formed Son who bears that Name is the unity all creation will own.
cards.s_text: Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD):
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Yahuah (LORD), and his name one.

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33). The command that *these words... shall be in thine heart* (Deuteronomy 6:6) is the very thing the new covenant fulfils — not Torah replaced, but Torah written inward. The covenant aim was always the heart.
cards.s_text: And these words, which I command you this day, shall be in your heart:
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God)* (Luke 4:12). Yahusha quotes Deuteronomy 6:16 to refuse the test — *Ye shall not tempt Yahuah your Elohim (God)* — succeeding where Yashar'el at Massah failed.
cards.s_text: You shall not tempt Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), as you tempted him in Massah.
cards.t_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) answering said unto him, It is said, You shall not tempt Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God).

cards.note: *And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and because they tempted Yahuah (LORD), saying, Is Yahuah (LORD) among us, or not?* (Exodus 17:7). The very name Massah is given here; Deuteronomy 6:16's warning *as ye tempted him in Massah* points back to this place where they doubted whether Yahuah was among them.
cards.s_text: You shall not tempt Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), as you tempted him in Massah.
cards.t_text: And he called the name of the place Massah, and Meribah, because of the chiding of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and because they tempted Yahuah (LORD), saying, Is Yahuah (LORD) among us, or not?

cards.note: *When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work* (Psalm 95:9). The fathers' testing at Massah, which Deuteronomy 6:16 forbids repeating — *as ye tempted him in Massah* — is held up as the warning Yashar'el must not relive.
cards.s_text: You shall not tempt Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), as you tempted him in Massah.
cards.t_text: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my work.

cards.note: *And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar'el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God)* (Jubilees 30:11). The restored witness reads Deuteronomy 7:3 as a standing law to guard the holy seed -- *abominable* because of defilement and apostasy, the same conduct-and-covenant reason, never blood-hatred.
cards.s_text: Neither shall you make marriages with them; your daughter you shall not give unto his son, nor his daughter shall you take unto your son.
cards.t_text: And do you, Moses, command the children of Yashar’el (Israel) and exhort them not to give their daughters to the nations, and not to take for their sons any of the daughters of the nations, for this is abominable before Yahuah (God).

cards.note: *And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 19:6). *Thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Deuteronomy 7:6) -- the *holy nation* of Sinai is the *holy people* of Moab, the priestly calling carried into the land.
cards.s_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has chosen you to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.
cards.t_text: And you shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which you shall speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which Yahuah (LORD) hath given you to eat* (Exodus 16:15). This is the bread *which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know* (Deuteronomy 8:3) — given to teach that life flows from the mouth of Yahuah, not from bread alone.
cards.s_text: And he humbled you, and suffered you to hunger, and fed you with manna, which you knew not, neither did your fathers know; that he might make you know that man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD) does man live.
cards.t_text: And when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) saw it, they said one to another, It is manna: for they wist not what it was. And Moses said unto them, This is the bread which Yahuah (LORD) has given you to eat.

cards.note: *And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Messiah (Christ)* (1 Corinthians 10:4). Paul names the giver of the water of *the rock of flint* (Deuteronomy 8:15): the Rock that followed Yashar'el (Israel) in the wilderness was the Formed Son, Messiah — the same One who *led thee through that great and terrible wilderness* (Deuteronomy 8:15).
cards.s_text: Who led you through that great and terrible wilderness, wherein were fiery serpents, and scorpions, and drought, where there was no water; who brought you forth water out of the rock of flint;
cards.t_text: And did all drink the same spiritual drink: for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Messiah (Christ).

cards.note: *I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for mine holy name's sake, which ye have profaned among the heathen* (Ezekiel 36:22). The prophet of the new heart echoes Moses exactly: *Speak not thou in thine heart... For my righteousness Yahuah (LORD) hath brought me in* (Deuteronomy 9:4) — Yahuah acts for His name and oath, then writes His Torah on the heart, never for the people's sake.
cards.s_text: Speak not you in your heart, after that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has cast them out from before you, saying, For my righteousness Yahuah (LORD) has brought me in to possess this land: but for the wickedness of these nations Yahuah (LORD) does drive them out from before you.
cards.t_text: Therefore say unto the house of Yashar'el (Israel), Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); I do not this for your sakes, O house of Yashar'el (Israel), but for my holy name’s sake, which you have profaned among the heathen, whither you went.

cards.note: *Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), thy servants, to whom thou swarest by thine own self... I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed* (Exodus 32:13). Deuteronomy 9:27 prays the identical plea — *Remember thy servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people* — resting the people's survival on the oath to the fathers, never on their righteousness.
cards.s_text: Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; look not unto the stubbornness of this people, nor to their wickedness, nor to their sin:
cards.t_text: Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), your servants, to whom you swore by your own self, and saidst unto them, I will multiply your seed as the stars of heaven, and all this land that I have spoken of will I give unto your seed, and they shall inherit it for ever.

cards.note: *Egypt, and Yahudah (Judah), and Edom... and all the house of Yashar'el (Israel) are uncircumcised in the heart.* (Jeremiah 9:26). Jeremiah's verdict measures the people by Deuteronomy 10:16 — *Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked* — flesh-circumcision without heart-circumcision leaves a man *uncircumcised in the heart*; the sign was never sufficient apart from the love and obedience it figured.
cards.s_text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
cards.t_text: Egypt, and Yahudah (Judah), and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab, and all that are in the utmost corners, that dwell in the wilderness: for all these nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Yashar'el (Israel) are uncircumcised in the heart.

cards.note: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Ezekiel 44:9). Ezekiel's sanctuary law holds BOTH circumcisions together — heart AND flesh — exactly as Deuteronomy 10:16 (*Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart*) joins them: the inward never voids the outward sign; both are demanded of those who would draw near.
cards.s_text: Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
cards.t_text: Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of Elohim (God);* (Ephesians 2:19). The stranger loved and provided for in Deuteronomy 10:19 — *Love ye therefore the stranger... ye were strangers in the land of Egypt* — is brought near as *fellowcitizens*: the sojourner grafted into the commonwealth of Yashar'el (Israel), not a separate people, the one covenant household enlarged.
cards.s_text: Love you therefore the stranger: for you were strangers in the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: Now therefore you are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of Elohim (God);

cards.note: The Redeemer Job knows liveth bears the Name in Isaiah: *Fear not, thou worm Jacob ... I will help thee, saith Yahuah (LORD), and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 41:14). Job's *I know that my redeemer liveth* (Job 19:25) confesses the same living Goel — the kinsman-redeemer who is Yahuah-of-the-Name and the Holy One who helps his own.
cards.s_text: For I know that my redeemer lives, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
cards.t_text: Fear not, you worm Jacob, and you men of Yashar'el (Israel); I will help you, says Yahuah (LORD), and your redeemer, the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: The Redeemer is named King and First and Last: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God)* (Isaiah 44:6). Job's living *redeemer* (Job 19:25) is this Goel — the Formed Son who bears the Name and stands as the First and the Last, who has a Father and is not another beside Him.
cards.s_text: For I know that my redeemer lives, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).

cards.note: The redeemer's Name is sounded over Babylon's fall: *As for our redeemer, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name, the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Isaiah 47:4). Job's confession *I know that my redeemer liveth* (Job 19:25) rests on this same living Name — the Goel who avenges and buys back his own.
cards.s_text: For I know that my redeemer lives, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
cards.t_text: As for our redeemer, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) is his name, the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Isaiah's coming Redeemer is sealed in the apostle: *And so all Yashar'el (Israel) shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob* (Romans 11:26). Job's living *redeemer* who *shall stand ... upon the earth* (Job 19:25) is this Deliverer — the Formed Son who comes to redeem all Yashar'el, both houses gathered.
cards.s_text: For I know that my redeemer lives, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:
cards.t_text: And so all Yashar'el (Israel) shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob:

cards.note: *Say unto them, As I live, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways; for why will ye die, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)?* (Ezekiel 33:11). The watchman's plea is Jeremiah's potter-word in the imperative — *If that nation... turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil* (Jeremiah 18:8). The remaking of the marred vessel waits only on the turning: *turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways.*
cards.s_text: If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
cards.t_text: Say unto them, As I live, says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked; but that the wicked turn from his way and live: turn you, turn you from your evil ways; for why will you die, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)?

cards.note: *But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand* (Isaiah 64:8). Isaiah confesses from the clay's own side the truth Jeremiah is shown at the wheel — *as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Jeremiah 18:6). The people are not their own makers; they are the work of Yahuah's hand, the clay yielding to the Potter who is also their father.
cards.s_text: O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? says Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But now, O Yahuah (LORD), you are our father; we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the work of your hand.

cards.note: *Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?* (Romans 9:21). Paul takes up Jeremiah's very sign — *as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Jeremiah 18:6) — and presses its plain force: the Potter has sovereign right over the clay, to make one vessel unto honour and another unto dishonour. The house of Yashar'el (Israel), like the marred vessel, is wholly in the Maker's hand.
cards.s_text: O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? says Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Has not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

cards.note: *O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? saith Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Jeremiah 18:6). The potter's right over the clay — to remake or to break — is the frame of both chapters. In chapter 18 the hand remakes; in chapter 19 the same hand breaks the fired vessel that *cannot be made whole again* (Jeremiah 19:11). The sovereignty is one; the people's hardening (19:15) is what turns the remaking into the shattering.
cards.s_text: And shall say unto them, Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); Even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel, that cannot be made whole again: and they shall bury them in Tophet, till there be no place to bury.
cards.t_text: O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? says Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are you in my hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). Jeremiah presses the ancient Deuteronomy decision to the streets of besieged Jerusalem — *Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death* (Jeremiah 21:8). The same two ways are always before Yashar'el (Israel): life is the way of obedience to Yahuah's (LORD's) word, and the charge is the same — *therefore choose life*.
cards.s_text: And unto this people you shall say, Thus says Yahuah (LORD); Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death.
cards.t_text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both you and your seed may live:

cards.note: *And Samuel said unto all Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that ye said unto me, and have made a king over you* (1 Samuel 12:1). Samuel's word at Gilgal — *Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there* (1 Samuel 11:14) — is the deed he testifies to in the very next breath: he *made a king over* Yashar'el. The renewing at Gilgal is Samuel's public confirmation of the throne the people had demanded, now established before Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Then said Samuel to the people, Come, and let us go to Gilgal, and renew the kingdom there.
cards.t_text: And Samuel said unto all Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I have hearkened unto your voice in all that you said unto me, and have made a king over you.

cards.note: *And thou shalt go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto thee, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shalt thou tarry, till I come to thee, and shew thee what thou shalt do* (1 Samuel 10:8). Gilgal was already appointed by Samuel for peace offerings before Yahuah; there the kingdom is now renewed — *there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before Yahuah (LORD); and there Saul and all the men of Yashar'el (Israel) rejoiced greatly* (1 Samuel 11:15). The throne is set before Yahuah at the appointed place, with the sacrifices of peace.
cards.s_text: And all the people went to Gilgal; and there they made Saul king before Yahuah (LORD) in Gilgal; and there they sacrificed sacrifices of peace offerings before Yahuah (LORD); and there Saul and all the men of Yashar'el (Israel) rejoiced greatly.
cards.t_text: And you shall go down before me to Gilgal; and, behold, I will come down unto you, to offer burnt offerings, and to sacrifice sacrifices of peace offerings: seven days shall you tarry, till I come to you, and shew you what you shall do.

cards.note: *And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Yashar'el (Israel)? for do not I know that I am this day king over Yashar'el (Israel)?* (2 Samuel 19:22). David, on the day his kingdom is restored, refuses to slay Shimei who had cursed him — the very mercy Saul shows at the height of his victory: *There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day Yahuah (LORD) hath wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Samuel 11:13). The day of salvation is the day of mercy, not vengeance; the king who is Yahuah's deliverer spares rather than destroys his own.
cards.s_text: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day Yahuah (LORD) has wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And David said, What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Yashar'el (Israel)? for do not I know that I am this day king over Yashar'el (Israel)?

cards.note: *And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines* (2 Samuel 19:9). The confession Yashar'el makes of David — *the king saved us* — is first earned by Saul at Jabesh, when *Yahuah (LORD) hath wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Samuel 11:13) through his hand. The throne is given to save the people; the anointed king is Yahuah's instrument of deliverance.
cards.s_text: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day Yahuah (LORD) has wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.

cards.note: *And when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) cried unto Yahuah (LORD), Yahuah (LORD) raised up a deliverer to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother* (Judges 3:9). The cry of besieged Jabesh and the weeping at Gibeah (1 Samuel 11:4) are answered as the judge-cycle was answered: Yahuah raises a deliverer and saves His people. Saul says it plainly — *to day Yahuah (LORD) hath wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel)* (11:13). The salvation is Yahuah's, wrought through the man He raises up.
cards.s_text: And Saul said, There shall not a man be put to death this day: for to day Yahuah (LORD) has wrought salvation in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) cried unto Yahuah (LORD), Yahuah (LORD) raised up a deliverer to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.

cards.note: *But the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet; and Abi-ezer was gathered after him* (Judges 6:34). As the Spirit upon Gideon turned a fearful man into a deliverer who mustered Yashar'el with a trumpet, so *the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Saul* (1 Samuel 11:6), and he hewed the yoke of oxen and sent through all the coasts of Yashar'el (Israel) to gather them (11:7). The same Spirit, the same summons, the same one Ruach of Yahuah raising up a saviour.
cards.s_text: And the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly.
cards.t_text: But the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon Gideon, and he blew a trumpet; and Abi-ezer was gathered after him.

cards.note: *And the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon him, and he judged Yashar'el (Israel), and went out to war: and Yahuah (LORD) delivered Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushan-rishathaim* (Judges 3:10). This is the judge-pattern exactly: the Spirit comes upon the man Yahuah raises, and he goes out to save. So with Saul — *the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly* (1 Samuel 11:6). The first deliverer of the kingship is roused as Othniel was: one Ruach of Yahuah upon the chosen.
cards.s_text: And the Spirit of Elohim (God) came upon Saul when he heard those tidings, and his anger was kindled greatly.
cards.t_text: And the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon him, and he judged Yashar'el (Israel), and went out to war: and Yahuah (LORD) delivered Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushan-rishathaim.

cards.note: Samuel's covenant-lawsuit — *that I may reason with you before Yahuah (LORD) of all the righteous acts of Yahuah (LORD), which he did to you and to your fathers* (1 Samuel 12:7) — is the very pattern Joshua used at Shechem a generation before: *Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham* (Joshua 24:2). The faithful leader rehearses Yahuah's saving acts before charging the people to serve him.
cards.s_text: Now therefore stand still, that I may reason with you before Yahuah (LORD) of all the righteous acts of Yahuah (LORD), which he did to you and to your fathers.
cards.t_text: And Joshua said unto all the people, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.

cards.note: Paul preaches the same recital in the Pisidian synagogue: *The Elohim (God) of this people of Yashar'el (Israel) chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought he them out of it* (Acts 13:17) — the very acts Samuel sets before Israel: *It is Yahuah (LORD) that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Samuel 12:6). The covenant-history is one story from the judges to the apostles.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said unto the people, It is Yahuah (LORD) that advanced Moses and Aaron, and that brought your fathers up out of the land of Egypt.
cards.t_text: The Elohim (God) of this people of Yashar'el (Israel) chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt, and with an high arm brought he them out of it.

cards.note: Samuel's prayer is heard instantly — *So Samuel called unto Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) sent thunder and rain that day* (1 Samuel 12:18) — exactly as at Mizpeh: *And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto Yahuah (LORD): and Samuel cried unto Yahuah (LORD) for Yashar'el (Israel); and Yahuah (LORD) heard him* (1 Samuel 7:9). The man whose word brings the thunder is the man who has ceased not to pray for the people.
cards.s_text: So Samuel called unto Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) sent thunder and rain that day: and all the people greatly feared Yahuah (LORD) and Samuel.
cards.t_text: And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto Yahuah (LORD): and Samuel cried unto Yahuah (LORD) for Yashar'el (Israel); and Yahuah (LORD) heard him.

cards.note: This is the anti-replacement spine of the whole canon: *For Yahuah (LORD) will not forsake his people for his great name's sake: because it hath pleased Yahuah (LORD) to make you his people* (1 Samuel 12:22) — and Paul, a thousand years on, asks and answers the same: *I say then, Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin* (Romans 11:1). Yahuah does not forsake Yashar'el for his own great Name's sake; the people he chose, he keeps.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah (LORD) will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it has pleased Yahuah (LORD) to make you his people.
cards.t_text: I say then, Has Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.

cards.note: Samuel binds his intercession to a holy obligation — *Moreover as for me, Elohim (God) forbid that I should sin against Yahuah (LORD) in ceasing to pray for you* (1 Samuel 12:23) — the very office Paul names of the prophet who pleads for Israel: *Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to Elohim (God) against Yashar'el (Israel)* (Romans 11:2). The prophet who will not cease to pray stands in the line that runs to the Formed Intercessor who ever liveth to make intercession.
cards.s_text: Moreover as for me, Elohim (God) forbid that I should sin against Yahuah (LORD) in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way:
cards.t_text: Elohim (God) has not cast away his people which he foreknew. Wot you not what the scripture says of Elias? how he makes intercession to Elohim (God) against Yashar'el (Israel), saying,

cards.note: *Wherefore Yahuah (LORD) said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant* (1 Kings 11:11). The same sentence falls on Saul: '*thou hast not kept the commandment of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)... now would Yahuah have established thy kingdom upon Yashar'el for ever*' (1 Samuel 13:13). The throne is conditioned on keeping the covenant-word — the Torah is the king's charter, never a curse; break it and the kingdom is rent, whether from Saul or from Solomon.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said to Saul, You have done foolishly: you have not kept the commandment of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which he commanded you: for now would Yahuah (LORD) have established your kingdom upon Yashar'el (Israel) for ever.
cards.t_text: Wherefore Yahuah (LORD) said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded you, I will surely rend the kingdom from you, and will give it to your servant.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Yashar'el (Israel) vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me* (Judges 7:2). Jonathan's creed — *there is no restraint to Yahuah (LORD) to save by many or by few* (1 Samuel 14:6) — is the very thing Yahuah engineered with Gideon: thin the host so the deliverance is unmistakably His, not the arm of flesh.
cards.s_text: And Jonathan said to the young man that bare his armour, Come, and let us go over unto the garrison of these uncircumcised: it may be that Yahuah (LORD) will work for us: for there is no restraint to Yahuah (LORD) to save by many or by few.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, The people that are with you are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Yashar'el (Israel) vaunt themselves against me, saying, My own hand has saved me.

cards.note: *And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saveth not with sword and spear: for the battle is Yahuah's (LORD'S)* (1 Samuel 17:47). Jonathan reads the Philistines' taunt as Yahuah's own sign — *Come up after me: for Yahuah (LORD) hath delivered them into the hand of Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Samuel 14:12) — the same certainty David carries into the valley.
cards.s_text: And the men of the garrison answered Jonathan and his armourbearer, and said, Come up to us, and we will shew you a thing. And Jonathan said unto his armourbearer, Come up after me: for Yahuah (LORD) has delivered them into the hand of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And all this assembly shall know that Yahuah (LORD) saves not with sword and spear: for the battle is the LORD’S, and he will give you into our hands.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you* (Judges 7:7). The chapter's verdict — *So Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day* (1 Samuel 14:23) — is Gideon's verdict again: when the few go up, it is Yahuah who saves, and the credit is His.
cards.s_text: So Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day: and the battle passed over unto Beth-aven.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into your hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place.

cards.note: *And whatsoever man there be of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)... that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people* (Leviticus 17:10). The gravity behind *the people sin against Yahuah (LORD), in that they eat with the blood* (1 Samuel 14:33) is this: eating blood sets Yahuah's own face against the eater.
cards.s_text: Then they told Saul, saying, Behold, the people sin against Yahuah (LORD), in that they eat with the blood. And he said, You have transgressed: roll a great stone unto me this day.
cards.t_text: And whatsoever man there be of the house of Yashar'el (Israel), or of the strangers that sojourn among you, that eats any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eats blood, and will cut him off from among his people.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into thine hand* (Judges 7:7). The people plead, *Shall Jonathan die, who hath wrought this great salvation in Yashar'el (Israel)?* (1 Samuel 14:45) — they recognise in Jonathan the deliverer Yahuah used, as Gideon was used; a man through whom Yahuah saved is not to be slain by a man's rash oath.
cards.s_text: And the people said unto Saul, Shall Jonathan die, who has wrought this great salvation in Yashar'el (Israel)? Elohim (God) forbid: as Yahuah (LORD) lives, there shall not one hair of his head fall to the ground; for he has wrought with Elohim (God) this day. So the people rescued Jonathan, that he died not.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Gideon, By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you, and deliver the Midianites into your hand: and let all the other people go every man unto his place.

cards.note: *For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation* (Exodus 17:16). When Samuel says *I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt* (1 Samuel 15:2), he is invoking the oath sworn at Rephidim — the standing seed-war that runs from the enmity of Genesis 3:15. Saul is sent to execute a war Yahuah Himself swore, not a private vendetta.
cards.s_text: Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), I remember that which Amalek did to Yashar'el (Israel), how he laid wait for him in the way, when he came up from Egypt.
cards.t_text: For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) has sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

cards.note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). The wisdom of Yashar'el (Israel) reads Samuel exactly: the keeping of Torah IS the acceptable offering — obedience does not abolish the altar but fills it. *To obey is better than sacrifice* (1 Samuel 15:22) because obedience is the offering Yahuah was always after.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said, Has Yahuah (LORD) as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of Yahuah (LORD)? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.
cards.t_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.

cards.note: *But now thy kingdom shall not continue: Yahuah (LORD) hath sought him a man after his own heart, and Yahuah (LORD) hath commanded him to be captain over his people, because thou hast not kept that which Yahuah (LORD) commanded thee* (1 Samuel 13:14). When Samuel declares *Yahuah (LORD) hath rent the kingdom of Yashar'el (Israel) from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou* (1 Samuel 15:28), the *neighbour... better than thou* is that man after Yahuah's own heart — David, already foretold at Gilgal.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said unto him, Yahuah (LORD) has rent the kingdom of Yashar'el (Israel) from you this day, and has given it to a neighbour of yours, that is better than you.
cards.t_text: But now your kingdom shall not continue: Yahuah (LORD) has sought him a man after his own heart, and Yahuah (LORD) has commanded him to be captain over his people, because you have not kept that which Yahuah (LORD) commanded you.

cards.note: *Elohim (God) is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of Adam, that he should repent: hath he said, and shall he not do it? or hath he spoken, and shall he not make it good?* (Numbers 23:19). Samuel's word *the Strength of Yashar'el (Israel) will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent* (1 Samuel 15:29) is Balaam's oracle exactly — the unchanging counsel of the Formed Son who bears the Name and leads Yashar'el. The relational grief of *it repenteth me* (15:11) and *Yahuah (LORD) repented* (15:35) is His sorrow over Saul, never a mutable purpose.
cards.s_text: And also the Strength of Yashar'el (Israel) will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.
cards.t_text: Elohim (God) is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of Adam, that he should repent: has he said, and shall he not do it? or has he spoken, and shall he not make it good?

cards.note: *And all Yashar'el (Israel), and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites... half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) had commanded before, that they should bless the people of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Joshua 8:33). The command of Deuteronomy 11:29 — *the blessing upon mount Gerizim, and the curse upon mount Ebal* — is enacted in Joshua 8:33: *half... over against mount Gerizim, and half... over against mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) had commanded*. The stranger stands with the homeborn; the whole people receives the word.
cards.s_text: And it shall come to pass, when Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) has brought you in unto the land whither you go to possess it, that you shall put the blessing upon mount Gerizim, and the curse upon mount Ebal.
cards.t_text: And all Yashar'el (Israel), and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD), as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) had commanded before, that they should bless the people of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation* (Numbers 16:33). The rebels Deuteronomy 11:6 names — *and their tents, and all the substance that was in their possession, in the midst of all Yashar'el (Israel)* — *went down alive into the pit* (Numbers 16:33). The greatness, the mighty hand, and the stretched out arm (11:2) include this terror the eyes of the people had beheld.
cards.s_text: And what he did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and all the substance that was in their possession, in the midst of all Yashar'el (Israel):
cards.t_text: They, and all that appertained to them, went down alive into the pit, and the earth closed upon them: and they perished from among the congregation.

cards.note: *And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree:* (2 Kings 17:10). The northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) did the very thing the Torah forbade — they kept the high places the charge to *overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire; and ye shall hew down the graven images of their gods* (Deuteronomy 12:3) had outlawed; the unexecuted command became the seed of the exile.
cards.s_text: And you shall overthrow their altars, and break their pillars, and burn their groves with fire; and you shall hew down the graven images of their gods, and destroy the names of them out of that place.
cards.t_text: And they set them up images and groves in every high hill, and under every green tree:

cards.note: *But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Yashar'el (Israel).* (2 Chronicles 6:6). Yahuah names the chosen place outright — Jerusalem — fulfilling *the place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose... to put his name there* (Deuteronomy 12:5); the Name and the Davidic king are bound to one location.
cards.s_text: But unto the place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall you seek, and thither you shall come:
cards.t_text: But I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and have chosen David to be over my people Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *For it is the life of all flesh; the blood of it is for the life thereof: therefore I said unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.* (Leviticus 17:14). The identical standing: *ye shall not eat the blood; ye shall pour it upon the earth as water* (Deuteronomy 12:16) — the life-in-the-blood is poured out, never consumed.
cards.s_text: Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it upon the earth as water.
cards.t_text: For it is the life of all flesh; the blood of it is for the life thereof: therefore I said unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), You shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eats it shall be cut off.

cards.note: *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) did secretly those things that were not right against Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.* (2 Kings 17:9). The very snare *Take heed to thyself that thou be not snared by following them... and that thou enquire not after their gods* (Deuteronomy 12:30) warned of — the north secretly took up the nations' worship and built their high places.
cards.s_text: Take heed to thyself that you be not snared by following them, after that they be destroyed from before you; and that you enquire not after their gods, saying, How did these nations serve their gods? even so will I do likewise.
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) did secretly those things that were not right against Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and they built them high places in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.

cards.note: *And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Yashar'el (Israel):* (Deuteronomy 17:4) Word for word the same diligent inquiry guards both cases against rumor: *Then shalt thou enquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought among you* (Deuteronomy 13:14).
cards.s_text: Then shall you enquire, and make search, and ask diligently; and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought among you;
cards.t_text: And it be told you, and you have heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Yashar'el (Israel):

cards.note: *And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Exodus 19:6). The holiness Deuteronomy 14:2 reaffirms — *thou art an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* — is priestly vocation: a whole nation set apart to Yahuah, the calling the dietary distinctions of this chapter daily enact.
cards.s_text: For you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and Yahuah (LORD) has chosen you to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.
cards.t_text: And you shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which you shall speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And he said unto them... Elohim (God) hath shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.* (Acts 10:28). Peter himself gives the vision's meaning, and it is about PEOPLE, not pork: the sheet of beasts taught him not to reckon the Gentile-born of Yashar'el unclean — the two-house ingathering. It is not a cancelling of Deuteronomy 14:8, *ye shall not eat of their flesh*; Peter still holds the food law (Acts 10:14) even as he receives the men.
cards.s_text: And the swine, because it divides the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: you shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.
cards.t_text: And he said unto them, You know how that it is an unlawful thing for a man that is a Yahudi (Jew) to keep company, or come unto one of another nation; but Elohim (God) has shewed me that I should not call any man common or unclean.

cards.note: *The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God). Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk.* (Exodus 23:19). Deuteronomy 14:21 repeats the command exactly — *Thou shalt not seethe a kid in his mother's milk* — a guard against a Canaanite fertility rite; the third Torah witness to the same word, marking Yashar'el off from the nations' worship.
cards.s_text: You shall not eat of any thing that dies of itself: you shall give it unto the stranger that is in your gates, that he may eat it; or you may sell it unto an alien: for you are an holy people unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God). You shall not seethe a kid in his mother’s milk.
cards.t_text: The first of the firstfruits of your land you shall bring into the house of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God). You shall not seethe a kid in his mother’s milk.

cards.note: *And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,* (Deuteronomy 31:10). The same release Moses opens here — *At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release* (Deuteronomy 15:1) — is set on the festal calendar: the shemittah falls in the year of release at the feast of tabernacles, and that is when the law is read aloud to all Yashar'el (Israel). The debt-release and the appointed time are one covenant order, not two.
cards.s_text: At the end of every seven years you shall make a release.
cards.t_text: And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,

cards.note: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto Yahuah (LORD).* (Leviticus 25:2). The release belongs to the land Yahuah gives — *because it is called the LORD'S release* (Deuteronomy 15:2) — the seventh year a sabbath kept unto him, the rhythm of rest written over field and creditor alike.
cards.s_text: And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD’S release.
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When you come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,* (Acts 4:34). The promise hung on the open hand — *Save when there shall be no poor among you* (Deuteronomy 15:4), if Yashar'el will *open thine hand wide* (15:10) — is what Luke records of the first assembly: when the people gave freely, none among them lacked. The shemittah ideal lived out.
cards.s_text: You shall surely give him, and your heart shall not be grieved when you give unto him: because that for this thing Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless you in all your works, and in all that you put your hand unto.
cards.t_text: Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold,

cards.note: *Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever openeth the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.* (Exodus 13:2). The firstlings Moses sets apart here — *All the firstling males that come of thy herd and of thy flock thou shalt sanctify unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (Deuteronomy 15:19) — are claimed back at the exodus: every opener of the womb belongs to Yahuah, redeemed firstborn for a redeemed people.
cards.s_text: All the firstling males that come of your herd and of your flock you shall sanctify unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): you shall do no work with the firstling of your bullock, nor shear the firstling of your sheep.
cards.t_text: Sanctify unto me all the firstborn, whatsoever opens the womb among the children of Yashar'el (Israel), both of man and of beast: it is mine.

cards.note: *And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna... that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD) doth man live* (Deuteronomy 8:3). Job lives the wilderness lesson before it was spoken to Yashar''el: *I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food* (Job 23:12) — the word of Yahuah''s mouth weighed above bread.
cards.s_text: Neither have I gone back from the commandment of his lips; I have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
cards.t_text: And he humbled you, and suffered you to hunger, and fed you with manna, which you knew not, neither did your fathers know; that he might make you know that man does not live by bread only, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of Yahuah (LORD) does man live.

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33). The heart promised the good figs — *I will give them an heart to know me, that I am Yahuah (LORD): and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim (God)* (Jeremiah 24:7) — is unfolded fully in the new covenant of chapter 31: the same Torah written on the inward heart, the same *they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim*. The heart to know Yahuah is the heart with the law written on it.
cards.s_text: And I will give them an heart to know me, that I am Yahuah (LORD): and they shall be my people, and I will be their Elohim (God): for they shall return unto me with their whole heart.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *Yahuah (LORD) also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but Yahuah (LORD) will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Joel 3:16). Joel hears the same roar Jeremiah heard — *Yahuah (LORD) shall roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation* (Jeremiah 25:30): the Judge roars from his place over the nations, yet the roar that terrifies the wicked is the hope and strength of his own people. One voice, two hearings.
cards.s_text: Therefore prophesy you against them all these words, and say unto them, Yahuah (LORD) shall roar from on high, and utter his voice from his holy habitation; he shall mightily roar upon his habitation; he shall give a shout, as they that tread the grapes, against all the inhabitants of the earth.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) also shall roar out of Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the heavens and the earth shall shake: but Yahuah (LORD) will be the hope of his people, and the strength of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *To fulfil the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years* (2 Chronicles 36:21). The Chronicler names what the seventy years MEAN — *this whole land shall be a desolation... seventy years* (Jeremiah 25:11): the land's unkept sabbaths repaid in rest. The desolation is the land at last keeping the sabbath-years that Yashar'el (Israel) withheld; the seventy is the measure of that owed rest.
cards.s_text: And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
cards.t_text: To fulfil the word of Yahuah (LORD) by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths: for as long as she lay desolate she kept sabbath, to fulfil threescore and ten years.

cards.note: *And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth* (2 Kings 19:15). The elders ask *did he not fear Yahuah (LORD), and besought Yahuah (LORD)* (Jeremiah 26:19) — and here is Hezekiah doing exactly that, going up to the house of Yahuah and praying. Because the king sought Yahuah, the threatened evil was turned away; the prophet's word is a summons to repent.
cards.s_text: Did Hezekiah king of Yahudah (Judah) and all Yahudah (Judah) put him at all to death? did he not fear Yahuah (LORD), and besought Yahuah (LORD), and Yahuah (LORD) repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them? Thus might we procure great evil against our souls.
cards.t_text: And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: *So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men* (Psalm 78:60). The psalm names the very precedent Jeremiah invokes — *Then will I make this house like Shiloh* (Jeremiah 26:6): Yahuah (LORD) once *forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh*, the tent he himself had placed among men, when Yashar'el (Israel) provoked him. The sanctuary stands or falls with the covenant; the building cannot save a Torah-forsaking people.
cards.s_text: Then will I make this house like Shiloh, and will make this city a curse to all the nations of the earth.
cards.t_text: So that he forsook the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent which he placed among men;

cards.note: *Thus saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes* (Jeremiah 29:21). The lying prophets *which prophesy a lie unto you in my name* meet the end Hananiah met — for Hananiah too *makest this people to trust in a lie* (Jeremiah 28:15), and died that same year. The lie spoken in the Name is answered by Yahuah's judgment.
cards.s_text: Then said the prophet Jeremiah unto Hananiah the prophet, Hear now, Hananiah; Yahuah (LORD) has not sent you; but you make this people to trust in a lie.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), of Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and of Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, which prophesy a lie unto you in my name; Behold, I will deliver them into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon; and he shall slay them before your eyes;

cards.note: *Of this man's seed hath Elohim (God) according to his promise raised unto Yashar'el (Israel) a Saviour, Yahusha (Jesus)* (Acts 13:23). The Spirit-anointed David of 1 Samuel 16:13 is the head of the seed-line through which the Saviour comes: the oil poured on the shepherd at Beth-lehem opens onto the promise that out of David's seed Yahuah raises Yahusha — the Branch, the Formed Son who took flesh as David's offspring.
cards.s_text: Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of Yahuah (LORD) came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.
cards.t_text: Of this man’s seed has Elohim (God) according to his promise raised unto Yashar'el (Israel) a Saviour, Yahusha (Jesus):

cards.note: *But thou, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Yahudah (Judah), yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting* (Micah 5:2). Samuel comes to Beth-lehem and Yahuah says of the shepherd-boy, '*Arise, anoint him: for this is he*' (1 Samuel 16:12). The town of David's anointing is the town from which the ruler over Yashar'el comes forth — the Beth-lehem shepherd-king whose goings forth are from everlasting, the seed of David who takes flesh.
cards.s_text: And he sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, and withal of a beautiful countenance, and goodly to look to. And Yahuah (LORD) said, Arise, anoint him: for this is he.
cards.t_text: But you, Beth-lehem Ephratah, though you be little among the thousands of Yahudah (Judah), yet out of you shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel); whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.

cards.note: *From following the ewes great with young he brought him to feed Jacob his people, and Yashar'el (Israel) his inheritance* (Psalm 78:71). David '*keepeth the sheep*' (1 Samuel 16:11) and is brought in from the flock — and that flock-keeping is the apprenticeship of the throne: the one who followed the ewes is set to feed Jacob, Yahuah's own inheritance, the shepherd-king pattern.
cards.s_text: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all your children? And he said, There remains yet the youngest, and, behold, he keeps the sheep. And Samuel said unto Jesse, Send and fetch him: for we will not sit down till he come hither.
cards.t_text: From following the ewes great with young he brought him to feed Jacob his people, and Yashar'el (Israel) his inheritance.

cards.note: *And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Yashar'el (Israel) a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people* (1 Samuel 9:2). This is the very stature Yahuah now refuses in Eliab — '*Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature... for Yahuah seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but Yahuah looketh on the heart*' (1 Samuel 16:7). Saul was chosen for the frame man sees and failed; the next king is weighed by the heart Yahuah sees.
cards.s_text: But Yahuah (LORD) said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for Yahuah (LORD) sees not as man sees; for man looks on the outward appearance, but Yahuah (LORD) looks on the heart.
cards.t_text: And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Yashar'el (Israel) a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.

cards.note: *Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword... and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled* (1 Samuel 17:51). Goliath set the terms of single combat — *choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me* (1 Samuel 17:8) — one champion for all; and the terms hold in reverse: when the one champion of Yashar'el (Israel) prevails, the enemy is broken for the whole people.
cards.s_text: And he stood and cried unto the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), and said unto them, Why are you come out to set your battle in array? am not I a Philistine, and you servants to Saul? choose you a man for you, and let him come down to me.
cards.t_text: Therefore David ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath thereof, and slew him, and cut off his head therewith. And when the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they fled.

cards.note: *And the men of Yashar'el (Israel) and of Yahudah (Judah) arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines... And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron* (1 Samuel 17:52). The wager was that one man's fight would settle a whole nation's fate — *if he be able to fight with me... then will we be your servants* (1 Samuel 17:9) — and so David's lone victory becomes the rout of both houses; one champion's triumph is the people's deliverance.
cards.s_text: If he be able to fight with me, and to kill me, then will we be your servants: but if I prevail against him, and kill him, then shall you be our servants, and serve us.
cards.t_text: And the men of Yashar'el (Israel) and of Yahudah (Judah) arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines, until you come to the valley, and to the gates of Ekron. And the wounded of the Philistines fell down by the way to Shaaraim, even unto Gath, and unto Ekron.

cards.note: *And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find thee; and thou shalt be king over Yashar'el (Israel), and I shall be next unto thee; and that also Saul my father knoweth* (1 Samuel 23:17). The love that loves *as he loved his own soul* (1 Samuel 20:17) costs Jonathan the very kingdom — he gladly takes second place to the anointed: *thou shalt be king... and I shall be next unto thee*; the heir lays down his own right for love of the one Yahuah chose.
cards.s_text: And Jonathan caused David to swear again, because he loved him: for he loved him as he loved his own soul.
cards.t_text: And he said unto him, Fear not: for the hand of Saul my father shall not find you; and you shall be king over Yashar'el (Israel), and I shall be next unto you; and that also Saul my father knows.

cards.note: *Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.* (Isaiah 1:17). This is the very thing Job did — *I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out* (Job 29:16). Isaiah commands of Yashar'el (Israel) what Job already lived: the covenant-justice that is the heart of Torah, not its ceremonies emptied of mercy.
cards.s_text: I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
cards.t_text: Learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.

cards.note: *Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and Elohim (God) himself shall be with them, and be their Elohim (God)* (Revelation 21:3). The feast of booths, where Yashar'el dwelt in temporary dwellings rejoicing (Deuteronomy 16:13-15), is fulfilled when the tabernacle of Elohim is pitched with men for ever.
cards.s_text: Seven days shall you keep a solemn feast unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which Yahuah (LORD) shall choose: because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless you in all your increase, and in all the works of your hands, therefore you shall surely rejoice.
cards.t_text: And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and Elohim (God) himself shall be with them, and be their Elohim (God).

cards.note: *Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 34:23). The thrice-yearly appearing of Deuteronomy 16:16 is fixed across all three Torah witnesses of the pilgrimage feasts.
cards.s_text: Three times in a year shall all your males appear before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which he shall choose; in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles: and they shall not appear before Yahuah (LORD) empty:
cards.t_text: Thrice in the year shall all your men children appear before Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto thee, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with thee.* (Exodus 18:22). Jethro's counsel set the pattern Deuteronomy 17:8 institutionalises — *If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment... then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah shall choose* — the great and hard matter brought up to the higher tribunal, the small judged below, a graded order of judgment in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: If there arise a matter too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between stroke and stroke, being matters of controversy within your gates: then shall you arise, and get you up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose;
cards.t_text: And let them judge the people at all seasons: and it shall be, that every great matter they shall bring unto you, but every small matter they shall judge: so shall it be easier for thyself, and they shall bear the burden with you.

cards.note: *Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), for the judgment of Yahuah (LORD), and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem.* (2 Chronicles 19:8). Jehoshaphat enacts the very tribunal of Deuteronomy 17:9 — *thou shalt come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days* — setting the Levites and priests at the chosen place to render *the judgment of Yahuah*, the supreme court Moses commanded brought to life.
cards.s_text: And you shall come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days, and enquire; and they shall shew you the sentence of judgment:
cards.t_text: Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), for the judgment of Yahuah (LORD), and for controversies, when they returned to Jerusalem.

cards.note: *And said unto him, Behold, thou art old, and thy sons walk not in thy ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.* (1 Samuel 8:5). The very words Moses foresaw — *I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me* (Deuteronomy 17:14) — fall from Yashar'el (Israel)'s mouth in Samuel's day: a king *like all the nations*. Deuteronomy had already provided for a king, but a king of Yahuah's choosing and Yahuah's pattern, not a copy of the nations.
cards.s_text: When you are come unto the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you, and shall possess it, and shall dwell therein, and shall say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me;
cards.t_text: And said unto him, Behold, you are old, and your sons walk not in your ways: now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 18:20). What Moses repeats here — *The priests the Levites... shall have no part nor inheritance with Yashar'el (Israel)* (Deuteronomy 18:1) — Yahuah first spoke to Aaron: the tribe set apart to the altar is given no field, because Yahuah Himself is their portion.
cards.s_text: The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Yashar'el (Israel): they shall eat the offerings of Yahuah (LORD) made by fire, and his inheritance.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Aaron, You shall have no inheritance in their land, neither shall you have any part among them: I am your part and your inheritance among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) was their inheritance, as he said unto them* (Joshua 13:33). When the land was divided this word stood fulfilled — Levi alone drew no lot, for *Yahuah (LORD) is their inheritance, as he hath said unto them* (Deuteronomy 18:2). The covenant promise kept exactly as spoken.
cards.s_text: Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: Yahuah (LORD) is their inheritance, as he has said unto them.
cards.t_text: But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) was their inheritance, as he said unto them.

cards.note: *A man also or woman that hath a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones: their blood shall be upon them* (Leviticus 20:27). The necromancer of Deuteronomy 18:11 stands under this sentence — the abomination is not tolerated within the camp of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
cards.t_text: A man also or woman that has a familiar spirit, or that is a wizard, shall surely be put to death: they shall stone them with stones: their blood shall be upon them.

cards.note: *Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver* (Acts 19:19). When Yashar'el (Israel) comes into the truth they do what Moses commanded — they *learn... not to do after the abominations of those nations* (Deuteronomy 18:9): the books of sorcery go into the fire, the old enchantments renounced.
cards.s_text: When you are come into the land which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
cards.t_text: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them before all men: and they counted the price of them, and found it fifty thousand pieces of silver.

cards.note: *This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), A prophet shall Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God) raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear* (Acts 7:37). Stephen, before the council, sets the same prophecy at the center of the witness — the *Prophet... like unto me* (Deuteronomy 18:15) is the One Moses himself foretold.
cards.s_text: Yahuah Elohayka (The LORD thy God) will raise up unto you a Prophet from the midst of you, of your brethren, like unto me; unto him you shall hearken;
cards.t_text: This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), A prophet shall Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God) raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall you hear.

cards.note: *Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet* (John 7:40). The hope built on Deuteronomy 18:15 was alive and known — Yashar'el (Israel) waited for *the Prophet*, and hearing Yahusha (Jesus), many confessed He was the One.
cards.s_text: Yahuah Elohayka (The LORD thy God) will raise up unto you a Prophet from the midst of you, of your brethren, like unto me; unto him you shall hearken;
cards.t_text: Many of the people therefore, when they heard this saying, said, Of a truth this is the Prophet.

cards.note: *And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he hath spoken to turn you away from Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)... So shalt thou put the evil away from the midst of thee* (Deuteronomy 13:5). The sentence is the same one Deuteronomy 18:20 pronounces — *even that prophet shall die*: the presumptuous and the idolatrous prophet alike are purged from Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
cards.t_text: And that prophet, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be put to death; because he has spoken to turn you away from Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God), which brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you out of the house of bondage, to thrust you out of the way which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) commanded you to walk in. So shall you put the evil away from the midst of you.

cards.note: *These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that killeth any person unawares may flee thither.* (Numbers 35:15). The case Moses opens — *Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past* (Deuteronomy 19:4) — is the same accidental slaying Numbers shelters: the refuge is for the one who kills *unawares*, and it reaches even the stranger and sojourner; the land's justice is one for all who dwell in it.
cards.s_text: And this is the case of the slayer, which shall flee thither, that he may live: Whoso kills his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past;
cards.t_text: These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that kills any person unawares may flee thither.

cards.note: *Speak to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:* (Joshua 20:2). The way prepared and the land divided into parts *that every slayer may flee thither* (Deuteronomy 19:3) is carried out in Joshua: the cities Moses commanded are now actually appointed in the land — Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron, Bezer, Ramoth, Golan (Joshua 20:7-8) — the word of the refuge moving from command to standing reality.
cards.s_text: You shall prepare you a way, and divide the coasts of your land, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gives you to inherit, into three parts, that every slayer may flee thither.
cards.t_text: Speak to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:

cards.note: *Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace* (Exodus 14:14). At the Red Sea the same assurance is given that the priest carries to the army: *For Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is he that goeth with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you* (Deuteronomy 20:4). The pattern of the Exodus deliverance becomes the standing law of war — the battle belongs to the One who already saved Yashar'el (Israel) out of Egypt.
cards.s_text: For Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is he that goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies, to save you.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.

cards.note: *No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of Elohim (God)* (Luke 9:62). The principle behind sending the *fearful and fainthearted* home — *lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart* (Deuteronomy 20:8) — is the undivided heart: the wavering man weakens the whole; the divided will is *not fit* for the work, whether the war of Yashar'el (Israel) or the kingdom of Elohim (God).
cards.s_text: And the officers shall speak further unto the people, and they shall say, What man is there that is fearful and fainthearted? let him go and return unto his house, lest his brethren’s heart faint as well as his heart.
cards.t_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of Elohim (God).

cards.note: *And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants* (Leviticus 18:25). The herem of Deuteronomy 20:16-18 is the land's own moral physics: the nations are cast out for the *abominations* (Deuteronomy 20:18) the land cannot bear, and the same warning hangs over Yashar'el (Israel) — *that the land spue not you out also, when ye defile it* (Leviticus 18:28). Victims of a corrupting system, never enemies hated for their flesh.
cards.s_text: That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should you sin against Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).
cards.t_text: And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.

cards.note: *Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you* (Leviticus 18:24). The casting-out is judgment on conduct — child-sacrifice, incest, idolatry — not on lineage; the very same standard is then laid on Yashar'el (Israel). Deuteronomy 20:18 names the danger plainly: *so should ye sin against Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* — the covenant people must not inherit the defiling system.
cards.s_text: That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should you sin against Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).
cards.t_text: Defile not you yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you:

cards.note: *And mine hand shall be upon the prophets that see vanity, and that divine lies: they shall not be in the assembly of my people, neither shall they be written in the writing of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 13:9).
