cards.t_text: O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word,

cards.note: *And David built there an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So Yahuah (LORD) was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Samuel 24:25). The parallel record of the same threshingfloor: the place where the plague was stayed by offering becomes the foundation of *the house of Yahuah... in mount Moriah* (2 Chronicles 3:1) — the one mount of substitution that points to the Messiah's own offering.
cards.s_text: Then Solomon began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.
cards.t_text: And David built there an altar unto Yahuah (LORD), and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So Yahuah (LORD) was intreated for the land, and the plague was stayed from Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Then David said, This is the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), and this is the altar of the burnt offering for Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Chronicles 22:1). David himself declared the threshingfloor of Ornan to be the appointed house and altar; *the place that David had prepared* (2 Chronicles 3:1) is exactly this — the spot where Akedah, the altar of mercy, and the temple converge on one mount.
cards.s_text: Then Solomon began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.
cards.t_text: Then David said, This is the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), and this is the altar of the burnt offering for Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb* (Revelation 21:14). The molten sea borne upon twelve oxen (2 Chronicles 4:4) sets the cleansing of the priests upon the twelve tribes; the New Jerusalem rests upon the same twelve-fold foundation — the whole house of Yashar'el (Israel) bearing up the worship of the Most High.
cards.s_text: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward.
cards.t_text: And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.

cards.note: *And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Revelation 21:12). The sea *stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north... west... south... east* (2 Chronicles 4:4) — the twelve tribes bearing up the means of cleansing, the same twelve set in the four quarters of the city of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.s_text: It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward.
cards.t_text: And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel):

cards.note: *And, behold, the glory of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory.* (Ezekiel 43:2). The Glory that had departed Solomon's house returns in Ezekiel's vision from the east. The same Glory that *had filled the house of Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 5:14) comes back to fill the restored temple — the Presence is not lost but regathered.
cards.s_text: So that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud: for the glory of Yahuah (LORD) had filled the house of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: And, behold, the glory of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came from the way of the east: and his voice was like a noise of many waters: and the earth shined with his glory.

cards.note: *But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Psalm 22:3). Yahuah is enthroned upon the praises of his people. So when the trumpeters and singers *were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Yahuah (LORD)... For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever* (2 Chronicles 5:13), the united praise builds the throne on which the Glory then descends — the cloud fills the house exactly as the one voice rises.
cards.s_text: It came even to pass, as the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Yahuah (LORD); and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of musick, and praised Yahuah (LORD), saying, For he is good; for his mercy endures for ever: that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of Yahuah (LORD);
cards.t_text: But you are holy, O you that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel), when they came out of the land of Egypt.* (1 Kings 8:9). The Kings account of the same dedication reads almost word for word with *There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb* (2 Chronicles 5:10) — two witnesses to one fact: the heart of the house held the Torah of the covenant.
cards.s_text: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel), when they came out of Egypt.
cards.t_text: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel), when they came out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *And I turned myself and came down from the mount, and put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be, as Yahuah (LORD) commanded me.* (Deuteronomy 10:5). Moses' own witness: *there they be* — the two tables in the ark. The Chronicler confirms the unbroken record: *the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 5:10). The covenant-word stays at the center.
cards.s_text: There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel), when they came out of Egypt.
cards.t_text: And I turned myself and came down from the mount, and put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be, as Yahuah (LORD) commanded me.

cards.note: *And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where Elohim (God) was.* (Exodus 20:21) At Sinai the people kept their distance while Moses entered the very *thick darkness* where Yahuah (LORD) was. Solomon names that same dwelling: *Yahuah (LORD) hath said that he would dwell in the thick darkness* (2 Chronicles 6:1). The house in Jerusalem is built to receive the Presence that met Yashar'el (Israel) at the mountain.
cards.s_text: Then said Solomon, Yahuah (LORD) has said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.
cards.t_text: And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where Elohim (God) was.

cards.note: *Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.* (Isaiah 56:7) Solomon opened the house to *the stranger, which is not of thy people Yashar'el (Israel), but is come from a far country* (2 Chronicles 6:32); Isaiah declares its very name — *an house of prayer for all people*. The nations who come to fear Yahuah's name are welcomed at the altar Solomon dedicated.
cards.s_text: Moreover concerning the stranger, which is not of your people Yashar'el (Israel), but is come from a far country for your great name’s sake, and your mighty hand, and your stretched out arm; if they come and pray in this house;
cards.t_text: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon my altar; for my house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.

cards.note: *Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Yashar'el (Israel) for ever, as I promised to David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man upon the throne of Yashar'el (Israel).* (1 Kings 9:5). The promise answers the condition: *Then will I stablish the throne of thy kingdom... There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 7:18). The Davidic throne is sworn, and walking in Yahuah's ways is its appointed path.
cards.s_text: Then will I stablish the throne of your kingdom, according as I have covenanted with David your father, saying, There shall not fail you a man to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Then I will establish the throne of your kingdom upon Yashar'el (Israel) for ever, as I promised to David your father, saying, There shall not fail you a man upon the throne of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Then will I cut off Yashar'el (Israel) out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Yashar'el (Israel) shall be a proverb and a byword among all people:* (1 Kings 9:7). The Kings word is nearly verbatim: the land cut off, the house cast out, the proverb and byword. *This house, which I have sanctified for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and will make it to be a proverb and a byword among all nations* (2 Chronicles 7:20) — one warning, doubly witnessed.
cards.s_text: Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them; and this house, which I have sanctified for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and will make it to be a proverb and a byword among all nations.
cards.t_text: Then will I cut off Yashar'el (Israel) out of the land which I have given them; and this house, which I have hallowed for my name, will I cast out of my sight; and Yashar'el (Israel) shall be a proverb and a byword among all people:

cards.note: *But go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Yashar'el (Israel).* (Jeremiah 7:12). Jeremiah points to Shiloh as the precedent the temple itself would follow — the place where Yahuah set His name, ruined for the people's sin. *Because they forsook Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers... therefore hath he brought all this evil upon them* (2 Chronicles 7:22) is the same lesson, that no house is safe for a covenant-breaking people.
cards.s_text: And it shall be answered, Because they forsook Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers, which brought them forth out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold on other gods, and worshipped them, and served them: therefore has he brought all this evil upon them.
cards.t_text: But go you now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts* (Leviticus 23:2). They are *my feasts* — Yahuah's own calendar — which Solomon offered upon *according to the commandment of Moses... on the solemn feasts* (2 Chronicles 8:13).
cards.s_text: Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.

cards.note: *Command the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, My offering, and my bread for my sacrifices made by fire, for a sweet savour unto me, shall ye observe to offer unto me in their due season* (Numbers 28:2). The daily, Sabbath, and new-moon offerings *in their due season* are spelled out in Numbers 28-29 — exactly the *certain rate every day... on the sabbaths, and on the new moons* (2 Chronicles 8:13) Solomon kept.
cards.s_text: Even after a certain rate every day, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts, three times in the year, even in the feast of unleavened bread, and in the feast of weeks, and in the feast of tabernacles.
cards.t_text: Command the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, My offering, and my bread for my sacrifices made by fire, for a sweet savour unto me, shall you observe to offer unto me in their due season.

cards.note: The queen blesses Yahuah *which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)* (2 Chronicles 9:8) — and the throne is named exactly: *Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahuah (LORD) as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Yashar'el (Israel) obeyed him* (1 Chronicles 29:23). The seat is Yahuah's own; the king reigns FOR him, never in his own right.
cards.s_text: Blessed be Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which delighted in you to set you on his throne, to be king for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): because your Elohim (God) loved Yashar'el (Israel), to establish them for ever, therefore made he you king over them, to do judgment and justice.
cards.t_text: Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahuah (LORD) as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Yashar'el (Israel) obeyed him.

cards.note: The rent garment was the spoken word: *And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). Rehoboam's hardness is not random folly but the hinge on which *Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word* (10:15) — judgment on Solomon's idolatry made history.
cards.s_text: So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of Elohim (God), that Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
cards.t_text: And he said to Jeroboam, Take you ten pieces: for thus says Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to you:

cards.note: The houses walk home together: *In those days the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers* (Jeremiah 3:18). The breach of 10:19 — Israel torn from Judah — is reversed as the northern house comes back out of the land of the north to walk beside the south.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day.
cards.t_text: In those days the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north to the land that I have given for an inheritance unto your fathers.

cards.note: The two houses gather under one head: *Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel* (Hosea 1:11). The rebellion *against the house of David* (10:19) is undone when both houses choose one head again — never one replacing the other, both reclaimed.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day.
cards.t_text: Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

cards.note: The reunion is total and final: *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all* (Ezekiel 37:22). The two kingdoms born in 2 Chronicles 10 are the very two that *shall be no more two* — the split real history, the gathering the promise.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day.
cards.t_text: And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:

cards.note: The division is the wound the prophets promise to heal: *Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Yahudah (Judah), and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand* (Ezekiel 37:19). *Yashar'el rebelled against the house of David unto this day* (10:19) is the very breach — two sticks — that Yahuah swears to rejoin.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day.
cards.t_text: Say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) his fellows, and will put them with him, even with the stick of Yahudah (Judah), and make them one stick, and they shall be one in my hand.

cards.note: One tribe is kept, and the reason is David: *Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake, and for Jerusalem's sake which I have chosen* (1 Kings 11:13). That *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that dwelt in the cities of Yahudah (Judah), Rehoboam reigned over them* (10:17) is the southern house of Yahudah preserved — the lamp of David not put out even as the kingdom splits.
cards.s_text: But as for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that dwelt in the cities of Yahudah (Judah), Rehoboam reigned over them.
cards.t_text: Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to your son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.

cards.note: The number was fixed by prophecy before it happened: *Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). When *all Yashar'el* turns from David's son, it is the ten torn pieces of Ahijah's rent garment taking flesh — the northern house of Israel/Ephraim breaking away.
cards.s_text: And when all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel): and now, David, see to your own house. So all Yashar'el (Israel) went to their tents.
cards.t_text: And he said to Jeroboam, Take you ten pieces: for thus says Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to you:

cards.note: The parallel in 1 Kings rings the same rupture word for word: *So when all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel): now see to thine own house, David. So Yashar'el (Israel) departed unto their tents* (1 Kings 12:16). The Chronicler's *every man to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel)* is the secession cry of the ten northern tribes from the house of David — the historical wound that makes Yahuah's people two.
cards.s_text: And when all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel): and now, David, see to your own house. So all Yashar'el (Israel) went to their tents.
cards.t_text: So when all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king hearkened not unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel): now see to your own house, David. So Yashar'el (Israel) departed unto their tents.

cards.note: *Yet I have left me seven thousand in Yashar'el (Israel), all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him* (1 Kings 19:18). When all the north seemed lost to the calf-cult, Yahuah preserves a remnant who would not bow to the counterfeit — the same kind as those who here *set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 11:16). The faithful are never wholly swept away with the system.
cards.s_text: And after them out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) such as set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers.
cards.t_text: Yet I have left me seven thousand in Yashar'el (Israel), all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which has not kissed him.

cards.note: *Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:11). The same movement runs again under Hezekiah — the northern tribes' faithful few coming south to Jerusalem, just as here *out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) such as set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came to Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 11:16). Across the two-house divide a heart-remnant always turns toward the house of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: And after them out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) such as set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem.

cards.note: *They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (Exodus 32:8). Jeroboam's *calves which he had made* (2 Chronicles 11:15) repeat the wilderness sin word for word — the same molten calf, the same boast *these be thy gods*. The counterfeit is ancient; the LORD names it idolatry from Sinai onward.
cards.s_text: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.
cards.t_text: They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be your gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which have brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi* (1 Kings 12:31). This is why *the priests and the Levites that were in all Yashar'el (Israel) resorted to him* (2 Chronicles 11:13) — Jeroboam *had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto Yahuah* (2 Chronicles 11:14) and *ordained him priests for the high places* (11:15). The true priesthood is displaced by a manufactured one.
cards.s_text: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.
cards.t_text: And he made an house of high places, and made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.

cards.note: *Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28). Here is *the calves which he had made* (2 Chronicles 11:15) — Jeroboam's counterfeit, set up precisely so the people need not go up to the house Yahuah chose. The system is built to keep hearts from Jerusalem; the people are the prey of it.
cards.s_text: And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made.
cards.t_text: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold your gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren* (Genesis 13:8). The patriarch refuses strife on the ground of kinship — *for we be brethren* — the very ground on which Shemaiah forbids Yahudah to fight Yashar'el: *Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren* (2 Chronicles 11:4). The two houses divided remain one blood, to be regathered, never to be slaughtered as enemies.
cards.s_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), You shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of Yahuah (LORD), and returned from going against Jeroboam.
cards.t_text: And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray you, between me and you, and between my herdmen and your herdmen; for we be brethren.

cards.note: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel): return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of Yahuah (LORD), and returned to depart, according to the word of Yahuah (LORD)* (1 Kings 12:24). The parallel record gives the same word Shemaiah carried here — *for this thing is done of me* (2 Chronicles 11:4). The division of the kingdom is not rebellion overpowering Yahuah but Yahuah's own ordering; and the two houses are *your brethren*, not to make war one upon the other.
cards.s_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), You shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of Yahuah (LORD), and returned from going against Jeroboam.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), You shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel): return every man to his house; for this thing is from me. They hearkened therefore to the word of Yahuah (LORD), and returned to depart, according to the word of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: The verdict on Rehoboam is given as a diagnosis of the heart, and its exact inverse is the praise of Ezra: *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments* (Ezra 7:10). Rehoboam *did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek Yahuah* (2 Chronicles 12:14) — the prepared heart seeks the Torah and does it; the unprepared heart is the root of the evil.
cards.s_text: And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.

cards.note: The principle that governs Yahuah's response to the humbled king is stated plainly in the apostolic witness: *But he giveth more grace. Wherefore he saith, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6). The strengthened, proud Rehoboam was resisted by Shishak; the moment *the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous* (2 Chronicles 12:6) grace is given — the same Yahuah, the same law of the proud and the humble.
cards.s_text: Whereupon the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous.
cards.t_text: But he gives more grace. Wherefore he says, Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but gives grace unto the humble.

cards.note: Solomon had been given the covenant formula at the dedication of the house: *If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land* (2 Chronicles 7:14). Rehoboam's court runs the formula to the letter — *the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous* (2 Chronicles 12:6) — and Yahuah answers exactly as promised, with partial healing rather than destruction.
cards.s_text: Whereupon the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous.
cards.t_text: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

cards.note: The mechanism Moses gave: *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage* (Deuteronomy 8:14). The lifted-up heart of the full man is exactly Rehoboam, who *had strengthened himself* and then *forsook the law of Yahuah, and all Yashar'el (Israel) with him* (2 Chronicles 12:1) — and his judgment fittingly comes by the hand of Egypt, the house of bondage he forgot he was redeemed from.
cards.s_text: And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of Yahuah (LORD), and all Yashar'el (Israel) with him.
cards.t_text: Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;

cards.note: *And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom* (2 Samuel 7:12). Abijah's charge, *Ought ye not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever* (2 Chronicles 13:5), reaches back to the very oath Nathan carried — the kingdom is not Abijah's achievement but Yahuah's sworn settlement upon David's seed.
cards.s_text: Ought you not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
cards.t_text: And when your days be fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, which shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.

cards.note: *Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Sirach 47:11). The second-Temple sage remembers David's grant exactly as Abijah does — *a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory... for ever* — the same perpetual Davidic settlement Abijah calls *a covenant of salt*.
cards.s_text: Ought you not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?
cards.t_text: Yahuah (God) took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28). Abijah names the very system Jeroboam built — *there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods* (2 Chronicles 13:8); the northern shrine is a counterfeit erected to keep the people from Jerusalem.
cards.s_text: And now you think to withstand the kingdom of Yahuah (LORD) in the hand of the sons of David; and you be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.
cards.t_text: Whereupon the king took counsel, and made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold your gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (Exodus 32:4). Jeroboam's *golden calves* are no new sin but the wilderness apostasy revived — the identical lie, *thy gods, O Israel* — set up again as a state religion.
cards.s_text: And now you think to withstand the kingdom of Yahuah (LORD) in the hand of the sons of David; and you be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods.
cards.t_text: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be your gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought you up out of the land of Egypt.

cards.note: *I come to thee in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)... that all the earth may know that there is a Elohim (God) in Yashar'el (Israel)... for the battle is the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 17:45-47). Abijah stands in David's own confidence: when *Elohim himself is with us for our captain* (2 Chronicles 13:12), the contest is not Judah against Israel but men *fighting against Yahuah Elohim of your fathers* — and against Him *ye shall not prosper*.
cards.s_text: And, behold, Elohim (God) himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Yashar'el (Israel), fight you not against Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of your fathers; for you shall not prosper.
cards.t_text: Then said David to the Philistine, You come to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to you in the name of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), the Elohim (God) of the armies of Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have defied.

cards.note: His father Abijah won the same way one chapter before: *Thus the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were brought under at that time, and the children of Yahudah (Judah) prevailed, because they relied upon Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers* (2 Chronicles 13:18). Yahudah prevails not by numbers but by reliance; Asa's *we rest on thee* (14:11) is the same faith that gave his father victory.
cards.s_text: And Asa cried unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and said, Yahuah (LORD), it is nothing with you to help, whether with many, or with them that have no power: help us, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God); for we rest on you, and in your name we go against this multitude. O Yahuah (LORD), you are our Elohim (God); let not man prevail against you.
cards.t_text: Thus the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were brought under at that time, and the children of Yahudah (Judah) prevailed, because they relied upon Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers.

cards.note: The Torah names exactly what Asa requires of Yahudah: *And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart and with all thy soul* (Deuteronomy 10:12). To *seek Yahuah... and to do the law and the commandment* (14:4) is this requirement kept — seeking and doing the Torah are one act, never opposed.
cards.s_text: And commanded Yahudah (Judah) to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.
cards.t_text: And now, Yashar'el (Israel), what does Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of you, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all your heart and with all your soul,

cards.note: *For the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim* (Hosea 3:4). Hosea's catalogue of absence matches Azariah's — *without the true Elohim (God), and without a teaching priest, and without law* (2 Chronicles 15:3). The long season of being stripped of true worship is the prophetic shape of the northern house's exile, the desolation that precedes the return.
cards.s_text: Now for a long season Yashar'el (Israel) has been without the true Elohim (God), and without a teaching priest, and without law.
cards.t_text: For the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim:

cards.note: *Afterward shall the children of Yashar'el (Israel) return, and seek Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and David their king; and shall fear Yahuah (LORD) and his goodness in the latter days* (Hosea 3:5). After the stripping comes the seeking, and on the seeking comes the finding. *But when they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and sought him, he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:4) is the very pattern Hosea sets for the latter days — return, seek, and be found.
cards.s_text: But when they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and sought him, he was found of them.
cards.t_text: Afterward shall the children of Yashar'el (Israel) return, and seek Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God), and David their king; and shall fear Yahuah (LORD) and his goodness in the latter days.

cards.note: *And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease* (2 Kings 1:2). The northern king in his sickness sends past Yahuah to Baal-zebub — and Asa in his sickness does the southern version of the same sin: *in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12). The fault is never the means consulted but the One bypassed; the angel of Yahuah answers Ahaziah, *Is it not because there is not a Elohim (God) in Yashar'el (Israel), that ye go to enquire?* (2 Kings 1:3).
cards.s_text: And Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians.
cards.t_text: And Ahaziah fell down through a lattice in his upper chamber that was in Samaria, and was sick: and he sent messengers, and said unto them, Go, enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron whether I shall recover of this disease.

cards.note: *Ye shall walk in all the ways which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you, that ye may live, and that it may be well with you, and that ye may prolong your days in the land which ye shall possess.* (Deuteronomy 5:33) Of Jehoshaphat it is written that he *sought to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 17:4) — the king does exactly what the Torah charged: he walks in all the ways Yahuah commanded, and the promised *that ye may live... and prolong your days* is answered in his stablished kingdom and abundance.
cards.s_text: But sought to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: You shall walk in all the ways which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) has commanded you, that you may live, and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which you shall possess.

cards.note: *Ye shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you: ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.* (Deuteronomy 5:32) Jehoshaphat *walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 17:4) — he neither turned to the apostate north nor *unto Baalim* (17:3), the very turning-aside the Torah forbids.
cards.s_text: But sought to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: You shall observe to do therefore as Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) has commanded you: you shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left.

cards.note: *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) thy law: they shall put incense before thee, and whole burnt sacrifice upon thine altar.* (Deuteronomy 33:10) The Levites Jehoshaphat sent, who *taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them* (2 Chronicles 17:9), are doing the very office Moses blessed Levi with — *they shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el thy law*.
cards.s_text: And they taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yahudah (Judah), and taught the people.
cards.t_text: They shall teach Jacob your judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) your law: they shall put incense before you, and whole burnt sacrifice upon your altar.

cards.note: *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.* (Ezra 7:10) The threefold order — seek, do, teach — that marks Ezra is exactly Jehoshaphat's pattern: he first *sought to Yahuah Elohim* (17:4), then *sent to his princes... to teach in the cities of Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 17:7). The Torah is taught, never set aside.
cards.s_text: Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Ben-hail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Yahudah (Judah).
cards.t_text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.

cards.note: *He gave to him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws.* (Ecclesiasticus 45:17) Ben Sira sets the teaching of the law at the heart of the priestly grant to Aaron — *that he should teach Jacob the testimonies* — the very office the Levites and priests of Jehoshaphat carry when they *had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them* (2 Chronicles 17:9).
cards.s_text: And they taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yahudah (Judah), and taught the people.
cards.t_text: He gave to him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws.

cards.note: *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* (2 Corinthians 6:14). Jehoshaphat the good king of Yahudah (Judah) *joined affinity with Ahab* (2 Chronicles 18:1), the wicked king of Yashar'el (Israel) — the very yoke Sha'ul forbids. Affinity with the house of Baal would all but cost him his life and bring wrath upon him.
cards.s_text: Now Jehoshaphat had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab.
cards.t_text: Be you not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship has righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion has light with darkness?

cards.note: *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 21:30). *A certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness* (2 Chronicles 18:33): the arrow loosed at random finds the one seam in the armour, for no counsel of disguise can stand against the word Yahuah has spoken.
cards.s_text: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn your hand, that you may carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
cards.t_text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness* (1 Kings 22:34). The parallel records the same arrow at a venture that fulfils Micaiah's word against Ahab in 2 Chronicles 18:33 — the true prophet's word stands exactly, while the four hundred who promised victory are proven liars.
cards.s_text: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness: therefore he said to his chariot man, Turn your hand, that you may carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.
cards.t_text: And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness: wherefore he said unto the driver of his chariot, Turn your hand, and carry me out of the host; for I am wounded.

cards.note: *Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:19). The great Hallel rehearses Numbers 21 as an act of covenant mercy — Sihon, who *would not suffer Yashar'el (Israel) to pass through his border* (21:23), fell because Yahuah (LORD)'s mercy toward His people endures for ever.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into your hand, and all his people, and his land; and you shall do to him as you did unto Sihon king of the Amorites, which dwelt at Heshbon.
cards.t_text: Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endures for ever:

cards.note: *Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan* (Psalm 135:11). The defeat of Sihon (Numbers 21:21-31) and Og (21:33-35) is gathered into Yahuah (LORD)'s praise: He *smote great nations, and slew mighty kings.* The victory was not Yashar'el (Israel)'s sword alone but the Formed Son delivering the kings into their hand.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) sent messengers unto Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
cards.t_text: Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan:

cards.note: *But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14). The well of Numbers 21:16-17 that Yahuah (LORD) gave and Yashar'el (Israel) sang over — *Spring up, O well* — finds its fulness in the living water Yahusha (Jesus) gives, the well *springing up* within unto everlasting life.
cards.s_text: Then Yashar'el (Israel) sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing you unto it:
cards.t_text: But whosoever drinks of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.

cards.note: *He... brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Yashar'el (Israel) did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan* (2 Kings 18:4). The very serpent of brass that Moses *put... upon a pole* (Numbers 21:9) for healing became an idol when the people worshipped the sign instead of the One who appointed it. Hezekiah's reform guards the type: the lifted-up sign points beyond itself, and to bow to the bronze is to lose the healing it once carried.
cards.s_text: And Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole, and it came to pass, that if a serpent had bitten any man, when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived.
cards.t_text: He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Yashar'el (Israel) did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.

cards.note: *Neither let us tempt Messiah (Christ), as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents* (1 Corinthians 10:9). Sha'ul names this wilderness scene as the warning written for us, and he names WHO they tempted: Messiah (Christ) — the Formed Son who led Yashar'el (Israel) in the wilderness. The discouraged soul of the people at *the way* (Numbers 21:4) provoked the One who walked before them, and the fiery serpents answered.
cards.s_text: And they journeyed from mount Hor by the way of the Red sea, to compass the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was much discouraged because of the way.
cards.t_text: Neither let us tempt Messiah (Christ), as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents.

cards.note: *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee* (Genesis 12:3) is the verdict behind *Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed* (Numbers 22:12). The blessing on Yashar'el (Israel) is not Balaam's to revoke — it stands on the oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) said unto Balaam, You shall not go with them; you shall not curse the people: for they are blessed.
cards.t_text: And I will bless them that bless you, and curse him that curses you: and in you shall all families of the earth be blessed.

cards.note: *Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Elohim's (God's) elect? It is Elohim (God) that justifieth.* (Romans 8:33) The same defence the oracle raised — *Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 23:23) — Paul carries to its end: no curse, no charge, no accusation can stand against those Yahuah has justified.
cards.s_text: Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, neither is there any divination against Yashar'el (Israel): according to this time it shall be said of Jacob and of Yashar'el (Israel), What has Elohim (God) wrought!
cards.t_text: Who shall lay any thing to the charge of Elohim's (God’s) elect? It is Elohim (God) that justifies.

cards.note: *Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.* (Psalm 32:1) David sings the blessedness the oracle declares from the mountaintop — *He hath not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither hath he seen perverseness in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 23:21): the covered people whose sin Yahuah does not behold.
cards.s_text: He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, neither has he seen perverseness in Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) is with him, and the shout of a king is among them.
cards.t_text: Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered.

cards.note: *And also the Strength of Yashar'el (Israel) will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.* (1 Samuel 15:29) Samuel quotes the oracle back as covenant axiom — *Elohim (God) is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of Adam, that he should repent* (Numbers 23:19). What Yahuah has spoken stands; the word does not bend to men.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) is not a man, that he should lie; neither the son of Adam, that he should repent: has he said, and shall he not do it? or has he spoken, and shall he not make it good?
cards.t_text: And also the Strength of Yashar'el (Israel) will not lie nor repent: for he is not a man, that he should repent.

cards.note: *Yashar'el (Israel) then shall dwell in safety alone: the fountain of Jacob shall be upon a land of corn and wine; also his heavens shall drop down dew.* (Deuteronomy 33:28) Moses' deathbed blessing speaks the very word the hired seer is forced to confess — *lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations* (Numbers 23:9). The dwelling-alone is election and safety, not abandonment: the same Jacob, the same covenant separation.
cards.s_text: For from the top of the rocks I see him, and from the hills I behold him: lo, the people shall dwell alone, and shall not be reckoned among the nations.
cards.t_text: Yashar'el (Israel) then shall dwell in safety alone: the fountain of Jacob shall be upon a land of corn and wine; also his heavens shall drop down dew.

cards.note: *But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication* (Revelation 2:14). When *the spirit of Elohim (God) came upon him* (Numbers 24:2) Balaam could only bless; but the NT keeps the darker memory — when cursing failed, his COUNSEL seduced Yashar'el to sin. The blessing-word stands; the warning against the doctrine of Balaam stands with it.
cards.s_text: And Balaam lifted up his eyes, and he saw Yashar'el (Israel) abiding in his tents according to their tribes; and the spirit of Elohim (God) came upon him.
cards.t_text: But I have a few things against you, because you have there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.

cards.note: *Nevertheless Yahuah Eloheyka (the LORD thy God) would not hearken unto Balaam; but Yahuah Eloheyka (the LORD thy God) turned the curse into a blessing unto thee, because Yahuah Eloheyka (the LORD thy God) loved thee* (Deuteronomy 23:5). When *Balaam saw that it pleased Yahuah (LORD) to bless Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 24:1), he ceased seeking enchantments — Yahuah had *turned the curse into a blessing*. No hireling's divination can reverse the love-word spoken over the seed.
cards.s_text: And when Balaam saw that it pleased Yahuah (LORD) to bless Yashar'el (Israel), he went not, as at other times, to seek for enchantments, but he set his face toward the wilderness.
cards.t_text: Nevertheless Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) would not hearken unto Balaam; but Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) turned the curse into a blessing unto you, because Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) loved you.

cards.note: *Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass* (1 Samuel 15:3). The sentence Balaam pronounced — *his latter end shall be that he perish for ever* (Numbers 24:20) — became Saul's charge. By sparing Agag (whom Balaam foresaw the Yashar'el king would tower over, 24:7), Saul forfeited the kingdom: *thou hast rejected the word of Yahuah (LORD), and Yahuah (LORD) hath rejected thee from being king* (15:23).
cards.s_text: And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.
cards.t_text: Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.

cards.note: *For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation* (Exodus 17:16). Balaam's oracle — *Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever* (Numbers 24:20) — seals the war Yahuah swore at Rephidim. The perpetual war and the for-ever perishing are one sentence on Amalek, first to strike Yashar'el coming out of Egypt.
cards.s_text: And when he looked on Amalek, he took up his parable, and said, Amalek was the first of the nations; but his latter end shall be that he perish for ever.
cards.t_text: For he said, Because Yahuah (LORD) has sworn that Yahuah (LORD) will have war with Amalek from generation to generation.

cards.note: *Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel* (Psalm 2:9). The Sceptre of Yashar'el that *shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth* (Numbers 24:17) is the iron rod of the begotten King — *Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee* (Psalm 2:7). The Star wields the Sceptre against the rebel nations; the Messiah-King, begotten of a Father, rules them with a rod of iron.
cards.s_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
cards.t_text: You shall break them with a rod of iron; you shall dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

cards.note: *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be* (Genesis 49:10). The *Sceptre* that *shall rise out of Yashar'el* (Numbers 24:17) is the one Jacob laid on Yahudah — held until Shiloh, the gathering of the people. Two oracles, one King: the sceptre-tribe of Genesis and the Sceptre-Star of Numbers meet in the Messiah of Yahudah.
cards.s_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
cards.t_text: The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.

cards.note: *And I will give him the morning star* (Revelation 2:28), spoken to the overcomer who is given *power over the nations... and he shall rule them with a rod of iron... even as I received of my Father* (Revelation 2:26-27). The Star of Jacob and the Sceptre of Yashar'el (Numbers 24:17) are the Messiah's own inheritance — the morning star and the iron rod — received OF a Father: the Formed Son who reigns, who HAS a Father, not a co-equal person.
cards.s_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
cards.t_text: And I will give him the morning star.

cards.note: *I Yahusha (Jesus) have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star* (Revelation 22:16). Yahusha names himself the very thing Balaam saw rising — *a Star out of Jacob* (Numbers 24:17) — *the bright and morning star*, and *the root and the offspring of David*, the Sceptre of Yashar'el. The seer's distant glimpse (*I shall see him, but not now... but not nigh*) is the King who closes the canon declaring himself the Star.
cards.s_text: I shall see him, but not now: I shall behold him, but not nigh: there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.
cards.t_text: I Yahusha (Jesus) have sent my angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.

cards.note: *Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).* (Numbers 31:16). The wiles for which Yahuah says *Vex the Midianites... For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor* (Numbers 25:17-18) are unmasked in chapter 31: it was *the counsel of Balaam* — the prophet who could not curse, so he taught Moab and Midian to seduce.
cards.s_text: For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, which was slain in the day of the plague for Peor’s sake.
cards.t_text: Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.* (Psalm 106:30). Yahuah's own verdict is that *Phinehas... hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake* (Numbers 25:11); the Psalm names the act that turned it — he *stood up* and *executed judgment* in the gate of the plague.
cards.s_text: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in my jealousy.
cards.t_text: Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.

cards.note: *Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.* (Psalm 106:30). The Psalm echoes the Torah verbatim: Phinehas *thrust both of them through... So the plague was stayed from the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 25:8). One man's righteous judgment halts the wrath upon the whole house.
cards.s_text: And he went after the man of Yashar'el (Israel) into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Yashar'el (Israel), and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Then stood up Phinehas, and executed judgment: and so the plague was stayed.

cards.note: *I found Yashar'el (Israel) like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved.* (Hosea 9:10). Hosea makes Peor the archetype of the northern house's harlotry — the wilderness-bride who *separated themselves unto that shame*, the same turning the Torah records when *Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor* (Numbers 25:3).
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Yahuah (LORD) was kindled against Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: I found Yashar'el (Israel) like grapes in the wilderness; I saw your fathers as the firstripe in the fig tree at her first time: but they went to Baal-peor, and separated themselves unto that shame; and their abominations were according as they loved.

cards.note: *They joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.* (Psalm 106:28). The Psalm sings the history in the same words the Torah uses: *And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor* (Numbers 25:3). The gods of Moab are *the dead* — lifeless idols — and to eat their sacrifices is to be yoked to death.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Yahuah (LORD) was kindled against Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: They joined themselves also unto Baal-peor, and ate the sacrifices of the dead.

cards.note: *But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.* (Revelation 2:14). The Messiah names Peor by its author: it was Balaam's counsel (Numbers 31:16) that baited Yashar'el to *commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab* and *joined himself unto Baal-peor* (Numbers 25:1,3). The two sins are one — idol-feast and fornication welded together, the same stumblingblock the risen Son still indicts at Pergamos.
cards.s_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Yahuah (LORD) was kindled against Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: But I have a few things against you, because you have there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.

cards.note: *An unwise king destroys his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.* (Ecclesiasticus/Sirach 10:3) Jehoram, *risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword* (2 Chronicles 21:4): the foolish king turning the sword on his own house, destroying the very princes of Yashar'el (Israel) given them by Jehoshaphat. The wisdom-tradition names the pattern — a king without the fear of Yahuah (LORD) is a devourer of his own people.
cards.s_text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: An unwise king destroys his people; but through the prudence of them which are in authority the city shall be inhabited.

cards.note: *Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.* (Galatians 6:7) Jehoram *slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 21:4) — and the same chapter reaps it back: his own sons carried off and slain, *so that there was never a son left him, save Jehoahaz* (21:17). The murderous sowing returns to the murderer's own house.
cards.s_text: Now when Jehoram was risen up to the kingdom of his father, he strengthened himself, and slew all his brethren with the sword, and divers also of the princes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Be not deceived; Elohim (God) is not mocked: for whatsoever a man sows, that shall he also reap.

cards.note: *And he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of Yahuah (LORD).* (2 Kings 8:18) The Kings account names the identical corruption that Chronicles records — *for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife* (2 Chronicles 21:6): the marriage-alliance binding the house of David to the apostate house of Ahab, so that the way of the northern kings flowed south into Yahudah (Judah).
cards.s_text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), like as did the house of Ahab: for he had the daughter of Ahab to wife: and he wrought that which was evil in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: And he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), as did the house of Ahab: for the daughter of Ahab was his wife: and he did evil in the sight of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Deuteronomy 17:20). The king who keeps the testimony prolongs the throne; the priest Jehoiada places that very testimony in the boy-king's hands (2 Chronicles 23:11) so the line may endure.
cards.s_text: Then they brought out the king’s son, and put upon him the crown, and gave him the testimony, and made him king. And Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and said, Elohim (God) save the king.
cards.t_text: That his heart be not lifted up above his brethren, and that he turn not aside from the commandment, to the right hand, or to the left: to the end that he may prolong his days in his kingdom, he, and his children, in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Exodus 19:6). The kingdom of priests is what the covenant-renewal restores: the king and people bound again *that they should be the LORD'S people* (2 Chronicles 23:16), the holy nation reclaimed from Baal.
cards.s_text: And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD’S people.
cards.t_text: And you shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which you shall speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem* (Joshua 24:25). As Joshua bound the people by covenant and statute, so Jehoiada the priest now binds king and people *that they should be the LORD'S people* (2 Chronicles 23:16) — the recurring covenant-renewal of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD’S people.
cards.t_text: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem.

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33). The covenant formula — *they shall be my people* — runs from Sinai through Jehoiada's renewal (2 Chronicles 23:16) to the law written on the heart: the same covenant deepened, not abolished.
cards.s_text: And Jehoiada made a covenant between him, and between all the people, and between the king, that they should be the LORD’S people.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *And thou shalt take the atonement money of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and shalt appoint it for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation; that it may be a memorial unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before Yahuah (LORD), to make an atonement for your souls* (Exodus 30:16). Joash rebukes the Levites by name of this Torah: *the collection, according to the commandment of Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD)... for the tabernacle of witness* (2 Chronicles 24:6) — the half-shekel ransom laid on Yashar'el in the wilderness, the appointed support of Yahuah's house.
cards.s_text: And the king called for Jehoiada the chief, and said unto him, Why have you not required of the Levites to bring in out of Yahudah (Judah) and out of Jerusalem the collection, according to the commandment of Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD), and of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel), for the tabernacle of witness?
cards.t_text: And you shall take the atonement money of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall appoint it for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation; that it may be a memorial unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) before Yahuah (LORD), to make an atonement for your souls.

cards.note: *Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls* (Numbers 1:2). At Sinai the army was mustered the first time; now *Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), from twenty years old and upward... all that are able to go to war* (Numbers 26:2) re-musters the new generation in the plains of Moab — the same command spoken over a wholly different host.
cards.s_text: Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), from twenty years old and upward, throughout their fathers’ house, all that are able to go to war in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Take you the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their polls;

cards.note: *From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Yashar'el (Israel): thou and Aaron shall number them by their armies* (Numbers 1:3). The very measure of the first census — *from twenty years old and upward* — is repeated for the second (Numbers 26:2,4), but the men counted at Sinai are dead; this is the army of the sons who will cross over.
cards.s_text: Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), from twenty years old and upward, throughout their fathers’ house, all that are able to go to war in Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Yashar'el (Israel): you and Aaron shall number them by their armies.

cards.note: *And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) hearkened unto him, and did as Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses.* (Deuteronomy 34:9) The charge given here — *Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him* (Numbers 27:18) — bears its fruit: the spirit passes by Moses' hands, and Yashar'el follows the Spirit-filled successor.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Take you Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay your hand upon him;
cards.t_text: And Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) hearkened unto him, and did as Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither.* (Deuteronomy 34:4) Yahuah's command *Get thee up into this mount Abarim, and see the land which I have given unto the children of Yashar'el* (Numbers 27:12) is the seeing-only; the land sworn to the fathers is given to the *seed*, but Moses may not cross.
cards.s_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Get you up into this mount Abarim, and see the land which I have given unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto your seed: I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you shall not go over thither.

cards.note: *So Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of Yahuah (LORD).* (Deuteronomy 34:5) The sentence given here — *when thou hast seen it, thou also shalt be gathered unto thy people* (Numbers 27:13) — is carried out on Nebo: Moses sees the land, and dies *according to the word of Yahuah*, the servant who could not himself bring Yashar'el in.
cards.s_text: And when you have seen it, you also shall be gathered unto your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered.
cards.t_text: So Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.* (Joshua 17:3) What Yahuah promised — *thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren* (Numbers 27:7) — is paid out when Yashar'el enters the land: the daughters who loved the land are remembered by name and receive it.
cards.s_text: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: you shall surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and you shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.
cards.t_text: But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

cards.note: *Now this is that which thou shalt offer upon the altar; two lambs of the first year day by day continually.* (Exodus 29:38) — Numbers' charge *It is a continual burnt offering, which was ordained in mount Sinai for a sweet savour* (Numbers 28:6) re-issues the very ordinance Yahuah gave at the altar of the tabernacle: the unbroken morning-and-evening lamb that frames every day of Yashar'el (Israel) in worship.
cards.s_text: It is a continual burnt offering, which was ordained in mount Sinai for a sweet savour, a sacrifice made by fire unto Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Now this is that which you shall offer upon the altar; two lambs of the first year day by day continually.

cards.note: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD).* (Leviticus 23:34). The feast Numbers 29:12 opens: *on the fifteenth day of the seventh month... ye shall keep a feast unto Yahuah (LORD) seven days* — the same Sukkot, the seven days whose decreasing bullocks (thirteen down to seven) Numbers 29:13-34 enumerates, with the eighth-day solemn assembly.
cards.s_text: And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have an holy convocation; you shall do no servile work, and you shall keep a feast unto Yahuah (LORD) seven days:
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). The trumpet of the seventh-month feast — *a day of blowing the trumpets* (Numbers 29:1) — is the same great sound at which the elect of both houses are gathered from the four winds, the prophetic regathering of scattered Yashar'el.
cards.s_text: And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have an holy convocation; you shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.
cards.t_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.

cards.note: *Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day. For this was a statute for Yashar'el (Israel), and a law of the Elohim (God) of Jacob.* (Psalm 81:3-4).
