The psalm sings the trumpet-blast Numbers 29:1 ordains — *a day of blowing the trumpets* — as *a statute for Yashar'el (Israel)*, the appointed-time calendar of Yahuah, not an arbitrary custom.
cards.s_text: And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have an holy convocation; you shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.
cards.t_text: Blow the trumpet at the dark new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day.

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses, saying, Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.* (Leviticus 23:24-25). The appointed-time decree that Numbers 29 supplies the offerings for: *In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, ye shall have an holy convocation... it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you* (Numbers 29:1). The same Feast of Trumpets, the same Yahuah (LORD) commanding.
cards.s_text: And in the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have an holy convocation; you shall do no servile work: it is a day of blowing the trumpets unto you.
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall you have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, an holy convocation.

cards.note: *And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Yahuah (LORD) was kindled against Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 25:3). The command *Avenge the children of Yashar'el (Israel) of the Midianites* (Numbers 31:2) reaches back to Baal-peor — the seduction-system that *kindled* Yahuah's anger and brought the plague. The war is not ethnic conquest but the dismantling of the apparatus that drew Yashar'el (Israel) into idolatry; the victims of the snare are avenged, the system judged.
cards.s_text: Avenge the children of Yashar'el (Israel) of the Midianites: afterward shall you be gathered unto your people.
cards.t_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) joined himself unto Baal-peor: and the anger of Yahuah (LORD) was kindled against Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core* (Jude 1:11). Jude pronounces the *Woe* on those who *ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward* — the hireling diviner whose *counsel* (Numbers 31:16) led Yashar'el (Israel) into the plague at Peor. The error is named alongside Cain and Korah as a way that *perished*; Balaam's own fall by the sword (Numbers 31:8) is the seal upon it.
cards.s_text: Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

cards.note: *Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness* (2 Peter 2:15). Peter brands the false teachers by Balaam's name — they walk *the way of Balaam*, the diviner who *loved the wages of unrighteousness*. It is the same greed-driven counsel that drove Yashar'el (Israel) into trespass *through the counsel of Balaam* (Numbers 31:16): doctrine sold for reward, leading the people into the snare.
cards.s_text: Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: Which have forsaken the right way, and are gone astray, following the way of Balaam the son of Bosor, who loved the wages of unrighteousness;

cards.note: *But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication* (Revelation 2:14). The Messiah names *the doctrine of Balaam* as a living danger in the assemblies — the very *counsel of Balaam* of Numbers 31:16, the teaching that mixes the table of idols with the body, fornication with worship. What Numbers slew with the sword, Revelation exposes again in Pergamos: the stumblingblock is recurring, and judged.
cards.s_text: Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: But I have a few things against you, because you have there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication.

cards.note: *And Yashar'el (Israel) abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab* (Numbers 25:1). This is *the matter of Peor* Moses names — *Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor* (Numbers 31:16). The seduction at Shittim was no accident of lust; it was Balaam's engineered counsel, fornication wielded as a weapon to draw Yashar'el (Israel) into idolatry and so onto Yahuah's judgment.
cards.s_text: Behold, these caused the children of Yashar'el (Israel), through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against Yahuah (LORD) in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.t_text: And Yashar'el (Israel) abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.

cards.note: *Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Yashar'el (Israel) slay with the sword among them that were slain by them* (Joshua 13:22). The later record names what Numbers states plainly — *Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword* (Numbers 31:8). He is the *soothsayer*, the hired diviner of Numbers 22–24 whose curse Yahuah turned to blessing; here the man who could not curse Yashar'el (Israel) outright, and so taught the snare instead, falls by the very people he tried to ruin.
cards.s_text: And they slew the kings of Midian, beside the rest of them that were slain; namely, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, five kings of Midian: Balaam also the son of Beor they slew with the sword.
cards.t_text: Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Yashar'el (Israel) slay with the sword among them that were slain by them.

cards.note: *And now Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath given rest unto your brethren, as he promised them: therefore now return ye, and get you unto your tents, and unto the land of your possession.* (Joshua 22:4). Their vow was *we will not return unto our houses, until the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have inherited every man his inheritance* (Numbers 32:18). Only when every man's inheritance is secured does Joshua release them home — the burden carried with the brethren until all have rest.
cards.s_text: We will not return unto our houses, until the children of Yashar'el (Israel) have inherited every man his inheritance.
cards.t_text: And now Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) has given rest unto your brethren, as he promised them: therefore now return you, and get you unto your tents, and unto the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of Yahuah (LORD) gave you on the other side Jordan.

cards.note: *Your wives, your little ones, and your cattle, shall remain in the land which Moses gave you on this side Jordan; but ye shall pass before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valour, and help them.* (Joshua 1:14). Reuben and Gad's pledge — *we ourselves will go ready armed before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), until we have brought them unto their place* (Numbers 32:17) — is held to the letter by Joshua a generation later: the eastern tribes cross armed at the head of the host, refusing rest while their brethren have none.
cards.s_text: But we ourselves will go ready armed before the children of Yashar'el (Israel), until we have brought them unto their place: and our little ones shall dwell in the fenced cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
cards.t_text: Your wives, your little ones, and your cattle, shall remain in the land which Moses gave you on this side Jordan; but you shall pass before your brethren armed, all the mighty men of valour, and help them;

cards.note: *Only rebel not ye against Yahuah (LORD), neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and Yahuah (LORD) is with us: fear them not.* (Numbers 14:9). Moses charges Reuben and Gad with the very sin of the first generation — *wherefore discourage ye the heart of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from going over into the land which Yahuah (LORD) hath given them?* (Numbers 32:7). At Kadesh the call was the same: do not rebel, do not fear, for Yahuah is with you to bring you in.
cards.s_text: And wherefore discourage you the heart of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from going over into the land which Yahuah (LORD) has given them?
cards.t_text: Only rebel not you against Yahuah (LORD), neither fear you the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and Yahuah (LORD) is with us: fear them not.

cards.note: *But ye shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves* (Exodus 34:13). The charge given at Sinai is repeated here at the threshold of the land — *destroy all their pictures, and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places* (Numbers 33:52). The same three blows fall: altars, images, groves. From the mountain to the plains of Moab the instruction has not changed; the high places of the land must be plucked down lest Yashar'el (Israel) be ensnared.
cards.s_text: Then you shall drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you, and destroy all their pictures, and destroy all their molten images, and quite pluck down all their high places:
cards.t_text: But you shall destroy their altars, break their images, and cut down their groves:

cards.note: *And Yahuah (LORD) hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Yashar'el (Israel): and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went out with an high hand* (Exodus 14:8). The phrase Numbers stamps on the departure — *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians* (Numbers 33:3) — is the very phrase of the sea-account. Not slaves slinking away but a delivered nation marching out in open triumph, *in the sight of all the Egyptians*, the high hand of Yahuah over them.
cards.s_text: And they departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month; on the morrow after the passover the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went out with an high hand in the sight of all the Egyptians.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued after the children of Yashar'el (Israel): and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went out with an high hand.

cards.note: *These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Yahuah (LORD), at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country* (Joshua 19:51). They whom *Yahuah (LORD) commanded to divide the inheritance unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the land of Canaan* (Numbers 34:29) finish the work at Shiloh — the appointed stewards complete the appointed division.
cards.s_text: These are they whom Yahuah (LORD) commanded to divide the inheritance unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the land of Canaan.
cards.t_text: These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), divided for an inheritance by lot in Shiloh before Yahuah (LORD), at the door of the tabernacle of the congregation. So they made an end of dividing the country.

cards.note: *And these are the countries which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), distributed for inheritance to them* (Joshua 14:1). The very men appointed in Numbers — *Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun* (Numbers 34:17) — are the men who carry out the division. The commission named here is the commission fulfilled there.
cards.s_text: These are the names of the men which shall divide the land unto you: Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun.
cards.t_text: And these are the countries which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, and Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), distributed for inheritance to them.

cards.note: *And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation* (Acts 17:26). The Yahuah who fixes Yashar'el's borders — *the land of Canaan with the coasts thereof* (Numbers 34:2) — is the same who appoints the bounds of every nation's habitation. The borders of the inheritance are not accident of conquest but the decree of the One who portions the earth.
cards.s_text: Command the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, When you come into the land of Canaan; (this is the land that shall fall unto you for an inheritance, even the land of Canaan with the coasts thereof:)
cards.t_text: And has made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and has determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;

cards.note: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This shall be the border, whereby ye shall inherit the land according to the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel): Joseph shall have two portions* (Ezekiel 47:13). The borders surveyed *with the coasts thereof round about* (Numbers 34:12) are re-drawn by the prophet for the restored land — the twelve tribes regathered, Joseph (the northern house) given a double portion. The same appointed inheritance, re-bounded for the two-house ingathering.
cards.s_text: And the border shall go down to Jordan, and the goings out of it shall be at the salt sea: this shall be your land with the coasts thereof round about.
cards.t_text: Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This shall be the border, whereby you shall inherit the land according to the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel): Joseph shall have two portions.

cards.note: *Be merciful, O Yahuah (LORD), unto thy people Yashar'el (Israel), whom thou hast redeemed, and lay not innocent blood unto thy people of Yashar'el's (Israel's) charge. And the blood shall be forgiven them.* (Deuteronomy 21:8) Because Yahuah (LORD) *dwell[s] among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 35:34), unsolved bloodshed must be lifted off the land by appointed rite — the elders cry for mercy that innocent blood not be charged to the people, *and the blood shall be forgiven them*: the same care to keep the land undefiled where Yahuah dwells.
cards.s_text: Defile not therefore the land which you shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I Yahuah (LORD) dwell among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Be merciful, O Yahuah (LORD), unto your people Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have redeemed, and lay not innocent blood unto your people of Yashar'el's (Israel’s) charge. And the blood shall be forgiven them.

cards.note: *Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man.* (Genesis 9:6) Why the land must not be defiled — *Defile not therefore the land which ye shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I Yahuah (LORD) dwell among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 35:34) — reaches back to the Noahic charge: man bears the image of Elohim (God), and Yahuah (LORD) dwelling in the midst will not abide blood spilled in his image-bearers' land.
cards.s_text: Defile not therefore the land which you shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I Yahuah (LORD) dwell among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of Elohim (God) made he man.

cards.note: *Speak to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:* (Joshua 20:2) The refuge commanded here — *These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them* (Numbers 35:15) — Joshua executes in the land, naming Kedesh, Shechem, Hebron, Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan: refuge for the covenant people and the sojourner alike, the word by the hand of Moses now planted in the cities.
cards.s_text: These six cities shall be a refuge, both for the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and for the stranger, and for the sojourner among them: that every one that kills any person unawares may flee thither.
cards.t_text: Speak to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Appoint out for you cities of refuge, whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses:

cards.note: *Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel).* (Genesis 49:7) Jacob's word over Levi was a curse of dispersion — yet here it is turned to blessing: *every one shall give of his cities unto the Levites according to his inheritance which he inheriteth* (Numbers 35:8). The tribe with no land-portion becomes the tribe dwelling in every tribe's cities; the scattering becomes priestly presence among all Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: And the cities which you shall give shall be of the possession of the children of Yashar'el (Israel): from them that have many you shall give many; but from them that have few you shall give few: every one shall give of his cities unto the Levites according to his inheritance which he inherits.
cards.t_text: Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were forty and eight cities with their suburbs.* (Joshua 21:41) What Yahuah commands here — *So all the cities which ye shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities; them shall ye give with their suburbs* (Numbers 35:7) — Joshua records done: the forty-eight cities scattered among the tribes, the priestly tribe present in every inheritance, holding no land-block of its own.
cards.s_text: So all the cities which you shall give to the Levites shall be forty and eight cities: them shall you give with their suburbs.
cards.t_text: All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were forty and eight cities with their suburbs.

cards.note: *These are the commandments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in mount Sinai.* (Leviticus 27:34) The twin colophon: Leviticus seals at Sinai, Numbers seals at the threshold of the land — *These are the commandments and the judgments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded by the hand of Moses... in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho* (Numbers 36:13); one continuous Torah, given through the one mediator.
cards.s_text: These are the commandments and the judgments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded by the hand of Moses unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in the plains of Moab by Jordan near Jericho.
cards.t_text: These are the commandments, which Yahuah (LORD) commanded Moses for the children of Yashar'el (Israel) in mount Sinai.

cards.note: *And Naboth said to Ahab, Yahuah (LORD) forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.* (1 Kings 21:3) Naboth keeps the very statute of Numbers 36 — that *every one of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers* (Numbers 36:7); he will not let his fathers' portion pass away, and dies a martyr to it.
cards.s_text: So shall not the inheritance of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
cards.t_text: And Naboth said to Ahab, Yahuah (LORD) forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto you.

cards.note: *The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: thou shalt surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father's brethren; and thou shalt cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.* (Numbers 27:7) The statute that granted the daughters their father's inheritance is here completed: *every one of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers* (Numbers 36:7) — the gift of chapter 27 guarded so it cannot drain away from its tribe.
cards.s_text: So shall not the inheritance of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) remove from tribe to tribe: for every one of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall keep himself to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
cards.t_text: The daughters of Zelophehad speak right: you shall surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brethren; and you shall cause the inheritance of their father to pass unto them.

cards.note: *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage* (Deuteronomy 8:14). Moses warned of this exact peril before Yashar'el (Israel) ever entered the land: full, built up, multiplied — *then thine heart be lifted up*. Uzziah is the warning come true: *when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction* (2 Chronicles 26:16). The strength Yahuah gave became the occasion to forget Yahuah; the very gift, ungratefully held, lifted the heart that should have bowed.
cards.s_text: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction: for he transgressed against Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God), and went into the temple of Yahuah (LORD) to burn incense upon the altar of incense.
cards.t_text: Then your heart be lifted up, and you forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought you forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage;

cards.note: *To be a memorial unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), that no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before Yahuah (LORD); that he be not as Korah, and as his company* (Numbers 16:40). The priests' rebuke to Uzziah — *It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron* (2 Chronicles 26:18) — is the brass-censer memorial enforced. Uzziah, a king and not of the seed of Aaron, does the very thing the memorial forbade, and stands in the company of Korah, who likewise seized the priesthood that was not his.
cards.s_text: And they withstood Uzziah the king, and said unto him, It appertaineth not unto you, Uzziah, to burn incense unto Yahuah (LORD), but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for you have trespassed; neither shall it be for your honour from Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God).
cards.t_text: To be a memorial unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), that no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before Yahuah (LORD); that he be not as Korah, and as his company: as Yahuah (LORD) said to him by the hand of Moses.

cards.note: *And Samuel spake unto all the house of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, If ye do return unto Yahuah (LORD) with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD), and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.* (1 Samuel 7:3). Samuel's charge — *prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD)* — is the same posture the chronicler praises in the king who *prepared his ways before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)* (2 Chronicles 27:6). The prepared heart precedes the deliverance.
cards.s_text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God).
cards.t_text: And Samuel spake unto all the house of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, If you do return unto Yahuah (LORD) with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD), and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

cards.note: *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.* (Ezra 7:10). Ezra shows what the prepared walk is FOR — to seek the Torah, to do it, to teach it. Jotham *prepared his ways before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)* (2 Chronicles 27:6); the same verb binds king and scribe, the ordered life set toward Yahuah's statutes.
cards.s_text: So Jotham became mighty, because he prepared his ways before Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God).
cards.t_text: For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments.

cards.note: *But he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), yea, and made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen, whom Yahuah (LORD) cast out from before the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Kings 16:3). The parallel reign-account confirms the verdict of 2 Chronicles 28:1 — Ahaz *did not that which was right in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), like David his father* — and names the depth of it: he walked not in David's way but in *the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel)*, the apostate northern pattern, even to passing his own son through the fire.
cards.s_text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem: but he did not that which was right in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), like David his father:
cards.t_text: But he walked in the way of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), yea, and made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen, whom Yahuah (LORD) cast out from before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Whosoever he be of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)... that giveth any of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones* (Leviticus 20:2). The abomination Ahaz commits in 2 Chronicles 28:3 — *burnt his children in the fire* — is a capital crime under the Torah; the king who should have stoned such a man instead does the deed himself.
cards.s_text: Moreover he burnt incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burnt his children in the fire, after the abominations of the heathen whom Yahuah (LORD) had cast out before the children of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Again, you shall say to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), Whosoever he be of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), or of the strangers that sojourn in Yashar'el (Israel), that gives any of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones.

cards.note: The shut porch and dark lamps of 2 Chronicles 29:7 — *Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* — are the same neglected house Haggai later rebukes: *Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Haggai 1:8). The house left waste must be raised again for Yahuah to be glorified in it.
cards.s_text: Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place unto the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Go up to the mountain, and bring wood, and build the house; and I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified, says Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *Yahuah (LORD) hath chosen you to stand before him, to serve him* (2 Chronicles 29:11) is taken up whole in Kepha's word to restored Yashar'el (Israel): *But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light* (1 Peter 2:9). The chosen ministers cleansed for service are the same people of Yahuah, gathered out and made to shew forth his praise.
cards.s_text: My sons, be not now negligent: for Yahuah (LORD) has chosen you to stand before him, to serve him, and that you should minister unto him, and burn incense.
cards.t_text: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that you should shew forth the praises of him who has called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:

cards.note: Hezekiah's resolve — *Now it is in mine heart to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that his fierce wrath may turn away from us* (2 Chronicles 29:10) — walks the path Asa cut before him: *And they entered into a covenant to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul* (2 Chronicles 15:12). The kings of Yahudah (Judah) turn away wrath not by sacrifice alone but by binding the people again to the covenant of their fathers.
cards.s_text: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
cards.t_text: And they entered into a covenant to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul;

cards.note: Asa's covenant carried the full weight of the covenant-people's seriousness: *That whosoever would not seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman* (2 Chronicles 15:13). Hezekiah's *covenant... that his fierce wrath may turn away from us* (2 Chronicles 29:10) renews that same total turning of the whole house back to Yahuah.
cards.s_text: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
cards.t_text: That whosoever would not seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman.

cards.note: The covenant-renewal that turns away wrath stands in the line that runs to Josiah: *And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD), to walk after Yahuah (LORD), and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book* (2 Kings 23:3). Hezekiah's heart *to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 29:10) is the same renewal — the Torah-covenant of the fathers taken up again, never a new covenant replacing it.
cards.s_text: Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that his fierce wrath may turn away from us.
cards.t_text: And the king stood by a pillar, and made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD), to walk after Yahuah (LORD), and to keep his commandments and his testimonies and his statutes with all their heart and all their soul, to perform the words of this covenant that were written in this book. And all the people stood to the covenant.

cards.note: The blood that *made reconciliation... to make an atonement for all Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 29:24) is the Day-of-Atonement promise: *For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that ye may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 16:30). The cleansed house and the cleansed people meet at the altar where blood makes all Yashar'el (Israel) clean.
cards.s_text: And the priests killed them, and they made reconciliation with their blood upon the altar, to make an atonement for all Yashar'el (Israel): for the king commanded that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: For on that day shall the priest make an atonement for you, to cleanse you, that you may be clean from all your sins before Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *So they killed the bullocks, and the priests received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar* (2 Chronicles 29:22) — the sprinkled blood is the law's unbroken testimony: *And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission* (Hebrews 9:22). The atonement *for all Yashar'el (Israel)* points forward to the blood of the Messiah, the substance every sin offering foreshadowed.
cards.s_text: So they killed the bullocks, and the priests received the blood, and sprinkled it on the altar: likewise, when they had killed the rams, they sprinkled the blood upon the altar: they killed also the lambs, and they sprinkled the blood upon the altar.
cards.t_text: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.

cards.note: *When the burnt offering began, the song of Yahuah (LORD) began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 29:27). The instruments are the very company of praise the Psalter commands: *Praise ye Yahuah (LORD). Praise Elohim (God) in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power* (Psalm 150:1) — with trumpet, psaltery, harp, and high sounding cymbals. The song of the house and the song of the Psalter are one.
cards.s_text: And Hezekiah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar. And when the burnt offering began, the song of Yahuah (LORD) began also with the trumpets, and with the instruments ordained by David king of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Praise you Yahuah (LORD). Praise Elohim (God) in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power.

cards.note: *And all the congregation worshipped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded* (2 Chronicles 29:28). The praise rising with the offering is the dwelling-place of Yahuah: *But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Psalm 22:3). Where his people sing his appointed song, there he is enthroned among them.
cards.s_text: And all the congregation worshipped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded: and all this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
cards.t_text: But you are holy, O you that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And thus shall ye eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and ye shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD'S passover.* (Exodus 12:11). Hezekiah's decree — *that they should come to the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 30:1) — is no new rite but the appointed feast of Exodus restored for the whole people. The Passover instituted at the exodus is the architecture; Hezekiah simply calls the houses back to it.
cards.s_text: And Hezekiah sent to all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and wrote letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem, to keep the passover unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And thus shall you eat it; with your loins girded, your shoes on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is the LORD’S passover.

cards.note: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Numbers 9:10). The king takes counsel *to keep the passover in the second month* (2 Chronicles 30:2) — not a deviation but the Torah's own provision for those unclean or afar to keep the feast a month late. Hezekiah keeps it *as it was written*.
cards.s_text: For the king had taken counsel, and his princes, and all the congregation in Jerusalem, to keep the passover in the second month.
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, If any man of you or of your posterity shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, yet he shall keep the passover unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And thou shalt rejoice in thy feast, thou, and thy son, and thy daughter, and thy manservant, and thy maidservant, and the Levite, the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within thy gates* (Deuteronomy 16:14). The decree goes *throughout all Yashar'el (Israel), from Beer-sheba even to Dan* (2 Chronicles 30:5) so that the whole people — every house and tribe — keep the feast Yahuah commanded; Hezekiah gathers them to the rejoicing Deuteronomy commands, *for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written*.
cards.s_text: So they established a decree to make proclamation throughout all Yashar'el (Israel), from Beer-sheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the passover unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) at Jerusalem: for they had not done it of a long time in such sort as it was written.
cards.t_text: And you shall rejoice in your feast, you, and your son, and your daughter, and your manservant, and your maidservant, and the Levite, the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, that are within your gates.

cards.note: *And shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul* (Deuteronomy 30:2). The posts carry the very word Moses foretold: *turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria* (2 Chronicles 30:6). The return from scattering, promised in the Torah, is here proclaimed to the northern remnant.
cards.s_text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and according to the commandment of the king, saying, You children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
cards.t_text: And shall return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shall obey his voice according to all that I command you this day, you and your children, with all your heart, and with all your soul;

cards.note: *O Yashar'el (Israel), return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); for thou hast fallen by thine iniquity* (Hosea 14:1). The fallen northern house is exactly whom the posts seek: *Ye children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 30:6). Hosea's summons to Ephraim and Hezekiah's invitation are the same gathering call.
cards.s_text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and according to the commandment of the king, saying, You children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
cards.t_text: O Yashar'el (Israel), return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God); for you have fallen by your iniquity.

cards.note: *Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, Return, thou backsliding Yashar'el (Israel), saith Yahuah (LORD); and I will not cause mine anger to fall upon you: for I am merciful, saith Yahuah (LORD), and I will not keep anger for ever* (Jeremiah 3:12). The cry is aimed *toward the north* — the scattered house — just as Hezekiah's posts pass *through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh even unto Zebulun* (2 Chronicles 30:10). Both promise mercy to the returning, *for Yahuah your Elohim is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if ye return unto him* (2 Chronicles 30:9).
cards.s_text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and according to the commandment of the king, saying, You children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
cards.t_text: Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, Return, you backsliding Yashar'el (Israel), says Yahuah (LORD); and I will not cause my anger to fall upon you: for I am merciful, says Yahuah (LORD), and I will not keep anger for ever.

cards.note: *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land* (Ezekiel 37:21). Hezekiah's Passover is the two-house gathering in miniature — Yahudah (Judah) in the south summoning Ephraim and Manasseh, the *remnant... escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria* (2 Chronicles 30:6), to the one house of Yahuah; the foretaste of the two sticks made one.
cards.s_text: So the posts went with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Yashar'el (Israel) and Yahudah (Judah), and according to the commandment of the king, saying, You children of Yashar'el (Israel), turn again unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Abraham, Isaac, and Yashar'el (Israel), and he will return to the remnant of you, that are escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria.
cards.t_text: And say unto them, Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:

cards.note: *And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) done so. And there was very great gladness* (Nehemiah 8:17). Both restorations of the feast crown the return to Yahuah with gladness unmatched in generations: *So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Yashar'el (Israel) there was not the like in Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:26).
cards.s_text: So there was great joy in Jerusalem: for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Yashar'el (Israel) there was not the like in Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: And all the congregation of them that were come again out of the captivity made booths, and sat under the booths: for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Yashar'el (Israel) done so. And there was very great gladness.

cards.note: *And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation* (Numbers 18:21). When Hezekiah's people *brought in abundance the firstfruits... and the tithe of all things* (2 Chronicles 31:5), they were not inventing a generosity-program but restoring the Torah's own provision: the tenth is the Levites' covenant inheritance because they have no land-portion, the appointed support of those who serve at the house of Yahuah (LORD).
cards.s_text: And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly.
cards.t_text: And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.

cards.note: *But the tithes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which they offer as an heave offering unto Yahuah (LORD), I have given to the Levites to inherit* (Numbers 18:24). Hezekiah commands the people *to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 31:4) — the very inheritance Yahuah assigned the Levites in the Torah, so the ministry can stand and the law be upheld.
cards.s_text: And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly.
cards.t_text: But the tithes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), which they offer as an heave offering unto Yahuah (LORD), I have given to the Levites to inherit: therefore I have said unto them, Among the children of Yashar'el (Israel) they shall have no inheritance.

cards.note: *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Isaiah 37:23) Where Chronicles records that Sennacherib *wrote also letters to rail on Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 32:17), Isaiah names what that railing was — blasphemy lifted against the Holy One Himself, not against an idol the work of men's hands.
cards.s_text: He wrote also letters to rail on Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and to speak against him, saying, As the gods of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people out of my hand, so shall not the Elohim (God) of Hezekiah deliver his people out of my hand.
cards.t_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *Whom hast thou reproached and blasphemed? and against whom hast thou exalted thy voice, and lifted up thine eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).* (2 Kings 19:22) The Kings account of the same siege answers the Assyrian's boast that *no god of any nation... was able to deliver* (2 Chronicles 32:15): the living Elohim is no carved no-god to be counted among them — the reproach falls on the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.s_text: He wrote also letters to rail on Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and to speak against him, saying, As the gods of the nations of other lands have not delivered their people out of my hand, so shall not the Elohim (God) of Hezekiah deliver his people out of my hand.
cards.t_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? and against whom have you exalted your voice, and lifted up your eyes on high? even against the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: The parallel record names the same provocations: 'For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Yashar'el (Israel); and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them' (2 Kings 21:3). Manasseh undoes his own father's reform and bows to the very abominations Yahuah cast the heathen out for — *he reared up altars for Baalim... and worshipped all the host of heaven* (33:3).
cards.s_text: For he built again the high places which Hezekiah his father had broken down, and he reared up altars for Baalim, and made groves, and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.
cards.t_text: For he built up again the high places which Hezekiah his father had destroyed; and he reared up altars for Baal, and made a grove, as did Ahab king of Yashar'el (Israel); and worshipped all the host of heaven, and served them.

cards.note: Passing the children through the fire was blood-guilt under Torah: 'Whosoever he be of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)... that giveth any of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death' (Leviticus 20:2). Manasseh *caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom* (33:6) — the very valley that became the figure of the fire of judgment.
cards.s_text: And he caused his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom: also he observed times, and used enchantments, and used witchcraft, and dealt with a familiar spirit, and with wizards: he wrought much evil in the sight of Yahuah (LORD), to provoke him to anger.
cards.t_text: Again, you shall say to the children of Yashar'el (Israel), Whosoever he be of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), or of the strangers that sojourn in Yashar'el (Israel), that gives any of his seed unto Molech; he shall surely be put to death: the people of the land shall stone him with stones.

cards.note: The character Joel preached is what Manasseh found: Yahuah is 'gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil' (Joel 2:13). The restored altar and the *commanded Yahudah (Judah) to serve Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (33:16) are the visible kindness of the One who let the worst king begin again.
cards.s_text: And he repaired the altar of Yahuah (LORD), and sacrificed thereon peace offerings and thank offerings, and commanded Yahudah (Judah) to serve Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.

cards.note: *And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel)* (Nehemiah 8:1). What Shaphan does before the king — *And Shaphan read it before the king* (2 Chronicles 34:18) — Ezra does before the whole people: the recovered book of the law of Moses read aloud. Both restorations turn on the public reading of the Word that had been laid aside.
cards.s_text: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, saying, Hilkiah the priest has given me a book. And Shaphan read it before the king.
cards.t_text: And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, saith Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people* (Jeremiah 31:33). The new covenant is not a new law but the same Torah written within — exactly what Josiah strives toward when he covenants *to keep his commandments... with all his heart, and with all his soul* (2 Chronicles 34:31). Jeremiah, who prophesied in Josiah's very days, points beyond outward reform to the law graven on the heart; the recovered Word is never abolished, but made inward.
cards.s_text: And the king stood in his place, and made a covenant before Yahuah (LORD), to walk after Yahuah (LORD), and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant which are written in this book.
cards.t_text: But this shall be the covenant that I will make with the house of Yashar'el (Israel); After those days, says Yahuah (LORD), I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts; and will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.

cards.note: *And ye shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall kill it in the evening.* (Exodus 12:6). Josiah's word — *they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month* (2 Chronicles 35:1) — keeps the Torah's appointed day exactly; the feast Yahuah ordained in Egypt is restored in Jerusalem without alteration.
cards.s_text: Moreover Josiah kept a passover unto Yahuah (LORD) in Jerusalem: and they killed the passover on the fourteenth day of the first month.
cards.t_text: And you shall keep it up until the fourteenth day of the same month: and the whole assembly of the congregation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall kill it in the evening.

cards.note: *Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Yashar'el (Israel), nor in all the days of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), nor of the kings of Yahudah (Judah);* (2 Kings 23:22). Both records crown Josiah's feast as unequalled: *there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet* (2 Chronicles 35:18) — the appointed time restored in a fullness not seen since the judges.
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: Surely there was not holden such a passover from the days of the judges that judged Yashar'el (Israel), nor in all the days of the kings of Yashar'el (Israel), nor of the kings of Yahudah (Judah);

cards.note: *And such a passover was not kept in Yashar'el (Israel) since the time of the prophet Samuel.* (1 Esdras 1:20). The restored witness agrees word for word with the chronicler: *there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet* (2 Chronicles 35:18) — the unrivalled feast remembered in both libraries.
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: And such a passover was not kept in Yashar'el (Israel) since the time of the prophet Samuel.

cards.note: *The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as musick at a banquet of wine.* (Ecclesiasticus 49:1). Ben Sira's praise of the fathers crowns Josiah's memory as sweet incense — the king of the great passover that *all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel)* could not match (2 Chronicles 35:18).
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary: it is sweet as honey in all mouths, and as musick at a banquet of wine.

cards.note: *Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us:* (1 Corinthians 5:7). Josiah's unequalled passover — *there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet* (2 Chronicles 35:18) — points forward to the Passover it foreshadows: the Messiah our Passover, the true lamb the feast was always testifying of.
cards.s_text: And there was no passover like to that kept in Yashar'el (Israel) from the days of Samuel the prophet; neither did all the kings of Yashar'el (Israel) keep such a passover as Josiah kept, and the priests, and the Levites, and all Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) that were present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
cards.t_text: Purge out therefore the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened. For even Messiah (Christ) our passover is sacrificed for us:

cards.note: *He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy* (Proverbs 29:1). The proverb is the chapter's epitaph: Zedekiah *stiffened his neck, and hardened his heart from turning unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 36:13), and so *the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) arose against his people, till there was no remedy* (2 Chronicles 36:16). The hardened neck, often reproved, brings the destruction *without remedy* the wisdom-word foretold.
cards.s_text: But they mocked the messengers of Elohim (God), and despised his words, and misused his prophets, until the wrath of Yahuah (LORD) arose against his people, till there was no remedy.
cards.t_text: He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.

cards.note: *Who is there among you of all his people? his Elohim (God) be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah), and build the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 1:3). The book of Chronicles ends on these very words — *Who is there among you of all his people? Yahuah Elohav (The LORD his God) be with him, and let him go up* (2 Chronicles 36:23). The last word of the Tanakh in the Hebrew order is the open door home: *let him go up*.
cards.s_text: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth has Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of heaven given me; and he has charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah). Who is there among you of all his people? Yahuah Elohav (The LORD his God) be with him, and let him go up.
cards.t_text: Who is there among you of all his people? his Elohim (God) be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah), and build the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), (he is the Elohim (God),) which is in Jerusalem.

cards.note: *For Jacob my servant's sake, and Yashar'el (Israel) mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me.* (Isaiah 45:4). Cyrus is wielded *for Jacob my servant's sake, and Yashar'el (Israel) mine elect* -- a pagan king surnamed before his birth, who *hath not known me*, yet who in Ezra 1:2 confesses *Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of heaven hath given me all the kingdoms*. The Formed Word names the unknowing instrument for the elect's sake.
cards.s_text: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, Yahuah Elohim (The LORD God) of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he has charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Yahudah (Judah).
cards.t_text: For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Yashar'el (Israel) my elect, I have even called you by your name: I have surnamed you, though you have not known me.

cards.note: *The children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought a willing offering unto Yahuah (LORD), every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all manner of work, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses.* (Exodus 35:29). When the chief of the fathers *offered freely for the house of Elohim (God) to set it up in his place* (Ezra 2:68), they walked the same path as their fathers at the tabernacle — the free-hearted gift for the house, *whose heart made them willing*. The pattern of the willing offering carries from Sinai to the second house.
cards.s_text: And some of the chief of the fathers, when they came to the house of Yahuah (LORD) which is at Jerusalem, offered freely for the house of Elohim (God) to set it up in his place:
cards.t_text: The children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought a willing offering unto Yahuah (LORD), every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all manner of work, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses.

cards.note: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). The remnant who *could not shew their father's house, and their seed, whether they were of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 2:59) point forward to the last reckoning, where the question is again whether a name is found written — *another book was opened, which is the book of life*. The register on earth foreshadows the register in heaven.
cards.s_text: And these were they which went up from Tel-melah, Tel-harsa, Cherub, Addan, and Immer: but they could not shew their father’s house, and their seed, whether they were of Yashar'el (Israel):
cards.t_text: And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.

cards.note: *And thou shalt put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron's heart, when he goeth in before Yahuah (LORD): and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) upon his heart before Yahuah (LORD) continually.* (Exodus 28:30). The Tirshatha defers the priests' case *till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim* (Ezra 2:63) — the very instrument of divine judgment Yahuah set in the breastplate, by which the answer of Elohim (God) is sought. The disputed lineage waits for the verdict of heaven.
cards.s_text: And the Tirshatha said unto them, that they should not eat of the most holy things, till there stood up a priest with Urim and with Thummim.
cards.t_text: And you shall put in the breastplate of judgment the Urim and the Thummim; and they shall be upon Aaron’s heart, when he goes in before Yahuah (LORD): and Aaron shall bear the judgment of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) upon his heart before Yahuah (LORD) continually.

cards.note: *And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls.* (Numbers 1:18). From the wilderness onward Yashar'el (Israel) was reckoned by the house of the fathers — the paternal bloodline declared and recorded. When the returning priests *sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found* (Ezra 2:62), it is this same standard they could not meet: the seed-line must be PROVEN, not merely claimed.
cards.s_text: These sought their register among those that were reckoned by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood.
cards.t_text: And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls.

cards.note: *An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in all places where I record my name I will come unto thee, and I will bless thee.* (Exodus 20:24). When the returned remnant *builded the altar of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses* (Ezra 3:2), they were resuming the very first command of worship given at Sinai — the altar where Yahuah records his name and comes to bless. The restoration begins not with novelty but with the Torah's own pattern.
cards.s_text: Then stood up Jeshua the son of Jozadak, and his brethren the priests, and Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, and his brethren, and builded the altar of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), to offer burnt offerings thereon, as it is written in the law of Moses the man of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: An altar of earth you shall make unto me, and shall sacrifice thereon your burnt offerings, and your peace offerings, your sheep, and your oxen: in all places where I record my name I will come unto you, and I will bless you.

cards.note: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 23:34). When the remnant *kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written* (Ezra 3:4), in *the seventh month* (Ezra 3:1,6), they were keeping the very feast of the very month Leviticus had fixed. The appointed time was not a relic abolished — it was the first festival the restored people observed.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *That your generations may know that I made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God)* (Leviticus 23:43). The feast the remnant kept *as it is written* (Ezra 3:4) is a memorial of the first exodus — and now a people brought up out of a second captivity in Babylon keep it again. Tabernacles binds the two deliverances into one testimony of the gathering God.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: That your generations may know that I made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).

cards.note: *And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles* (Deuteronomy 31:10). Moses had fixed Tabernacles as the feast for reading the law before all Yashar'el; so when the remnant *kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written* (Ezra 3:4), they were resuming the very festival appointed for the public hearing of the Torah — the restoration of the feast and the restoration of the word go together.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: And Moses commanded them, saying, At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles,

cards.note: *When all Yashar'el (Israel) is come to appear before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which he shall choose, thou shalt read this law before all Yashar'el (Israel) in their hearing* (Deuteronomy 31:11). The remnant gathered *as one man to Jerusalem* (Ezra 3:1) — *all Yashar'el* come to the chosen place — to keep Tabernacles *as it is written* (Ezra 3:4). The Torah's own appointment for the assembly of the whole people is fulfilled in the very pattern of the return.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: When all Yashar'el (Israel) is come to appear before Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) in the place which he shall choose, you shall read this law before all Yashar'el (Israel) in their hearing.

cards.note: *And they found written in the law which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded by Moses, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month* (Nehemiah 8:14). The same restoration generation keeps the same feast by the same standard: *as it is written* (Ezra 3:4). What Ezra 3 begins at the altar, Nehemiah 8 carries on at the reading of the law — the appointed times of Yahuah re-established in the land, found written and therefore kept.
cards.s_text: They kept also the feast of tabernacles, as it is written, and offered the daily burnt offerings by number, according to the custom, as the duty of every day required;
cards.t_text: And they found written in the law which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded by Moses, that the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month:

cards.note: *O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever* (1 Chronicles 16:34). This is the very song David appointed when the ark came up to Jerusalem; and when the foundation of the second temple is laid *after the ordinance of David king of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 3:10), the Levites sing *because he is good, for his mercy endureth for ever toward Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 3:11). The restoration takes up David's own refrain — the praise of the first temple sung over the foundation of the second.
cards.s_text: And they sang together by course in praising and giving thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); because he is good, for his mercy endures for ever toward Yashar'el (Israel). And all the people shouted with a great shout, when they praised Yahuah (LORD), because the foundation of the house of Yahuah (LORD) was laid.
cards.t_text: O give thanks unto Yahuah (LORD); for he is good; for his mercy endures for ever.

cards.note: *Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Yashar'el (Israel) now say* (Psalm 129:1). The hiring of counsellors *to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia* (Ezra 4:5) is one more chapter in the long affliction of Yashar'el (Israel) the Psalm sings — the people of promise opposed from the beginning.
cards.s_text: And hired counsellors against them, to frustrate their purpose, all the days of Cyrus king of Persia, even until the reign of Darius king of Persia.
cards.t_text: Many a time have they afflicted me from my youth, may Yashar'el (Israel) now say:

cards.note: *Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith Yahuah (Lord), and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you* (2 Corinthians 6:17). The call to come out and be separate is the same covenant fidelity that moved Zerubbabel and Jeshua to build *unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* alone (Ezra 4:3); separation here is for the sake of undivided worship, the boundary of the house, not the rejection of any people.
cards.s_text: But Zerubbabel, and Jeshua, and the rest of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), said unto them, You have nothing to do with us to build an house unto our Elohim (God); but we ourselves together will build unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), as king Cyrus the king of Persia has commanded us.
cards.t_text: Wherefore come out from among them, and be you separate, says Yahuah (Lord), and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you,

cards.note: *Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (Philippians 1:6). The pattern of Ezra 6:14 — *they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* — is the pattern Paul leans on: the work Yahuah begins, Yahuah finishes. The house begun under Cyrus and finished under Darius foreshadows the faithful Finisher who performs the good work he starts.
cards.s_text: And the elders of the Yahudim (Jews) builded, and they prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah the son of Iddo. And they builded, and finished it, according to the commandment of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and according to the commandment of Cyrus, and Darius, and Artaxerxes king of Persia.
cards.t_text: Being confident of this very thing, that he which has begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):

cards.note: *And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto Yahuah (LORD), two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) dedicated the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (1 Kings 8:63) The returned remnant keep *the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) with joy* (Ezra 6:16) — the second house dedicated as the first was. Smaller in scale but the same act: Yashar'el dedicating the house of Yahuah with offering.
cards.s_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel), the priests, and the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) with joy,
cards.t_text: And Solomon offered a sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offered unto Yahuah (LORD), two and twenty thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Yashar'el (Israel) dedicated the house of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty and two thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep: so the king and all the people dedicated the house of Elohim (God).* (2 Chronicles 7:5) At the second dedication they *offered... an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 6:17). The twelve-goat sin offering binds the dedication to all twelve tribes — the whole two-house people held in view at the restored altar.
cards.s_text: And offered at the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And king Solomon offered a sacrifice of twenty and two thousand oxen, and an hundred and twenty thousand sheep: so the king and all the people dedicated the house of Elohim (God).

cards.note: *Thus shalt thou separate the Levites from among the children of Yashar'el (Israel): and the Levites shall be mine.* (Numbers 8:14) At the dedication they *set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of Elohim (God)... as it is written in the book of Moses* (Ezra 6:18). The orders set here are the orders Moses received — the Torah-given Levitical service restored exactly as written, never set aside.
cards.s_text: And they set the priests in their divisions, and the Levites in their courses, for the service of Elohim (God), which is at Jerusalem; as it is written in the book of Moses.
cards.t_text: Thus shall you separate the Levites from among the children of Yashar'el (Israel): and the Levites shall be mine.

cards.note: *And to the dedication of the temple of Yahuah (God) they offered an hundred bullocks two hundred rams, four hundred lambs* (1 Esdras 7:7). The restored library preserves the same dedication, the same numbers: *an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats* (Ezra 6:17). The second-temple witness confirms the offering verse for verse.
cards.s_text: And offered at the dedication of this house of Elohim (God) an hundred bullocks, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs; and for a sin offering for all Yashar'el (Israel), twelve he goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And to the dedication of the temple of Yahuah (God) they offered an hundred bullocks two hundred rams, four hundred lambs;

cards.note: *And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised Yahuah (LORD) day by day* (2 Chronicles 30:21). Hezekiah's restored Passover is the pattern Ezra 6 repeats: *kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful* (Ezra 6:22). Each great covenant-renewal recovers the same feast with the same joy.
cards.s_text: And kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that were present at Jerusalem kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness: and the Levites and the priests praised Yahuah (LORD) day by day, singing with loud instruments unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: *And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God), for that he had turned the counsel of the king of Assyria toward them, to strengthen their hands in the works of Yahuah (God) of Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Esdras 7:14-15). The restored library's own account matches Ezra word for word: *kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them* (Ezra 6:22). Two witnesses to the joy of the restored feast.
cards.s_text: And kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days with joy: for Yahuah (LORD) had made them joyful, and turned the heart of the king of Assyria unto them, to strengthen their hands in the work of the house of Elohim (God), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And they kept the feast of unleavened bread seven days, making merry before Yahuah (God),

cards.note: *And all the people gathered themselves together as one man into the street that was before the water gate; and they spake unto Ezra the scribe to bring the book of the law of Moses, which Yahuah (LORD) had commanded to Yashar'el (Israel)* (Nehemiah 8:1). The man introduced here as *a ready scribe in the law of Moses* (Ezra 7:6) is the same Ezra the people summon to bring the Torah and read it before the congregation — the scribe's skill is not antiquarian but ministerial: the Torah carried out to be heard and done by the gathered people.
