The father-son word over Solomon reaches past the type to the greater Heir: *Thou art my Son... I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?* (Hebrews 1:5) — the chosen house-builder become the everlasting King.

threads.title: Thine Is the Kingdom, the Power, and the Glory — David's Great Doxology
threads.summary_md: This is the great ascription of the whole canon. *Blessed be thou, Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) our father, for ever and ever* (1 Chronicles 29:10), and then: *Thine, O Yahuah (LORD), is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O Yahuah (LORD), and thou art exalted as head above all* (1 Chronicles 29:11); *Both riches and honour come of thee... and in thine hand is power and might* (1 Chronicles 29:12); *Now therefore, our Elohim (God), we thank thee, and praise thy glorious name* (1 Chronicles 29:13). The Messiah sealed the disciples' prayer with these very words: *For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen* (Matthew 6:13). Heaven sings it back: *Thou art worthy, O Yahuah (Lord), to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things* (Revelation 4:11), and every creature cries *Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever* (Revelation 5:13). Paul ends his doxology the same way: *For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever* (Romans 11:36); and the apostolic blessing crowns *the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise Elohim (God)* with *honour and glory for ever and ever* (1 Timothy 1:17). David's own house already sang it: *Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations* (Psalm 145:13). Even in exile the captive prays it: *Blessed be Yahuah (God) that lives for ever, and blessed be his kingdom* (Tobit 13:1). All the greatness, the power, and the glory are Yahuah's — for ever and ever.

threads.title: The Throne of Yahuah: Solomon Sat as King Instead of David
threads.summary_md: The chronicler does not call it the throne of David or the throne of Israel — he calls it Yahuah's own: *Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahuah (LORD) as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Yashar'el (Israel) obeyed him* (1 Chronicles 29:23). David had named it so already: Yahuah *hath chosen Solomon my son to sit upon the throne of the kingdom of Yahuah (LORD) over Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Chronicles 28:5). The king sits only because Yahuah enthroned him: *Yet have I set my king upon my holy hill of Zion* (Psalm 2:6). The Davidic king is Yahuah's vicegerent, never his rival — and the throne is finally the inheritance of the greater Son: *He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) shall give unto him the throne of his father David* (Luke 1:32). Solomon prospered and passed; the true Heir does not: *And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end* (Luke 1:33). The throne of Yahuah that Solomon held is the seat the Formed Son holds without end.

threads.title: The censers made a sign — let no stranger come near
threads.summary_md: The very censers the rebels seized are not destroyed but hammered into a covering for the altar, a standing witness: *The censers of these sinners against their own souls, let them make them broad plates for a covering of the altar... and they shall be a sign unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 16:38). The judgment is fixed into the worship itself as a memorial: *that no stranger, which is not of the seed of Aaron, come near to offer incense before Yahuah (LORD); that he be not as Korah, and as his company* (Numbers 16:40). The lesson of the swallowed and the burned is bolted to the altar where Yashar'el (Israel) cannot forget it — the priesthood is Yahuah's gift to whom he chooses, and the uninvited who press in are warned in beaten brass.

threads.title: Aaron's Rod That Budded — the Chosen, Living Priesthood
threads.summary_md: Twelve rods, one per tribe, are laid up before the testimony, and Yahuah (LORD) declares the test: *the man's rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 17:5). On the morrow only one is alive — *the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds* (Numbers 17:8). The chosen priest is named not by man's claim but by LIFE out of a dead stick. This answers the very question of Korah's rebellion: *even him whom he hath chosen will he cause to come near unto him* (Numbers 16:5), while the presumptuous who seized the censer were devoured — *there came out a fire from Yahuah (LORD), and consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense* (Numbers 16:35). The budded rod is then enshrined in the ark itself: *wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant* (Hebrews 9:4). The branch that lived from death is the sign of the true and risen Priest after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).

threads.title: The Rod Kept for a Token Against the Rebels
threads.summary_md: The budded rod is not buried away but enshrined as a standing memorial: *Bring Aaron's rod again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels; and thou shalt quite take away their murmurings from me, that they die not* (Numbers 17:10). It is the twin of the other memorial drawn from the same rebellion — the censers of Korah's company, *let them make them broad plates for a covering of the altar... and they shall be a sign unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 16:38). Plated censers and a living branch, kept together before the ark, declare the one verdict: none may seize what Yahuah (LORD) has not given, and the chosen priesthood stands.

threads.title: Whosoever Cometh Near Shall Die — the Terror of Approach
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes in dread. The people cry, *Behold, we die, we perish, we all perish. Whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of Yahuah (LORD) shall die: shall we be consumed with dying?* (Numbers 17:12-13). This is the fear of drawing near to the Holy without a mediator. The answer comes at once in the priesthood ordained as a guard: *ye shall keep the charge of the sanctuary, and the charge of the altar: that there be no wrath any more upon the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 18:5), while *the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death* (Numbers 18:7) — the boundary is mercy, keeping the congregation alive. And the terror finds its full answer in the true Priest: *Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Yahusha (Jesus)* (Hebrews 10:19), so that those who once cried *we perish* may *draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience* (Hebrews 10:22). The way is opened, not the guard abolished.

threads.title: The priests' portion — a covenant of salt
threads.summary_md: Having no land, the priests are fed from the altar. Yahuah gives Aaron *the charge of mine heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)... by an ordinance for ever* (Numbers 18:8) — the most holy things, the firstfruits of *the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and of the wheat* (Numbers 18:12), the firstborn, *every thing devoted in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 18:14). The whole grant is then sealed: *it is a covenant of salt for ever before Yahuah (LORD) unto thee and to thy seed with thee* (Numbers 18:19). Salt was the sign of the unbreakable bond already commanded on every offering — *neither shalt thou suffer the salt of the covenant of thy Elohim (God) to be lacking from thy meat offering* (Leviticus 2:13) — and the same everlasting formula seals the Davidic throne: Yahuah *gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever... by a covenant of salt* (2 Chronicles 13:5). Priesthood and throne, both granted in salt, both gathered at last in the Formed Son. And the principle abides under the gospel: *they which minister about holy things live of the things of the temple... even so hath Yahuah (Lord) ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel* (1 Corinthians 9:13-14). The ministers still live of the altar they serve.

threads.title: I am thy part and thine inheritance
threads.summary_md: At the heart of the chapter is the grant that costs and gives everything: *Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Numbers 18:20). The Levite forfeits land and is given Yahuah himself. Moses restates it plainly — *Levi hath no part nor inheritance with his brethren; Yahuah (LORD) is his inheritance* (Deuteronomy 10:9) — and what was the priestly tribe's peculiar lot becomes the song of every worshipper who learns to want Yahuah more than land. The singer claims it: *Yahuah (LORD) is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup* (Psalm 16:5); Asaph claims it when flesh fails: *Elohim (God) is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever* (Psalm 73:26); the psalmist of the law joins it to obedience: *Thou art my portion, O Yahuah (LORD): I have said that I would keep thy words* (Psalm 119:57); and the mourner over the ruined land holds it when all else is lost: *Yahuah (LORD) is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him* (Lamentations 3:24). The inheritance was never the land — it was Yahuah.

threads.title: The tithe for the ministry
threads.summary_md: Because the Levites have no land, Yahuah assigns them the tithe as their portion: *I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Yashar'el (Israel) for an inheritance, for their service which they serve* (Numbers 18:21). The tithe was already declared holy to Yahuah — *all the tithe of the land... is the LORD'S: it is holy unto Yahuah (LORD)* (Leviticus 27:30), and *the tithe of the herd, or of the flock... the tenth shall be holy unto Yahuah* (Leviticus 27:32) — so Yahuah gives his own holy tenth to sustain the ministry. The Levites in turn render a tithe of the tithe to the priest: *ye shall offer up an heave offering of it for Yahuah (LORD), even a tenth part of the tithe* (Numbers 18:26). The returned remnant under Nehemiah bound themselves to keep exactly this: *the Levites shall bring up the tithe of the tithes unto the house of our Elohim (God)* (Nehemiah 10:38). And Hebrews names this very commandment — *the sons of Levi... have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law* (Hebrews 7:5) — only to show that even tithe-receiving Levi *payed tithes in Abraham* (Hebrews 7:9) to a higher priest: Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), whose order the Formed Son fills.

threads.title: Death defileth — the water of separation
threads.summary_md: Why was a water of purification needed at all? Because death is the deepest defilement in the Torah. *He that toucheth the dead body of any man shall be unclean seven days* (Numbers 19:11), and *whosoever toucheth the dead body of any man that is dead, and purifieth not himself, defileth the tabernacle of Yahuah (LORD); and that soul shall be cut off from Yashar'el (Israel): because the water of separation was not sprinkled upon him* (19:13). This is the same uncleanness that puts a man outside the dwelling of Yahuah: *put out of the camp every leper, and every one that hath an issue, and whosoever is defiled by the dead* (Numbers 5:2). And death's defilement is contagious — when Haggai presses the priests, *If one that is unclean by a dead body touch any of these, shall it be unclean? And the priests answered and said, It shall be unclean* (Haggai 2:13). Death spreads; what the dead touch becomes unclean, and what touches that is unclean in turn. The whole rite of the heifer exists because the wages of sin is death, and death corrupts everything it reaches — only the appointed water of separation, sprinkled, can break its hold.

threads.title: Defiled the sanctuary — cut off
threads.summary_md: The chapter closes with a solemn guard: *the man that shall be unclean, and shall not purify himself, that soul shall be cut off from among the congregation, because he hath defiled the sanctuary of Yahuah (LORD): the water of separation hath not been sprinkled upon him; he is unclean* (Numbers 19:20). The purification is no ritual nicety — to refuse it is to defile the holy dwelling itself, and *whatsoever the unclean person toucheth shall be unclean* (19:22). This is the same holiness-guard that runs through Leviticus: *thus shall ye separate the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from their uncleanness; that they die not in their uncleanness, when they defile my tabernacle that is among them* (Leviticus 15:31). Yahuah dwells in the midst of his people, and his sanctuary must be kept undefiled; uncleanness left unpurged threatens both the dwelling and the life of the one who carries it. The water of separation shields the tabernacle — and the people who live in its presence.

threads.title: Miriam died there — the wilderness generation's leaders pass
threads.summary_md: The chapter opens with a death and a burial: *Then came the children of Yashar'el (Israel), even the whole congregation, into the desert of Zin in the first month: and the people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there* (Numbers 20:1). The Miriam who is buried is the prophetess of the Red-sea deliverance — *And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances* (Exodus 15:20) — and one of the three children Jochebed bare: *and she bare unto Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister* (Numbers 26:59). The leaders of the Exodus generation now begin to be gathered to their people; before this one chapter is done, Aaron too will die. The generation that came out of Egypt does not enter the land — even its prophetess, even its priest.

threads.title: Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me — Moses barred
threads.summary_md: The cost is spoken at once: *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them* (Numbers 20:12). The place is named for the strife: *This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Yashar'el (Israel) strove with Yahuah (LORD), and he was sanctified in them* (Numbers 20:13). The failure was not the magnitude of a sin but the failure to hallow Yahuah before the watching people — to take the glory of the gift, *must we fetch you water* (Numbers 20:10), as though the water were Moses' and Aaron's to give. Psalm 106 weighs both sides: the people's provoking and Moses' answer — *They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes* (Psalm 106:32); *Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips* (Psalm 106:33). Yahuah's own later words fix the charge unchanged: *because ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Deuteronomy 32:51); *to sanctify me at the water before their eyes: that is the water of Meribah* (Numbers 27:14). This is conduct held to account WITHIN the covenant — the leader bound to the higher standard, the holiness of Yahuah upheld even in His own servant's discipline — never Torah made a curse.

threads.title: Edom refused his brother passage — the brother denied
threads.summary_md: Moses appeals to Edom on the ground of kinship: *Thus saith thy brother Yashar'el (Israel), Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us* (Numbers 20:14), and asks only safe passage by the king's high way, offering even to pay for water. Edom answers with the sword: *Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword* (Numbers 20:18), and *Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand* (Numbers 20:20). So *Edom refused to give Yashar'el (Israel) passage through his border: wherefore Yashar'el (Israel) turned away from him* (Numbers 20:21). Yashar'el (Israel) did not force the brother's land, for Yahuah had given Seir to Esau and forbidden the seizure: *Ye are to pass through the coast of your brethren the children of Esau* (Deuteronomy 2:4); *Meddle not with them... because I have given mount Seir unto Esau for a possession* (Deuteronomy 2:5). But the refusal of the brother is the early seed of a long enmity — the seed-war of Esau against Jacob that Obadiah indicts: *For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee* (Obadiah 1:10); *In the day that thou stoodest on the other side... even thou wast as one of them* (Obadiah 1:11); *thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger* (Obadiah 1:12). The kinship Moses invoked is the kinship Edom betrayed.

threads.title: Fishers of men — the beginning of the regathering of scattered Yashar'el (Israel) (Jeremiah 16, Ezekiel 47, Amos 4, Habakkuk 1)
threads.summary_md: *And he says unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men* (Matthew 4:19). This is not the launch of generic evangelism; it is the first stroke of the second exodus the prophets foretold — the regathering of scattered Yashar'el (Israel). Jeremiah names a coming day defined not by the first exodus but by the ingathering: *Therefore, behold, the days come, says Yahuah (LORD), that it shall no more be said, Yahuah (LORD) lives, that brought up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) out of the land of Egypt; But, Yahuah (LORD) lives, that brought up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them* (Jeremiah 16:14-15). And he names the means: *Behold, I will send for many fishers, says Yahuah (LORD), and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every mountain, and from every hill, and out of the holes of the rocks* (Jeremiah 16:16). The apostles are the first of those fishers. The fishing-image runs the length of the prophets: the hooks that dragged Yashar'el OUT in judgment — *he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks* (Amos 4:2) — and the conqueror's net that caught them — *they catch them in their net, and gather them in their drag* (Habakkuk 1:15), men made *as the fishes of the sea* (Habakkuk 1:14) — are reversed by the fishers Yahuah sends to bring them home, standing on the banks of the river of life: *the fishers shall stand upon it from En-gedi even unto En-eglaim; they shall be a place to spread forth nets... as the fish of the great sea, exceeding many* (Ezekiel 47:10), where *every thing shall live whither the river comes* (47:9). The catch is the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el scattered among the nations (Matthew 10:6; 15:24) — a two-house restoration, NOT the grafting of the nations by faith-confession, and never a casting-off of his people: *Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid... Elohim (God) hath not cast away his people which he foreknew* (Romans 11:1-2).

threads.title: Fishers of men — the beginning of the regathering of scattered Yashar'el (Israel) (Jeremiah 16, Ezekiel 47, Amos 4, Habakkuk 1)
threads.summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Come you after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men* (Mark 1:17). The call is the first stroke of the second exodus the prophets foretold — the regathering of scattered Yashar'el (Israel), not the launch of generic evangelism. Jeremiah names the coming day by the ingathering itself: *it shall no more be said, Yahuah (LORD) lives, that brought up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) out of the land of Egypt; But, Yahuah (LORD) lives, that brought up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from the land of the north, and from all the lands whither he had driven them* (Jeremiah 16:14-15) — and the means: *Behold, I will send for many fishers, says Yahuah (LORD), and they shall fish them; and after will I send for many hunters* (Jeremiah 16:16). The apostles are the first of those fishers. The prophets' fishing-image is first judgment — *he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks* (Amos 4:2); men made *as the fishes of the sea* (Habakkuk 1:14), *they catch them in their net, and gather them in their drag* (Habakkuk 1:15) — the hooks and net that dragged Yashar'el OUT into exile. The fishers Yahuah sends reverse them, standing on the river of life: *the fishers shall stand upon it from En-gedi even unto En-eglaim; they shall be a place to spread forth nets... exceeding many* (Ezekiel 47:10), where *every thing shall live whither the river comes* (47:9). The catch is the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el scattered among the nations (Matthew 10:6; 15:24) — two-house restoration, NOT the nations grafted by faith-confession, and never a casting-off: *Hath Elohim (God) cast away his people? Elohim (God) forbid... Elohim (God) hath not cast away his people which he foreknew* (Romans 11:1-2).

threads.title: "Ask what I shall give thee" — Yahuah appears to Solomon at Gibeon
threads.summary_md: Solomon, *strengthened in his kingdom* (2 Chronicles 1:1), gathers all Yashar'el (Israel) to the tabernacle Moses made, at the great high place of Gibeon, and *offered a thousand burnt offerings upon it* (2 Chronicles 1:6). That worship is no empty ritual; the same lavish devotion is recorded in Kings: *the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar* (1 Kings 3:4). Then comes the open door: *In that night did Elohim (God) appear unto Solomon, and said unto him, Ask what I shall give thee* (2 Chronicles 1:7) — the very words Kings preserves, *In Gibeon Yahuah (LORD) appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and Elohim (God) said, Ask what I shall give thee* (1 Kings 3:5). Yahuah lays his whole treasury before the king and waits to see what the heart will choose. That same invitation stands open still: *If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of Elohim (God), that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him* (James 1:5).

threads.title: A House for the Name, and a Wise Son Given
threads.summary_md:
*And Solomon determined to build an house for the name of Yahuah (LORD), and an house for his kingdom* (2 Chronicles 2:1). The building is not Solomon's invention; in the wisdom tradition the son confesses the charge and its pattern: *You have commanded me to build a temple upon your holy mount, and an altar in the city in which you dwellest, a resemblance of the holy tabernacle, which you have prepared from the beginning* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:8). The house is a resemblance of the pattern Yahuah prepared from the beginning.

Even the nations confess the Maker behind it. Huram (Hiram) the king of Tyre answers: *Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that made heaven and earth, who hath given to David the king a wise son, endued with prudence and understanding, that might build an house for Yahuah (LORD), and an house for his kingdom* (2 Chronicles 2:12). The wisdom prayer addresses that same Creator — *O Yahuah (God) of my fathers, and Yahuah (God) of mercy, who have made all things with your word* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:1) — and names the wisdom that builds: *And wisdom was with you: which knoweth your works, and was present when you madest the world* (Wisdom of Solomon 9:9). A king of the nations blesses the Creator; the wise son builds by the wisdom given to make heaven and earth.

threads.title: The House Built for the Appointed Worship — An Ordinance For Ever
threads.summary_md:
Solomon names exactly what the temple is for: *Behold, I build an house to the name of Yahuah Elohai (the LORD my God), to dedicate it to him, and to burn before him sweet incense, and for the continual shewbread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the sabbaths, and on the new moons, and on the solemn feasts of Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God). This is an ordinance for ever to Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 2:4). The house is raised to house the appointed worship — and every element is already a perpetual command in the Torah.

The sweet incense: *And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at even, he shall burn incense upon it, a perpetual incense before Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations* (Exodus 30:8; with 30:7, morning by morning). The continual shewbread: *Every sabbath he shall set it in order before Yahuah (LORD) continually, being taken from the children of Yashar'el (Israel) by an everlasting covenant* (Leviticus 24:8). The morning-and-evening offering: *two lambs of the first year without spot day by day, for a continual burnt offering* (Numbers 28:3). And the sabbaths, new moons, and solemn feasts are Yahuah's own calendar: *Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts* (Leviticus 23:2).

Solomon calls it *an ordinance for ever*, and the word holds to the end. Isaiah sees the same new moon and sabbath kept in the world to come: *And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:23). The appointed times the temple was built to keep are never abolished — they are the worship of the new earth.

threads.title: The house of Yahuah on mount Moriah — the place of the offering
threads.summary_md: *Then Solomon began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD) at Jerusalem in mount Moriah, where Yahuah (LORD) appeared unto David his father, in the place that David had prepared in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite* (2 Chronicles 3:1). One verse binds three altars into one mount. It is the land of Moriah of the Akedah: *get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering* (Genesis 22:2), where Abraham named the place in prophecy — *Yahuah Yireh (Jehovah-jireh): as it is said to this day, In the mount of Yahuah (LORD) it shall be seen* (Genesis 22:14). It is the threshingfloor of Ornan where the angel of Yahuah halted the plague and David was commanded to build: *set up an altar unto Yahuah (LORD) in the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite* (1 Chronicles 21:18), and fire from heaven sealed it — *he answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering* (1 Chronicles 21:26; cf. the parallel *the plague was stayed from Yashar'el (Israel)*, 2 Samuel 24:25). David himself declared it: *This is the house of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), and this is the altar of the burnt offering for Yashar'el (Israel)* (1 Chronicles 22:1). Akedah, the altar of mercy, and the temple converge on one ground — the place of substitution, where Yahuah provides the offering in the stead of the son, pointing to the Messiah's own offering. And before the house stand the two pillars: *the name of that on the right hand Jachin (he shall establish), and the name of that on the left Boaz (in him is strength)* (2 Chronicles 3:17).

threads.title: The Molten Sea and the Lavers — The Washing to Approach the Holy
threads.summary_md: *Also he made a molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim... He made also ten lavers... to wash in them: such things as they offered for the burnt offering they washed in them; but the sea was for the priests to wash in* (2 Chronicles 4:2,6). After the altar comes the water: no one approaches the holy unwashed. This is the wilderness laver multiplied — *Thou shalt also make a laver of brass... to wash withal... and thou shalt put it between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar* (Exodus 30:18), a washing that was a matter of life: *they shall wash with water, that they die not* (Exodus 30:20). The bronze water foreshadowed the cleansing the Messiah provides: *the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit)* (Titus 3:5), the bride *cleansed with the washing of water by the word* (Ephesians 5:26), the drawing near *having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water* (Hebrews 10:22). And the sea *stood upon twelve oxen* facing the four quarters (2 Chronicles 4:4) — the twelve tribes bearing up the means of cleansing, the same twelve whose names stand on the gates and foundations of the city of Yahuah (LORD): *the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Revelation 21:12). Cleansing precedes communion, and the whole house of Yashar'el (Israel) bears it up.

threads.title: The Two Tables in the Ark — the Torah at the Heart of the House
threads.summary_md:
When the ark is carried into the Most Holy place of Solomon's temple, the Chronicler stops to tell us what it holds: *There was nothing in the ark save the two tables which Moses put therein at Horeb, when Yahuah (LORD) made a covenant with the children of Yashar'el (Israel), when they came out of Egypt* (2 Chronicles 5:10). At the very center of the sanctuary, under the wings of the cherubim, sits the Torah — the covenant words written at Horeb.

This was the ark's purpose from the first: *And thou shalt put into the ark the testimony which I shall give thee* (Exodus 25:16); *And he took and put the testimony into the ark... and put the mercy seat above upon the ark* (Exodus 40:20) — mercy enthroned ABOVE the tables, never apart from them. Moses bore witness, *I... put the tables in the ark which I had made; and there they be* (Deuteronomy 10:5), and the parallel record agrees: *There was nothing in the ark save the two tables of stone, which Moses put there at Horeb* (1 Kings 8:9).

Generations later the apostle looks back and names the same contents — the ark *wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant* (Hebrews 9:4). Not a discarded relic, but *the tables of the covenant*: the covenant instruction is the thing the holiest place was built to guard. The Torah is not abolished; it is central.

threads.title: As One, to Make One Sound — the United Praise That Inhabits the Presence
threads.summary_md:
Before the Glory descends, the worship is gathered into a single voice: *the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking Yahuah (LORD); and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of musick, and praised Yahuah (LORD), saying, For he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever* (2 Chronicles 5:13). The priests and the Levite singers — Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun — do not merely sing together; they make ONE sound.

The psalm tells why this matters: *But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Psalm 22:3). Yahuah is enthroned upon the praises of his people. The united confession — *his mercy endureth for ever* — builds the throne, and the cloud fills the house in the very moment the one voice rises. The setting of the descending Glory is a people made one in praise.

threads.title: The Glory Filled the House — the Manifest Presence Claims the Finished Temple
threads.summary_md:
As the one voice rises, the Presence comes down: *then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of Yahuah (LORD); So that the priests could not stand to minister by reason of the cloud: for the glory of Yahuah (LORD) had filled the house of Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 5:13-14). The completed house is claimed exactly as the completed tabernacle was: *Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) filled the tabernacle* (Exodus 40:34); *And Moses was not able to enter... because the cloud abode thereon* (Exodus 40:35). The parallel record agrees: *the cloud filled the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (1 Kings 8:10), *So that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud: for the glory of Yahuah (LORD) had filled the house of Yahuah (LORD)* (1 Kings 8:11).

This Glory is the manifest Presence — the visible One whom Isaiah saw enthroned, when *the house was filled with smoke* (Isaiah 6:4) at the threefold *Holy*. He is the Formed Son, the visible Glory who has a Father, not a co-equal second person. When the Glory departs Solomon's house in judgment it does not vanish forever: *behold, the glory of the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came from the way of the east... and the earth shined with his glory* (Ezekiel 43:2), and *the glory of Yahuah (LORD) filled the house* (Ezekiel 43:5) — the Presence regathered to the restored temple.

The pattern reaches its end in the temple in heaven: *And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of Elohim (God), and from his power; and no man was able to enter into the temple* (Revelation 15:8) — the same Glory, the same overwhelmed servants who *could not stand to minister*, from Horeb's tent to the consummation.

threads.title: An House of Habitation in the Thick Darkness
threads.summary_md: Solomon opens the dedication where Yashar'el (Israel) first met Yahuah (LORD): *Then said Solomon, Yahuah (LORD) hath said that he would dwell in the thick darkness. But I have built an house of habitation for thee, and a place for thy dwelling for ever.* (2 Chronicles 6:1-2). The *thick darkness* is no new place — it is Sinai. *And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where Elohim (God) was.* (Exodus 20:21); *the mountain burned with fire unto the midst of heaven, with darkness, clouds, and thick darkness.* (Deuteronomy 4:11). David had already sung the dwelling: *He made darkness his secret place; his pavilion round about him were dark waters and thick clouds of the skies.* (Psalm 18:11). The twin scroll preserves the same dedication word: *Then spake Solomon, Yahuah (LORD) said that he would dwell in the thick darkness.* (1 Kings 8:12). The Glory that veiled itself on the mount comes to rest in the house built for its name.

threads.title: No Elohim Like Thee, Which Keepest Covenant and Mercy
threads.summary_md: At the altar Solomon prays the very Torah formula of Yahuah's faithfulness: *O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), there is no Elohim (God) like thee in the heaven, nor in the earth; which keepest covenant, and shewest mercy unto thy servants, that walk before thee with all their hearts:* (2 Chronicles 6:14). It is Moses' word verbatim: *Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), he is Elohim (God), the faithful Elohim (God), which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations;* (Deuteronomy 7:9). Mercy is kept with *them that love him AND keep his commandments* — never love without obedience. The exiles carry this same prayer back to heaven: *the great and terrible Elohim (God), that keepeth covenant and mercy for them that love him and observe his commandments:* (Nehemiah 1:5); *O Yahuah (Lord), the great and dreadful Elohim (God), keeping the covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his commandments;* (Daniel 9:4). The prayer in the house and the prayer from captivity are one covenant prayer.

threads.title: The Stranger — An House of Prayer for All People
threads.summary_md: Solomon throws the doors open to the outsider: *Moreover concerning the stranger, which is not of thy people Yashar'el (Israel), but is come from a far country for thy great name's sake... if they come and pray in this house; Then hear thou from the heavens... that all people of the earth may know thy name, and fear thee, as doth thy people Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 6:32-33). Isaiah names the house exactly so: *make them joyful in my house of prayer... for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.* (Isaiah 56:7) — the nations who come to fear the Name welcomed at the altar. When the temple is corrupted, the Formed Son defends that founding purpose: *It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.* (Matthew 21:13). And the prayer the house was built to receive is the lowly cry for mercy: *And the publican, standing afar off... smote upon his breast, saying, Elohim (God) be merciful to me a sinner.* (Luke 18:13). The stranger from a far country and the despised publican alike find the house of prayer answers all who fear Yahuah's name.

threads.title: If Thou Wilt Walk Before Me: the Throne Established
threads.summary_md: To Solomon himself Yahuah sets the Davidic throne on a covenant condition of obedience: *if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded thee, and shalt observe my statutes and my judgments; then will I stablish the throne of thy kingdom, according as I have covenanted with David thy father, saying, There shall not fail thee a man to be ruler in Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 7:17-18). The Kings account preserves the same night-word — *if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked, in integrity of heart... and wilt keep my statutes and my judgments* (1 Kings 9:4), *Then I will establish the throne of thy kingdom upon Yashar'el (Israel) for ever* (1 Kings 9:5). The promise rests on the covenant sworn to David: *He shall build an house for my name, and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever* (2 Samuel 7:13). And the Psalm sings the same conditioned line: *If thy children will keep my covenant and my testimony that I shall teach them, their children shall also sit upon thy throne for evermore* (Psalm 132:12). The throne is secured by walking in Yahuah's statutes — Torah-keeping is its appointed path, not its enemy — and it points beyond Solomon to the one Davidic King in whom the throne stands for ever.

threads.title: If Ye Forsake My Statutes: Plucked Up by the Roots
threads.summary_md: The same night-word that promises the throne sets the other fork plainly: *But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments, which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship them; then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land... and this house, which I have sanctified for my name, will I cast out of my sight, and will make it to be a proverb and a byword among all nations* (2 Chronicles 7:19-20). This is the Deuteronomy-28 curse exactly — *if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to observe to do all his commandments... that all these curses shall come upon thee* (Deuteronomy 28:15) and *Yahuah (LORD) shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other* (Deuteronomy 28:64). The curse falls for FORSAKING the statutes and serving other gods; it is the penalty for breaking the covenant, never the Torah itself. The Kings word is nearly verbatim — *But if ye shall at all turn from following me... and will not keep my commandments and my statutes... but go and serve other gods* (1 Kings 9:6), *Then will I cut off Yashar'el (Israel) out of the land... and this house... will I cast out of my sight; and Yashar'el (Israel) shall be a proverb and a byword* (1 Kings 9:7). The Sinai covenant set the same clause — *if ye will not hearken unto me, and will not do all these commandments* (Leviticus 26:14), *I will scatter you among the heathen... and your land shall be desolate* (Leviticus 26:33). And Jeremiah points to Shiloh as the precedent the temple would follow — *go ye now unto my place which was in Shiloh, where I set my name at the first, and see what I did to it for the wickedness of my people Yashar'el (Israel)* (Jeremiah 7:12), *Therefore will I do unto this house, which is called by my name... as I have done to Shiloh* (Jeremiah 7:14). The reason is one: *Because they forsook Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers... therefore hath he brought all this evil upon them* (2 Chronicles 7:22).

threads.title: Because the places are holy, whereunto the ark hath come
threads.summary_md: Before the offerings are named, the chapter shows what kind of regard the holy commands. Solomon will not let Pharaoh's daughter dwell on ground the ark has touched: *And Solomon brought up the daughter of Pharaoh out of the city of David unto the house that he had built for her: for he said, My wife shall not dwell in the house of David king of Yashar'el (Israel), because the places are holy, whereunto the ark of Yahuah (LORD) hath come* (2 Chronicles 8:11). This is the coming he guards — the ark set into the most holy place: *And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of Yahuah (LORD) unto his place, to the oracle of the house, into the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubims* (2 Chronicles 5:7). Holiness has been graded by the ark's presence from the first: *And the vail shall divide unto you between the holy place and the most holy* (Exodus 26:33). And the ark carries a holiness that cannot be treated lightly: *they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die* (Numbers 4:15). Solomon honours that same weight. Where the ark of Yahuah has come, the ground is no longer common; the king orders his own household around the holiness of the place.

threads.title: "To be king for Yahuah" — the throne of Yahuah, to do judgment and justice
threads.summary_md: The queen's blessing reaches past the king to the One who set him there: *Blessed be Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which delighted in thee to set thee on his throne, to be king for Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God): because thy Elohim (God) loved Yashar'el (Israel), to establish them for ever, therefore made he thee king over them, to do judgment and justice* (2 Chronicles 9:8). The seat is named without ambiguity: *Then Solomon sat on the throne of Yahuah (LORD) as king instead of David his father* (1 Chronicles 29:23). It is Yahuah's throne; the king reigns FOR him, never in his own right, and the charge is *judgment and justice*. The royal psalm prays for exactly that gift — *Give the king thy judgments, O Elohim (God), and thy righteousness unto the king's son* (Psalm 72:1); *He shall judge thy people with righteousness, and thy poor with judgment* (Psalm 72:2). Righteous rule is Yahuah's judgments lent to his vicegerent. What Solomon does in figure, the promised Branch will do in truth and for ever: *I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth* (Jeremiah 23:5).

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The kingdom divides: the two houses begin
threads.summary_md: Here is the wound that runs the rest of the canon. When *all Yashar'el (Israel) saw that the king would not hearken unto them, the people answered the king, saying, What portion have we in David? and we have none inheritance in the son of Jesse: every man to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel)* (10:16), and *Yashar'el (Israel) rebelled against the house of David unto this day* (10:19). The ten northern tribes — Israel, Ephraim, Joseph — tear away from the southern house of Yahudah (Judah) and the throne of David. The parallel says it the same: *to your tents, O Yashar'el (Israel)... So Yashar'el (Israel) departed unto their tents* (1 Kings 12:16). The number was prophesied: *Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). Yet a remnant is kept — *I will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant's sake* (1 Kings 11:13) — and so *Rehoboam reigned over* the children of Yashar'el in the cities of Yahudah (10:17). This is the origin of the TWO houses. The division is real history, the judgment on Solomon's idolatry; it is NEVER one house replacing the other. And it is the very breach the prophets swear to heal: *I will take the stick of Joseph... and the stick of Yahudah (Judah), and make them one stick, and they shall be one in mine hand* (Ezekiel 37:19); *they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all* (Ezekiel 37:22); *the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head* (Hosea 1:11); *the house of Yahudah (Judah) shall walk with the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and they shall come together out of the land of the north* (Jeremiah 3:18). The split is the history; the regathering is the hope.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The cause was of Elohim: Ahijah's word performed
threads.summary_md: Rehoboam's hardness is not blind chance. *So the king hearkened not unto the people: for the cause was of Elohim (God), that Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat* (10:15). The word came years earlier in a field: *the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field* (1 Kings 11:29), and rending the garment he said, *Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee* (1 Kings 11:31). The folly of the young men is the instrument; the judgment is Yahuah's — exile-grade discipline for Solomon's idolatry, never the Torah itself failing. And even as ten tribes are torn away, the covenant lamp is kept: *I will give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there* (1 Kings 11:36). The throne is wounded but not extinguished — the lamp the Branch will one day fill.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 10 — The heavy yoke and the easy yoke
threads.summary_md: Rehoboam's threat was to crush: *For whereas my father put a heavy yoke upon you, I will put more to your yoke: my father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions* (10:11), and again *My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add thereto* (10:14). The tyranny of the false shepherd drove Yashar'el away. Against him stands the true King, whose call is the opposite: *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest* (Matthew 11:28); *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls* (Matthew 11:29). Where the proud son of David's line laded the people heavier and scattered them, the meek and lowly Son — the Formed One of David's house — lifts the load and gives the soul rest, gathering what tyranny scattered.

threads.title: This Thing Is Done of Me: Fight Not Against Your Brethren
threads.summary_md:
Rehoboam gathers a hundred and fourscore thousand chosen warriors *to fight against Yashar'el (Israel), that he might bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam* (2 Chronicles 11:1). But the word of Yahuah stops him through Shemaiah: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren: return every man to his house: for this thing is done of me. And they obeyed the words of Yahuah (LORD), and returned from going against Jeroboam* (2 Chronicles 11:4).

Two things are settled in that one sentence. First, the division is Yahuah's own doing — *for this thing is done of me*. The parallel record says it plainly: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren the children of Yashar'el (Israel): return every man to his house; for this thing is from me* (1 Kings 12:24), and the chapter before names the cause — *for the cause was of Elohim (God), that Yahuah (LORD) might perform his word, which he spake by the hand of Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat* (2 Chronicles 10:15). The tearing of the kingdom was a prophesied judgment, not an accident to be reversed by the sword.

Second, the two houses are *brethren*. The same word that splits them forbids them to war, because they remain one blood. It is the ground Abram took with Lot: *Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren* (Genesis 13:8). Yahudah (Judah) and Yashar'el (Israel) are divided, but they are not made two peoples to destroy each other — they are one people to be regathered.

threads.title: Jeroboam's Calves and Devils: The Counterfeit Worship
threads.summary_md:
When the kingdom split, Jeroboam feared the people's hearts would turn back if they kept going up to Jerusalem, so he built a rival worship: *the priests and the Levites that were in all Yashar'el (Israel) resorted to him* — that is, fled to Rehoboam — *for Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto Yahuah (LORD): And he ordained him priests for the high places, and for the devils, and for the calves which he had made* (2 Chronicles 11:13-15).

Every piece of it is a counterfeit. The calves are the old wilderness idol resurrected: *he made two calves of gold, and said unto them, It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem: behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28) — word for word the sin at Sinai, *they have made them a molten calf... and said, These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (Exodus 32:8). The priesthood is a counterfeit: *he made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi* (1 Kings 12:31), having cast off the true Levites. And the *devils* are the very thing the Torah forbade for ever: *they shall no more offer their sacrifices unto devils, after whom they have gone a whoring. This shall be a statute for ever unto them throughout their generations* (Leviticus 17:7).

The restored witness names the whole apparatus before it ever happened: *And they will make to themselves high places and groves and graven images, and they will worship, each his own (graven image), so as to go astray, and they will sacrifice their children to demons, and to all the works of the error of their hearts* (Jubilees 1:10). The system is the enemy here, not the people — they are the prey it was built to capture, kept from the house Yahuah chose by a king's fear.

threads.title: The Heart-Remnant of the North Seek Yahuah at Jerusalem
threads.summary_md:
The calf-cult did not capture everyone. After the Levites came south, the text adds: *And after them out of all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel) such as set their hearts to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) came to Jerusalem, to sacrifice unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers* — and *so they strengthened the kingdom of Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 11:16-17). A heart-remnant out of the northern tribes refuses Jeroboam's high places and turns toward the house Yahuah chose.

They are doing exactly what the Torah commanded: *unto the place which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) shall choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, even unto his habitation shall ye seek, and thither thou shalt come* (Deuteronomy 12:5). The same movement runs again generations later under Hezekiah — *divers of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humbled themselves, and came to Jerusalem* (2 Chronicles 30:11). And it is the same remnant Yahuah names to Elijah when all the north seemed lost: *Yet I have left me seven thousand in Yashar'el (Israel), all the knees which have not bowed unto Baal, and every mouth which hath not kissed him* (1 Kings 19:18).

This is the two-house pattern in miniature: the houses are divided, but across the divide there are always those who *set their hearts to seek Yahuah* and gather to true worship. The faithful are never wholly swept away with the counterfeit, and the seeking remnant is the seed of the regathering to come.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:1 — Strengthened, He Forsook the Law of Yahuah (Prosperity Breeds Apostasy)
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler states the tragedy in one sentence: *And it came to pass, when Rehoboam had established the kingdom, and had strengthened himself, he forsook the law of Yahuah (LORD), and all Yashar'el (Israel) with him* (2 Chronicles 12:1). Strength is the occasion of the forsaking — and the thing forsaken is named exactly: *the law of Yahuah*. The Torah is not the curse here; it is the covenant inheritance abandoned the moment the king felt secure.

Moses had foretold this very mechanism in the wilderness. *Beware that thou forget not Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), in not keeping his commandments, and his judgments, and his statutes, which I command thee this day* (Deuteronomy 8:11) — and the trigger he named was fullness: *Then thine heart be lifted up, and thou forget Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage* (Deuteronomy 8:14). Rehoboam is the lifted-up heart of the full man, and Yahuah's discipline comes fittingly by the hand of Egypt — the house of bondage he forgot.

The Song of Moses had carved it into an image: *But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked... then he forsook Elohim (God) which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation* (Deuteronomy 32:15). And Hosea names the same disease in the northern house — *they were filled, and their heart was exalted; therefore have they forgotten me* (Hosea 13:6). Fullness, an exalted heart, then forgetting: one apostasy that fells both houses. The warning stands over every season of strength — it is precisely when we are strengthened that we are most apt to forsake the very instruction that made us.

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:6-8 — They Humbled Themselves: "Yahuah Is Righteous" (Mercy, and the Servitude That Teaches)
threads.summary_md:
Shishak comes up because *they had transgressed against Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 12:2), and Shemaiah delivers the sentence in the covenant's own grammar: *Ye have forsaken me, and therefore have I also left you in the hand of Shishak* (2 Chronicles 12:5). But the response turns the judgment: *Whereupon the princes of Yashar'el (Israel) and the king humbled themselves; and they said, Yahuah (LORD) is righteous* (2 Chronicles 12:6).

That confession is the heartbeat of the whole canon's history. To say *Yahuah is righteous* is to justify the chastening and accuse oneself — exactly Daniel's plea, *Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) is righteous in all his works which he doeth: for we obeyed not his voice* (Daniel 9:14), and the Levites' return-prayer, *thou art just in all that is brought upon us; for thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly* (Nehemiah 9:33). It is the formula Solomon was given at this very house: *If my people... shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face... then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin* (2 Chronicles 7:14).

And Yahuah answers in kind: *when Yahuah (LORD) saw that they humbled themselves... I will not destroy them, but I will grant them some deliverance* (2 Chronicles 12:7) — the not-consuming mercy Jeremiah sings from the ruins, *It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not* (Lamentations 3:22). Yet mercy is not the cancelling of discipline: *Nevertheless they shall be his servants; that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries* (2 Chronicles 12:8). The servitude is pedagogy — they will learn by contrast the difference between serving Yahuah and serving the nations. The apostolic word names the unchanging law beneath it all: *Elohim (God) resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble* (James 4:6); *Humble yourselves in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), and he shall lift you up* (James 4:10).

threads.title: 2 Chronicles 12:14 — He Prepared Not His Heart to Seek Yahuah (the Root Diagnosis)
threads.summary_md:
The Chronicler closes Rehoboam's reign with a single, piercing diagnosis: *And he did evil, because he prepared not his heart to seek Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 12:14). The evil is traced not to circumstance but to the heart — the heart that was never set, never prepared, to seek. This is the religion of the inward man: not ritual, not lineage, but the heart turned to seek.

The canon supplies the exact inverse as its standing portrait. *For Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel) statutes and judgments* (Ezra 7:10) — the prepared heart seeks the Torah, does it, and teaches it; Rehoboam's unprepared heart did none. Samuel had named this as the very condition of deliverance: *prepare your hearts unto Yahuah (LORD), and serve him only: and he will deliver you* (1 Samuel 7:3). The Chronicler himself sets up Jehoshaphat as the deliberate foil — *thou hast... prepared thine heart to seek Elohim (God)* (2 Chronicles 19:3) — measuring two kings by the single ruler of the prepared heart.

Hezekiah's intercession reveals how heavily Yahuah weighs it, even above ceremonial purity: he pleads pardon for everyone *that prepareth his heart to seek Elohim (God), Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his fathers, though he be not cleansed according to the purification of the sanctuary* (2 Chronicles 30:19). And Asaph's history-psalm warns the children not to become *a generation that set not their heart aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with Elohim (God)* (Psalm 78:8). Rehoboam is that fathers' generation in one man: the unprepared heart is the seedbed of the evil.

threads.title: The Kingdom to David For Ever — by a Covenant of Salt
threads.summary_md: Standing on mount Zemaraim, Abijah grounds the whole war not in his own right but in a sworn covenant: *Ought ye not to know that Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) gave the kingdom over Yashar'el (Israel) to David for ever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt?* (2 Chronicles 13:5). The phrase reaches straight back to Nathan's oracle — *I will set up thy seed after thee... and I will stablish the throne of his kingdom for ever... thy throne shall be established for ever* (2 Samuel 7:12-16). "Covenant of salt" is Torah's own idiom for a bond that cannot spoil or lapse: the priesthood was given *by a covenant of salt for ever* (Numbers 18:19), and *the salt of the covenant of thy Elohim (God)* was laid on every offering (Leviticus 2:13) — salt that preserves, a covenant that does not fail. The psalmist sings the same oath: *I have sworn unto David my servant, Thy seed will I establish for ever* (Psalm 89:3-4), and Yahuah swears *My covenant will I not break... I will not lie unto David* (Psalm 89:34-35). The second-Temple witnesses remember it identically — *he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Sirach 47:11), a *root to David* that abides (Sirach 47:22), the kingdom *to his posterity alone* (Sirach 45:25). And it all comes to rest on the Formed Son: *Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) shall give unto him the throne of his father David: And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end* (Luke 1:32-33). Note that Abijah pleads with the north as brethren — *O children of Yashar'el (Israel), fight ye not against Yahuah Elohim of your fathers* — both houses are still Yashar'el; the salt covenant is the throne under which the two will one day be one.

threads.title: The Golden Calves — the Counterfeit Against the Charge of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Abijah's indictment of the north is precise: *ye be a great multitude, and there are with you golden calves, which Jeroboam made you for gods. Have ye not cast out the priests of Yahuah (LORD), the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and have made you priests after the manner of the nations* (2 Chronicles 13:8-9). The calves are no innovation — Jeroboam *made two calves of gold, and said... behold thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel), which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt* (1 Kings 12:28), reviving the very wilderness lie: *These be thy gods, O Yashar'el (Israel)... they have made them a molten calf* (Exodus 32:4,8). Over against the counterfeit, Abijah sets the kept charge: *as for us, Yahuah (LORD) is our Elohim (God), and we have not forsaken him... they burn unto Yahuah every morning and every evening burnt sacrifices and sweet incense... for we keep the charge of Yahuah Eloheinu* (2 Chronicles 13:10-11). That charge is Torah's own appointment — *two lambs... day by day, for a continual burnt offering... in the morning... at even* (Numbers 28:3-4), and *sweet incense every morning... a perpetual incense* with the lamps (Exodus 30:7-8). So when Abijah cries *Elohim (God) himself is with us for our captain, and his priests with sounding trumpets to cry alarm against you. O children of Yashar'el (Israel), fight ye not against Yahuah Elohim of your fathers; for ye shall not prosper* (2 Chronicles 13:12), he is preaching the war-Torah of Deuteronomy — *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) is he that goeth with you, to fight for you* (Deuteronomy 20:1,4) — and standing in David's confidence against Goliath, *the battle is the LORD'S* (1 Samuel 17:45-47). The system is the enemy, not the people: Jeroboam built the calf-cult, and the northern brethren are its victims, kept from Jerusalem by a king's counterfeit.

threads.title: Without the True Elohim, Without a Teaching Priest, Without Law
threads.summary_md:
Azariah names Israel's long desolation by what it lacked: *Now for a long season Yashar'el (Israel) hath been without the true Elohim (God), and without a teaching priest, and without law* (2 Chronicles 15:3). The desolation is not the Torah set aside — it is the Torah withheld and unsought, a people stripped of true worship, the teaching priest gone silent, the law unread.

The prophets call this a famine. *Behold, the days come, saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD), that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahuah (LORD)* (Amos 8:11) — and the famine bites when men *run to and fro to seek the word of Yahuah (LORD), and shall not find it* (Amos 8:12). Hosea sets the same catalogue of absence over the northern house: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim* (Hosea 3:4). The lack of the Torah and the true priesthood IS the judgment — never their abolition.

But the desolation is not the end of the story, because the seeking heart still finds. *But when they in their trouble did turn unto Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), and sought him, he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:4). Hosea writes the same return: *Afterward shall the children of Yashar'el (Israel) return, and seek Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God)... in the latter days* (Hosea 3:5). The Torah foretold the turning-in-trouble: *When thou art in tribulation... if thou turn to Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt be obedient unto his voice* (Deuteronomy 4:30). And the restored witness traces the captive people who *in the land of their captivities... shall remember themselves* (Baruch 2:30) and are brought back. Trouble drives the turn; the turn ends the famine.

threads.title: A Covenant to Seek Yahuah With All the Heart: The Northern Remnant Join
threads.summary_md:
Asa heard the prophecy and acted: he *put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin... and renewed the altar of Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 15:8). Then the gathering widens beyond the south — *he gathered all Yahudah (Judah) and Benjamin, and the strangers with them out of Ephraim and Manasseh, and out of Simeon: for they fell to him out of Yashar'el (Israel) in abundance, when they saw that Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) was with him* (2 Chronicles 15:9). The faithful of the NORTHERN tribes come south in abundance — the two-house remnant gathering to true worship across the divide, drawn by the LORD's presence with Judah. This is never replacement; it is the seeking remnant of one people regathering.

There they bind themselves by covenant: *they entered into a covenant to seek Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul... And they sware unto Yahuah (LORD) with a loud voice, and with shouting, and with trumpets... and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and Yahuah (LORD) gave them rest round about* (2 Chronicles 15:12-15). The wholehearted seeking is the Shema lived: *thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might* (Deuteronomy 6:5).

This is the covenant-renewal pattern that recurs at every true reform. Joshua sealed it at the founding: *So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem* (Joshua 24:25). The returned remnant under Nehemiah did the same — *we make a sure covenant, and write it; and our princes, Levites, and priests, seal unto it* (Nehemiah 9:38) — entering *into an oath, to walk in Elohim's (God's) law, which was given by Moses... and to observe and do all the commandments of Yahuah (LORD)* (Nehemiah 10:29). To covenant to SEEK Yahuah is to covenant to KEEP his Torah; the two are one. And the promise meets the seeking exactly as Jeremiah foretold — *ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart* (Jeremiah 29:13) — for *he was found of them* (2 Chronicles 15:15).

threads.title: Asa hires Syria — the arm of flesh where once was faith
threads.summary_md: Threatened by Baasha king of Yashar'el (Israel), Asa *brought out silver and gold out of the treasures of the house of Yahuah (LORD) and of the king's house, and sent to Ben-hadad king of Syria* (2 Chronicles 16:2), buying a foreign alliance against his brother-house. The tragedy is measured against the same king's earlier faith: against the vast Ethiopian host he had *cried unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God)... for we rest on thee, and in thy name we go against this multitude* (2 Chronicles 14:11) — and was delivered. Azariah had already set the covenant terms: *if ye seek him, he will be found of you; but if ye forsake him, he will forsake you* (2 Chronicles 15:2). Hanani now collects the debt: *Because thou hast relied on the king of Syria, and not relied on Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), therefore is the host of the king of Syria escaped out of thine hand* (2 Chronicles 16:7). To lean on the arm of flesh was to forsake the One who would have been found of him — and the very host he hired escaped his grasp.

threads.title: Diseased in his feet — he sought not Yahuah but the physicians
threads.summary_md: The same self-reliance that hired Syria follows Asa to his sickbed: *Asa in the thirty and ninth year of his reign was diseased in his feet, until his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he sought not to Yahuah (LORD), but to the physicians* (2 Chronicles 16:12). The indictment is not that he consulted physicians but that he *sought not to Yahuah* — the heart that departed in v.7 does not turn back even under affliction. The northern king Ahaziah shows the same sin in starker dress: in his sickness he sends *to enquire of Baal-zebub the god of Ekron* (2 Kings 1:2), and the angel of Yahuah answers, *Is it not because there is not a Elohim (God) in Yashar'el (Israel), that ye go to enquire?* (2 Kings 1:3). Ben Sira guards the reading against any condemnation of medicine: the order is to *pray to Yahuah (God), and he will make you whole* (Sirach 38:9) FIRST, and THEN *give place to the physician, for Yahuah (God) has created him* (Sirach 38:12) — both, in order, the heart turned first to its Maker. The physician is Yahuah's own creation, honourably consulted; the wrong is to seek him INSTEAD of Yahuah. So the proverb that frames Asa's end is exact: *He that sinneth before his Maker, let him fall into the hand of the physician* (Sirach 38:15) — to fall into that hand ALONE, having forsaken Yahuah, is the judgment on the heart that departs.

threads.title: He walked in his commandments, and his heart was lifted up in the ways of Yahuah
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat is the Torah-faithful king drawn in life: *And Yahuah (LORD) was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim; But sought to Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Yashar'el (Israel)* (2 Chronicles 17:3-4). This is the Torah's own charge kept — *Ye shall walk in all the ways which Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) hath commanded you, that ye may live... and that ye may prolong your days* (Deuteronomy 5:33) — and the warning not to turn aside obeyed: *ye shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left* (Deuteronomy 5:32). When *his heart was lifted up in the ways of Yahuah (LORD): moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Yahudah (Judah)* (17:6), he is Joshua's king, the one charged *turn not from it to the right hand or to the left, that thou mayest prosper* (Joshua 1:7) and *thou shalt meditate therein day and night... for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous* (Joshua 1:8). He is Psalm 1 walked out: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly* (Psalm 1:1), whose *delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night* (Psalm 1:2), and who therefore *shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water... and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper* (Psalm 1:3) — answered in *Therefore Yahuah (LORD) stablished the kingdom in his hand... and he had riches and honour in abundance* (17:5). The Torah is not the king's burden; it is the spring of his strength.

threads.title: They taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of Yahuah with them
threads.summary_md: The heart of Jehoshaphat's revival is the itinerant teaching of the Torah to the whole people: *he sent to his princes... to teach in the cities of Yahudah (Judah)* (2 Chronicles 17:7), *and with them he sent Levites... and... priests* (17:8), *And they taught in Yahudah (Judah), and had the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Yahudah (Judah), and taught the people* (17:9). This is the household command of Deuteronomy widened to a kingdom — *thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou... walkest by the way* (Deuteronomy 6:7) — and the Levitical office Moses blessed: *They shall teach Jacob thy judgments, and Yashar'el (Israel) thy law* (Deuteronomy 33:10). It is the priestly charge of Malachi: *the priest’s lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (Malachi 2:7), and the grant Ben Sira sets on Aaron — *that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Yashar'el (Israel) in his laws* (Ecclesiasticus 45:17). Ezra walks the same threefold path, *prepared his heart to seek the law of Yahuah (LORD), and to do it, and to teach in Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezra 7:10), and the Levites of Nehemiah finish it: not bare reading but the Torah made understood, *gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading* (Nehemiah 8:8). The pattern runs straight into the Great Commission — *Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway* (Matthew 28:20). The Torah is taught and kept, never abolished; this teaching, understood by all the people, is the very substance of true revival.

threads.title: The Unequal Yoke: The Good King Joined to the House of Ahab
threads.summary_md: Jehoshaphat the righteous king of Yahudah (Judah) *had riches and honour in abundance, and joined affinity with Ahab* (2 Chronicles 18:1), the wicked king of the northern house of Yashar'el (Israel) — and at Ahab's feast he bound himself to Ahab's war: *I am as thou art, and my people as thy people; and we will be with thee in the war* (2 Chronicles 18:3). This is the unequal yoke Sha'ul forbids: *Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?* (2 Corinthians 6:14), and against which Yahuah summons his own, *come out from among them, and be ye separate* (2 Corinthians 6:17). The next chapter names the entanglement for what it is: *Shouldest thou help the ungodly, and love them that hate Yahuah (LORD)? therefore is wrath upon thee from before Yahuah (LORD)* (2 Chronicles 19:2). It is the blessed man's first warning lived out backward — *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners* (Psalm 1:1) — the danger is not the wicked's hatred but the righteous man's willingness to sit at his table and take his cause.

threads.title: The True Word Stands: No Disguise Escapes the Arrow Drawn at a Venture
threads.summary_md: Ahab tries to outwit the prophecy: *I will disguise myself, and will go to the battle; but put thou on thy robes* (2 Chronicles 18:29). But no stratagem hides a man from the word Yahuah has spoken — *be sure your sin will find you out* (Numbers 32:23). *And a certain man drew a bow at a venture, and smote the king of Yashar'el (Israel) between the joints of the harness* (2 Chronicles 18:33): an arrow loosed at random finds the one unguarded seam, for *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD)* (Proverbs 21:30). The parallel records the same arrow at a venture (1 Kings 22:34), and Ahab dies *about the time of the sun going down* (2 Chronicles 18:34) exactly as Micaiah foretold: *If thou certainly return in peace, then hath not Yahuah (LORD) spoken by me* (2 Chronicles 18:27). The four hundred who promised victory are proven liars, the one true prophet is vindicated, and the despised word stands — the disguise was no escape, and the venture-arrow no accident.

threads.title: The priests, the Levites, for the judgment of Yahuah — the higher court of Deuteronomy 17
threads.summary_md: Beyond the city gates Jehoshaphat re-establishes the supreme tribunal: *Moreover in Jerusalem did Jehoshaphat set of the Levites, and of the priests, and of the chief of the fathers of Yashar'el (Israel), for the judgment of Yahuah (LORD), and for controversies* (2 Chronicles 19:8). This is precisely the court Moses appointed for the cases too hard for the local judge — *If there arise a matter too hard for thee in judgment, between blood and blood... then shalt thou arise, and get thee up into the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose* (Deuteronomy 17:8); *And thou shalt come unto the priests the Levites, and unto the judge that shall be in those days... and they shall shew thee the sentence of judgment* (Deuteronomy 17:9). The king names the same docket — *between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and judgments* (2 Chronicles 19:10) — the very matters Deuteronomy sends up, *And thou shalt do according to the sentence... thou shalt observe to do according to all that they inform thee* (Deuteronomy 17:10), *According to the sentence of the law which they shall teach thee... thou shalt not decline from the sentence... to the right hand, nor to the left* (Deuteronomy 17:11). And so Jehoshaphat seats Amariah the chief priest over them and bids the bench, *Deal courageously, and Yahuah (LORD) shall be with the good* (2 Chronicles 19:11) — the Torah's teaching-court, courageously kept.

threads.title: The serpent of brass lifted up — beheld, and they lived
threads.summary_md: When the fiery serpents bit the people, Yahuah (LORD) said, *Make thee a fiery serpent, and set it upon a pole: and it shall come to pass, that every one that is bitten, when he looketh upon it, shall live* (Numbers 21:8), and *Moses made a serpent of brass, and put it upon a pole... when he beheld the serpent of brass, he lived* (Numbers 21:9). Yahusha (Jesus) takes this very sign as the figure of His own cross: *And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Adam be lifted up* (John 3:14), *That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life* (John 3:15). The bare look that healed the venom prefigures the believing look that gives life. Yet the sign was never the Saviour: when Yashar'el (Israel) burned incense to it, Hezekiah *brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made... and he called it Nehushtan* (2 Kings 18:4) — a piece of bronze. The lifted-up sign points beyond itself to the Formed Son; to worship the bronze is to lose the healing it once carried.

threads.title: Spring up, O well — the water springing up unto everlasting life
threads.summary_md: At Beer Yahuah (LORD) gave water, and *Yashar'el (Israel) sang this song, Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it* (Numbers 21:17), the well *digged... by the direction of the lawgiver, with their staves* (Numbers 21:18). Isaiah makes that song the song of the redeemed: *Therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation* (Isaiah 12:3). And Yahusha (Jesus) fills the figure to the brim: *the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life* (John 4:14), and at the feast, *out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water* (John 7:38) — the Spirit poured out. The well Yahuah (LORD) opened in the wilderness sings forward to the living water that never fails.

threads.title: Sihon and Og delivered into the hand of Yashar'el (Israel)
threads.summary_md: Sihon king of the Amorites *would not suffer Yashar'el (Israel) to pass through his border* (Numbers 21:23) and fell by the edge of the sword, and when Og king of Bashan came out, *Yahuah (LORD) said unto Moses, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand* (Numbers 21:34). Moses' own retelling seals the cause: *Yahuah Eloheinu (the LORD our God) delivered him before us; and we smote him, and his sons, and all his people* (Deuteronomy 2:33) — the deliverance was Yahuah (LORD)'s doing. The psalms gather both kings into His praise: He *smote great nations, and slew mighty kings... Sihon king of the Amorites, and Og king of Bashan, and all the kingdoms of Canaan* (Psalm 135:10-11), and the great Hallel rehearses each by name — *Sihon king of the Amorites: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:19), *And Og the king of Bashan: for his mercy endureth for ever* (Psalm 136:20). The victory was covenant mercy toward His people, not the sword alone.

threads.title: Thou Shalt Not Curse, For They Are Blessed
threads.summary_md: Balak the son of Zippor, terrified of a people *many* and victorious, sends to hire a curse: *Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me... for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed* (Numbers 22:6). But the verdict is already sealed in heaven. Elohim answers Balaam plainly: *Thou shalt not go with them; thou shalt not curse the people: for they are blessed* (Numbers 22:12). The blessing on Yashar'el (Israel) is not Balaam's to revoke — it stands on the oath to the fathers: *And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed* (Genesis 12:3).
